items.h: BLACKHEATH HARRIER'S WINTER TRACK MEETING, CRYSTAL PALACE, SUN. 21.3.71
items.sum: Report on Belgrave youths at Blackheath Harriers' winter track meeting at Crystal Palace, with four wins (Dave Raffell shot, Reg Hopkins high jump, Stephen Crosbie long jump, Jimmy McAffee 1000m), plus an editor's note on Martin Bloice's broken arm.
items.s: BLACKHEATH HARRIER'S WINTER TRACK MEETING, CRYSTAL PALACE, SUN. 21.3.71 Report on Belgrave youths at Blackheath Harriers' winter track meeting at Crystal Palace, with four wins (Dave Raffell shot, Reg Hopkins high jump, Stephen Crosbie long jump, Jimmy McAffee 1000m), plus an editor's note on Martin Bloice's broken arm. We went to this meeting with just eight club members - and recorded four wins. This is, I would think, the biggest of the winter meetings, with Clubs from all over the South of England (and indeed a few from the North represented) Most of those who enter are just out to get the feel of things again after the winter recess, and so the competition is none too serious. Nevertheless, some worthwhile performances were recorded, in spite of the fact it was a miserable, cold, windy day. Our lads performed equally well, Our first win was in of all things the Youth's Shot putt, Dave Raffell reaching 11 metres with the 10lb ball. Dave is a big lad for his age, and a keen sportsman, he is now taking this event very seriously, training most nights with the use of weights. We expect him to do great things this summer, indeed I would prophesy that other things allowing - education etc.,we now have at last a future international field events man in the Club. Our second win of the day was with Reg Hopkins doing his thing (Fosbury) high jump. Like Dave,Reg is now taking this field event seriously, working to a schedule with weights and excercises and trying to perfect a technique. He managed to equal his personal best of 1.73 (5 ft. 8 ins) in spite of the winter conditions already mentioned. This height would have won him the junior event and placed him 5th in the senior. His ambition is to clear 6 ft. this summer, while still aged 16 years. You would think we had done well enough with two field event wins but we had forgotten Stephen Crosbie. Although he failed in the sprints, finishing last in his race, he came back with a vengance in the long jump and recorded 5-67m to win the Youths event. Our interest in the track was equally rewarding, Jimmy McAffee showing tremendous form in coming through the field and taking a commanding lead to win the Youths 1000m in 2m49.2s. Simon Holmes made it a Belgrave one-two finishing second in 2m55.7s. We are so used to seeing Martin Bloice first past the post that we were a little disappointed to see him finish 4th in the Junior 300m in 38.0s. Martin was the first to agree on leaving the track that he sadly needed training having done virtually nothing for weeks. This run shook him up and he has since got down to work and is determined to recapture his old form. David Harvey ran in the 600m and although not in the first four, his was a very worthwhile effort. His ambition is to break 2.00 for the 800mts this season, I have every reason to believe he will manage it if he continues the way he is going. His time in this race of 1m31.9s seems to point the way. Our only other competitor was Tony Holmes. Although Tony is not yet in the same class as the other members he is very keen and trains hard in a business like manner. This I'am sure will bring him sooner or later up with the others. He managed, however, 3m17.5. in the Youths 1000m although still only a boy. (Ed.'s note: Since Reg wrote this, Martin Bloice has been out of action with a broken arm. Before his accident, however, Martin showed promising form for Lambeth in Paris. The latest news is that he is on the mend , so that there is still time for some good performances this summer. As will be seen from reports elsewhere in the magazine, there have been a number of excellent results from our youths since the Blackheath meeting.) items.sum: Report of the youths' and juniors' National cross-country championships at Norwich, where the youths were a disappointing eighth and the juniors 24th of 25 teams.
items.s: NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIPS - NORWICH 6th March 1971 Report of the youths' and juniors' National cross-country championships at Norwich, where the youths were a disappointing eighth and the juniors 24th of 25 teams. YOUTHS The big day our lads had spent months building up for saw us finish a dissappointing eighth. Once again only Mark Clancy (153rd) ran to form. Bill Curtin (28th) led the team home with Peter Carton four places behind. Tony Binda came 50th, John Stow 175th and Pat Breslin 197th The whole team except Mark appeared jaded - Bill although physically below par lacked nothing in determination - to beat Peter. A pity Peter wasn't on form, if he had come 5th or 6th one imagines Bill would still have run "eyeballs out" to beat him and perhaps have come 3rd or 4th. Lets hope in years to come Bill can channel his energies into trying to carve up the rest of the field, and not just his clubmates. Of course afterwards we had the usual 'What went wrong'? questions. The truth is that the team got fit far too early in the season and did not ease right off for the odd week or so now and again. The team manager accepts responsibility for having got the runners to their peak so early but feels that two of the runners in particular ignored advice to ease down at certain periods. The blame for our lack of success must be shared therefore. On the basis, however that "a man who never made a mistake never made anything" the individuals concerned having learned vital lessons, and are not in the least perturbed now the event is over. There are many seasons ahead to make amands, and this will surely happen. JUNIORS. Twenty fourth place out of twenty five teams inspires one to write just "what else can one expect if runners train irregularly" 227 finished 1st team 64 points Belgrave Harriers 850 points (one detects room for improvement) J. items.sum: Report on Bill Curtin finishing 27th for the Republic of Ireland in the International Junior cross-country at San Sebastian while still a youth.
items.s: 20th March San Sebastion - International Junior C.C. Report on Bill Curtin finishing 27th for the Republic of Ireland in the International Junior cross-country at San Sebastian while still a youth. Bill Curtin, representing the Rebublic of Ireland, excelled himself to finish twenty-seventh in this event coming just below halfway up the field. The bulk of the field in this event were in the true junior category whilst Bill is still a youth. This makes his fine position even more praiseworthy. A run of this calibre in the National Youths two weeks earlier would surely have placed Bill in the first six of this event at least. Now that Bill has been recognised by the Irish selectors, one must hope that regular international appearances over the next dozen or more years will provide the stimulus to keep him going for many seasons to come. Even if Bill does have to miss the occasional club appearance (as in the Southern this year because of selection for an invitation event in Spain) the eventual outcome will be very much for the good of the Club, as these international events will raise his standard even higher. items.s: LONDON SCHOOLS' CHAMPIONSHIPS - Crystal Palace, June 12, 1971 Report on Belgravians at the London Schools' Championships, with Reg Hopkins (high jump record), Peter Carton (800m) and Mick Marshall (100m) selected for the All-England schools' championships. Three Belgravians will represent London in the All-England schools' championships, following some fine performances in the London championships. Pride of place must go to Reg Hopkins, who set a record in winning the intermediate high-jump at 5' 11¾" - and must now have high hopes of clearing 6' this summer, at the age of sixteen. Peter Carton was our other winner at this meeting, taking the senior 800m. in 1m. 55.7s., while Mick Marshall scorched his way up the 100m. track, for second place in the senior race in 11.0s., the same time at the winner's. The above three have been selected for the All-England meeting, but Dave Harvey is still in with a chance of selection, following his third place in the intermediate 800m. in 2m. 3.2s. He only needs to record a somewhat faster time. Fourth place in the intermediate 1,500m. went to Simon Holmes in 4m. 19s., while Dave Raffell was fourth in the intermediate shot. items.label: September 1972
items.sum: Editorial explaining the gazette's difficult 18 months, announcing Alan Mead as the new Honorary Editor from the December issue, and saying this delayed issue condenses five issues' material.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial explaining the gazette's difficult 18 months, announcing Alan Mead as the new Honorary Editor from the December issue, and saying this delayed issue condenses five issues' material. Yes, believe it or not, you are looking at another edition of THE BELGRAVIAN. Our gazette has survived many difficult periods during it's existence these last 47 years, and the last 18 months has been no exception. This is not the time, however, to dwell on those difficulties. Let us instead tell you of the interesting prospects in store. First, we are delighted to announce that Alan Mead has offered to take on the Editorship of the gazette. Alan played a part in many editions during the 1960's and his experience and enthusiasm will surely produce a publication to which we can all look forward. The magazine is intended to reflect the results, news and views of the whole membership, and any contributions the membership can make towards a better magazine will be welcomed by the new Honorary Editor at 17, High Ashton, Kingston Hill, Kingston, Surrey. Second, the first edition of the new Editorship will be the December issue, which it is hoped will be in your hands by the end of that month. So you will have the relative luxury of two gazettes in the span of a month - this issue having been delayed until November. This edition has not been produced in the form we would have liked. With the need to condense the material for five issues into one much editting was necessary. This was done with the two principal functions of our magazine in mind. They are 1. To distribute Club news of a wide range to the whole membership and thus maintain contact with our distant and non-active members 2. To provide a comprehensive record of Club activities. We believe that when it becomes impossible to achieve both of these aims then the latter takes priority. We would therefore ask you to bear with us when ploughing your way through the many pages of historical results and hope that you will find the December issue a refreshing contrast. Alan Mead Alan Mead new Honorary Editor of The Belgravian from the December 1972 issue; played a part in many editions during the 1960s Alan Mead Alan Kingston Hill Kingston

items.label: September 1972
items.sum: Congratulations to John Bicourt, Wil Wesch and Cliff Brooks on their selection for the 1972 Munich Olympics, with their results, and sympathy for Ray Middleton, who was not selected for the 50 kilos walk.
items.s: Congratulations to John Bicourt, Wil Wesch and Cliff Brooks on their selection for the 1972 Munich Olympics, with their results, and sympathy for Ray Middleton, who was not selected for the 50 kilos walk. Our belated congratulations go out to three Belgravians who achieved selection for the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich. JOHN BICOURT, who for much of the season was Britain's No 2 steeplechaser, was selected for the 3000 metres steeplechase. Despite a time of 8:38.8 in his heat he was eliminated, as were the other two Britons in this event. WIL WESCH, who was the life and soul of Belgrave walking teams last year, is now back in Germany. His efforts during the year earned him a place in West Germany's 20 kilometres walk team. Wil finished 16th in 1:35:20.6. CLIFF BROOKS has shown a marked improvement in his all-round abilities these last two years. His efforts were rewarded by selection for the Olympic decathlon by his native Barbados. Cliff was going well at Munich until the third event on the second day - the pole vault. He was unable to achieve a height, along with many competitors of note (Gabbett, GB, was 4th when eliminated at the vault), and ceased competition with a 7 event score of 4842 (11.19, 22'-4¼", 38'-5", 5'-8.7/8", 49.8, 16.37, 111'-2½"). We are indeed proud of all three. Spare a thought, though, for the man who has served his Club and Country so well in the past, and so very nearly did so again -- if he had been allowed to. RAY MIDDLETON was put forward by the R.W.A. as third string for the 50 kilos walk, but only two names were selected by the British Board. Just as it seemed that RAY would fill the vacant third spot the Board announced that Paul Nihill would "double up" and do the 50 kilos as well as the 20 kilos. They are just the bare facts, but they are enough for us to accord Ray our every sympathy. He also has our admiration for the way he overcame his disappointment and the temptation to retire from competition, and resumed training to carry our colours to the fore once again. items.label: September 1972
items.sum: The outgoing president's 1971 notes: thanks for his second term, hopes for a keener competitive edge, and tributes to Micky Pyer, John Moullin (Tommy Green Cup for the 100 miles walk), Jack Goswell (new R.W.A. President), Rodney Heward-Mills and South London Harriers on their centenary.
items.s: PAST PRESIDENTS' PARS 1971 The outgoing president's 1971 notes: thanks for his second term, hopes for a keener competitive edge, and tributes to Micky Pyer, John Moullin (Tommy Green Cup for the 100 miles walk), Jack Goswell (new R.W.A. President), Rodney Heward-Mills and South London Harriers on their centenary. PAST PRESIDENTS' PARS 1971 I am very grateful to the Club for the honour they accorded me when I became President for the second time, in 1970-71. I have enjoyed my extra year in office, and now look forward to making my contribution from the main body of the Committee, instead of from the platform as for so many years past. It will not be easy to accustom myself to changed circumstances, but no doubt the new President and new Hon. Secretaries will be indulgent towards an old-stager! There is no doubt that as a Club the Belgrave Harriers are in good heart - the spirit of service to our Sport and our own particular organisation is as good as ever it was. I do confess, however, that I would like to see rather more cutting edge to our competitive ventures, a little more intensity of effort, a little more "devil" in taking on the opposition, a little more long-term appreciation of what we could do if we really made up our minds well in advance. The standards we set ourselves are, of course, very high, and we know that our failures could spell out relative success to other clubs. We can easily justify these high standards we have set if everyone will do just that little bit extra in every field of Club life. We have many young athletes of great potential appearing in our colours throughout the whole of the year. A few more good friends in our ranks, some conscientious preparation and determined competition and Belgrave will be the "tops" in all the main branches of amateur athletics. What a tremendous example Micky Pyer is to us all! Micky started his running with the Club almost fifty years ago and attained a good measure of success in Surrey and Club championships over the country and on the track. Years later he coached many of our younger middle-distance runners, and recently decided to add to his coaching qualifications by studying javelin throwing. He duly qualified, and is now a recognised coach and doing excellent work with the youngsters, which we hope will long continue. He has shown that advancing years are no excuse for any of us, and that we can all add to our usefulness if so minded What an example to us all! The Committee has decided that the "Tommy Green" Cup for the best single performance of the year by a Club member should go to John Moullin for winning the Open 100 Miles Walk held in June in the Ewhurst area. John's performance is the second best ever recorded and we congratulate him most heartily on his splendid win - and on holding for a year the Cup presented by our 1932 Olympic winner. Congratulations also to Past President Jack Goswell, who has been elected President of the Race Walking Association. Jack has given (and still gives) tremendous service to our Club, and to Walking, and his many years of really hard work fully justify his elevation to the Presidency of the R.W.A. This election honours the Club as well as the individual; and in this connection we acknowledge with grateful thanks the additional hard work and support given by Mrs. Joan Goswell over many years. A young member who deserves the highest praise from us and the heartiest of congratulations is Rodney Heward-Mills. Competing for Somerset in the English Schools' Championships at the Crystal Palace on July 9/10 in the Senior Boys' Triple Jump, he achieved 50' 9" (15.47m.) and set up a U.K. Junior Record and a Championship Best Performance. He is a student at Millfield School, and we hope that next season we may have his services in at least some senior competitions, and that we shall see him achieve international honours. We congratulate South London Harriers on attaining their Centenary in November, and wish them well in the future. Over the years they have distinguished themselves on the country and on the track, and have a great record. In the last year or two things have been on the quiet side for them, but we may be sure that the "Irrepressibles" will rise again. Our own beginnings have a close connection with the South London Harriers, for following an S.L.H. Open track meeting at the Oval in September, 1887, a number of lads who had cycled across from the Westminster area decided on their way home to form their own athletic club. And so the Belgrave Harriers came into existence. A.A.H. A.A.H. A.A.H. items.label: September 1972
items.sum: Gordon Doubleday recalls Belgrave news found in a News of the World of June 16, 1935, including the Three Miles match with Birchfield at the White City, the National and London to Brighton wins, and individual successes.
items.s: THOSE WERE THE DAYS! Gordon Doubleday recalls Belgrave news found in a News of the World of June 16, 1935, including the Three Miles match with Birchfield at the White City, the National and London to Brighton wins, and individual successes. THOSE WERE THE DAYS! From Gordon Doubleday: I was recently given an old copy of the News of the World, dated June 16, 1935. On the front page was a description of the famous "Mile of the Century" held in New Jersey, U.S.A. It was won by Jack Lovelock, the Oxford and New Zealand runner, in 4m. 11.2s. - four yards ahead of the leading American milers including Glen Cunningham, holder of the world record of 4m. 6.7s. (a record next broken by Sydney Wooderson at Motspur Park). Turning to the other pages, I was hoping for some news of Belgrave, and I was not disappointed. The Whitsun British Games, organised by Joe Binks at the White City, drew a crowd of 20,000, and one of the highlights of the meeting was a Three Miles match between ourselves and Birchfield H. Earlier in the year, the Bels had ended Birchfield's long run of wins in the National C.C. Championship, by winning at Beaconsfield, and a few weeks later had beaten them again in the London to Brighton Relay. It was an exciting race, won by our own Jim Ginty, but the Birchfield tail proved stronger than ours, and they beat us by four points. (I believe it was six to score.) Representative honours were more scarce in those days, but we had a member in the A.A.A. team which beat Cambridge University. Tommy Scrimshaw, already an International, was third in the 880 yards, the winner's time being 1m. 56.2s. There had been a big Open Meeting at Plymouth, and one of the chief events was a Three Miles Open in which Jim Ginty (already mentioned) and Pat Parker were second and third, the winner's time being 15m. 7.4s. I do not suppose that anybody at that time thought that we would see 10 miles being covered at a greater speed than five minutes a mile; and that the marathon would be done at 12 m.p.h. - the British record was still a shade over 2hrs. 30m., and only a few had covered the distance at over 10 m.p.h. In the Middlesex Junior Championships, Stan Botwright won the 220 yards in the 17-19 class, and was runner up in the 100 yards. Stan developed into one of our best sprinters, and in 1939 was Club Champion at 100, 220, and 440 yards. Sussex County held their Jubilee Championships at Preston Park, Brighton, and Joe King retained his two-miles walk title in 14m. 31s., beating the previous record by 3s. Looking back, we had at the time achieved the unique position of being National Team Champions at Cross-Country and Road Walking (50 kilometres), a feat that no Club had previously achieved, and one that we were able to repeat. When are we going to do it again? As for the rest of the country, I noticed in the advertisements slimming pills (presumably for the ladies), and, wait for it, Fags 10 for 4d. Footnote: Jim Ginty and Pat Parker both subsequently gained International Vests over the country. In the 1937 Championship (National) at Stratford-upon-Avon, they gave the team a fine start by finishing third and fourth, but Birchfield gained the title by a very narrow margin of points. items.label: September 1972
items.sum: Profile of the new club president Micky Pyer: his running career from the early 1920s, his coaching of middle-distance runners and javelin, with a 1924 photograph of him in a 2 miles team race.
items.s: Our President A.D.(MICK)PYER Profile of the new club president Micky Pyer: his running career from the early 1920s, his coaching of middle-distance runners and javelin, with a 1924 photograph of him in a 2 miles team race. Our President A.D.(MICK)PYER We have paid ourselves a great compliment in electing MICKY PYER to the highest position in the Club and we can be quite sure that he will do everything possible for the Club, as he has done for so many years past. It is just over fifty years since Micky first drew on a Belgrave vest and impressed himself as a more than useful runner and a valuable member of our teams. In 1922 he won the Club Mile Championship, a win he repeated the following year, and succeeded in taking the Surrey County Championship at the distance also In the 1923 7 miles Club Cross-Country Championship Mick finished second to Jimmy Flatt; but in 1924 he won the event from A.E. Smith. The 10 miles Championship for the MACHER SHIELD in both 1923 and 1924 were won by Micky from Dick Savage, and Wally Bayliss respectively. Mick Pyer showed up prominently in our teams at this time and contributed to our early minor championship wins as Belgrave began to assert itself in the cross-country world. The claims of work took Mick away for a while but on his return he made a very valuable contribution in coaching the younger runners. This he was able to do by reason of his own experience and the AAA qualification he possessed, and in later years he has become a duly authorised Coach in Javelin throwing and many of our boys know how well he understands and promotes the technique of this event even though it was not particularly fashionable in his early days on the track. Our President, for some years past has attended most of the Meetings--Summer and Winter--in which the Club is concerned, and we can truly acclaim him as our Number One Belgrave Harrier---trebly underlined this year when he proudly carries the title of President. We wish him well in his year of office, and we may be sure he will exert all his endeavours for the betterment of the Club. The Presidency is in safe hands!. items.s: PRESIDENT'S MESSAGE President Micky Pyer's message urging members to be ready for the coming County, Area, National, relay and Southern League races, in the spirit of the club motto 'Semper Paratus'. PRESIDENT'S MESSAGE Life goes on, another year is with us, and once again our minds turn to 'battles' to come - the County, Area and National Races, the Relay, and the Southern League, etc. Some older competitors retire or do not now make team selection, and younger ones come in. All are determined to do their best on the day. I am not worried about the day but am mindful of the Club 'motto', "Semper Paratus", which broadly translated means 'always ready'. Let your preparation be right and 'the Day' will look after itself. Well, with this in mind, get down to it lads, and ensure that Belgrave is in the reckoning. - Good luck! Micky Pyer Micky Pyer Micky Pyer Club President Southern League

items.sum: Obituary of Dave Martin Shepherd (1916-1971), who joined in 1931 and served Belgrave as junior runner, Social, Running and Treasurer secretary, Life Member and President in 1962/63, and many outside athletics bodies.
items.s: OBITUARY Obituary of Dave Martin Shepherd (1916-1971), who joined in 1931 and served Belgrave as junior runner, Social, Running and Treasurer secretary, Life Member and President in 1962/63, and many outside athletics bodies. OBITUARY DAVE MARTIN SHEPHERD (23.2.1916 - 20.12.1971) It is with very real regret that we have to chronicle the passing of Dave Shepherd, after a very short illness; and we extend our sympathetic condolences to his wife, Winn, and her mother (our two lady vice-presidents) and other members of the family on their very great loss. It is a loss which we feel also, and shall continue to feel for a long time to come. Dave joined the Club in July, 1931, and quickly showed himself to be a real, stolid Club supporter in every way. He trained under the supervision of Dick Savage, and was a member of our junior team which finished fourth in the Southern Counties C.C. Championship in 1934, and was one of our winning Surrey County junior team. The demands of his career prevented Dave from giving as much time and effort to our activities as he would have liked during the next few years, although he was to be seen at many of our meetings; and in later years Dave really shone as one of our hardest and most enthusiastic workers. As a Social Hon. Secretary, he worked tremendously hard on our behalf; and his technical abilities were at our disposal when the time came for a rented St. John's Hall to become a leasehold, and later a freehold, Belgrave Hall. Dave prepared the first plans embracing the alterations at the rear end of the Hall and the installation of hot water, plumbing etc., and gave us the ammunition to seek planning permissions and building leases for the improvement of our headquarters. Dave also served as an efficient Running Hon. Secretary for several years, and more recently as a conscientious and energetic Hon. Treasurer. Small wonder that he was elected a Life Member as a mark of appreciation of his valiant work for the Club over a long period; and that he became President in 1962/63, worthily filling that position. In addition to his work within the Club, he found time to serve the Club and the Sport by his membership of many other athletic associations. For several he had served on the Southern Counties A.A.A., the Southern Counties Cross-Country Association, the South of Thames C.C. Association, the Surrey A.A.A., and as Chairman of the Surrey County Women's A.A.A. He was one of the four delegates from the South to the English Cross-Country Union; and all branches of our Sport are in debt to Dave for the work he essayed and accomplished. He arranged Suppers, juggled with discs in the funnels at muddy cross-country races, wrote out receipts for subscriptions, advised on hot water problems at the Hall, and generally gave us a life of service, and of good humour, affection and example. He was, indeed, a "cheerie chappie", of high integrity and great loyalty, with an enthusiastic and burning faith for Belgrave, and a real worker for our Sport in many ways, over many years. We mourn his passing - without doubt we shall all miss him tremendously - and we feel grateful that we should have had the opportunity of lasting friendship with one we were all very, very proud to know. R.I.P. - A.A.H. Dave Martin Shepherd DAVE MARTIN SHEPHERD 23.2.1916 - 20.12.1971; joined July 1931; junior team 4th in Southern Counties C.C. 1934 and winning Surrey County junior team; Social Hon. Secretary, Running Hon. Secretary, Hon. Treasurer, Life Member, President 1962/63; Chairman of Surrey County Women's A.A.A. From the Hon. Treasurer The jumble sale held at the Hall was a great success, mainly due to the hard work put in by Gwen and Bill Couzens. There was a good crowd, all eager to spend their money on bargains, and over fifty pounds was raised for the Club funds. I would like to thank all Club members, their wives and girl friends who helped on Friday evening and Saturday morning, but we still need more help if we are going to continue to raise funds in this way. I have recently moved to Kingston, and although I put the Belgrave Hall address on the subscription reminders, some members are sending their subs elsewhere. Please address all correspondence to me at Belgrave Hall, and you can be sure I will receive it. - J.V.B. J.V.B. J.V.B. Hon. items.label: September 1972
items.sum: Obituary by A.A.H. of Olympic walker Harry Churcher, who died on June 24th aged 61, tracing his Belgrave walking career from 1931 through six AAA Championship wins, a world 5 miles record and R.W.A. 10 miles titles to fifth place in the 1948 Olympic 10000 metres track walk.
items.s: OBITUARY H.G.("HARRY") CHURCHER. Obituary by A.A.H. of Olympic walker Harry Churcher, who died on June 24th aged 61, tracing his Belgrave walking career from 1931 through six AAA Championship wins, a world 5 miles record and R.W.A. 10 miles titles to fifth place in the 1948 Olympic 10000 metres track walk. OBITUARY H.G.("HARRY") CHURCHER. It is with great sorrow that we have to advise the death on June 24th of Harry Churcher at the age of 61 years. Harry carried the Belgrave colours to six AAA Championship wins and with his many other distinctions, carved for himself a place in Belgrave history which may never be surpassed. Our sincere condolences go to his widow, and brother Charlie; and we are glad to have had Harry's help and determination over such a long period in our history. It was in August 1931 that the writer, having competed in a two miles event at Stamford Bridge Track and leisurely dressing thereafter, was approached by a middle-aged man then unknown to him. He pressed some forms and money into my hand with the words "Here are a couple of lads who will bring fame to Belgrave"-----and disappeared. As a Belgrave holiday trip to Switzerland was imminent the matter passed out of mind temporarily, but a little later I discovered that the mysterious man was W.C. Wheeler, a former Kent walking champion, and uncle of Charlie and Harry Churcher. His words certainly came true in the years that followed. Charlie became Club Captain and led our teams to many victories; whilst Harry recorded success on success confining himself in the main distances of 10 miles and below, and culminating in Olympic honours in 1948. In early October 1931 Harry had his first race with us in a Club handicap over five miles, with the competitors starting off their marks. Charlie was first to finish and Harry was third, and recorded the fastest actual time in the field of 28 walkers. Incidentally on the same day 43 started in the 3 miles Run and the "Belgravian" says "it is a pity that more did not start in this race". Later in the year Harry won the HORWOOD CUP, with Redgrave second, Speechley third and Harley fourth----the first of many trophies he was to hold over the years. Harry continued to improve, and in 1933 in the RWA Junior 10 miles Championship (30 teams, 211 starters) at Fort Dunlop, he led the Club team to victory. He finished in third position, the team being completed by DON BROWN (6), BERT FIELD (7), and ALF HARLEY (10). Numerous successes now came Harry's way and he won the Inter-County, Southern, Surrey, L.B.H. and Club Championships and Open events week after week with almost monotonous regularity. He even won the Joe Lyons Cake twice, given for the most meritorious performance of the week!. His first placing in AAA Championships came in 1936 when he was third in the 2 miles event. He was second in the 7 miles Championship in 1937, beaten only by J. MIKAELSON of Sweden, later to become an Olympic Champion. 1938 gave Harry a third placing in the 2 miles event, but in 1939 he surpassed himself and had a double Championship win the 2 and 7 mile Championships. Incidently, Joe Coleman was third in the latter event. The War then descended upon us and most of us found ourselves in uniform and decanted in different parts of the world. Harry was in the RAF and covered his miles on a motor-cycle, the walking track being well out of mind. In 1946, however, he strove to get back to his previous fitness and form, and experienced much disappointment in so doing. However he persevered and won through, and demonstrated his strength of character and his will to succeed to such an extent that he was again placed (2nd and 3rd) in the AAA "2' and "7' ; Hindmar of Sweden, winning both Championships. Hindmar was again winner of the 2 miles event in 1947 with Harry second and KRESEVICH of Italy third. In the 7 miles race however, Harry scored a win beating DISALVO and KRESEVICH. 1948----Olympic Year----and Harry scored a double-win in the two AAA Walking Championships and was selected for the British Olympic team. In the Olympic event Harry was somewhat off form----probably due to an early caution, and eventually finished fifth in the 10000 metres track walk. There were 19 competitors from 10 nations. Harry Churcher was always a quick, short-striding walker and his fluid style sometimes brought forth criticism, and occasionally disqualification. It was interesting however to have the opportunity of seeing a film of Harry walking in slow motion; and to have confirmation that his positive contact and rhythmic balance were maintained even at the highest speeds. In fact his action was the very poetry of motion. In contrast, some long-standing walkers normally regarded as near-perfection were found to be at fault in their action and merited disqualification on the progress displayed in the slow motion films. However, this is by the way. In the 1949 AAA Championships Harry won the 7 miles event, and was second to BORJESSON of Sweden in the shorter event. A third place in the 1951 "7" brought to a close Harry's remarkable sequence of AAA Championship placings. Continued: (Cont'd.) Harry's successes on the track were many as has been shown. He competed in Sweden, set up records in France and Ireland and held the World record for 5 miles Walking at one time. So too on the road, at distanes up to 15 miles Harry had tremendous success; and scarcely a week passed without a Churcher win being recorded. The inaugeral R.W.A. 10 miles Championship at Sheffield in 1947 gave Harry another Championship at Sheffield in 1947 gave Harry another Championship win, and with Jack RUTLAND (2), R.D. McMULLEN (4) and Joe COLEMAN (6) following close behind, Belgrave had an easy win with 13 points. The following year in Hyde Park, Harry and Belgrave repeated their wins of the previous year; and week after week Harry and Belgrave hit the headlines. The foregoing is by no means fully comprehensive, and merely gives emphasis to the highlights of a brilliant athlectic career which brought considerable honour to a great sportsman, and to his Club which held him in such high esteem, and will continue to have him in mind wherever the giants of the past are discussed. items.s: A.G.M. REPORT. 1971 Report of the 84th A.G.M. on Wednesday September 22nd 1971: tributes to members who had died, the secretary's and treasurer's reports, new life members, Micky Pyer elected President, vice presidents elected and cups presented. A.G.M. REPORT. 1971 As a break with tradition the 84th A.G.M. was held this year on Wednesday September 22nd , a change from the customary fourth Thursday in the month. There were 59 club members present with apologies from a further 13 , and the meeting was quickly away with the approval of the minutes of the last A.G.M. Our new secretary Peter Hillier , prior to presenting his maiden speech then called upon the members to stand in silence in tribute to a sadly large number of senior members who had passed on during the previous year. Tribute was paid to Jack Chappell , Jim Flatt, W. Isaacs , Ernie Kemp, Fred [illegible]c[illegible]ay and Bill Redgrave. Peter then presented his report and outlined the club's running,walking, and field event's activities on track, road and country during the last year. He made reference to the sterling performances of several of the club's athletes whose exploits had been duly recorded in the Belgravian during the past year . Reference was also made to the taking of another club photograph, which resulted in the largest attendance of club members at Belgrave Hall for many years. In conclusion he spoke of the work put in by all club officials and the report was duly adopted. The much awaited report of the treasurer John Baker followed and he was congratulated on keeping the club out of financial difficulties . John paid tribute to our fund raising stalwarts Bill Couzens and Frank Webb and also called for a vote of thanks to our auditors. Life membership was next on the agenda and duly elected were Gerry North and Micky Pyer. Micky was soon to be mentioned again when it came to the time for electing our new President. Alf Harley president for the past year proposed Micky and with considerable enthusiasm he was unanimously elected. So Micky pulled off the distinguished double of president and life member in the same year. Before vacating the chair Alf Harley spoke of his 45 years as a Belgravian and thanked members for making him president twice . He wished Micky all success in his year of office. Vice presidents were next on the list and duly elected were [illegible].Donovan , T.Hart, Reg Hop[illegible]ins and W.Ashford. Presentation of the Ryan cup to J.Beaumont and the Shield Cup to R.Hopkins, almost brought matters to a close and with a few minutes discussion on general matters another annual general meeting had come and gone. items.h: "LESS TIME AT THE TABLES AND MORE TIME ON THE DANCE FLOOR "
items.sum: Report of the 84th Annual Dinner and Dance at the Wimbledon Hill Hotel in November, with short speeches from Alf Harley and new president Micky Pyer and the Tommy Green cup presented to the walker of the 100 miles road walk.
items.s: "LESS TIME AT THE TABLES AND MORE TIME ON THE DANCE FLOOR " Report of the 84th Annual Dinner and Dance at the Wimbledon Hill Hotel in November, with short speeches from Alf Harley and new president Micky Pyer and the Tommy Green cup presented to the walker of the 100 miles road walk. "LESS TIME AT THE TABLES AND MORE TIME ON THE DANCE FLOOR " That was the theme of past president Alf Harley's speech at the 84th Annual Dinner and Dance at the Wimbledon Hill Hotel in November. And true to his word Alf took just FIVE MINUTES - and apart from a few cries of " unbelievable " , it was just what the assembled multitudes wanted. Welcoming [illegible]icky Pyer , the new president, who has been with Belgrave for almost fifty years Alf said, "We hope to bring honour and distinction to his year of office." But not to be outdone by Alf's speedy utterances Micky was on his feet for no less than FOUR MINUTES , during which time he sd he hoped to be associated with the club for many more years. He then presented the Tommy Green cup to walker John [illegible]oullin for his performance in the 100 miles road walk , where he set up the second best time ever recorded. So with speeches concluded inside ten minutes - a record by any standards - the 170 members and guests spent a delightful evening dancing ,( Well that's what J.P. calls it - and after taking lessons he should know )shuffling, and generally doing their own thing to the music of the Frank Charles Quartet. items.h: FROM 'The Belgravian' 25 years ago and 40 years ago
items.sum: Extracts from The Belgravian of December 1946 (captains, ATHLETICS magazine, Sutton and Martin's 24 hours walk, Etienne Gailly) and December 1931 (Surrey Junior cross-country win, Berman Cup, the club's Open Walk at Wimbledon).
items.s: FROM 'The Belgravian' 25 years ago and 40 years ago Extracts from The Belgravian of December 1946 (captains, ATHLETICS magazine, Sutton and Martin's 24 hours walk, Etienne Gailly) and December 1931 (Surrey Junior cross-country win, Berman Cup, the club's Open Walk at Wimbledon). FROM 'The Belgravian' 25 years ago DECEMBER 1946 -- "The winter season is now in full swing and we are getting good musters at Belgrave Hall. Our runners will do their utmost to retain their many championships, including the English and Southern titles. The walkers will strive to regain the championships we have held in the past. Our respective captains, Bert Footer and Charlie Churcher, will have watchfull eyes over their men and will be pleased to advise any member on training." "The new monthly magazine ATHLETICS is now well established and needs no introduction to most members. For those not acquainted with ATHLETICS it is edited by one of our members P.W.(Jimmy) Green: the annual subscription for twelve issues is 10/- post free." "Heartiest congratulations to Colin Sutton and Jock Martin upon their performances in the 24 hours walk held at the White City on July 14th-15th. Both covered 100 miles within the 24 hours and so qualified to become members of the famous Centurions' Club. Their times were: Sutton 20:40:11, Martin 22:16:57, and both have been presented with a suitably inscribed certificate from the Club. The winner of the event was our Poly member, Percy Reading, who set up three new records viz. 19 hours: 105 miles 466 yards, 110 miles: 19:57:16, 20 hours: 110 miles 410 yards. Percy also beat the unofficial record for a non-stop walk, covering 129 miles 749 yards." "ETIENNE GAILLY, perhaps better known as 'Steve', is now commissioned in the Belgian Army, and sends his best wishes to his Belgrave friends. 'Steve' joined us in 1943, having escaped from occupied Europe." (Ed: Two years later Etienne was the first marathoner to enter Wembley Stadium at the London Olympic Games, only to be passed by Cabrera and Richards on the track. In 1971 he died tragically in a motor accident in Belgium.) and 40 years ago DECEMBER 1931 -- "Congratulations to our Junior team that recently won the Surrey Junior Cross Country Championship. In Messrs. S. Garland (4th), A.T. Jordan (6th), D. Martin (11th), and E. Pointer (14th) - the winning team - we have some very capable runners who should enhance the Club name in years to come." "The Road Walking Association have decided not to promote any handicap events in future, and so the Highgate Harriers held their Open '7' on October 31st and it was decided that the 'Berman' Cup should be competed for in connection with this walk. We were holders of this trophy, presented to the first team in the scratch race, but on this occasion we had to take second place to Enfield A.C." "35 of our members (comprising four teams) entered our own Open Walk at Wimbledon, out of a total entry of 157. A remarkable feature of the result is that, despite the fact that we had three 'A' team men ruled out, there were no less than 15 Belgrave walkers in the first 42 positions, a proportion of something better than one in three!" items.s: TRACK AND FIELD — BILL LETS FLY! Malkin Trophy, Wimbledon Park, June 13, 1971 Report and results of the Malkin Trophy match at Wimbledon Park, where Belgrave tied for second with Luton behind the Police, with Alan Black winning the A-string steeplechase and Bill Couzens throwing the javelin 170ft 3in. TRACK AND FIELD BILL LETS FLY! Malkin Trophy, Wimbledon Park, June 13, 1971 Alan Black was our only "A" string winner in the 'Malkin', taking the 3,000m steeplechase in 9m. 43.4s. But Mick Marshall, John Martin and Reg Hopkins, Jr., were all winners in the "B" string events, and in tying for second place, with Luton, behind the Police, we were not disgraced. We are becoming used to ever more impressive performances from Rimmer ; his 1m. 57.5s (a personal best) in second place in the 800m. was in the accustomed mould. More eyebrow-raising was Bill Couzens's 170' 3" for second in the javelin. It must be a few years since Bill flung one that far. John Martin was obviously inspired, and produced 157' 7" to take the "B" string event. SOUTHERN CHAMPIONSHIPS, CRYSTAL PALACE, JUNE 25/26, 1971 It cannot be said to have been a distinguished Southern Championships meeting for Belgrave, but John Bicourt produced some good form for third in the 3,000m. steeplechase, with a sub-nine minutes clocking, and Steve White was sixth in both the 200m. and the long-jump. Four of our men recorded personal bests, however, so there was considerable satisfaction for us. items.h: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. 1 — Enfield Playing Fields, July 3, 1971
items.sum: Adrian Major's report and Belgrave results from the second Southern League Division 1 match at Enfield, where a weak team finished sixth (fourth in the league standings), with Steve White the only A-string winner.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. 1 — Enfield Playing Fields, July 3, 1971 Adrian Major's report and Belgrave results from the second Southern League Division 1 match at Enfield, where a weak team finished sixth (fourth in the league standings), with Steve White the only A-string winner. SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. 1 Enfield Playing Fields, July 3, 1971 Adrian Major writes: On this chilly and windy summer day, Belgrave's fortunes reached a low ebb at the second league meeting. It looked on paper as though even with the meagre team fielded, we might manage fourth position, and not the sixth place. With the misfortune of having the 3,000m. steeplechase cancelled, because the barrier at the water jump was not aligned properly for the competitors as they came round the bend, Belgrave missed some very valuable points. With Alan Black and Mark McNair present, and Ferdie Gilson, of Hercules Wimbledon, the only other competitor who could have given our runners trouble, it seemed that we may have missed maximum points in this event. Our only winner in the "A" string events was Steve White, who scored an impressive victory in the 200m. - and also took part in the 100m., long-jump and both relays. Jim Rimmer also had a first place in his group in the final straight, but had to give way to Melvern, of Windsor, in the final yards, though recording a personal best time. This was a good run by Jim, who is proving his worth these days. Thanks must also go to the other team members, who all tried their utmost to gain us valuable points. Junior Willie Williams tackled the first event on the timetable, that laborious race, the 400m. hurdles. And we must not forget Brian Gorman - now making his mark in our veterans' ranks. items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS - Hurlingham Park, July 10, 1971 Report and full senior, junior and boys' results of the poorly supported 1971 Belgrave club championships at Hurlingham Park, with hat-tricks for Steve White, John Martin and Willie Williams. CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS [illegible] IN CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS - Hurlingham Park, July 10, 1971 Not the best supported Club Championships meeting we have ever seen. And one lacking in outstanding performances. Steve White got a good hat-trick, in the 100m., 200m., and long-jump, however, while John Martin took the shot, discus, and (unlikely story) the high-jump with a personal best of 5' 2", and failed to add a fourth title, in the javelin, by just 2cm. Jim Rimmer confirmed his new "star" rating, by winning the 800m., and Bill Kerr won a surrealist steeplechase. Willie Williams was a hat-trick man in the junior events, while old rivals and team-mates John Stow and Bill Curtin shared the 800m. and 1,500m. titles, with John taking the former, and Bill the latter. The Boys' events were notable, as they often are, for the readiness of our youngsters to have a crack at anything. Report of Belgrave's Annual Schools' Relay at Battersea Park on 14 July 1971, won by Spencer Park School, and of the same evening's senior and boys'/junior inter-club wins over London A.C. and Hercules Wimbledon. SPENCER PARK WIN OUR SCHOOLS' RELAY (800m.x200m.x200m.x400m.) Battersea Park, July 14, 1971 Spencer Park School, which has developed a fine athletics reputation in recent years, and, we are happy to say, a close friendship with the Belgrave Harriers, won our Annual Schools' Relay with some yards to spare from Beverley School, and for good measure placed its "B" team in third position. There cannot be too close a relationship between schools' and club athletics, and we are always glad of the chance to promote events for schools. It doesn't matter too much about the standard of the race we put on, provided we can do something to encourage the enthusiasm of the participants. But on this occasion, it can be said that both Spencer Park and Beverley would have shown a few more elderly teams the way home. 1. Spencer Park "A" 4m. 1.4s.; 2. Beverley Sch. 4m. 5.4s.; 3. Spencer Park "B" 4m. 12.2[illegible] The same evening, we turned in a double victory, in senior and Boys'/Junior matches against London A.C. and Hercules Wimbledon One of our Spencer Park products, Mick Marshall scored a nippy win in the 200m., while in the Boys' events there was to be noticed a 16' 3" win in the long-jump by Tom Mates, the winner of the Boys' 800m. and high jump at our championship meeting the previous Saturday. Mick Marshall Mick Marshall Spencer Park School product; won the 200m Tom Mates Tom Mates won boys' long jump with 16' 3"; winner of boys' 800m and high jump at the club championships Schools' Relay Inter-Club Meeting Battersea Park Spencer Park School Beverley School London A.C. items.s: 'Brockman' — ENCOURAGING PERFORMANCE IN BROCKMAN TROPHY - Wimbledon Park, July 17, 1971 Report and results of the 1971 Brockman Trophy at Wimbledon Park, where Belgrave were third behind Thames Valley Harriers; the text gives Keith Schofield's javelin as 56.90m but the results list 59.90m (both /186' 8"). 'Brockman' ENCOURAGING PERFORMANCE IN BROCKMAN TROPHY - Wimbledon Park, July 17, 1971 Amid our disappointing Southern League performances, we could draw some encouragement from this display. Although well behind Thames Valley, the winners, we took third place with a much more solid performance than we can be sure of achieving at the moment. Steve White made a major contribution, with second places in the 200m. and in the long-jump, while Glyn Ratcliffe, as ever, was a tower of strength in the shot and discus, and Keith Schofield gave us a boost with a 56.90m./186' 8" javelin throw. John Bicourt got a third in the 1500m. and Gerry North a third in the 5,000m., while Trevor Hart went one better in the 10,000m. A lot of credit, however, must go to junior Mick Marshall, for his 11.3s. third in the 100m., behind Thames Valley's Martin Reynolds and Hercules Wimbledon's John Gostelow. 100m. 3. M. items.s: Inter-Club Meeting at Norbiton Tuesday 20th July 1971 — Beaten - BUT ONLY SLIGHTLY BOWED Report and Belgrave results from an evening inter-club match at Norbiton on 20 July 1971, where Belgrave finished third behind Surrey A.C. and Epsom and Ewell but fielded nine of the 15 runners in the 800m. Inter-Club Meeting at Norbiton Tuesday 20th July 1971 Beaten - BUT ONLY SLIGHTLY BOWED An evening match at Norbiton saw us beaten by our hosts, Surrey A.C., and by Epsom and Ewell. But as we provided nine runners out of 15 in the half-mile (sorry, 800m.), we came away with our heads only slightly bowed. Our turn-outs in the half lately have been reminiscent of the palmy days when we used to be well beaten in the Kinnaird, but were invited. But that's another story. Steve White chalked up yet another sprint double, and Bill Kerr took the 1500m., while Jim Rimmer (3rd in 1m. 57.5s.) and John Boardman (fourth in 1m. 58s.) can be said to have run well in the 800m. 100m 1.S.White 11.4s 5.M.Elliott 12s 200m 1.S.White 22.2s 6.M.Elliott 23.7s 7.P.Gee 23.8s 800m 3.J.Rimmer 1m 57.5s 4.J.Boardman 1m 58s 6.P.Gee 2m 1s 9.B.Gorman 2m 14s 10.D.McMillan 2m 14s 12.B.Merry 2m 17s 13.D.Davies 2m 17s 14.C.Manning 2m 18s 15.R.Glover 2m 24s 1500m 1.W.Kerr 4m 4.2s 5.D.Jardine 4m 15.4s Hammer 2.J.Martin 22.40m Shot 2.J.Martin 12.24m Discus 3.J.Martin 31.40m Result 1.Surrey A.C. 164 pts 2.Epsom/Ewell 106 pts 3.Belgrave H. 51 pts Steve White Steve White sprint double, 100m and 200m Steve White S.White Bill Kerr Bill Kerr won 1500m in 4m 4.2s Bill Kerr W.Kerr Jim Rimmer Jim Rimmer 3rd in 800m in 1m 57.5s Jim Rimmer J.Rimmer John Boardman John Boardman fourth in 800m in 1m 58s John Boardman J.Boardman M. items.sum: Report and results of the club 5,000m championship (won by Laurie O'Hara), 110m hurdles championship and 300m handicap at Battersea Park on 28 July 1971.
items.s: O'HARA WINS GRIFFEN CUP — LAURIE O'HARA IN FINE FORM - Battersea Park, July 28, 1971 Report and results of the club 5,000m championship (won by Laurie O'Hara), 110m hurdles championship and 300m handicap at Battersea Park on 28 July 1971. O'HARA WINS GRIFFEN CUP LAURIE O'HARA IN FINE FORM - Battersea Park, July 28, 1971 Laurie O'Hara has been in great form lately, and he skated away with our 5,000m. championship in the fastish time of 14m. 51.8s. Gerry North had to draw on his well-known ability to hold off Guy Monnet for second place (Gerry was not taking his running too seriously at the time - though he has been getting back towards top form this winter). Guy, in turn, had to show his sprinting powers to hold off the defending champion, Lionel Mann (not at the peak of fitness). In the 110m. hurdles championship, Willie Williams, out junior high jump champion, won his first senior title, with a narrow victory over John Martin, our shot, discus and senior high jump champion. The scratchman's main problem in a 300m. handicap is often how to get round the fiel[illegible] without running 320m. But Philip Gee, however far he ran to do it, got to the tape first, in 38.2s. items.h: LITTLE BUT GOOD — Copthall Stadium, July 31, 1971
items.sum: Report of seven Belgrave athletes at an informal Shaftesbury Harriers meeting at Copthall Stadium, Hendon, with wins for Philip Gee (800m) and Jim Rimmer (1500m).
items.s: LITTLE BUT GOOD — Copthall Stadium, July 31, 1971 Report of seven Belgrave athletes at an informal Shaftesbury Harriers meeting at Copthall Stadium, Hendon, with wins for Philip Gee (800m) and Jim Rimmer (1500m). LITTLE BUT GOOD Copthall Stadium, July 31, 1971 A small squad of Bels. travelled to Hendon for an informal meeting put on by Shaftesbury Harriers. Several clubs were present, but teams scores, apparently, were not kept. Our men would hardly have been in the running for a team award, there were only seven of them. But they came away with two firsts, two seconds and two thirds on an individual basis, so can be said to have performed pretty creditably. Philip Gee was second in the 400m. in 52.4s., but went even more strongly in the 800m., to win in 2m. 3.7s. Also in the 800m. were Colin Pearson, 5th in 2m. 09.5s., and Richard Moody 7th in 2m. 10.6s. New star Jim Rimmer took the 1500m. in 4m. 04.5s., and to prove what a useful performance this was, we can say that Laurie O'Hara was third in 4m. 05.6s. Those indefatigable field events twins John Martin and Bill Couzens carried our colours in the field. John was second in the shot, with 11.28m., and Bill Couzens third with 9.73m. In the javelin, however, Bill led the way, finishing fourth with 43.08m., and John was fifth, with 39.68m. items.s: O'HARA WINS TOM CARTER CUP — DOUBLE UP! Club 10,000m. championship - Battersea Park, August 4, 1971 Report and results of the club 10,000m championship at Battersea Park on 4 August 1971, won by Laurie O'Hara for the Tom Carter Trophy, and of a four-event handicap won by Derek Glendinning. O'HARA WINS TOM CARTER CUP DOUBLE UP! Club 10,000m. championship - Battersea Park, August 4, 1971 Laurie O'Hara, one of our most consistent performers over a number of years, was an easy winner of the 10,000m. championship - adding the Tom Carter Trophy to the Griffen Cup (5,000m.). Last year's winner, Lionel Mann, was his closest challenger, but headed Adrian Major by only a few yards. Derek Glendinning finished in the first four in each of the events in the four events handicap, to take an overall first place. Kelly and C. Williams. HERNE HILL HARRIERS' INTER-CLUB MEETING, Tooting Bec, August 11, 1971 No team result is available for this meeting, but we gave a satisfying display of strength throughout the age groups. This time we had nine runners in the first ten in the 800m., and the individual winner in up-and-coming two-lapper Philip Gee, in the good time of 2m. 2.2s. Steve White won the 200m., but suffered a rare reversal at the hands of a Club-mate, when junior Mick Marshall won the 100m. Mick - already a great asset - also took the junior long-jump, while Willie Williams made a jumping double in the junior events by clearing 1.52m. to win the high jump. K. Kelly pushed our jumping reputation a bit higher, by winning the youths' long-jump, and had two good sprint performances to his credit by the end of the evening, as well. Only one of our members figure in the Boys' results, but C. Williams, with two first and a third, kent us to the front of the picture. items.sum: Report by track captain A.M. on Belgrave's fifth place in the final 1971 Southern League fixture at Wimbledon Park, with an editor's note on the field events, A and B string results, the final league table (Belgrave 4th) and three photos.
items.s: Southern League — Wimbledon Park, August 21, 1971 Report by track captain A.M. on Belgrave's fifth place in the final 1971 Southern League fixture at Wimbledon Park, with an editor's note on the field events, A and B string results, the final league table (Belgrave 4th) and three photos. Southern League Wimbledon Park, August 21, 1971 This was our last League fixture of the year. This coming summer we will see a completely different approach to the Southern League system. Whereas previously we have had three meetings between the same six clubs, we will now have six meetings - and with 25 clubs in the competition - we will take on sets of five differing clubs a time. Let us hope that Belgrave will benefit from the new system. I am afraid that we were not much better off at Wimbledon Park than we were at Enfield. We did field a more competent team, but could not move higher than fifth position. Our only track winner of the day was none other than Steve White, in the "B" 100m. Steve also competed in the 200m. and both relays . Peter Carton ran a sound race in the 800m., as did Jim Rimmer in the 1500m. The usual crowd pulled together, doing two or three events apiece. Mick Marshall turned out in the 100m., 200m. and 4x100m., Steve White in the 100m., 200m., 4x100m., and 4x400m., Philip Gee in the 400m. and 4x400m., and Cliff Brooks in the 4x400m. and 4x100m. Thanks must go to these, and also, especially, to Chris Keavey, who donned his kit to do the "B" 3,000m. steeplechase. Thanks go to to every competitor this summer, as I am sure they tried their hardest, and also to officials, notably Bob Taylor, who put in so much hard work and worry. I am sure some of us do not realise how much Bob put into it. Next year - after the 1972 season - Bob will retire from being track secretary. So if there are any volunteers, I am sure Bob will co-operate and offer advice, so that they would not be at a loose end in the 1973 season. Next year Philip Gee will be your Track Captain, and I hope he will be more competent than I was. - A.M. Commentator comments: A.M. is too modest. The thanks of all Belgravians go to him for his competence. While A.M. has described the track side of things at the final League fixture, there remains some considerable field events achievement on which to report. Where better to start than with Glyn Ratcliffe, who won the discus, with a mighty 46.32m. (if you haven't got conversion tables, its time you bought some - I shall buy some tomorrow), took second in the shot, and finished up with fourth in the hammer. But it is worth noting that Cliff Brooks was just as busy on the field, as he was on the track, and in fact competed in rather more field events than track events, if you count the hurdles in the field events side of things. At the same time, Steve White took time off from his track exploits to win the long-jump. items.h: BELGRAVE v DJK TRAUNSTEIN — Sunday 1st August '71
items.sum: Light-hearted account of a two-man Belgrave 'international' race against German runners of DJK Traunstein near Bolney, Sussex, on 1 August 1971, with Charles Manning second and Robert Glover third.
items.s: BELGRAVE v DJK TRAUNSTEIN — Sunday 1st August '71 Light-hearted account of a two-man Belgrave 'international' race against German runners of DJK Traunstein near Bolney, Sussex, on 1 August 1971, with Charles Manning second and Robert Glover third. BELGRAVE v DJK TRAUNSTEIN Sunday 1st August '71 Only two representatives of our club turned out for this international meet held deep in the heart of Sussex on the East side of the Brighton Road opposite Bolney. The day before the race our team, Bob Glover and Charlie Manning, flushed with success from their recent 5,000 metre Club Championship, were out from their training camp and did two laps of the course with Ted Stimpson, Ian and Martin Gillings. On the Sunday morning, after a light breakfast, they went to the tent of the competitors - who had accepted their challenge, after they'd taken the xxxx out of them on their return from training the day before. To Bob and Charlie's surprise the Germans looked too much like runners, having removed their paper hats and set aside their bugle, they appeared in Adidas, shorts, etc. The pace was hot right from the start. Chas was running with the leading German and Bob alongside the other at the back. They pushed the pace on the first mile out - mostly downhill. At the steep, short, climb to the left onto the long leg they went like a couple of greyhounds with our men still in contact. This was the order as they commenced the long uphill struggle towards the finish. Halfway along this stretch Bob moved to the front - can't you picture it?- the multitudinous voices, "GLOV-ER - GLOV-ER - GLOV-ER". England were now 1st and 3rd. With less than a mile to go the leading German, spying yet another hill, expired and dropped back! Bob, with gentlemanly aplomb, returned to make sure his adversary continued along the course. Chas, well in command at the front eased down at the camp shop (he reckoned that to be the finish) only to be surprised by the remaining German sprinting right down to the tents for the congratulations and considering himself the winner. 1. items.s: YACHT '3' — WIMBLEDON, October 9, 1971 Report and full handicap result of the Yacht 3 mile race at Wimbledon on 9 October 1971, won on handicap by Dudley Gordon, with Trevor Hart fastest. YACHT '3' WIMBLEDON, October 9, 1971 The writer of this note has no hesitation in saying that Dudley Gordon is a handicapper's nightmare. Dudley does not win many pots in scratch competition these days (we believe it may not always have been thus). But he clearly turned up at Wimbledon on this October day secure in the knowledge that it was Boxing Day, and everyone knows that Boxing Day is Dudley's personal prize-day - everyone except the handicapper, that is. Even the calendar can do nothing with Dudley in a Boxing Day mood, and he romped home in 13m. 56s. It was pleasing to see a new face in second place - G. Collins clocking 14m. 06s. off 4m. 30s. Third place went to Guy Monnet, who also clocked the third fastest scratch time. items.s: BELGRAVE '20' — BILL WELLER WINS FIRST CLUB TITLE - FAIRCLOTH TAKES OPEN "20" Report and results of the Belgrave Open 20 miles at Wimbledon on 17 July 1971, won by Don Faircloth (Croydon), with Bill Weller fifth and winning the club championship (Lady Fell Shield). BELGRAVE '20' BILL WELLER WINS FIRST CLUB TITLE - FAIRCLOTH TAKES OPEN "20" Belgrave Open 20-miles run, Wimbledon, July 17, 1971 The open "20" saw another distinguished name added to the list of winners of our open competitions - that of Don Faircloth (Croydon), who took an early lead, to race almost four minutes clear of the second man, Ian McIntosh (Ranelagh), for what can only be described as a resounding victory. The race also saw a distinguished name added to the roll of Belgrave champions, however, with Bill Weller taking the first of what we are sure is going to be a string of Club titles. Unfortunately, Bill was not at this stage eligible to represent us in open competition, and we finished a lowly fifth in the team race. Pat O'Connor ran well to break 1hr. 50m. by a handsome margin, but Lionel Mann was but a shadow of the runner of a few months earlier. - 115 started, 93 finished Surrey championship (in conjunction): 1. items.s: NEWPORT TO TREDEGAR 22-MILES ROAD RUN - DECEMBER 18, 197[illegible] Don Bonser's report on the Newport to Tredegar 22 miles road run on 18 December, praising organiser John Hall (Bels/Gilwern), with Bonser 25th and Hall 26th. NEWPORT TO TREDEGAR 22-MILES ROAD RUN - DECEMBER 18, 197[illegible] A special report by Don Bonser The course was similar to that of previous years, being confined to the main valley road, passing through Risca, Blackwood and Markham on the way to Tredegar. It is in no sense monotonous; the several uphill stretches, with little downhill running keep mind and body fully occupied, and the green hills, even though some are grassed coal tips, provide a distinct change. The exact distance is difficult to assess. For various reasons the finish always seems to be in a different place. John Hall's vehicle recorded 22¼ miles. Thanks to Bernard Baldwin and Angus Donaldson, the manager of the Castle Hotel, Tredegar, the facilities and organisation were of good standard. Praise is also due to John Hall, who made an equally important contribution to the success of the event by his attention to detail. Mile markers were provided after 15, there were buckets and sponges and two girls to produce a result sheet. He even found time to run himself John wishes to be remembered to all his friends and rivals at Belgrave Hall. He misses the competition, but hopes to take part in the long distance road races this year. 1. R. Calvert (Small Heath), 1hr. 56m. 40s. ..... 25. D. Bonser (Belgrave), 2hrs. 29m. 12s.; 26. J. items.s: WIMBLEDON CUP for WELLER — BELGRAVE 5¾ MILES ROAD RACE Report and full handicap result of the Belgrave 5¾ miles road race of 18 March 1972, in which Bill Weller won the Wimbledon Cup and Derek Crookes the handicap. WIMBLEDON CUP for WELLER BELGRAVE 5¾ MILES ROAD RACE------18th March 1972 Bill Weller has his name insribed on the "Wimbledon Cup" for the first time, and he ran well enough to suggest that it will not be the last either. Laurie O'Hara almost a veteran was a comfortable second, well ahead of John Stow(almost a senior) who is 20 years Laurie's junior. Peter Carton was below form and Charlie Walker lost his vets crown to two new recruits to the "aged" division, Brian Gorman and Clive Shippen. The handicap, deservedly, went to Derek Crookes who produced his best run for many years. RESULT. 1. W. Weller (0.15) 27:53 2. L. O'Hara (0.30) 28:13 3. J. Stow (2.15) 29:09 4. A. items.sum: Stage-by-stage report of the Southern Counties AAA road relay of 8 April 1972, where Belgrave took the bronze medals behind Hercules Wimbledon and Reading, with the full team result.
items.s: Southern Road-Relay — BELS BACK IN THE MEDALS — BELGRAVE & SOUTHERN COUNTIES AAA ROAD RELAY---8th April 1972 Stage-by-stage report of the Southern Counties AAA road relay of 8 April 1972, where Belgrave took the bronze medals behind Hercules Wimbledon and Reading, with the full team result. Southern Road-Relay BELS BACK IN THE MEDALS BELGRAVE & SOUTHERN COUNTIES AAA ROAD RELAY---8th April 1972 Last year's 7th place was our worst ever performance in the Southern Road Relay, so there was a determination afoot to wipe out the memory of that unhappy occasion. Thanks to Tony Brien we achieved the necessary good start and thereafter we were attacking the leaders on each stage. Only when Bob Holt swept our local rivals away and out of sight on stage eight was it clear that we would be fighting it out for bronze. We won this secondary battle without difficulty, pushing the holders (TVH) into 4th place. It was a good all-round effort by a team showing much verve and all running pretty well to, and above, form. STAGE 1: A. BRIEN (24:42, 7th fastest). Tony was always with the main leading group, which allowed just four runners to get away. The evergreen Harland (Camb.) led them all home, 10 secs ahead of our second claim member, Bob Richardson (B'Hth). Tony was involved in a mass scramble for the following positions where six seconds covered six runners. Four of our main rivals, T.V.H., Herc/Wimb., Hillingdon and Medway (all ahead of us last year) finished 14th,15th,and 21st respectively. STAGE 2: P. CARTON (15:31, 2nd fastest) Peter set off shoulder to shoulder with Hicks of Aldershot, 42secs behind the leaders. Showing impressive form, the young pair forged their way through the string of teams ahead, passing the front runner in the final stretch. Of the 165 runners who tackled the short stage this day these two were the fastest---Hicks getting home 3 seconds ahead of Peter, with Reading in 3rd place. STAGE 3: W. WELLER (24:46--5th fastest) This was Bill's first outing for us in this event and he proved right away what a valuable addition he is to our relay teams. Although he had to give best to Aldershot (Adams 24:15) and Portsmouth (Cain 24:21) he stuck to our forward position very well and opened up a further 10 seconds on Reading. STAGE 4: W. CURTIN (16:02, 6th fastest) This was one of Bill's better days. Showing much ferocity he attacked the field in his best style, destroying the Portsmouth runner and closing within 11 seconds of the leader (Aldershot). STAGE 5: GERRY NORTH (24:32, 3rd fastest) Much can happen on a long stage, and it was here that Aldershot was pushed right back to 6th place, 1½ minutes down, and out of the medals. Gerry, and Biscoe of Reading, fought out the lead for the whole of the 5½ miles; Gerry giving best by a mere 4 secs at the end. It was a fine run which showed so well what a great competitor this man is. T.V.H. and Herc/Wimb. were still lanquishing back in 8th and 9th places, 2 minutes down. STAGE 6: C. PEARSON (16:52, 9th fastest Colin, who has been reserve runner on so many occasions, stepped in here and acquitted himself very well. Although several of the following teams closed up, he gave very little away up front and finished 16 seconds behind the leaders, Reading. STAGE 7: J. PHELAN (25:08, 10th fastest) John was another having his first outing in this race, and what an initiation it was! As he waited to start he found himself alongside McAndrew (Reading), Ford (Aldershot), Watson (Cambridge) & D. Holt (H/W). The race was now burning hot. Although John slipped two places, only 61 seconds covered the first five teams---and Hercules Wimbledon were just 15 seconds behind us. STAGE 8: J. Stow (16:22, 6th fastest) John was our third junior this day to race over the short stage, and he followed the example of his predecessors by carrying the claret and gold further forward to regain 3rd place. Reading was still in front with Hercules Wimbledon now 9 seconds in arrears. STAGE 9: P. O'CONNOR (25.00 , 7th fastest) Its a good job that Pat has a cool disposition. To take off just 9 seconds ahead of a Bob Holt in full flight is an unenviable situation in which to find oneself. Two more internationals, Ashton (Reading) and Thomas (TVH) were also doing much damage, so Pat found himself in a similar situation to fellow Irishman Phelan 40 minutes earlier. He did well to hold third place by passing the Aldershot runner, 3 seconds down. T.V.H. were now 5th, only 17 seconds behind us. STAGE 10: T. HART (16:07 , 3rd fastest) Trevor has usually been one of our long stage runners so there were high hopes that he would bite into the lead of the two teams ahead. Unfortunately, Wallis (H/W) was fastest on this stage, but Trevor took 10 to 18secs off the other top four teams to help stabilise our 3rd place. We were now 91 seconds behind Reading and 72 seconds behind Hercules Wimbledon. STAGE 11: L. O'HARA (24:34, 2nd fastest) Just 2 months away from becoming a 40 yrs old veteran, Laurie O'Hara was faced with a situation where he had little to gain (Piotrowski and Badgery were well ahead) and everything to lose (T.V.H., Aldershot, Portsmouth and Cambridge were all within striking distance). Laurie rose to the occasion in great style and only Cass of Portsmouth was faster on this stage. We were virtually assured of medals. STAGE 12: A. BLACK (16:29, 6th fastest) This is not always the glory stage that it's made out to be. With Reading and Herc/Wimb fighting it out ahead Alan ran a solo effort just hard enough to keep out of trouble from a second scrap going on behind. And so it was that Hercules Wimbledon, through Halliday, took the lead for the very first time just yards from the tape to win the title from Reading (Bacon) by a mere second after 4 hours of racing. Belgrave were third, 9[illegible] seconds in arrears, and T.V.H. (Standen) just held off a fast finishing Aldershot (Fletcher, 15:49) to take 4th place. RESULT. 1. Herc/Wimb. AC 4:04:25 2. National Relay BELS IMPROVE 7 PLACES IN NATIONAL RELAY Sutton Park, Sutton Coldfield ------- 29th April 1972 Belgrave were a much livelier looking team in this year's championship. Another fine start was made by Tony Brien who brought us home in 7th place on stage 1, and for the next 4 hours we hovered between 2nd and 7th positions before settling finally in the latter place. Our old rivals Birchfield lost their title on the last stage to Tipton, whilst our newer rivals and Southern holders Hercules Wimbledon finished one place behind us. RESULT: Fastest Laps: Long, R. items.h: WELLER WINS OUR BIRTHDAY '20' — BELGRAVE OPEN 20 MILES ROAD RACE
items.sum: Report and result of the Belgrave Open 20 miles road race at Wimbledon on 22 July 1972, won by Bill Weller, who also took the Surrey title.
items.s: WELLER WINS OUR BIRTHDAY '20' — BELGRAVE OPEN 20 MILES ROAD RACE Report and result of the Belgrave Open 20 miles road race at Wimbledon on 22 July 1972, won by Bill Weller, who also took the Surrey title. WELLER WINS OUR BIRTHDAY '20' BELGRAVE OPEN 20 MILES ROAD RACE --------- Wimbledon, 22nd July 1972 Showing some of his most impressive form, Bill Weller put the icing on our 21st promotion with an intelligent win in the open race and added a cherry too by taking the Surrey title held in conjunction. But the team race escaped us, Ealing & Southall AC having a 2 point edge. The weather was fine and warm, perhaps too warm, for the heat and humidity accounted for a mammoth drop out figure of 30%. The most notable retirer was Alan Cass of Portsmouth who shot into a 12 seconds lead at 5 miles and stretched it to 22 seconds at 10 miles, only to find himself back on his heels after taking "Copse" for the second time, 4th at the 15 miles mark and in an ambulance a mile or so later. Weller bided his time nicely. He ran with Pratt and Macintosh for 10 miles, took the lead near the end of the second lap and eased away gradually to a 25 seconds margin at 15 miles and on to a 43 seconds winning lead. His team-mates O'Connor and Mann were always well placed but couldn't match the second half running of Ealing's Warren and Case. Colin Pearson produced a very good debut at 20 miling and was rewarded with the Newcomer's prize and a third place team medal in the Surrey Championship. With Clive Shippen doing a "Cass" at 18 miles, Joe Dooley stepped into the breach with a fine run to preserve our Surrey medals. Others forced to withdraw were Hilton, Baker, Paget, Laws and Fairfield. The organisation was as excellent as usual and Gordon Biscoe now becomes our longest serving race secretary for this promotion with six consecutive efforts, one ahead of Arthur Whitehead who initiated the event 21 years ago. items.s: CROSS-COUNTRY — "B" team cross-country at Ruislip, November 6, 1971 Report and results of a Belgrave "B" team cross-country fixture at Ruislip on 6 November 1971, with seniors fourth and a youths team also fourth. CROSS-COUNTRY "B" team cross-country at Ruislip, November 6, 1971 Once again, it fell to the lot of a couple of "A" team men to give a semblance of respectability to a "B" team turn out. Winning "B" team fixtures may not matter a great deal, but the only way the Club's members can ensure that there is a fixture on when they want one is to support the whole programme. Without Gerry North and Laurie O'Hara , both unable to get to the "A" team at Oxford the same day, our numbers would have been extremely thin. A good run apiece by these two established stars was backed by the new veteran's star Brian Gorman, while John Davies made a welcome appearance to lead in the second wave of Bels. While the seniors were disporting themselves over 5-miles, a small youths team, led by Simon Holmes and David Harvey were tackling a 3-mile course, and although the result below shows that they took fourth place, it can be seen that they were not so far out of snatching second. 1. items.s: Blackstaffe Shield — LAURIE TAKING OVER Report and handicap result of the club 7½-miles cross-country championship for the Blackstaffe Shield at Wimbledon on 4 December 1971, won by Laurie O'Hara, with John Blair-Fish winning the handicap. Blackstaffe Shield LAURIE TAKING OVER Club 7½-miles championship - "Blackstaffe Shield" - Wimbledon, December 4, 1971 Laurie O' Hara has been taking over from Lionel Mann in the Club championships. Back in the summer, he took Lionel's 5,000m. and 10,000m. titles, and now he had added the 7½-miles c.c. championship. Once Laurie broke away there was little doubt about the winner. But junior Peter Carton did not surrender without a struggle, and had every reason to be pleased with his running. Good to see John Thresher well advanced along the come-back trail, while Colin Pearson kept his improvement going, with fourth place in front of some star names. John Blair-Fish showed a glimpse of the form we know he possesses, and his tenth place gave him a well-deserved win in the handicap, ahead of Laurie and Charlie Manning. m.s. - handicap - 1. L.
