items.label: March 1973
items.sum: The cross country and road running secretary laments the loss of the North Surrey League and poor turnouts, urging maximum team effort in the races that matter.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY The cross country and road running secretary laments the loss of the North Surrey League and poor turnouts, urging maximum team effort in the races that matter. At the time of writing, with the 'National' the only cross country race left to go, one cannot actually look back and say that our record this season has been in any way impressive, having just lost the North Surrey League for the first time in seven years. True it was lost by only 13 points and it's very easy to explain it away by theorising as to what we could have done if other people had turned out, etc. But lost it was, through our inability to concentrate our efforts in the races that matter. This is surely the reason for many of our failures. Take the pathetic turn out in the Surrey Championship, only six runners from a club of over 450 members; or how about only nine runners instead of the permissable twelve in the Southern as a further example. Is it too unreasonable to assume that anyone joining an athletic club and who has taken the trouble to train 50, 60, 70 or more miles per week would also wish to compete ? Is it also too unreasonable to assume that those who are good enough to have been entered, and then subsequently picked to represent their club in the major events should take some pride in turning out ? Apparently not, from some of the excuses and 'reasons' one is expected to believe. Now it's fully appreciated that everyone goes down with colds, 'flu and injuries from time to time but some of the recoveries from indispositions that strike after a training session on Thursday or Friday and then are cleared up by Sunday morning are truly remarkable. Support for the teams is always welcome but to have members who have been picked to run, and are quite capable of competing, tearing round the course training and cheering on a depleted team is not going to endear them to anyone. We are often told that the average age of our leading teams is high and although much improved of late, this is still basically true. However, it would be nice to think that in future some of these years of experience and wisdom could be put to good effect and that members will realise that no one is asked or expected to race every week but that we do expect a maximum team effort on the occasions that matter and that those concerned should realise which are the occasions that matter without having to be told, and gear their training accordingly. It should not be assumed by the way, that any or all of the above remarks are being directed solely at our 'A' team runners, as a check on our record of percentage turnout (and wasted team fees) in races such as the South of the Thames Junior, etc., will show that our efforts have been far to slack at all levels. Our past achievements and tradition has made Belgrave great but we cannot live on in the past and as soon as everyone realises that our future successes and trophies will only come by winning them and that we are not going to be given them by some Divine right, then the better for all. Let's hope the coming road and relay season proves the point. Gordon Biscoe CROSS COUNTRY & ROAD RUNNING HON. SEC. Gordon Biscoe Gordon Biscoe Cross Country & Road Running Hon. Sec. items.s: Phelan Finishes First Report and handicap result of the club 7½ mile cross country championship at Wimbledon on 2 December 1972, won by John Phelan, held with a match against Polytechnic Harriers. DECEMBER 2nd 1972 - 7½ MILE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP - WIMBLEDON. It was a day for the lightly built men. Torrents of rain during the preceding week had turned the stretches of our course that follow the horse rides into a glutinous morass, and Bob Smith, who had been going like a rocket in the weeks leading up to the race and who was tipped by many as the next holder of the 'Blackstaffe Shield', had to give best to his more wiry rivals. Revelling in the conditions was John Phelan who grabbed a handy lead early on and at no time looked like losing it. That handicappers nightmare, Doug Maughan, pulled another fast one and must now have ruined his chances of picking up further "pots" in this way. Still, the way he improves with each run (this time putting the wind up Doug Jardine amongst others) leads one to believe that he will be in amongst the the medals one day. A special presentation in the form of a silver Elizabethan dish, inscribed with an English Rose, was made after the race to Tony Binda on the eve of his departure from the Belgrave fold. items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Tongue-in-cheek notice that Bernard Merry is giving up 'serious' athletics after 15 years, listing his mock career highlights.
items.s: Bernard Merry to quit 'serious' athletics ! Tongue-in-cheek notice that Bernard Merry is giving up 'serious' athletics after 15 years, listing his mock career highlights. Bernard, the local boy who made good, dropped this bombshell recently after a training session. It seems that after 15 years of punishing training, ever striving towards the ultimate of his potential, he is going to round off an illustrious career that has included such highlights as: 3rd place out of four runners in the London Telephone Exchanges 1 mile championship (when it was unkindly said by some that 4th place went to a non-athlete), 1st in a keep fit class 1 mile, and that heroic performance on 25th March 1968 when he led the Belgrave 'B' team to victory over all other 'B' teams in the Tonbridge '10'. Happily, Bernie is going to continue to run in our races but will not be showing that old fire and determination. Instead he is going to concentrate on his style and you can rest assured that just as soon as the 'dressage' is included in the Olympic athletic programme, Britain and Belgrave will be on to a winner! Bernard Merry Bernard Merry led Belgrave 'B' team in Tonbridge '10', 25 March 1968 Bernard Merry Bernard Bernie London Telephone Exchanges 1 mile championship Tonbridge '10' Olympic Games Tonbridge

items.s: CARTON SHINES IN BELGRAVE GLOOM Report and results of the Surrey County Cross Country Championship at Morden Park on 6 January 1973, where Peter Carton won the junior race and a depleted Belgrave senior team finished 4th. Surrey County Championship JANUARY 6th 1973 - MORDEN PARK. On an afternoon that was grim for Belgrave Harriers, Peter Carton provided the only highlight. John Lee of Croydon H. soon sped away from the main pack in the Junior 5 mile race, and with Peter the only taker, Lee tried everything he could to shake off his adversary. Several times he looked like doing so as he put in burst after burst but when they reached the hilly sections on each lap our man closed right up to his shoulder, looking strong and biding his time. Last time up the main incline and with about half a mile to go, Peter impressively let loose and the Croydon Harrier had no answer. A worthy champion! It was interesting to note that not one club managed to close in a Junior team. What colour medals would our Senior team take home this year? Silver, most people thought, although the odd optimists forecast that we would go even better. Twentythree Belgravians had been entered for the event but shortly before the race only three had arrived. By the time the starter had sent the field on its way our team had stretched to the minimum of six that are required to complete a team. Injuries and 'flu accounted for some but where were the rest. Gerry North, only recently returning from injury himself, led our diluted team in to an ignoble 4th with not one of our number making the team for the Inter-counties. Team Result:- 1. items.s: a saturday saga Comic verse account of the Belgrave Harriers 10 miles cross country championship on 20 January 1973, continued on page 30 with a short note and the full result with handicaps and lap times: won by L. O'Hara, handicap by D. Wiseman. JANUARY 20th 1973 - BELGRAVE H. 10 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. I'll tell you a tale of great bravery, Of struggles 'tween more than mere men. And it all took place in that terrible race That they call - the Belgrave '10'. Of course it was won by 'young Laurie' From Lionel, Trevor and Bob But nearer the back of the Claret-Gold pack Are the stories to make your heart throb. John Baker went of like a rocket, George Piddington gave it the gun, But a steadier crowd led by battler Bert Stroud Knew it was only begun. They both came back two miles later When Charlie and Don pushed on through. And now Dave McMillan, the hairy young villain, Had a bad patch and knew nowt what to do. Halfway, and with a huge effort Up came Alan Mead With his eyes on a 'pot' to match the last one he got. Oh! How it made the heart bleed. The wind increased its intensity. The runners' eyes became glazed. Three laps had gone and they now weren't so strong But the battle continued to rage. Now was the moment of truth With two and a half miles to go. Some of them 'died' and fell by the side, Whilst others began to slow. Many were already finishing, Paul Pringle and Joe Dooley were locked As they fought for the line (they both got the same time) - Sixty-eight, forty-eight they had clocked! Back into the fray came George Piddington. Back into the fight came Dave Mac. And even John Baker, not ready for his maker, Cried, "Hooray, I'm not at the back". Ten Miles of muddy, cold agony - It's over again till next year. Then our heroes will meet and again they'll repeat The struggle all Belgravians fear. BELGRAVE 10 MILE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP continued. A great run as usual by Laurie but what about Danny Wiseman! He is certainly coming on well. items.s: BELS 3rd AFTER RECOUNT Report and Belgrave placings in the South of the Thames Senior cross country championship on Wimbledon Common on 27 January 1973, where Belgrave were third team after Medway A.C. were pushed down on a recount and Peter Carton took bronze. JANUARY 27th 1973 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SOUTH OF THAMES SNR. CC CHAMP. This year the South of the Thames Senior race came to Wimbledon Common and somehow about 300 runners managed to get changed in Belgrave Hall without too much chaos. In fact the whole thing went off quite slickly. Course markers and pointsmen were plentiful and a new 2½ mile lap gave some variety to our team who know the old route blindfolded. After the courageous starter called everyone back for a false start they were away and streaking to the front in a short lived bid for glory was John Kelly but as the race progressed it was clear that Peter Carton would once again comfortably lead our team home. Medway A.C. managed to finish with six men in the first twenty with Dick Newble 3rd and seemed to have an unassailable lead. Unfortunately for them, later checking revealed that two of their runners were ineligible and a recount of the points pushed them well down the list with ourselves scraping in as third team and Peter moving up to the bronze medal position just a week after his Inter-Counties run. items.sum: Report and results of the Southern cross country championships, won by Dave Bedford, where Belgrave's depleted senior team finished 11th and Peter Carton was second in the junior race.
items.s: Another good one from CARTON but seniors sink to 11th in 'SOUTHERN' Report and results of the Southern cross country championships, won by Dave Bedford, where Belgrave's depleted senior team finished 11th and Peter Carton was second in the junior race. Dave Bedford of Shaftesbury made it all look so easy but it was not our day. Amongst the multi-coloured mass that streamed away from the pens in lashing rain, there were only nine of our men and even then Gerry North was forced to come out with what was later diagnosed as tonsilitis after he had grittily kept going for six miles. What would we do without the ever-dependable Laurie O'Hara ? Once again he was the first Belgravian into the finishing funnel, twelve places ahead of John Bicourt who was up with the leaders at the crest of the first hill and then went to sleep until he found himself in the seventies with two of the three laps gone. With the battle done, we found ourselves 11th of the 45 teams that closed in and, perhaps, with our "bad one" behind us we can hope for a better showing in the National, to be held over the same course. Star of the day was our sole Junior representative Peter Carton, who strode in to a lonely 2nd place 50 seconds behind Coupland of Southampton & Eastleigh and 75 yards ahead of the next man. He looked quite untroubled and with a similar run on National day he must have a good chance of making the Junior International Team. What a pity that our once unbeatable team of Tony Binda, Bill Curtin and John Stow , backing up Peter if not battling with him for individual honours, has now disintegrated. SENIOR RACE Teams:- 1. items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Report and results of the third National veterans' cross country championship at Perry Bar Park, Birmingham, on 18 February 1973, where Laurie O'Hara won the 40-49 race and Belgrave took the team trophy for the first time.
items.s: NATIONAL VET'S CHAMPIONS Report and results of the third National veterans' cross country championship at Perry Bar Park, Birmingham, on 18 February 1973, where Laurie O'Hara won the 40-49 race and Belgrave took the team trophy for the first time. FEBRUARY 18th 1973 - PERRY BAR PARK, BIRMINGHAM . By winning the third National Championship for veteran runners on this cold and windy Sunday afternoon, Belgrave annexed the team trophy for the first time and furnished the individual champion also in the sprightly form of Laurie O'Hara. Laurie didn't just win - he slaughtered the opposing runners. Belgrave didn't just win - they annihilated the opposing teams. It was that sort of day, Claret and Gold all the way. And it really was like the old days to hear the whistles of surprise at the presentation ceremony when our winning score of 29 points was announced. The Group 2 (50-59) and Group 3 (Over 60) fields were combined and their race began at midday over three laps of a fast grassland course. We had no entries in these categories. The premier event (Group 1, 40-49) was held at 1 p.m. over the same 10,000 metres course and 200 runners toed the line. A vicious start saw Laurie back in the twenties at the first turn, but as the field swept up a long slope into a bitter wind he moved through to the front group where Meadows (Portsmouth) was forcing the pace from Harland (Cambridge) - both newcomers to the ranks. Not far behind at this point, in the twenties, were Clive Shippen and Pat Newell running together, while in the ruck of the field Fred Paget and Arthur Bruce were well placed to provide team support if required. On the second circuit, Harland opened up 20 yards in an effort to break clear, but Laurie was supremely confident and with marked coolness closed the gap and put in his own burst, which stretched and stretched and stretched to a winning margin of 34 seconds - a brilliant effort. Meanwhile, Clive was having his best race for a long while, making ground steadily to finish 10th, and closer to Laurie than he has been for many years; and Pat settled in to 18th which, with no racing of late, was an excellent performance. With three to score, that was that; but just in case something went wrong Fred and Arthur were fighting it out with the opposition in the sixties. It says much for their fine efforts that if our third scorer had failed to finish we still would have won with either of these two scoring. Further back down the field was the man who had more confidence in us than anyone - John Baker. He ran down that finishing straight like a man inspired. With over 20 runners behind him it was his day too! But for Reg Hopkins giving the team a day of his leisure to ferry the team up and back, and Gordon Biscoe rising at 6 a.m. to ensure that everyone (including Reg!) met and departed on time, it is questionable whether a team would have appeared at all. Well, you know what it is like when you reach second childhood! Teams. 1. BELGRAVE H 29 pts; 2. Springburn 87 pts; 3. T.V.H. 94 pts. 1. L.O'Hara (BELGRAVE H) 32:35 2. K.Harland (Camb.H) 33:01 3. items.s: SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV.1) Report and results of the last two Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 matches of 1972-73 (Streatham Common, 9 December 1972; Coulsdon, 17 February 1973), in which newcomers Aldershot, Farnham & District took the title from Belgrave by 12 points. With the coming of Aldershot, Farnham & District to the Surrey Cross Country League it was hoped that a little more excitement would be injected into what, for the past seven years, has become a bit of a procession. It certainly was! In the 3rd match at Streatham Common we were beaten by a mere 8 points with Les Presland, running with even more vigour since his move from Surrey A.C., providing the individual winner. So, we went into the final act of this desperately close struggle just 18 points up and with our grip on the trophy gradually being loosened. With Gerry North still suffering from tonsilitis, John Stow stuck in a train at Raynes Park and our veterans girding themselves for the following days National Veteran's race, our chances became even slimmer. Over the Coulsdon course, still patchy with snow, the men from west Surrey romped home 30 points clear and gained an overall lead of 12 points. Well done Aldershot! But keep that trophy polished. 1. items.h: FROM THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago ...... and 40 years ago
items.sum: Look-back column recalling Belgrave's results in November 1947 (English senior cross-country championship at Apsley and the new 10 miles National walk) and March 1933 (Bert Footer's 'Southern' win, the RWA Ten Miles Junior walk at Birmingham and Belgrave's first placing and International selections in the National), with results tables; the 1933 National results run on at the foot of page 39.
items.s: FROM THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago ...... and 40 years ago Look-back column recalling Belgrave's results in November 1947 (English senior cross-country championship at Apsley and the new 10 miles National walk) and March 1933 (Bert Footer's 'Southern' win, the RWA Ten Miles Junior walk at Birmingham and Belgrave's first placing and International selections in the National), with results tables; the 1933 National results run on at the foot of page 39. NOVEMBER, 1947.................... The ENGLISH SENIOR CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP was held at Apsley over a course almost knee-deep in snow. This was definitely not a fair test to the runners, although A.A. Robertson ran in really magnificent style and fully deserved his win. LEN HERBERT (our Southern Champion) finished 6th and so gained yet another International vest, while ALBERT FROST ran in great style to finish 17th and so gain his Club Honours Badge. Sutton Harriers, the Northern champions, beat us for the team championship, although we retained the "Finch-Wayte" Cup awarded to the first Southern club to finish. Belgrave positions were as follows: Teams: 1. Sutton H. 160pts; 2. BELGRAVE H. 184pts; 3. Reading A.C. 187pts; 4. Blackheath H. 255pts; 5. Aylesford P.M. 256pts; 6. T.V.H. 300pts. Highlight of the Race Walking season was the double win in the new 10miles National Championship. Following a succession of wins in open road races over a similar distance, everyone looked forward to the Bels giving a good account of themselves. With our scoring 4 in the first 6 and an aggregate of 13 points, it should be many years before the record is equalled, let alone beaten. Belgrave placings were: MARCH, 1933..................... The three successive Saturdays, February 25th, March 4th and March 11th, brought with them three performances of outstanding merit which focussed the eyes of all the athletic world upon Belgrave and more than ever fortified our right to be considered the greatest all-round athletic club in the country. With February 25th came the 'Southern', our best team position yet - second; and as individual win for H.E. Footer with A.W. Penny third. All honour to Bert upon his wonderful success! It is very fitting that one who has done so much for the Club.....should be the first to receive the Club Honours Badge - even if Arthur Penny earned his one minute later! On March 4th "that remarkable club Belgrave" - we quote the SHEFFIELD SPORTS ECHO - won the Road Walking Association Ten Miles Junior Championship at Birmingham and so once again became proud holders of the 'Garnet' Cup. This is our 4th win - a record superior to that of any other club in the country - and was an example of good team work. The score of 26 points is the second lowest ever recorded in the history of this competition, and the best Belgrave score yet. Further honours came on March 11th, when for the first time in our Club history we were placed in the National Cross-Country Championship; and had two men in the first five home, so securing International selection. Our heartiest congratulations go out to Bert Footer and Arthur Penny upon their well-deserved honour. We trust it will become an annual affair for them, and that in future years there will be other Belgravians to accompany them. .....continued at foot of next page Teams: 1. Birchfield H. 80pts; 2. items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Cross country columnist's review of a disappointing Belgrave winter, praising Peter Carton's junior season, lamenting the loss of his former team-mates, and celebrating Laurie O'Hara and the National Veterans title at Perry Barr.
items.s: COUNTRYMAN'S JOTTINGS Cross country columnist's review of a disappointing Belgrave winter, praising Peter Carton's junior season, lamenting the loss of his former team-mates, and celebrating Laurie O'Hara and the National Veterans title at Perry Barr. Belgravians have not had a great deal to shout about over the country this winter. No medals in the Surrey County Championship for the first time in 8 years; a lowly 11th in the 'Southern' at Parliament Hill; and the loss of our Surrey League title, also for the first time in 8 years, hardly merits self-satisfaction. But base statistics can often cloud the picture, and there were several moments worth dwelling upon. There was the excitement of both South of Thames races - 4th in the 'Junior' and 3rd in the 'Senior'; pruned opposition perhaps, but still healthy for morale to see a goodly splash of claret and gold up front. There was the sight of a much weakened team in the final league race at Coulsdon, fighting to the death against a full strength Aldershot F.D. squad before going down by the smallest margin yet in the history of the league. And last, but not least, there was the sight of Peter Carton finishing inside the first eight whenever he ran, whether it was the Southern Junior (2nd), the Surrey County Junior (1st), the Inter-Counties Junior (8th) or the South of Thames Senior (3rd). Peter has been regularly fighting it out at the front and is surely on the brink of a successful career as a Senior. I have been most impressed with his mature approach to running. He covers merely half the mileage of his close rivals yet is able to channel his efforts so effectively. Unlike the others, he also has more in hand for building up his training in the years ahead. I feel sure that we have only seen the beginnings of the real Peter Carton and the coming track season is likely to underline this observation. Talk of Peter Carton inevitably reminds us of the other members of that quartet which regularly put fear into the hearts of opposing boy and youth teams a few years back. "Come back Tony Binda!" is the first thought, for Tony had already shown that he was about to break through and provide Peter with close support before his move to the West Indies wrecked the possibility. But the lad who showed the best natural flair, on the track at any rate, was John Stow. John has kept in shape regularly enough to find that a solid year's work could also get him up to his rightful place in the forward position. What Peter has done, the others can still do. Is Bill Curtin listening? From the young to the (relatively) old. What about this man Laurie O'Hara? Can he really go on achieving life-time bests every year now that he is in his forties? Against veteran athletes he is truly incincible, and many of his conquests have been against former internationals. Students of veteran running have had to re-write many of their theories since Laurie came on to the scene. For instance, how does he fit on to a graph of deteriorating form? How does one compare his best ever performance with his veteran bests where the latter are superior? As someone remarked when Laurie cantered the Veterans 'National' at Birmingham a few weeks ago "That lad looks to have a good future"! Talking of Vets., it was good to see Belgrave win the National Veterans title at Perry Barr, Birmingham. This championship is not the push-over that some may think, and the ferocity of the running had to be seen to be believed. There were 200 starters in the 40-49 age group alone, and those with memories of Nationals of 20 years ago saw much to make them reminisce. There was George Rhodes (7th) fighting it out with Eddie Kirkup (8th) just as they did for England vests in 1955. And the diminutive Johnny Wild was there, just 5 places down on his 8th spot of 1956. The man they all feared in the late fifties was Gerry North, and Gerry has been making sounds that suggests he is out to hammer them again in 3 years time when he "comes of age". items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Track captain Alan Mead's preview of the 1973 track season, covering the Surrey relays and championships, Southern League, the National Knockout and the chance of Commonwealth Games selection, and urging members to tell their secretaries their plans.
items.s: TRACK & FIELD Track captain Alan Mead's preview of the 1973 track season, covering the Surrey relays and championships, Southern League, the National Knockout and the chance of Commonwealth Games selection, and urging members to tell their secretaries their plans. In just a few weeks the track season will be under way and sprinters and other "explosive" event men will be emerging from their winter hiding places eager for competition after dark and lonely nights of heaving weights and pounding sodden tracks. Our middle and long distance men will already be going through their road relay paces, prior to stepping on to the sacred tartan and cinder. This season is going to take some planning, with the Surrey County relays as early as April 14/15 and the main championships a month later, through to Southern League meetings as late as the end of September. Then of course, for those who really make the grade, there is always the possibility of a trip to New Zealand in the middle of next winter for the Commonwealth Games. The National Knockout competition kicks off in May and in the first round we have a fight on our hands with only two clubs to qualify for the subsequent round and with Hillingdon and Blackheath amongst our opposition. Planning is definitely the key. Keep your fixture card to hand, know what you are going to do this summer and let your Track or Field Event Secretary know your plans, they are not psychic. Of course it is hoped that you will turn out as often as possible but if you are selected for a League, Trophy or Knockout match and you know you cannot make it, again, please let your Secretary know. See you down at the track then and let's hope we can carry on from where we left off in '72 - winning! Alan Mead Track Captain. items.sum: Junior Hon. Secretary Reg Hopkins Snr.'s report on the revival of the club's junior section, naming promising colts, boys and youths from the winter season.
items.s: YOUTHS & BOYS Junior Hon. Secretary Reg Hopkins Snr.'s report on the revival of the club's junior section, naming promising colts, boys and youths from the winter season. It is with great satisfaction that I report the Junior section is once again springing into life with new members joining almost every week. It does seem as if we are in the same position we were in just a few seasons ago, when, although we could not at that time claim to have many successes, there was a great spirit in circulation among the young members. This was the springboard from which our winning Youth and Junior teams sprang later on. It looks like history repeating itself, all it needs is for each member to train painstakingly, have patience and not to look for immediate success but to be content to improve outing by outing. COLTS We have had a good turn out from these lads for most of our Winter fixtures. Very pleasant to see has been the steady progress made by Adrian Cook. We hope this will continue as we see in him a future Team Captain. Backing him up so well has been James Roberts, another very good prospect. Two others I must mention from this section are Gary Wallace and Gary Budginger, two youngsters who are prepared to give everything in a race and wear their Club colours with pride. Simon Nelson is another we have great hopes for after his brave efforts in the Surrey Boys Championships. Nice to see Ian and Martin Gillings in action again, we hear they have been doing some great running at school. If we were to give a medal for perseverance it would have to go to Ivan Beaumont. Never seeming to have the success we all feel he deserves he nevetheless always turns out regardless of the weather or conditions. He has, without doubt, all that it takes to make the grade. BOYS Turning now to our Boys section, although not large in number, this section too is coming to life. With Steve Waters, Tony Ambler, Toby Staffs and Steve Watts we now have the nucleus of a winning team. YOUTHS We can just manage to raise a Youth team from Simon Holmes, Reg Hopkins, David Cobb and the occasional odd member, but with the recent joining of twins Pat and Anthony Jenkins I now feel our strength will grow. Congratulations to new member Simon Shanks on completing his first cross country race in such a brave fashion. Reg Hopkins, Snr. Junior Hon. items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Profile, with portrait photo, of 13-year-old Belgrave colt James Roberts, his running, schooling and other interests.
items.s: MEET JAMES ROBERTS Profile, with portrait photo, of 13-year-old Belgrave colt James Roberts, his running, schooling and other interests. James is 13 years old and joined us early in 1971, following the example of his near neighbour and friend Adrian Cook. He has already proved to be one of our most reliable youngsters, turning out to run in Belgrave colours whenever he can and often arriving up at the Hall carrying his Leeds United bag, all set for a training run. He plays both cricket and football at his school, Davis's School at Hampstead, and also gets great enjoyment from his running, favourite events being 400 netres on the track and 2 miles cross country. When it comes to cross country James prefers the "real thing" as opposed to the many courses that involve so many laps around a playing field, and the muddier it is the better. Last year he gained his AAA 5 star award in the under-13 age group and hopes to qualify for the under-14 award this coming summer. Recruiting of youngsters should be one of Belgrave's top priorities, says James, but just as it should be, sport is not the only interest in his life. He is fond of all types of music and takes regular piano lessons. James Roberts James Roberts aged 13, joined early 1971; AAA 5 star award under-13 Adrian Cook Adrian Cook James Roberts's neighbour and friend AAA 5 star award Hampstead

items.sum: Profile, with portrait photo, of 14-year-old Belgrave cross country runner Adrian Cook, his school races and his hopes for more track sessions for youngsters.
items.s: MEET ADRIAN COOK Profile, with portrait photo, of 14-year-old Belgrave cross country runner Adrian Cook, his school races and his hopes for more track sessions for youngsters. At 14 years of age Adrian already shows signs that he has embarked upon a promising athletic career. He lives locally, attending Raynes Park High School,and became a Belgravian two years ago when introduced by Ron Linstead. Although he is interested in most sports and is a supporter of Brentford Football Club, his preference is for cross country running. Last year he came fourth in the Surrey schools race but was too young to be entered in the All-England race. This season he started off very well with a win in the Merton schools championship but found the slippery going a bit too much for him in the Surrey event. No long term aims yet of course. He intends to carry on running a couple of times a week and just "let it come". He would like to gain more knowledge of track running and thinks it would be a good idea to have a few more track get-togethers for our youngsters. items.sum: Notice explaining the AAA 5 Star Award Scheme, which the club will run for youngsters at its summer meetings, with contact via Reg. Hopkins Snr.
items.s: Notice explaining the AAA 5 Star Award Scheme, which the club will run for youngsters at its summer meetings, with contact via Reg. Hopkins Snr. This coming summer we intend to run the AAA 5 Star Award Scheme in conjunction with the Youths and Boys medal competitions and the open meeting on May 13th but if you wish to be tested on any other occasion do not hesitate to contact Reg. Hopkins Snr., whose address you will find on the inside cover of this magazine, or turn up at any of our home fixtures at Battersea Park. Many of you may have come across this scheme at school but for those of you who haven't, this is the idea. The competition is designed to take in all age groups from under 11 years to under 20 years. Points are scored for each event you wish to take part in, depending upon the standard you manage to attain in each event. The points for your best three performances (which must be two field events and one track event or vice versa) are added together and you will gain an award ranging from one to five stars in value, in the form of a certificate. Cloth or metal badges suitable to wear on your tracksuit are also available. It is also possible to gain a decathlon star award by competing in ten different events. So, we look forward to seeing you down at the track this summer - good luck! Reg. Hopkins Snr. Reg. Hopkins Snr. contact for AAA 5 Star Award testing AAA 5 star award Battersea Park

items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Jack Goswell's obituary of Syd Roberts, Belgrave walker, Walking Secretary, Club Treasurer, President and R.W.A. official, who died on 10 January 1973 aged 66.
items.s: S. C. (SYD) ROBERTS Jack Goswell's obituary of Syd Roberts, Belgrave walker, Walking Secretary, Club Treasurer, President and R.W.A. official, who died on 10 January 1973 aged 66. It is with great sorrow that we have to advise the death on January 10th of Syd Roberts at the age of 66 years, after a distinguished career as a walker then administrator for the Club and the R.W.A. Our sincere condolences go to his widow in her sad loss and we are grateful for having had the assistance and comradeship over nearly 36 years of a true 'Belgravian' and gentleman. Syd joined the Club on 4th March 1937 and was soon making his mark in a very strong walking fraternity at that time. In May 1938 he finished 5th in the Barking to Southend Police Championship in 5:38:02 and led the winning team , B Div., home. This was the year when Belgrave had F.Bentley 1st in 5:1:11.4, F.Rickards 2nd, A.Readman 3rd, S.Roberts 5th, R.Martin 6th and five others amongst the finishers including F.Jarvis 44th. At Manchester in 1939 he was a member of our winning Club team in the R.W.A. National Junior 10 miles. Like many others, the war took care of 1939/45 for him but afterwards Syd took over as Walking Secretary and soon helped to once again bring Belgrave to the fore by his wise administration and help for all. I still have the letter he sent me, pointing out all the snags when I was taking over from him as Walking Secretary in 1952. Syd then moved to the office of Club Treasurer which he held from 1952 to 1962 and during these years he did a 1st class job in reorganising the membership book and finances - no mean job. He was elected to the highest office as Club President in 1957/58. During these years Syd was also an active member of the S.R.W.A. Committee and held various offices. On the parent body of the R.W.A. he was really active, acting as Chief Recorder at many national championships, Judge Sub-Committee Secretary, then the first National Coaching Secretary for R.W.A. in 1963/64 an office he held with distinction. In the late sixties he underwent a serious operation. After a period of convalescence he moved to St. Annes on Sea, Lancs., and it was from there that he and his wife travelled the 30 miles to Hulton, Manchester on the occasion of the R.W.A. 20 miles championship in 1972. It was a great pleasure to greet him once again and speak with them both. Quite contented and although a lot slower moving, he maintained that he was improving all the time. Little did I realise that it was to be the last time I would see him. The sport of Race Walking and Athletics in general is the poorer for his passing. The R.W.A. President and other members of the N.R.W.A. represented the Club at his funeral on the same day as Alf Harley's, Monday 15th January 1973 - a black day for the Club with the passing on of two fine English gentlemen. items.label: March 1973
items.sum: Feature on Belgrave race walkers who became Centurions by walking 100 miles within 24 hours, with their badge numbers and times.
items.s: CENTURIONS ALL Feature on Belgrave race walkers who became Centurions by walking 100 miles within 24 hours, with their badge numbers and times. A Centurion is one who, as an Amateur, has walked in competition, in Great Britain, 100 miles within 24 hours. To become a Centurion is the ambition of every long-distance walker. Most Walking Clubs in Great Britain can claim a number in their membership, and Belgrave, with its great traditions and record is no exception. We recently mourned the death of Ernest Neville, Centurion Number 7, who was associated with a number of Clubs and was one of our Vice-Presidents. I have been unable to check which of the early Centurions were Belgravians, for example when I was competing in the North some years ago a chap wearing a Centurion badge said that he was a member of the Bels in his racing days. Coming to 1921 we find that Jimmy Belchamber finished second in the Brighton and Back race in 20:53:35 to become No. 64. Jimmy was a Past President of the Club and served in many offices, for instance for many years he was Hon. Auditor. He loved walking and covered many miles in his native Sussex. Our own 50 Km Championship carries a cup named after him. Five years later Jim Chalk did a fine 19:03:30 for 100 miles in the "B and B". Jim was a staunch Belgravian and figured in many winning teams. After he had retired from competition he walked miles to come and support our teams on the road, invariably accompanied by his dog. After World War II the first event at the distance was a 24 hours walk at the White City in 1946. It rained for many hours and Colin Sutton clocked 20:44:11 to become No. 125. Colin was a great performer at all distances, an R.A.F. pilot during the war he re-enlisted after a short spell as a civilian and was killed by a sniper in Malaya. In the same race was Bob Martin, a policeman who also figured in many of our teams, and who clocked 22:16:57 to become No. 127. He was killed in an accident whilst on a motor-cycle patrol a few years later. The above four, now departed, showed the way for other Belgravians to follow. The first post-war "B and B" was eagerly awaited by the writer who fulfilled an ambition when he heared Ernest Neville call, "23:26:41" at the 100 miles point to become No. 142. When he is not timekeeping he still enjoys a walk (Wimbledon Common and Richmond Park are close at hand) followed by a warm bath! 1948 saw a 24 hours race at Motspur Park which resulted in a Belgrave win for Jack Stirling-Wakeley, whose death was recently reported. He covered 100 miles in 18:56:13 to become No. 143 and went on to cover 122 miles 1411 yards. Three years later he won the "B and B" in 18:46:0. In the same race Joe Wilson walked his usual sound race to become No. 164 in 21:04:46. Joe needs no introduction and is often at the roadside judging or helping with the feeding, or, indeed, giving his Club vest an airing. Joe always wears a Belgrave vest when competing - do you ? Further down the field came Harry Stallard, a Dover based enthusiast who worked hard for the sport in his area, in 23:20:04 to become No. 173. In 1952 another classic route was walked, Bath to London (Chiswick) and Chelsea policeman Syd Spencer recorded a very fine 20:09:45 for badge No. 181. A solid Clubman who was a regular in "Belgrave" and Police teams for a good many years. Now retired, we often see him judging. In the same race Fred Herring, an R.A.F. man gained badge No. 191 in 21:50:00. We haven't seen Fred for a number of years but he did a lot to encourage Race Walking in the R.A.F. before retiring. In the 1955 "B and B" there were 31 new Centurions, amongst them three Belgravians. Harry Shields followed up a great career as a runner (twice a member of winning E.C.C.U. teams) and an equally great one as a walker (member of winning team in R.W.A. 50 Kilos Championship) to become No. 235 in 20:02:22. Harry is still a well known official at Running and Walking events, he is also handy with the measuring tape and at raking the long jump pit! With brother Joe qualifying in the 1951 race Percy Wilson took his turn to become No. 246 in 21:53:55. Like Joe you cannot keep him away from the sporting scene, he recently had a spell in hospital due to a stroke but is now fighting his way back to fitness. Completing the Club trio was Frank Jarvis in 23:25:22, No. 258. Frank was another "regular" in Belgrave and Police teams. Nowadays he is kept busy as General Hon. Secretary of the R.W.A. Another to qualify in this race was Les Fairman in the colours of Poly. H. Now a Belgravian and well known figure at Belgrave Hall he walked a fine race to become No. 232 in 19:31:33. The next "B and B" (1963) saw two Belgravians doing the journey stride by stride, Cyril Yescombe (another Police stalwart) who died tragically a few years ago and Bernard Eglington, former runner from Derby and R.A.F. man. They came through the 100 miles point in torrential rain in 21:28:57 earning themselves badges 344 and 345. Bernard now lives in N. Wales and occasionally makes a welcome appearance. In 1965 the M.P.A.A. promoted a race on a lap course at Chigwell and amongst those to qualify was Doug. Fotheringham in 21:31:09 for badge No. 373. Doug. is still going strong - if not stronger! The older he gets the faster he goes! He is the Hon. Sec. of the M.P.A.A. Walking Section. The Surrey W.C. 100 miles at Ewhurst (1971) is of recent memory, when our own John Moullin won in a phenomènal world-class performance of 16:55:44 to become No. 462. Lower down the field, stride for stride, came John Keown (473) and John Morris (474) finishing together in 20:49:27. They took second team prize and are still active, further anecdotes unnecessary! We have many potential Centurions in Belgrave who, when the time comes, will add to the list. Good luck to them! They will need it. Gordon S. items.sum: Editor's reply to Bob Barnes apologising for missing walking times in the club all-time best performances and asking for someone to keep walking records for 1973.
items.s: missing walk times in club rankings Editor's reply to Bob Barnes apologising for missing walking times in the club all-time best performances and asking for someone to keep walking records for 1973. Bob Barnes writes and asks, "Why no ranking lists for Walking in the last 'Belgravian' ?". Well, Bob there are no real excuses and before anyone else writes, apologies are due for the missing Walking times in our 'Belgrave All Time Best Performances' in this issue. Does anyone amongst the Walking Section usually keep a record of these things? If not, perhaps some statistically minded stroller would be good enough to keep a list during 1973 for all the regular track walks plus, of course, for the Olympic distance road events. Meanwhile, if anyone can come up with some best times over metric distances, we will be pleased to publish them in the next issue. items.s: POSTBAG Letter from Dave De Bondi in Ringwood East, Victoria, Australia, thanking the club for The Belgravian and giving news of his track season and plans. 30 Everard Road, Ringwood East, Victoria, Australia 3135. ..... It was really great to receive "The Belgravian", I had almost given up hope of ever seeing the familiar red and gold cover again. It's always nice to know how the "Bels" are faring on the home front. If you happen to drop into "The Denmark" after training, please give my regards to Colin Pearson and Co. I guess there must be a lot of new faces in the Club by now. We are half way through our track season here and I'm doing quite well, although the winter season with its longer distances always suit me better. Hope we see Carl over this way next year for the Commonwealth Games, or perhaps even Ray. If ever a fellow deserves a trip it's Ray. I will be starting teachers college this year and as yet don't know how much time I'll have to train. Plenty I hope, as Australia will probably send a full team of walkers to New Zealand. Hope the year goes well for you, and of course sees the maroon and gold colours well to the fore in British Athletics again. Till later, all the best, Regards, Dave De Bondi Dave De Bondi Dave De Bondi writing from Ringwood East, Victoria, Australia; walker Colin Pearson Colin Pearson Carl Carl hoped to be at the Commonwealth Games Ray Ray hoped to be at the Commonwealth Games Commonwealth Games Ringwood East Victoria Australia The Denmark New Zealand

items.sum: Letter from Nancy Harley to the club President thanking Belgravians for their donation to Mount Vernon Hospital in tribute to Alf Harley.
items.s: Letter from Nancy Harley to the club President thanking Belgravians for their donation to Mount Vernon Hospital in tribute to Alf Harley. This following letter was received by our President but will be of interest to all. Dear Clive, Will you please convey my sincere thanks to all Belgravians for the very generous donation for Mount Vernon Hospital - which I feel is a great tribute to Alf. I know this is as he would have wished, instead of flowers withering away the money will be used in a very worthwhile cause. With renewed thanks, Very sincerely, Nancy Harley. Nancy Harley Nancy Harley widow of Alf Harley (implied) Clive Clive club President Alf Alf tribute donation to Mount Vernon Hospital Mount Vernon Hospital

items.label: June 1973
items.sum: Editorial on the International Track Association's professional circus, athletes' expenses and the Wembley meeting before the F.A. Cup Final, with a word of encouragement to young new members.
items.s: COMMENT Editorial on the International Track Association's professional circus, athletes' expenses and the Wembley meeting before the F.A. Cup Final, with a word of encouragement to young new members. COMMENT The International Track Association's professional athletic circus seems to have got off the ground in the United States in spite of one or two set backs but the organisers still appear to be searching for some really outstanding performances to set things alight. There is no doubt that although things are slowly changing in amateur athletics in Britain, we could still do with a lot more showmanship and presentation to attract and keep the public's interest. However, when one hears stories of the athletes in the ITA not breaking their professional records by too much each time out, because they will find it that much harder to earn their bonus next time, then one feels sure that the touring athletic circus is not the "be all and end all" of professional athletics. What is unfair is that men and women in the higher echelons of our sport spend hours every day, winter and summer, to become the best, and yet are not allowed to defray their losses by endorsing products or accepting reasonable expenses. Athletics at Wembley before the F.A. Cup Final was a great idea and was appreciated by the crowd and TV viewers alike. Now, shouldn't those who took part receive some material benefit for their efforts, like their footballing brothers who took the field afterwards. * * * Youngsters are becoming interested in sport at an earlier and earlier age and we welcome with open arms those lads that have shown an interest in athletics and have joined Belgrave Harriers. Please remember though that you have years ahead of you so take things steadily and enjoy your new activities. It is inevitable that you will meet in competition boys some years your senior and you will be beaten. Don't be disheartened. Your time will come and your natural growth and increasing strength will see you through. F.A. Cup Final United States Britain Wembley International Track Association

items.label: June 1973
items.sum: Grapevine column of club news and gossip about members.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine column of club news and gossip about members. grapevine Whenever professional soccer managers hit the headlines there are many Belgravians who grimace and hope that a career in the limelight will not eventually attract our Manager cum Cross Country and Road Running Secretary GORDON BISCOE. Fortunately Gordon's soccer interests at the moment only extend to the occasional appearance in his firm's colours. They recently took on a team of girls and were thrashed 2-0 ! Many will remember our Club Record holder GERRY LeROY, one of our outstanding squad of quarter-milers in the late 50's/early 60's. He is still running 400 metre races - and good ones. A win in the Kent County Championship in 50.7 earned him a run in the Inter-Counties meeting. Time and again it is proved that advancing years are no excuse for a falling off in ability. Our evergreen walker DAVE McMULLEN was recently selected to represent Surrey at the age of 53. Congratulations and best wishes to DOUG. JARDINE and his new wife CAROL on their recent marriage. The sneaky so-and-so didn't tell anyone until it was all over but we won't hold it against him. Next Sunday when driving home from your training session, why not tune in to Radio London on 206 metres. CHARLIE GILLETT our Track Vice-Captain presents his weekly rock 'n' roll programme from noon until 1pm. Charlie is not our only representative on this station by the way. You may be lucky (?) enough to hear 'news-hound' TOM POLLOCK giving a round up of athletic results during the sportsnews, or even DAVE McMILLAN on the traffic reports. MEL FORD is another to have an interesting job. He is a member of the Special Air Service and spends a good deal of his time skiing, free fall parachuting, etc. No wonder he keeps so fit. Our President and past Hon.Editor CLIVE SHIPPEN couldn't keep his literary talents suppressed for long. He has become the Editor of a new quarterly publication 'Veteris', the magazine of the Association of Veteran Athletes. Athletics for veterans seems to be becoming more and more popular and 'Veteris' is sure to give this branch of our sport an even greater boost. The globe-trotting CHRIS STEER is off again to the United States shortly and hopes to be in Los Angeles in time to see Laurie O'Hara run in the U.S.Masters Meeting. As we bade him farewell in the pouring rain after the Club 10,000 metre Championship one could only feel envy as he called out to those who will be going to the meeting, "See you in California". When it comes to buying your shoes, bags etc. don't forget to call in at the friendly sports shop down in Kingston Road, South Wimbledon. W. & G. Hales, whose advertisement appears elsewhere in this magazine are sure to be able to supply just what you want - and there's discount too if you are a member. items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS JULY 7th HURLINGHAM PARK Notice of the club track and field championships at Hurlingham Park on 7 July, with start times, directions and the list of events for seniors, juniors and boys. items.sum: President's column (signed Clive Shippen) on Belgrave wins on 12 May, Harry Churcher's medal collection, the youngsters' day at Wimbledon Park, an old Price's A.C. team photograph from Earlsfield (printed on page 6) featuring five future Club Presidents, Percy Wilson's illness, 5th place in the National Road Relay and the Lawtons' Surrey titles, with a Sunday Times wedding photograph of Carl and Barbara Lawton.
items.s: PRESIDENT'S PARS President's column (signed Clive Shippen) on Belgrave wins on 12 May, Harry Churcher's medal collection, the youngsters' day at Wimbledon Park, an old Price's A.C. team photograph from Earlsfield (printed on page 6) featuring five future Club Presidents, Percy Wilson's illness, 5th place in the National Road Relay and the Lawtons' Surrey titles, with a Sunday Times wedding photograph of Carl and Barbara Lawton. PRESIDENT'S PARS Saturday, May 12th, was a particularly successful day for Belgrave Harriers with wins being recorded at all points of the compass. I was at Victoria Park in East London where, on a beautifully sunny day, the claret and gold shone forth to produce a display of team packing which was truly invincible. To see five Belgravians finish between 11th and 18th in a National Championship was indeed meritorious and underlines our continuing strength in this field of our activities. Meanwhile, well to the West of London our track and field team were engaged in their opening Southern League fixture at Oxford. An excellent turn-out and some good performances saw us run away to the highest score of the day. Not to be outdone, our road runners were far to the South busily annexing the Chichester to Portsmouth '16', with Bill Weller, Pat O'Connor and Trevor Hart carrying the colours at this venue. Despite all that success, we still had Laurie O'Hara spare to skate away with the Veteran's 10 mile championship in Richmond Park. May we have many more such days in store. * * * When that great Belgrave walker Harry Churcher died on 24th June 1972 he left behind a unique collection of medals - a collection which spanned 20 years from 1932 to 1952 and included complete sets of A.A.A. track championship medals at 2 and 7 miles besides numerous National and International awards. Mrs. Churcher has most generously handed these to the Club and it was your Committee's wish that these should be held in trust for her. At the last meeting of your Committee it was agreed that the medal collection of this great Belgravian would be mounted in a wall case and displayed in the clubroom so that, in the words of Mrs. Churcher, "they will perhaps help to inspire the younger members of the Club and popularise the art of Race Walking still further". * * * What a joy it was to be at Wimbledon Park Track all day on Sunday, May 13th. Yes, all day! I was not training you appreciate, simply present at an occasion which brought together over 60 unattached youngsters between the ages of 8 and 14 years. In the morning they were all introduced, in groups, to each of the principal field events. That alone required 5 coaches and 5 helpers! But there were plenty more as well - no less than 6 timekeepers and 6 judges were on parade for the afternoon's running while the field event competitions were in full swing. There is a strong spirit pervading through the Club at this time and if there are any doubters they would have done well to witness that day's programme. Our thanks go to Bill Couzens, whose brain-child it was, and to that large number of hard working helpers who saw it through. With each youngster receiving a certificate recording his performances at three chosen events we can feel satisfied that we were truly implementing Rule 4 of our Constitution - " The object of the Club shall be the encouragement of amateur athletics". * * * The picture shown on the left hand page was taken no less than 51 years ago at Earlsfield. Price's candle factory at Battersea(now in the process of partial demolition) had a strong sports club and Price's A.C. had more than its fair share of Belgravians, though not all worked for the firm. The picture was taken on a training day and features several Belgravians, five of whom became Club Presidents. They were Teddy GORDON, Harry HARE, Jock McKAY, Harry EVANS and Micky PYER. If anyone can fill in the missing names I would be pleased to hear from them. We are saddened to hear that the Percy half of the stalwart Wilson brothers is seriously ill in Bolingbroke Hospital. Percy and Joe featured in our walking teams for many many years and I know that Joe will do all he can to keep the partnership going by conveying to Percy our best wishes for his recovery. * * * I was very pleased to hear the many praises that were sung as a result of Belgrave's 5th place in the National Road Relay at Derby, particularly those that came from outside the Club. All will agree that we had a very sound and confident team. Indeed, our weakest link (if you could find one[illegible] was the strongest of any team on view, and each of the four teams that beat us had spells well to our rear. For over 4 hours of running we were always between 5th and 9th positions as the eventual medallists yo-yo'd around us. Birchfield needed four fastest stages and Coventry two to beat us, while our local rivals Hercules Wimbledon who had the most solid 'big six' on view could only squeeze ahead of us by 6 seconds to become first Southern Club. Bouquets to those who beat us, but if ever a team deserved a special medal this day it was ours. * * * The Surrey County Championships at Motspur Park produced two sets of husband and wife champions. John and Judy Vernon took the men's long jump/ women's hurdles double, while our own Carl and Barbara Lawton took the men's walk/women's high jump double. Barbara is now a regular supporter of our walkers. Perhaps our walkers will reciprocate when it comes to the Women's A.A.A. Championships! items.sum: Extracts from The Belgravian of 1948 on club members at the London Olympic Games, and of 1933 on the Southern Amateur Athletic League team races.
items.s: FROM THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago... and 40 years ago... Extracts from The Belgravian of 1948 on club members at the London Olympic Games, and of 1933 on the Southern Amateur Athletic League team races. FROM THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago... THE LONDON OLYMPIC GAMES 1948 ................. we had the satisfaction of seeing three of our club members compete in the Olympic Games as members of the Great Britain team. Actually another member, E.Gailly, was a member of the Belgium team and put up a magnificent performance in finishing 3rd in the Marathon race. Will Nankeville also ran the "race of his life" by finishing 6th in the 1,500 metres final and when one looked through the list of those qualifying for the final, this was indeed a sterling performance. Harry Churcher and Bill Lucas also performed well without actually "hitting the high-spots" and cannot be said to have let the team down, rather was/it a question of our men being outclassed by the wealth of opposition they were up against. and 40 years ago... THE SOUTHERN AMATEUR ATHLETIC LEAGUE........... As Champions of Division I of this league, we have every hope of again distinguishing ourselves this season. The first event of the season was held at Finsbury Park Track on May 6th, a team race at 3 miles, and we ran out easy winners, scoring 23 points to the 38 points of South London H., and 42 points of Herne Hill H. Our successful team consisted of A.Penny (2), C.T.Carter (6), H.E.Footer (7), A.Allum (8). Unfortunately, this excellent start was not maintained, for in the 4 x 440 yards race held at Deptford Park on May 20th, we finished last of the six clubs. If we are to finish at the head of the league this season, we shall have to make amends in the remaining four events to compensate for this lapse. At the moment we are placed third with South London Harriers and Herne Hill Harriers ahead of us. The next fixture is the 4 x 220 yards relay on June 10th at the White City Track. E. items.sum: Track Captain and Field Events Secretary's review of the start of the 1973 track season, the Surrey Championships turn-out, and welcomes to javelin thrower Dave Moulder and returning thrower Eric Barker.
items.s: TRACK & FIELD Track Captain and Field Events Secretary's review of the start of the 1973 track season, the Surrey Championships turn-out, and welcomes to javelin thrower Dave Moulder and returning thrower Eric Barker. TRACK & FIELD We've made a pretty good start to the season and the morale of our team is second to none. Of course most clubs have to get their competitors to 'double-up' to cover all events in league type matches but the willingness of our lads to do this is really pleasing. In fact the whole team seems to be constantly aware of how we are doing pointswise during a meeting and are prepared to do anything to grab those few extra marks. A little disappointing was our turn-out in the Surrey Championships. There is a trophy for the club with the most points scored throughout the whole championships including the relay meeting at Wimbledon Park and somehow we managed to get 3rd place. When you consider those of our number who didn't enter and the fact that the pole vault for instance had only one competitor (not from Belgrave) and was won in 9 feet odd, you will realise that we could swamp this meeting and carry away the 'goodies'. Welcome to Dave Moulder, ex-marine Javelin thrower who was introduced to Belgrave by Cliff Brooks. Dave was Navy Javelin Champion in 1970 and is capable of throws over 200 feet. He has already competed for us in the Southern League Meeting at Oxford and threw 176 feet without training for almost two years. He is keen to get fit again and will add the much needed strength to this event. Watch out Southern League ! Eric Barker is back and has already recorded good performances in the Hammer, Shot and Discus. Eric who really needs eight days in a week to fit athletics in with his working commitments will add to our field event strength by turning out as often as possible Alan Mead & Bill Couzens Track Captain Field Events Hon. IN THE 1st ROUND Report and results of the first round of the new British Athletics Cup at West London Stadium on 6 May 1973, where Belgrave finished fourth and went out; John Bicourt won the steeplechase. K.O'd. IN THE 1st ROUND MAY 6th 1973 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - BRITISH ATHLETICS CUP. One hundred clubs at sixteen venues throughout the British Isles were engaged in this first ever round of the British Athletics Cup with the first two clubs at each match to go on to the semi-finals, hoping to challenge for a place in the final at Crystal Palace in September. It was thought that it would be touch and go whether we would survive and as it happened our rivals Hillingdon and Queens Park H. were far better suited to the one per event rule than ourselves, and even Blackheath got home ahead of us. Nevertheless it was a great opportunity to get our main track and field men together for the first time of the season and blow some of those cobwebs away. Eric Barker produced three very promising efforts in the Hammer, Discus and Shot events and one looks forward to seeing him in action regularly throughout the summer. Talent with the power to exploit it is a rare combination. Another to score heavily was Snowy Brooks, although for him this was a rather quiet day as he only took part in six events including the relays. Our only winner was John Bicourt whose 8:57.4 in his speciality, the steeplechase, was a particularly fine run for so early in the season. In the 5000m Laurie O'Hara sat in on Buchanan of Hillingdon until the final 80 metres when he leapt to the fore with his customary burst but surprise, surprise, the Hillingdon runner had more in hand and with a grin regained the lead, leaving Laurie with 2nd. 100m: 4. items.s: Great start to SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. 1 Report and results of the first Southern League Division I meeting of 1973 at Iffley Road, Oxford, on 12 May, which Belgrave won with 140 points to take the Shuttleworth Trophy. Great start to SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. 1 MAY 12th 1973 - IFFLEY ROAD, OXFORD. What a glorious start to the 1973 Southern League Division I meetings this was. In the tranquil surroundings of Oxford, at the Iffley Road track where Roger Bannister took man into the sub 4 minute mile era, Belgrave were inspired to a great win. Our team excelled on the field and the cinders and many of our 'A' string men found themselves involved in a healthy struggle to keep our 'B' string athletes at bay. When the time came for the final tally, our score of 140 points proved to be the highest of the day throughout the League - so we proudly headed the tables after the first fixture and additionally took home the 'Shuttleworth Trophy', put up by Oxford City A.C. for the winner of their home meeting. John Bicourt's 5000m/1500m stint was a particularly good effort one feels but for sheer grace and power, the running and jumping of Steve White had no comparison, times not meaning a great deal in the windy conditions. Snowy Brooks and Arnold Bentt each contributed a handy 15 points as they dashed from one event to another, the former also running in both relays where we gained maximum points, our team in the 4 x 400m being kind enough to give him a 100m lead on the last leg, allowing him a casual circuit in 57 seconds! For determination and courage however, the kudos must go to Colin Pearson for his 'gutty' finish in the steeplechase. Entering the finishing straight, in this one of the toughest events, he was 20 metres down on the leading 'B' runner yet somehow got to the line before him. As one watched him struggling to recover as he knelt beyond the finish one could only feel pride in the whole team and pleasure in being one of its number. 4 x 100m 1. Surrey County Championships MAY 15th/17th/19th 1973 - MOTSPUR PARK. For the first time ever the Surrey Champs. were a mixed affair or, as the 'Surrey Comet' put it - Unisex Championships ! The atmosphere at the "Surrey's" has been declining gradually over the years and although torrents of rain on finals day (19th), put a real damper on the proceedings the fact that it was mixed did a lot to brighten the event up. Charlie Gillett won the 400 hurdles with a great run, lopping 2 seconds off of his seasonal best and he also managed to pip a tiring Snowy Brooks on the tape in the flat event. Lee Sullivan equalled his best ever in the Long Jump with 6.90m for =3rd, whilst Reg. Hopkins was 2nd in the Junior event with the same distance as the winner but with an inferior second best leap. Steve Crosbie was another to improve his best ever in this event. Mick Marshall's 200 metre runs have improved no end in the last few weeks and he won his heat in grand style. He took silver medal in the 100 metre race but then found that after a 3½ hour wait in the rain for the final of the longer sprint that the snap had gone out of his running. 100m: 2. items.s: 10,000m Championship retained by O'Hara Report and result of the Belgrave 10,000 metres club championship at Battersea Park on 23 May 1973, won by Laurie O'Hara for the fourth time to equal Pat Newell's record of Tom Carter Trophy wins; the text says Newell's four wins came 'from 1956 - 1958'. 10,000m Championship retained by O'Hara MAY 23rd 1973 - BATTERSEA PARK - BELGRAVE 10,000 METRE CHAMPIONSHIP. Pat Newell's presence in the field gave rumour to the fact that as he has been the holder of the 'Tom Carter Trophy' more times than any other Belgravian ( four times from 1956 - 1958) he was out to stop Laurie equalling his record. Laurie's previous victories were in '68, '71 and '72 and now, in spite of pressure throughout the race from Lionel Mann, he chalked up his 4th win to equal Pat's achievement. At the gun O'Hara was straight to the front shadowed by Lionel and Tony Fairclough who gradually dropped away as the race progressed leaving the other two to fight on together. Several times Laurie seemed to stretch Lionel to the limit but still he hung on only a stride behind. Meanwhile, Pat O'Connor was working on the flagging Tony until with 9 laps to go he got past him. With 1 of the 25 laps left, the leading two were still together and one began to wonder if Lionel's doggedness was going to pay off....but no! Laurie's long finishing burst winding up from the bell was just too much and with 250 metres to go they parted company. Leo Coy put up a personal best time ahead of the Bedfordshire 5000m champion Doug Maughan and Eddie Thorpe should not be disappointed with this his first race on the track. dnf. items.s: BELS STILL TOP THE LEAGUE Report and results of the second Southern League Division I meeting at Croydon on 2 June 1973, which Belgrave won by 26 points to stay top of the league. BELS STILL TOP THE LEAGUE JUNE 2nd 1973 - CROYDON. That Southern League wind blew up again to impede those out for a good time or distance but as before when it came to what really counts - the points - we found ourselves at the top again. We lost marks all over the place and still ended up 26 points clear of the battle for second place in which 5 points covered the other four clubs. With no second string Pole Vaulter, Glyn Ratcliffe arriving after a long journey too late for the Discus, Snowy Brooks disqualified in the high hurdles for two false starts, Eric Barker three times fouling a winning Hammer throw by just edging out of the circle, the list went on. This is the mark of the good team though, to overcome the bad luck and still win. The 800m gave Peter Carton his first race and first win of the season with a nonchalant 1:55.2 after leading for the full distance. There are obviously some good runs to come from him as the summer progresses. Glyn Ratcliffe and Eric Barker made mincemeat of the Shot opposition and it is so good to see two BIG men wearing Belgrave colours. Our Track Secretary Philip Gee ran a powerful 400m to win the 'B' race and Charlie Gillett gave of his best with a 400 Hurdles 'B' win, a 3rd in the 'A' 200m where he was only just caught on the line with the first four clocking the same time, and his usual sparkling run round the third leg bend in the short relay. Mick Marshall seemed to pop up everywhere, scoring well in events in which we do not usually see him. And Arnold Bentt, well, at one time his name was being called at either end of the stadium for the High Jump and Pole Vault. Where was he ? items.s: MARCH 3rd 1973 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA R.W.A. MEETING. Walking report and results from the Southern Area RWA meeting at Battersea Park on 3 March 1973, where Belgrave had walkers in all four races and Len Duquemin won the 6 miles; the text gives his time as 44:03 but the table prints 44:02. WALKING MARCH 3rd 1973 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA R.W.A. MEETING. For the first time in many years Belgrave had starters in all four races covering each age group. First away in the Boy's 2 miles race was John Dunsford, who unfortunately was later disqualified with only 200m to go. The reason was that he overdid the early part and had to fight over the second half. Re-adjustment of tactics should help him. Also in this race was Darin Stroud who was slightly outclassed in the field but only due to the fact that he had never walked two miles before. Initially his progression was very ragged as one would expect but as he neared the end his style was something to be desired. These two lads have got a promising future if they can retain their ambition and allow it to come steadily. In the Youth's 3 miles we again had two starters, Stuart Bennett and Malcolm Dodds. They produced good efforts for 6th and 7th positions. The combined Junior and Senior 6 miles was last away and for the Juniors Belgrave had Martin Bennett who produced a class 18th in a field of 100 plus. The overall race was won by Len Duquemin who once again proved that age is something to be ignored. He ground Carl Lawton, and for the second time that week Jackie Lord, into the dust with an astounding 44:03. Carl came in with a good time although far from his best. Filling in the places behind were Ray Middleton and John Hall, with our other lads just out for the sake of racing with no prizes at stake. 1. L.Duquemin (BELGRAVE) 44:02 2. C.Lawton 44:23 3. items.sum: Walking report and results from the National 10 miles championship at Leyland on 17 March 1973, won by John Webb, where Belgrave were second team to Sheffield and Carl Lawton was 7th in a personal best.
items.s: NATIONAL '10' NARROWLY LOST Walking report and results from the National 10 miles championship at Leyland on 17 March 1973, won by John Webb, where Belgrave were second team to Sheffield and Carl Lawton was 7th in a personal best. NATIONAL '10' NARROWLY LOST MARCH 17th 1973 - LEYLAND - NATIONAL 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP. The Bels took their team up part way by car on the Friday night to ease the train travelling situation. With two cars, they got parted not far from Hendon and so one party ended up at a "3 star" at Coventry and the other at a "not recommended" at Stoke on Trent. As it turned out, the travellers by train made it without any problems. The race with its 200 starters was away at 1-15pm on a one-lap course. For the first two miles there were 15 walkers grouped together at the front including Len, John and just hanging on at no. 15, Carl. With mile times being given it became obvious that the speed was rather excessive for some of those in the group, and slowly they peeled off as ........ continued on next page continued..... John Webb,with Roger Mills in close pursuit, broke away. These positions were held to the finish to enable Webb to win his first National title at the age of 36. Third was Jake Warhurst who put in a final burst to pull up past the flagging Flynn. Carl, only a week after his wedding, turned in a stormer to finish 7th in a personal National '10' best. Unfortunately our boys behind were not quite as sharp as they might have been. This was possibly due to the long journey from Coventry on the Saturday morning, or perhaps it was the training weekend the previous week. Thus, although we had John Moullin, Len and Ray all in the first 22 places it was not enough to beat Sheffield. Further back, John Hall walked quite a good one in the hot conditions to beat Southend's Banyard and Rosser whilst Dave McMullen came under the judges ban as did many other men. John Dunsford was at one time seen walking backwards! Gerry Cameron, after a long trip down from Dunfermline, held off Ray Hall. Finally came Pat Duncan, and although many of the walkers at the front went off faster than him he was unable to pull them back again when he began to "come through" with 20 yards to go. Bernard Eglington unfortunately arrived too late to start. Teams:- 1. Sheffield 43pts; 2. BELGRAVE H 50pts; 3. Southend 84pts. 1. J.Webb (Basildon) 72:43 2. R.Mills (Ilford) 73:06 3. items.label: June 1973
items.h: A BELGRAVIAN NORTH OF THE WALL
items.sum: Light-hearted profile by Carl Lawton of Gerry Cameron, Belgrave's Scotland-based walker and Grade One walking coach, recalling his career highlights.
items.s: A BELGRAVIAN NORTH OF THE WALL Light-hearted profile by Carl Lawton of Gerry Cameron, Belgrave's Scotland-based walker and Grade One walking coach, recalling his career highlights. Little mention has been made of the work being done by our 'North of the Border' paid up member Gerry Cameron. Our roving correspondent, however, whilst on a round trip, discovered Gerry hiding in the small village of Carnock, in the shadow of Dunfermline. Despite rumours that he is spending his time cultivating children as some people cultivate potatoes, this is in fact untrue, as his total to date is only two girls and one boy (the latter also being a paid up member of Belgrave). Our correspondent was given excellent hospitality as well as sporting activity in the form of football and wrestling in the spacious garden. Gerry is of course a Grade One Walking Coach (what's that ?) the only one that we have in Belgrave. He is working hard to help the continuation of walking in Scotland but as usual comes up against the 'hard nuts' of athletics who don't want to know anything about walking. He welcomes any other Belgrave members to visit him and stay, and always has plenty of food in, although not much space to eat it in as so much room is taken up by the freezer. Our junior members, Dave McMullen, Ray Middleton, etc., will wonder just who Cameron is or has been. Well, 'has been' sums it up. Gerry joined Belgrave 12 years ag when working in London. His work has since taken him to Market Harborough, Swindon and Scotland (north of Watford for the uninitiated). His walking has tended to suffer due to this moving around - at least that's his story. He has, however, many successes to his name including consecutive wins in the Belgrave Junior 5 mile championship and the Belgrave Horwood Cup races. He also reached the dizzy heights of third in the Southern Area Garnet 10 miles, and will casually mention that he gained a national first team medal in the National 20 kilo's at Coventry in May '67. .... John Moullin was fading badly and Belgrave looked in a bad way when the battle sound of the bagpipes and swirling haggis was heard as Cameron stormed through to win the day...... Finally, the high point of Gerry's walking career was a glorious performance in the Dawlish '5' a few years ago, a win in fact that he is too modest to talk about to many people.
