items.s: grapevine Club news column: Charlie Smart's illness, Bernard Eglington's marriage, Gordon Doubleday's poor health, Hall cleaning, New Zealand Belgravians, Alf Taylor, a donor's letter, Surrey County AAA posts, Ed. Lacey's commended photograph, Derek Crookes as new Belgrave '20' organiser, membership of 469, Linda Manning's raffle sales and a wedding rumour. grapevine Unfortunately CHARLIE SMART suffered a setback recently in his fight back to good health and he is unable at present to get out of the house. Visitors would be more than welcome at his home - 25 Borneo Street, SW15. Meanwhile, all the best Charlie, and may we soon see you about once again. Congratulations to Vice-President BERNARD EGLINGTON upon his recent marriage. He joined the Club about thirty years ago when he was a full time member of the R.A.F., and was previously with Derby & County. He made the switch from running to walking and soon made his mark over the longer distances and figured in many of our winning teams. By walking step for step with the late Cyril Yescombe from Brighton to London and back he became Centurion No. 344. Now living in the Colwyn Bay area he keeps himself fit and we are always glad when he makes a trip to town to line up with the Bels team. We wish Bernard and Grace many years of health and happiness. Unhappy news comes from GORDON DOUBLEDAY. It seems that he is having to take things very quietly at the moment after suffering a patch of bad health. Treatment has consisted of having to sleep sitting up and taking a vast array of pills amongst other things. Let us hope that his recovery is swift and that once again,armed with stop-watch,he will be presiding over the finish of our races. There is a notice in Belgrave Hall asking for volunteers to clean the Hall. Please add your name to the accompanying list if you are one of those who regularly use our facilities. It might even be worth your while - our Hon. Treasurer (who else) found some loose change whilst Field Events Sec. Bill Couzens even found a couple of old runners under the tables amongst the dust! Our walkers in New Zealand for the Commonwealth Games met up with two Belgravians from "Down Under" while they were there. DAVE DE BONDI and VIC TOWNSEND both send their regards to all Bels. It is pleasing to hear (via Harry Shields) that our Past President ALF TAYLOR and his wife JENNY are both well in their Somerset retreat. Alf was a member of our winning E.C.C.U. teams and was also Social Secretary for some time. An irate letter, using the President's pre-stamped envelope, was returned with 20p and a curt note saying this was not for the appeal as a club like ours didn't ought to have to stoop to this sort of thing - it was for our mag. the "Belgravian". Thank you donor - but are you aware that it barely pays for ONE magazine and postage and you have FOUR each year. The christmas pudding won in one of our raffles by a Blackheath Harrier was duly consumed by our Kentish friends at a Blackheath supper. ........ ..What's that, you mean we forgot to put in the "special" ingredient. Congratulations to FRANK JARVIS who was elected President of the Surrey County A.A.A. in February. CLIVE SHIPPEN and GORDON BISCOE were voted onto the "Surrey" committee. The work of ED. LACEY, a member since 1948 and whose photographs have appeared in the "Belgravian" for many years, was highly commended in the Sports Picture of the Year category in a competition promoted jointly by the Sports Council and the Royal Photographic Society. GRAPEVINE continued .... Good to see ARTHUR PENSTONE jogging again after the operation on one of his achilles tendons. It is very pleasing to see that a new Race Organiser for the Belgrave '20' has stepped forward. DEREK CROOKES, once our Road Running Secretary, is taking over this year so the continuance of our popular event is once more assured. We now have 469 members made up as follows:- 298 Seniors, 35 Juniors, 27 Youths, 72 Boys and 37 Honorary members. Well done LINDA MANNING - only 14 years old and she made over £8 profit sitting for two hours in the cold entrance to our Hall, selling raffle tickets at the Veteran's Southern C.C. Champs. - Made the place look a lot more attractive too. Finally, the most unlikely rumour reached "Grapevine" in mid-February. It seems that someone is spreading the news that MARIANNE DEW and ALAN BLACK have got themselves hitched and that JOHN BICOURT was best man at the occasion. Of course it couldn't possibly be true ....... items.label: March 1974
items.h: WHO KNOWS WHERE WE ARE GOING ?
items.sum: Bill Laws questions the purpose of the President's fund-raising appeal, argues Belgrave's performance has declined, and proposes a wider membership with a ladies section, a rebuilt larger clubhouse, appeal funding and a community-club model.
items.s: WHO KNOWS WHERE WE ARE GOING ? Bill Laws questions the purpose of the President's fund-raising appeal, argues Belgrave's performance has declined, and proposes a wider membership with a ladies section, a rebuilt larger clubhouse, appeal funding and a community-club model. Bill Laws writes:- WHO KNOWS WHERE WE ARE GOING ? I am sure that all active members were delighted at the choice of our current President and awaited with anticipation the first actions from this energetic man. We soon learned that his self-set task for the year was a fund raising appeal and I, like many others, eagerly responded. However, with the first flush of enthusiasm gone, it occurred to me that the reasons for the fund raising were not clear. Perhaps some new scheme, carefully nurtured but still to see the light of day, was afoot. Certainly rumours had been circulating. The rebuilding of Belgrave Hall was mentioned. The possibility of selling the Hall was being considered and even a deal with the local Council involving new facilities at Wimbledon Park track had been hinted at. The possibilities seemed endless and surely our President's appeal must have some direct relation to one of these plans. But no, re-reading the last "Belgravian" made it clear that the fund raising aims were to improve liquidity and [illegible] provide for a building maintenance fund. So perhaps there were to be no new plans, no new building and certainly no fresh appraisal of where we as a club are going and what our targets for the future should be. So what about it? How does Belgrave rate as a club now? Are we satisfied with the way things have gone over the last ten years and do we see any need to establish new aims for the future? I should like to see members from all sections of the Club seriously thinking about these matters and the following should stimulate discussion. During these last few years, which have seen the amalgamation of many clubs, the performance of Belgrave has declined. Fewer trophies, and fewer road and country wins have been the trend. The same old faces have provided stalwart service but where are the new names? We are not attracting and holding enough good youngsters and I believe that we must change our organisation, finances and facilities to compete with many of today's other attractions so here are some proposals:- 1) Widen the membership of the Club. Initiate a ladies section (Yes, I've mentioned the unmentionable). Start a family jogging section and build up a supporters club. Aim for a total membership of several thousand. 2) Re-build, preferably on a larger site, to provide adequate social and recreational facilities for all the groups mentioned above. Provide facilities for additional leisure sports, say table tennis, badminton and squash. 3) Finance these projects initially through an appeal fund but later through increased membership fees and profits from peripheral activities. 4) Make Belgrave a community club and get financial support from local Councils and Government agencies. By now several members will be pouring their second whisky and soda. But let them consider this. We have modified our role before (remember we were once a boxing club) and we can adjust and expand if we have the desire. In my view we must do this to establish ourselves as the premier athletics club. By introducing the joys of running to a much wider range of people we would attract and hold the membership from which new champions would surely emerge. Bill Laws Bill Laws Belgrave Hall Wimbledon Park track

items.sum: Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's report on a quiet winter: a team win in the Belgrave Open, B-team outings at Bexley and Imber Court, and Lawton's 10 km win in New Zealand.
items.s: WALKING Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's report on a quiet winter: a team win in the Belgrave Open, B-team outings at Bexley and Imber Court, and Lawton's 10 km win in New Zealand. WALKING An uneventful winter season has produced no outstanding performances. In fact it has generally been a depleted Belgrave team that has faced the starting line. Our last win was in the Belgrave Open when our Commonwealth Games representatives of Lawton, Callow, Duquemin and Moullin were victorious. Our 'B' team was then left to represent us at the subsequent Bexley and Imber Court races. Out in New Zealand, Carl Lawton won a 10 kilometre event with Alan Callow 3rd and John Moullin 4th, but the main reason for their trip, the 20 miles race at the 'Games' was less productive. items.label: March 1974
items.sum: Report on the four Belgrave walkers in the 20 miles walk at the 10th British Commonwealth Games in Christchurch, New Zealand, in January 1974, with the leading and Belgrave placings.
items.s: BELGRAVE WERE THERE Report on the four Belgrave walkers in the 20 miles walk at the 10th British Commonwealth Games in Christchurch, New Zealand, in January 1974, with the leading and Belgrave placings. BELGRAVE WERE THERE JANUARY 29th 1974 - CHRISTCHURCH, NEW ZEALAND THE TENTH BRITISH COMMONWEALTH GAMES Halfway round the World, Belgrave were well represented in the 10th British Commonwealth Games. The first appearance of our Walkers was in a pre-Games 10 kilometre track event in which they achieved a promising 1, 3, and 4. The 20 miles Walk was held over an out-and-back course with a 5 p.m. start to avoid the worst of the sun, and of the fifteen starters four were Belgravians, with Len Duquemin and John Moullin for Guernsey, Carl Lawton for England and Allan Callow representing the Isle of Man. England's Warhurst and Thorpe led all the way. Allan was in the second group for a while but gradually fell off the back. John Moullin was going steadily until the turn when he found the going extremely tough due to the head wind and the cold. Len Duquemin also suffered but it was Carl Lawton who again faded on the big occasion. He was seventh at the turn in 79:25 but slowed drastically before eventually retiring at 14½ miles. Overall a disappointing result for the Bels but a trip not to be forgotten in a hurry. Other Belgravians making an appearance were Vic Townsend who was 2nd in a veterans race and Dave De Bondi over from Australia to watch. 1. John Warhurst (England) 2:35:23.0 2. Roy Thorpe (England) 2:39:02.2 3. Peter Fullager (Australia) 2:42:08.2 8. ALLAN CALLOW ( ISLE OF MAN) 2:53:12.2 9. LEN DUQUEMIN (GUERNSEY) 2:53:37.4 10. items.label: March 1974
items.sum: Coaching secretary's column on the club's young membership, the winter coaching and weight-training sessions, the application to Merton's Youth Committee and an appeal for volunteer helpers for summer training.
items.s: COACHING Coaching secretary's column on the club's young membership, the winter coaching and weight-training sessions, the application to Merton's Youth Committee and an appeal for volunteer helpers for summer training. COACHING At the last count we had no less than 134 colts, boys, youths and juniors on our books. Of the 335 remaining seniors, no more than a third are active, so with the right efforts we could ensure that the majority of our active members are under 21. What an insurance for the future this would be! However, the under-21's need far more encouragement, attention and coaching than their senior counterparts, for their drop-out rate is higher. There are many senior members in our club who are not committed to the competition programme and who could contribute tremendously to our efforts with the youngsters. A minor committment to assist would be welcome and, I am sure, would give them much satisfaction. So how about it seniors? Give me a "ring" at 660-0480 and let's talk about it. o o o The winter coaching programme got off to a belated start and whilst we have not exactly been over-run with youngsters at least we have established a routine. It is hoped that the future will see no more breaks of contact at the close of the summer season, and that members will appreciate the need to continue through the winter with running and weight training programmes - whatever their event may be. Those who do will have a decided advantage when the next summer season comes around. o o o Friday night is weight night. And thanks to the expertise and enthusiasm of BILL COUZENS and JOHN MARTIN has been a success from the outset. The rate of improvement has been most marked and the lads follow their progress sheet with much interest. To provide variety, short, sharp sessions of handball are played; and circuit training has proved to be very popular. Refreshments at the close are as welcome as any after a hard run! o o o Although our emphasis has been on the Club's Youth in recent months, the seniors are also able to take advantage of the facilities and equipment. With three sets of weights and dumb-bells at the hall, Tuesday evening is fast becoming the senior's weight training night. Once again, BILL COUZENS and JOHN MARTIN are to the fore in setting the pace. o o o Because of our large membership of young athletes the Club has applied for affiliation to the Youth Committee of the London Borough of Merton. Should the Borough decide we are eligible and approve our application, then our membership could well bring us closer still to the Borough's Youth and be of mutual advantage to us both. o o o The track and field season fast approaches and our summer training programmes at Battersea Park and Wimbledon Park tracks will be underway before the next issue of the gazette is published. So once again I appeal for volunteers to assist with these programmes; particularly the Sunday morning sessions. The only qualification needed is a keen interest. We need persons who are prepared to time runners, measure throws or supervise jumps By such modest, helpful beginnings are coaches made. Again, let me know if you are interested. o o o Reproduced on the following page is Belgrave's winter training programme. Much of it will extend into the summer programme, particularly the indoor training Clive Shippen COACHING HON.SECRETARY. Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Coaching Hon. Humorous anecdote about John Bicourt's joke to his wife Val that he would finish his Commonwealth Games race in the nude, and the radio report she later heard about a sensation in the steeplechase. Bicourt threatens to reveal all..... Before leaving for New Zealand and the Commonwealth Games, John Bicourt told his wife Val that if he found himself likely to come last in his race, he would strip off shorts and singlet and finish the race in the nude. "After all", he said,"I could get more publicity from that than from winning any number of races". Imagine Val's consternation when listening to the radio on the day of the race....... "And now we go over to Christchurch, New Zealand to hear the latest on the sensation that occurred in the 3000 metres steeplechase." John Bicourt John Bicourt ran the 3000 metres steeplechase at the 1974 Commonwealth Games, Christchurch Val Bicourt Val John Bicourt's wife Val British Commonwealth Games New Zealand Christchurch

items.sum: Charles Dabbs's tongue-in-cheek report on President Charles Manning's 'Festival of Culture' stag evening at the club HQ, with a comedian, strippers and a ventriloquist.
items.s: The Festival Of Culture Charles Dabbs's tongue-in-cheek report on President Charles Manning's 'Festival of Culture' stag evening at the club HQ, with a comedian, strippers and a ventriloquist. The Festival Of Culture CHARLES DABBS (recently fired from the "Longford Committee") REPORTS:- As I have often been criticized for my infrequent visits to HQ I was grateful to accept the invitation of the well known "impressario" (among other things) and Belgrave President Charles Manning to attend his very discreetly advertized Festival of Culture. Much to my amazement, on arrival at HQ, I discovered that not only were our own sober gentlemen members in attendance but also the intemperate louts from the other local club which changes its name frequently enough for it to elude me! With a delay somewhat similar to that at the start of a cross country race your actual culture commenced. A comedian, speaking mostly in very readily understandable vernacular, related some of his experiences to the discerning audience. At one point the writer, commenting on the intellectual appeal of the material, was verbally attacked but managed to survive. Following the comedian, the audience were considerably shocked by the unexpected naked appearance of the female of our species - not normally seen unattired in our revered HQ. The effect of this arrival, followed by another (the President would not, of course, be satisfied by just one - would he?) was to stir the audience into the edging forward of the chairs, the eyes protruding, etc., etc! Not only two naked females but also a ventriloquist's (that's how it's spelt) dummy with an intelligence way above that of some of the runners (especially those of the other club previously referred to) and almost equal to our own! Eventually, after all the drinking, all the bawdy jokes and all the T's and B's the evening closed as another great Belgrave success. In retrospect, considering the attendance and interest shown, there may well be a future for this type of activity as a regular feature of the revitalized Belgrave Training Programme. Charles Dabbs CHARLES DABBS Charles Manning Charles Manning Belgrave President; organised the Festival of Culture Festival of Culture Belgrave Hall

items.sum: Light-hearted account of the club Barn Dance in February, with the 'Swinging Jock Straps' skiffle group, and thanks to Bill and Gwen Couzens, Mrs. Manning and the bar helpers.
items.s: Barn Dance Frolics Light-hearted account of the club Barn Dance in February, with the 'Swinging Jock Straps' skiffle group, and thanks to Bill and Gwen Couzens, Mrs. Manning and the bar helpers. Barn Dance Frolics The Barn Dance in February was a great success, although what the country dance band thought of our efforts on the floor is probably better left unsaid. "Girls to the centre", the caller would cry out. And into the centre amongst the delicately stepping lady friends and wives would troop the stomping John Martin or John Kelly with all the finesse of a couple of pampas bulls. "Now spin your partner round." Upon which Leo Coy would link arms with Bernard Merry whilst their good ladies could only stand back and laugh helplessly. Only Eve Stimpson and Bob Taylor seemed to be able to get it all together. But seriously, one of the most enjoyable things was to get your arm around a girl's waist once again. Those "rave ups" with everyone waving arms and legs .... continued on page 18 BARN DANCE FROLICS continued ....... and rolling their eyes in time to the beat are all very well but let's face it, it's nice once in a while to dance with someone. The "Swinging Jock Straps", Belgrave's resident skiffle group made another welcome appearance, and their rendition of "My Ol' Man's A Dustman" was enough to make even the most hardened member's eyes come over all misty. Again Bill and Gwen Couzens are owed our gratitude for the arrangements. It takes a lot of hard work to put on an evening such as this. Mrs. Manning, who obviously knows how to feed a hungry athlete, looked after the refreshments, whilst in the bar John Martin did sterling work in ordering the beer, etc., and was ably assisted by Denis MacManus, Jack Carter and Stu. Barrett in the most important job of all - dispensing it to thirsty revellers. In the Surrey Championship we once again secured double honours, Harry Churcher leading the team in his usual style, followed by Charlie, Mac (Dave McMullen) and Bert East. Our nine were fairly well away and could be seen battling for their positions in the field of 273 runners as they ran over the first few hundred yards of slightly uphill parkland. ..... At seven miles Burns (Elswick) had increased his lead to one of over 100 yards from Holden (Tipton) and Dodd (Wirral), who were together. Penny had shaken off some of his opposition and was now sixth. Footer seemed to be gaining places throughout the race, having been about 50th when first noticed and now inside the first twenty. Allum and Taylor were running together, about 25th and altogether we had our six in 48 places, including individual runners. .... The finish came in a torrent of rain with our boys totalling 113 points. Surely, we thought, 113 points is good enough for second team place. Why, this score has won the Championship before now! A hurried enquiry at the Salford dressing room disclosed that they had scored 112 points. 1. Birchfield 88pts; 2. Salford 112pts; 3. items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's appeal for helpers at the Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay at Wimbledon on 6 April, run with the Southern Counties, and for members not to follow the race in cars.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY Gordon Biscoe's appeal for helpers at the Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay at Wimbledon on 6 April, run with the Southern Counties, and for members not to follow the race in cars. ROAD AND COUNTRY On April 6th, in conjunction with the Southern Counties, we shall once again be holding our 12 Stage Road Relay. This is our biggest promotion of the year and in view of this I would like to take the opportunity of making two important requests. Firstly, will anyone who can possibly assist on the day, particularly as a pointsman, etc., please contact me as soon as possible. As will be appreciated, several weeks of effort go into staging and making a race such as this a success. All of this effort could be in vain with say one team going off course on the day. Secondly, over the years we have been continuously faced with the problem of increased traffic on the roads but have so far been very fortunate in having the kind co-operation of the local police. Therefore may I ask all Belgrave members who are present on the day to observe the request printed in the programme. - PLEASE DO NOT FOLLOW THE RACE IN CARS OR CAUSE ANY CONGESTION ON THE ROAD - failure to heed this warning could result in a club being disqualified or even the race being banned - a fate of one road relay already this year! These instructions are issued to all clubs entering the race and as the promoters we must be the first to observe them. So come to Wimbledon and support your team on April 6th (start is at 12 noon) and enjoy this popular event. Gordon Biscoe CROSS COUNTRY & ROAD RUNNING HON. SEC. Gordon Biscoe Gordon Biscoe Cross Country & Road Running Hon. Sec. Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay Wimbledon Southern Counties

items.s: GERRY BACK ON TOP Report and results of a Belgrave handicap race on Wimbledon Common on 1 December 1973, won outright by club captain Gerry North, with L. Morris winning on handicap. GERRY BACK ON TOP DECEMBER 1st 1973 - WIMBLEDON COMMON. In icy conditions it was Gerry North all the way, running at his most aggressive and seemingly oblivious of anything but the path before him leading to victory. Lionel Mann and Jim Rimmer were not far behind him over the first two laps but that last circuit was a real scorcher and our Captain came home with a clear one minute lead. A challenge from Laurie O'Hara did not materialize as almost immediately after the start he pulled up having re-injured a calf muscle. Hopefully it will not be too long before he is back on the scene. Colin Pearson ran most of the race in isolation whilst behind him in 5th place came R. Joicey with a very promising run. BELS. 2ND IN 'SURREY' JANUARY 5th 1974 - GUILDFORD Considerably improving upon last year's performance, the Belgrave team scored a well deserved second place, just edging South London Harriers by two points although a full thirty points down on Hercules Wimbledon. The conditions were atrocious with oceans of mud, a cold wind and even electrified fences to contend with. Our members from north of the Thames have always insisted that the Middlesex race is the toughest on the calendar but even Pat O'Connor, who has now switched his allegiance to Surrey, was heard to utter," The'Middlesex' has never been any worse than this". Gerry North also found it tough but nevertheless it suited him well and he once again qualified for the county team with a splendid run into 5th place. Jim Rimmer, another who has switched to Surrey, this time from Shropshire, ran particularly well to lead in the rest of our team. Teams: 1. Hercules Wimbledon 78pts; 2. BELGRAVE H 108pts; 3. items.s: RIMMER TAKES CLUB '10' Report and results of the Belgrave 10 mile cross country championship at Wimbledon on 19 January 1974, won by James Rimmer, who also took the handicap. A photo of Lionel Mann in the race appears on page 24. RIMMER TAKES CLUB '10' JANUARY 19th 1974 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 10 MILE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMP. A superb run by James Rimmer took him to his first Belgrave Championship over road or country and the handicap prize to boot. He looked impressive over the initial circuit as he took a handy lead from Lionel Mann, with Laurie O'Hara and Colin Pearson strung out behind. Would he hold it though? We all know that Jim is capable of racing with the best but due to injuries and perhaps an occasionally too inhibited approach to his races, he does not always do himself justice. Lionel tenaciously fought back during laps two and three and the pressure was really on Jim as the gap narrowed. However, he was more than equal to the task and strode away with a brisk final lap to win the "Macher Shield" by a convincing margin. Well done James! Colin Pearson again put in the sort of good work that fully deserves a championship medal but 4th place was his lot, and Laurie, after running the Mitcham '15' the previous week, seems to be on the road to recovery after his leg trouble. Leading the 'cyclists' home came Les Morris and another to excel was John Baker who turned in his best ever time for the course. Handicap:- 1. J.Rimmer 55:47; 2. R.Freullett 56:32; 3. items.sum: Obituary of Tom Pritchard, who died aged 66 after 50 years as a Belgrave member, Life Member, Vice President and assistant treasurer.
items.s: Tom Pritchard Obituary of Tom Pritchard, who died aged 66 after 50 years as a Belgrave member, Life Member, Vice President and assistant treasurer. Tom Pritchard It is with great regret that we have to advise the death of Tom Pritchard who passed on at the age of 66 years. Tom joined the Club on the 10th June 1924, and I think he must have been the longest serving active member - 50 years. Tom was never a champion but was known for his enthusiasm which he showed in Open and Club Handicaps, win or lose. He was of a quiet disposition and would never push himself but was ever willing to help others either as Track or Field events official. During the last few years he had taken on the position as Assistant Treasurer. Due to his helpful nature Tom was elected a Life Member and a Vice President and would no doubt have been elected President in the near future. Tom was also a Past President and Life Member of the Veteran's Athletic Club. He will be missed by all. We mourn one who has served the Club well and we offer our condolences to his wife Flo and daughter Jill and son Brian who is a member of Belgrave Harriers. R.I.P. F. R. items.s: O'HARA AND BELS. 1ST Report and results of the National Veterans cross country championships at Great Barr, West Bromwich, on 24 February 1974, where Laurie O'Hara won the Class I title and Belgrave retained the San Sebastian Cup team award, with a page of photos by Al Rockall. O'HARA AND BELS. 1ST FEBRUARY 24th 1974 - WEST BROMWICH - NATIONAL VETERANS C.C. CHAMPS. Belgrave went to the National Veterans Cross Country Championships at Great Barr, West Bromwich, on 24th February as holders of the Class I title (40 - 49). Although the Club has a strong veterans section, only last year's three scorers and John Baker made the trip - but that was good enough for, once again, the Bels returned with the individual trophy and the impressive San Sebastian Cup for the team award. The field was slightly depleted through changes of date and venue, but the Class I field of 140 still contained some tough opposition. Laurie O'Hara, who had shown a slight lapse in form in recent weeks, was out for revenge over his Southern victor, George Brown of Verlea, and both were hard on the tails of the leaders after a fast start. But it was not Brown that Laurie had to fear. New recruit to the ranks Peter Goodfellow of City of Stoke AC was making a determined bid for the title himself and soon found he was in a 20 yards lead. To make matters worse Laurie took a tumble and it was almost two laps gone before he closed on the tall, rangy runner from Stoke. For the final circuit, Laurie just sat 'under the armpit' of the leader and did his famous waiting act and, sure enough, with just 80 yards left he shot to the front for the first, but most important, time. It was a fine victory. Meanwhile, the winner was getting plenty of support. Clive Shippen had moved through after a bad patch and had taken Pat Newall with him, and the two Belgravians steadily consolidated their positions for the rest of the race to finish 9th and 10th. The team score of 20 points was even better than last year's record low of 29. Those with long memories will also be impressed by the Derby line-up which included internationals Peter Wilkinson (13th), Joe Keily (17th) and Ted Matley (45th) but who had to be content with 3rd place on this day. A pity we couldn't have done that when they ran in the English National 10 to 15 years ago! Teams:- 1. BELGRAVE H 20pts; 2. Rochdale H 47pts; 3. Derby & C 75pts; 4. Tipton H 86pts. 1. items.s: THE 'NATIONAL' Report and results of the National cross country championship at Graves Park, Sheffield, on 2 March 1974, Gerry North's last National, with Belgrave's team placing unconfirmed at press time but printed as 1470pts. THE 'NATIONAL' MARCH 2nd 1974 - GRAVES PARK, SHEFFIELD. In what was his last 'National' appearance, our Captain Gerry North still managed to be first Belgravian home although he did not have a very comfortable run. He was hoping for a position inside the first 50 and after the first small lap was lying in the 50 - 60's with John Bicourt in close attendance. Unfortunately, by the end of the second lap he was suffering from stomach cramp and was gradually dropping back. John had by now gone way back down the field, looking as if he would be a lot more comfortable on a tartan track rather than an undulating, snow patched course that was more than a little boggy in the dips. Lionel Mann had a particularly good run as did Leo Coy in his first 'big time' role and with about 600 runners behind him. At the time of going to press we were unable to confirm our team placing but it was certainly well down in the twenties and although this sounds disappointing at first, it must be borne in mind that we were not the only ones to suffer by a long chalk. Coventry Godiva our rivals from the 60's were well down (with our old friend Mel Thorpe still making the team) and Reading and TVH were also out of the first ten. However, it could be the beginning of a lean spell for us on the country, and a time for building up again from scratch. Teams: 1. Derby & County 337pts; 2. Airdale & Spen Valley 376pts; 3. items.s: SURREY X-COUNTRY LEAGUE Review of a disappointing 1973-74 Surrey Cross Country League season, with results of the Croydon, Hayes and Coulsdon matches and the final standings, Belgrave third and Gerry North fifth individually. SURREY X-COUNTRY LEAGUE The Surrey Cross Country League proved to be extremely disappointing this season. In fact we were lucky to finish as highly placed as third overall. Apathy crept in with each successive race and a turn-out, poor enough at Hayes with 14 Bels. at the starting line, became positively nightmarish in the last race at Coulsdon. Here we had the bare 10 men necessary and two of those were second claim members. All right, so we are going through a bad patch but there's no need for it to be this bad. We must not forget the sterling work done by Gerry North however. He turned out in every race and was rewarded with 5th place overall in the individual trophy. NOVEMBER 24th 1973 - CROYDON. items.label: March 1974
items.sum: Account of John Bicourt's fourth place in the 3000 metres steeplechase at the British Commonwealth Games in Christchurch on 26 January 1974, his illness beforehand, his meeting with Arthur Lydiard and his plans.
items.s: BICOURT 4TH IN N.ZEALAND Account of John Bicourt's fourth place in the 3000 metres steeplechase at the British Commonwealth Games in Christchurch on 26 January 1974, his illness beforehand, his meeting with Arthur Lydiard and his plans. BICOURT 4TH IN N.ZEALAND JANUARY 26th 1974 - CHRISTCHURCH, NEW ZEALAND THE TENTH BRITISH COMMONWEALTH GAMES What a line up the Commonwealth Games 3000 metres Steeplechase produced; Benjamin Jipcho the World Record holder, Amos Biwott the Mexico Olympic Champion, Evans Mogaka who was ranked sixth in the World in 1973, and amongst those from these Isles our own John Bicourt who so narrowly missed the British Record last year. John suffered a throat infection at Christmas and it still hadn't cleared up as the 'Games' approached. The team doctor diagnosed the trouble as a touch of bronchitis and with only nine days to the race, advised no running for three to five days! Better prepared was John Davies the Thames Valley Harrier representing Wales. He was lucky enough to spend two weeks in Nairobi over Christmas, getting the sun to his muscles. So the race was on. The Kenyans made the running with the Welshmen Davies and Hayward following. John, not feeling too confident after the doctor's advice, played it safe and kept back down the field. At the half-way mark Biwott was dropping back but our man was still running steadily in seventh place. Running the race of his life, Davies stepped up the pressure with two laps to go. By now John was up with Hayward about 40 metres behind the leaders. Shortly after the 'bell' the incident occurred in which Mogaka and Davies fell, leaving Jipcho to run home comfortably. They were both soon up again and heading hard for the finish but John Bicourt too was now moving really fast, feeling that he had something left in him. He had overtaken Hayward with just over a lap left and by the time the finish was reached there was a margin of six seconds between them. Mogaka, just out of reach, crossed the line in the bronze medal position ahead of him. John wasn't disappointed with the result. How could he be with his second best time, running out of season and with a slight lack of confidence due to the illness. But still, he finished so strongly that he is certain that he could have run a faster time if he had felt more sure of himself early in the race. During the period of dispute that followed, he at no time considered that he would move up into a medal position with the possible disqualification of Davies. As far as John was concerned Davies had run a magnificent race and thoroughly deserved his second place come what may. Thankfully the race positions were upheld. A trip to Mount Cook with Arthur Lydiard made some impression on John who states," He produces the winners so you've got to listen to the man". John's training consists of running a regular 70 miles per week the majority of which is at a steady pace. He has not liked the idea of fast time trials over the flat, feeling that he wants to save it for the races that matter. Lydiard's men, however, may run a trial at 90% of full effort only a week before a major championship, and include infinitely more fartlek type running in their training. Talking with the famous New Zealand coach has influenced John to the extent that he now badly wants to improve his times on the flat over 1500 metres and 5000 metres. His hurdling is acknowledged to be fine and if he can work up some real pace he is convinced that it will give him that bit more edge and the ability to take on and beat the very best. He hopes to run in the Surrey County 5000 metres Championship and if international Norman Morrison, the Scottish athlete with a Surrey qualification, turns out that could be quite a race. John's target now for the 'chase - 8 minutes 20 seconds! 1. Benjamin Jipcho (Kenya) 8:20.8 (Games Record) 2. John Davies (Wales) 8:24.8 (U.K. Record) 3. Evans Mogaka (Kenya) 8:28.6 4. items.s: STEVE WHITE IN FINE FETTLE ! Note that Steve White was third in the 100 metres final at the inaugural City of London Road Races on 6 January, reported by Gordon Doubleday. STEVE WHITE IN FINE FETTLE ! On Sunday 6th January Gordon Doubleday attended the inaugural City of London Road Races, organised jointly by the Road Runners Club, the British Milers Club and the British Sprint Club. Steve White showed terrific winter form with 3rd place in the 100 metres final. He won his heat in 12.0 and then as there was quite a headwind they ran the final in the opposite direction and this time he clocked 11.1. The winner was Steve Green (Kent) in 10.9. Amongst the spectators was veteran sprinter Duncan Maclean still looking very fit at 80+. items.label: March 1974
items.sum: Humorous first-person account by a new member, 'Thumper', of winning the Boxing Day 2 miles handicap at Battersea Park in new Tiger shoes, with an editor's note.
items.s: THE FLYING TIGERS Humorous first-person account by a new member, 'Thumper', of winning the Boxing Day 2 miles handicap at Battersea Park in new Tiger shoes, with an editor's note. THE FLYING TIGERS by Thumper As Battersea Park is almost on my doorstep I was more or less pressed into running the Boxing Day 2 miles by all my mates. So, there I was - new Club vest, baggy track suit bottoms and without a clue as I had only been in the Belgrave Harriers a few weeks and all this was quite new to me. I managed to get hold of an official looking fellow who entered my name and collected my money. He asked me what my handicap was and well, I almost said, "these two legs". After a bit of a haggle I found myself on a line way down the track. Also on the line were two very fit looking types, a young lad with a bandage round his leg and Charlie Manning our beloved President. I still did not really know what was going on except that two miles was a hell of a long way on a Boxing Day. Then I noticed a peculiar phenomenon. All the runners were facing the wrong way. It took me a little while to figure out that I was wrong and I then gently turned myself round (it being the day after Christmas I was still a trifle numb). Well, there was a sort of GO or OFF or something and we were all away at a fair old trot. Now the last time I was on a running track was sports day in "Wings For Victory Week" 1944 but I soon got the hang of it and with six laps to go my feet were thumping quite well. However, it soon became evident that I was building up a terrible oxygen debt. Legs were alright but my breath was pumping in and out in short pants, pyjamas and a scarf. Just when I thought that the Almighty had mis-read the instructions when he made me and had left out a lung or two, the young lad with the bandage dropped out and Charlie dropped back just to see if he was OK and keep him company. Thus there I was running at a fair old totter in the slipstream of the two fit heathens and with about four laps to go. Admittedly we were moving at a good doddle but I was feeling as if my lungs were going to burst although the rest of me was tonking over quite well. I pottered on and then one of the heathens 'packed' leaving two of us all alone in front with half the Club howling on our tails. Two laps left and I gathered up all my strength from mind, body and soul and staggered on 'eyeballs out'. I forgot about breathing and I must have looked a terrible sight judging by the amazed look on the officials' faces as into the last lap I sped. With my famous 'Thames Embankment sprint' I flashed across the finishing line. I did not realise I had won (modesty prevents me from revealing my time). Coughing and spluttering at the finish like an old steam engine that has past its best, I gradually 'came to' and trotted back to the dressing room for a good shower, a light massage and a little powder on my feet. I was soon as good as new. An organiser chap said that I must collect my prize (a very nice glass vase) and I would very much like to thank all those who made the Boxing Day meeting possible. But the best is yet to come, dear readers, for my mother had bought me a pair of lightweight Tiger running shoes for Christmas and I was trying them out for the first time in this race. Hence the title of this story. I must say they do make a difference from running round the streets of London in ex-WD army boots, Zatopek style! Editor's Note: Could this new member be Belgrave's answer to the legendary Wilson and Alf Tupper (Britain's first four minute smiler)? Watch out for future developments. items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Introduction to the renamed 'Young Athletes' section covering AAA 5 Star badges, the new under-20 junior age rule and the section's scope, with photos of Gary Budinger and Simon Holmes. YOUNG ATHLETES Those of you who qualified for a AAA 5 Star badge last year and who have not previously received it, should find it enclosed with this magazine - congratulations once again. As you know, the number of points required for a badge of a certain standard is higher in each age group. Make it your aim this year to at least attain the same level that you did last summer. You are going to have to go faster, higher and longer to do it but with another winter behind you now, there is no reason why you should not even jump up a grade. Some of our Junior athletes are in for a bonus season this year. The AAA Rule regarding age groups has been amended and the upper end of the Junior age group has been extended to under 20 at midnight on December 31st. This brings us into line with the age groups used in European competitions. You may have noticed that the name of this section has been changed to 'Young Athletes' and it will now cover results for our Juniors, Youths and Boys (Senior Boys and Junior Boys). Of couse the older ones amongst you will often be competing in our Senior competitions and these results will be found throughout the rest of the magazine. Two regulars in action this winter past. items.s: Adrian Cook wins Youths Championship Report and result of the club youths cross country championship on Wimbledon Common on 1 December 1973, won outright by Michael Manning, with Adrian Cook (2nd) first boy, as the heading says he won. Adrian Cook wins Youths Championship DECEMBER 1st 1973 - WIMBLEDON COMMON. This race promised to be a 'cracker' with Adrian Cook facing stiff opposition from new members Michael Manning and John Flynn. Unfortunately John came off his motor bike the day before and although he was not hurt, he was shaken and bruised, and understandably left the fight for first place to the other two. When the field reached the Windmill on the outward stretch of the two and a half mile course, Adrian appeared to be breaking away and a mile later after climbing the hill from Queensmere he had a lead of about 20 yards. But now it was Michael's turn. Showing great strength over the final stages he took the lead and held it to the finish. The going was very muddy indeed after torrential rain and some parts of the course looked more suitable for slalom canoe racing. Gary Budinger was at one point seen ploughing along waist deep! items.sum: Obituary of J. (Pat) Parker, Belgrave's 1930s international, Empire Games 3 miles bronze medallist and fourth in the 1937 National.
items.s: Pat Parker Obituary of J. (Pat) Parker, Belgrave's 1930s international, Empire Games 3 miles bronze medallist and fourth in the 1937 National. Pat Parker Older members will be sorry to learn of the recent death of one of our international stars of the 'thirties' J. (Pat) Parker. When he joined us he was already an Empire Games Bronze Medallist (London 1934) at 3 miles. He lived at Brighton yet rarely missed not only the Saturday race or training run but the Tuesday and Thursday training runs from the Rising Sun, Ebury Bridge Road. He was a Sussex County Champion and put up many fine performances for us over the country, on the track and in road relays. Perhaps his best effort for us was when he finished fourth in the 'National' at Stratford Upon Avon in 1937. To him life and running was fun - a great Club Character. G. S. Doubleday J. items.s: COMMENT: TOP CLUB IN SURREY Editorial noting that Peter Matthews' NUTS club rankings placed Belgrave top club in Surrey in 1973, quoting his view on strong clubs, and recording the club's win of the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy at the Surrey County Championships. COMMENT TOP CLUB IN SURREY Each year Peter Matthews of the National Union of Track Statisticians compiles a list of club rankings, calculating positions by scoring the best performance by a first-claim member of a club at each standard track and field event using the I.A.A.F. scoring tables. Last year's list, published in the 'Athletics Weekly' on April 13th 1974 makes interesting reading and shows that we were the top club in Surrey in 1973. Additionally we were placed ahead of all the clubs which contest the Southern League Division I with one unlikely exception, that of Queens Park H., who were in fact relegated to Division II A pointed quote from Mr. Matthews was as follows: "I firmly believe that there are too many clubs in some areas, South London for example, and that the best interest of athletes are best served by strong clubs offering good competition, good training and coaching facilities and good social amenities. Naturally there must be enough clubs to provide competition, but many amalgamations have proved highly successful and there must be scope for more." Our claim to the position of top club has been speedily reinforced this season. In the Surrey County Championships we annexed the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy, awarded to the club scoring most points in the Senior Championships. Peter Matthews Peter Matthews National Union of Track Statisticians; compiles club rankings Peter Matthews Mr. Matthews Charles Peach Charles Peach named in the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy Southern League Surrey County Championships Surrey South London Queens Park H.

items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: Ron Linstead's map of Belgravian competition venues, Bill Lucas as team manager, Harold King's recovery, Ron Langheim seeking old Belgravians, a 1956 Poly Road Relay result, Charlie Smart's recovery, Peter North's Duke of Edinburgh award, the Annual Dinner venue, Gordon Doubleday's return, John Hall in Zambia, promotional T-shirts, Win Shepherd and Mrs. Savage, the 'Bemax' advert, Mrs. Aplin and the Frank Elson Cup, Jim McGrath and Barry Sawyer in Australia, and Denzil Winsborrow. grapevine RON LINSTEAD requests the help of Club members. He intends making a map indicating where Belgravians have competed in various parts of the globe. If you can supply a name, event, venue and date, send it to Ron, c/o Belgrave Hall, Denmark Road, Wimbledon, SW19 4PG. It doesn't have to be of international standard - any Bel, any event, anytime and anywhere. Congratulations to BILL LUCAS who is now on the official list of team managers. His first assignment was as manager to Bernie Plain on his trip to Monza, Italy. One Belgravian always to be seen at Walking events is Hon. Life Member, HAROLD KING. We were particularly pleased to see him at the Club 20 miles Walking Championship as he has recently undergone three operations and has obviously made good progress. In his active days (some forty odd years ago) he was a fine stylist and was Kent County Champion. Nowadays as one of the country's top walking judges, his services are in demand, it is always good to go to a meeting to find some of our older members on the list of officials. Carry on! Harold. If you have any old copies of the "Belgravian" that you no longer require RON LANGHEIM will be pleased to hear from you as he is eager to build up a complete set and is prepared to travel anywhere to pick them up Ron's address is; 1 Cranleigh Road, Feltham, Middlesex. Following the anecdote related in the last edition regarding the member who donated the princely sum of 20p towards the cost of the Belgravian, have you heard of the one who, when approached to buy a programme at our recent 12 Stage Road Relay, declined with the comment, "I've already seen someone else's". A result sheet from way back came to light the other day. It was for the Poly Road Relay, 1956, and amongst the 'B' team were the following:- J. Heathfield 14:31, G. Biscoe 14:25, C. Shippen 15:35. An immediate comment from one of the above was, " What! Vets! It's no good Clive Shippen doing it now, he should have done it then!" We are pleased to report that CHARLIE SMART continues to make progress in his fight back to health and is now managing to take a daily stroll 'round the block' near his home. He will, of course, still be pleased to see anyone who cares to call but rumour has it that he is hoping to build up enough speed training during the coming months to be able to escape quickly out of the backdoor when John Walker appears to deliver one of his famous three hour lectures on his recent training and races! Belated congratulations to PETER NORTH who has gained the Duke of Edinburgh's Silver Award. He is now attempting the Gold Award which involves completing five sections; a residential qualification, where one has to learn to live with others, an expedition, service, physical efficiency involving a series of exercises and interests. Peter's expedition will be to the Lake District where 4 days and 3 nights will be under canvas, and it is no surprise to learn that athletics covers the "interests" section. There will be a change of venue this year for the Annual Club Dinner. It will be held on November 23rd at the "Worcester", directly opposite the railway station, Worcester Park. It was good to see GORDON DOUBLEDAY back in action timekeeping at the Belgrave Road Relay for the first time after his illness, and subsequently getting back into the swing of things again. Our longer distance runners will remember JOHN HALL who moved to Wales some years back. Now he is on the move again and has taken a position as horticultural supervisor for three years in Lusaka, Zambia. CHAS. MANNING would like to point out that the Belgrave promotional T-Shirts are primarily for fund raising and advertising, and they are not approved Club racing strip. WIN SHEPHERD was at her usual place a few weeks ago at the Surrey Women's A.A.A. Championships giving out competitors numbers. We were sorry to learn that her mother, MRS. SAVAGE, was ill last winter, but is now making a recovery and we hope that she will soon be herself again. Older members will recall the enthusiastic help which our two lady Vice Presidents have given us over many years, not forgetting those welcome cups of tea so cheerfully dispensed on wet and cold Saturday afternoons. In April a number of Belgrave boys were involved in the filming of an advertisement for 'Bemax' so watch out for them when the advert reaches T.V. They earned £40 for the Club with their efforts and this will be spent on a vaulting pole and javelins suitable for use by the youngsters. One who never misses the Club 10,000m Walk Championship is MRS. APLIN, and again we were pleased to see her at Battersea Park on May 1st. She was accompanied by Mr. Aplin and after the event she presented the Frank Elson Cup to the winner. It is good to know that through her our links with the Elson family who have done so much for the Club in the past are maintained. In the recent Australian Veterans' Championships the pole vault was won by JIM McGRATH, once our leading field events' exponent. Nice to know that he is still keeping in trim. Another Belgravian, BARRY SAWYER was 5th in the 5,000m at the same meeting. Barry was the man who took up running to get fit for chess and went on to become our Club Record Holder for the marathon. At the recent London Schools Meeting was DENZIL WINSBORROW, an all-rounder for Belgrave in the sixties. Denzil is now teaching in South London but spends his spare time playing cricket for Blackheath. He passes on his best wishes to all. items.label: June 1974
items.sum: President Chas. Manning replies to Bill Laws' article 'Who knows where we are going?', setting out his priorities for Belgrave's future (raising money to enlarge the Headquarters, livelier committees, a ladies section, public relations) and the progress made, including reaching the £500 financial target.
items.s: TALK'S CHEAP! President Chas. Manning replies to Bill Laws' article 'Who knows where we are going?', setting out his priorities for Belgrave's future (raising money to enlarge the Headquarters, livelier committees, a ladies section, public relations) and the progress made, including reaching the £500 financial target. In our last issue BILL LAWS wrote:- WHO KNOWS WHERE WE ARE GOING ? ... and in typical succint and diplomatic style the President answers "TALK'S CHEAP!" I'm sorry the first flush of enthusiasm has waned - honeymoons (so we are told) are invariably a disappointment and confirm that anticipation is better than realization. However, let's consider the points made. Firstly, when I took office I deliberately avoided saying, "I want you to win the National", or, "Bring back three trophies", or, "More effort - train harder - get some team spirit", etc., etc. Why? Because; a) I'm a weak athlete and appreciate that what I ask is beyond me; and b) athletes are fundamentally selfish - this is particularly true of the better class ones who train and compete with a savage intensity for self gratification and if the club benefits it is a spin-off from their personal accomplishments - one can't and mustn't condemn this attitude because this is how champions are made, and when you have your champions in a team you're in the medals. So, with our efficient sectional secretaries I could safely leave the athletes but what was I personally to do? The planting of trees, laying foundation stones, starting a race or presenting prizes was to me so much dross. What really mattered was, what will Belgrave Harriers be in five or ten years time? I don't want to upset the status quo. You read in this mag. "25 Years Ago - 40 Years Ago" - it's not a lot different from today (except that with only 273 runners in the National in 1934 I'm not suprised our runners did well! what?). Time and tide wait for no man and we should guide Belgrave progressively on in the direction we want it to go, if not, events could overtake us. For instance, what if the Borough of Merton built a tartan track - who will be given the right to lease? Councillors, J.P.'s are concerned with Civic Pride - sympathetic approval is already evident with certain other clubs. Our voice must be heard. Again, how are we to compete at National levels with a surfeit of clubs like Ranelagh, Thames Hare & Hounds, Mitcham AC, Sutton & Cheam, Epsom & Ewell, Hercules Wimbledon, Herne Hill, etc. all vying for members? The result is a dilution of talent. Birchfield, Coventry, Cardiff, Aldershot, Wolverhampton, etc. are basically one club towns - the inference is obvious. Therefore the way seemed clear and what mattered most was the future. Having decided what the priority was, one had to investigate the peripheral activities that would further that aim. Thus:- Raise money - it has to be a practical, attainable amount but one which will noticeably swell our funds. The object of more money is to substantially improve our facilities for athletes. This would encourage new members. The form it should take would be to increase the floor area to give a) a more suitable environment for all our activities - changing, training gymnasium, social, administration - whilst b) providing an independant area for letting. (You don't take a sledge hammer to crack a nut and conversely you don't say the Presidential appeal is to build a second floor in our Headquarters - but just hope that it will help.) Committee Arthur Bruce says," The decisions of a committee are the sum total of its fears". And, "A camel is a horse designed by a committee". This of course is not really true but decisions have to be taken and made positive. They may not be popular but rather that than, "reporting back at the next meeting - " which can become an interminably frustrating process. Try to generate more dynamic thinking and break down the lethargic stereotyped habits. Ladies - consider seriously a section which might range from young ones competing to their more mature sisters in official positions (no, seriously) supporting juniors, catering, etc. Public Relations - project the club to a wider audience via the press, radio and public shows. Well, what progress have we made? In the political field we have established who we are, what we are, and where we are going. We have talked to the Mayor, to Councillors, heads of local government departments. We have our representatives on the Surrey and Middlesex A.A.A. Committees. Discussions on the enlargement of the club are taking place. The promoting of the name of our club is in progress - not as fast as I'd like, partly I think our own fault and also through certain partisan activities by a person known to many of us! The question of a Ladies Section has been mentioned and no doubt will be considered further. Committees have not been all sweetness and light but decisions have been made and acted upon. The financial target was set for £500. Not easy, not easy at all but it is now a fait accompli although the pressure's STILL ON! Thinking. Alan Mead, by putting himself out, thought of a way of saving the club a possible £150. Ron Langheim, on an exciting modification to one of our races which would have been extremely popular, although inadvisable at the moment. Neither of their ideas were used - but they did think. And now Bill Laws writing, having given considerable thought to the subject Great! So, Bill, instead of leaving them as castles in the air, what can you do to make them facts ? CHAS. items.label: June 1974
items.sum: Report and full A and B string results of Belgrave's narrow win in Southern League match one at Sutcliffe Park on May 11th 1974, highlighted by Martin Scott's two wins over Herne Hill's Wayne Tarquini in the 400m and 4 x 400m.
items.s: FIRST LEAGUE MATCH WON Report and full A and B string results of Belgrave's narrow win in Southern League match one at Sutcliffe Park on May 11th 1974, highlighted by Martin Scott's two wins over Herne Hill's Wayne Tarquini in the 400m and 4 x 400m. FIRST LEAGUE MATCH WON MAY 11th 1974 - SUTCLIFFE PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH ONE. We could so easily have lost this first match in the Southern League thereby immediately dashing our hopes of reaching the qualifying competition for the National League in 1974. It is ironic that in our club where the majority of active members are middle and long distance runners, we have the greatest difficulty in turning out a good team in the longer track races and of our more established runners only big-hearted Laurie O'Hara heeded the call, and this after doing shift work all through the previous night. Most outstanding for Belgrave was Martin Scott who came up against another remarkable Junior in the 400m, Herne Hill's Wayne Tarquini, the self styled "whizz-kid from outer space". Martin was drawn in the outside lane but held his nerve when his rival closed to his shoulder down the back stretch and then kicked away off the final bend into the howling gale. that blew up the finishing straight throughout the meeting. His time was worth well under 50 seconds in normal conditions. That wind killed any ideas of pacemaking in the longer races and lap times were often reduced to a dawdle. We picked up some good points on the field where although we were short handed, luck was with us for a change. Bill Couzens and an injured John Martin backed up our mainstay "Snowy" Brooks in the throws and kept the score moving along nicely. A pleasing personal best came from Reg. Hopkins in the Pole Vault, and Arnold Bentt and Reg. teamed up together again in the short hurdles and the High Jump. We rely heavily upon these two willing characters. It is in the sprints, however, that we are at our most powerful, Steve White's flowing movement contrasting with Mick Marshall's power-house action but both with the same effect. When it came to the relays the points position was critical with Herne Hill Harriers breathing down our necks. Superb baton changing from Mick to Charlie Gillett and on to Steve gave us a comfortable win in the 4 x 100m and now, as so often in these meetings, the overall result depended on the 4 x 400m. Reg. Hopkins in his 5th event of the day opened for us and brought us to the first take-over in 3rd spot behind our red and black clad rivals. Making a welcome appearance over one lap was Steve White who cruised round in a stylish 52 seconds, getting the feel of the distance, and confessing later to having had several seconds in hand. Steve pulled us right up and Philip Gee gave another "gutty" performance, fighting to keep us in a good position so that the sting in our tail, Martin Scott, would be all set for another clash with Tarquini. Martin immediately went to the front but ran steadily, holding back as much as possible, knowing he could outsprint the other man in the final stretch. Neck and neck they hit the straight and for the second time in the afternoon our man carried Belgrave's colours to the tape. The match was ours, albeit with the lowest winning score of the day throughout the South. Match Result: 1. BELGRAVE H 122pts; 2. Herne Hill H 115pts; 3. Epsom & Ewell H 103½pts; 4. items.sum: Report and Belgrave results from the Surrey Championships at Motspur Park on May 14th/16th/18th 1974, where Reg Hopkins' points helped Belgrave win the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy.
items.s: SURREY CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and Belgrave results from the Surrey Championships at Motspur Park on May 14th/16th/18th 1974, where Reg Hopkins' points helped Belgrave win the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy. SURREY CHAMPIONSHIPS MAY 14th/16th/18th 1974 - MOTSPUR PARK This was a "Surrey" to remind one of the vintage years of the late fifties and early sixties. There was glorious weather, a reasonable standard of competition, and a Belgravian in every Senior track final. The rabble of Bels. sitting on the grassy slopes overlooking the back straight took in the sunlight on bared chests, sank the odd ale, and generally enjoyed themselves. Reg. Hopkins, Surrey Decathlon Champion already, had a busy day. During the heats he drastically improved his best 400m time and qualified for the final but on the Saturday he was not quite at his best. To add insult to injury, he was knocked out of the final six in the Long Jump by club mate Steve Crosbie who chose this occasion to up his best ever distance. However, it was due mainly to Reg that we won the Charles Peach Memorial Trophy for the club scoring most points in the Championships. Mick Marshall narrowly beat Charlie Gillett in a tight 200m, having gained 3rd in the 100m and Philip Gee was at his most aggressive, tearing out that first 200m in the one lap event and hanging on to gain a medal. In the middle distances Colin Pearson improved his best 1500m time and Danny Wiseman recorded an impressive 1:54.7 in the 800m heat only to find that the 'snap' had gone when it came to the final. John Bicourt's 5000m bid seemed to be going well until the last few laps when a rapid acceleration by the leaders left him stranded. 100m: 3. M.Marshall 11.4; 5. P.Williamson 12.4. 200m: 2. items.s: STEVE WHITE~10.6/21.2! Note on Steve White's wind-assisted 10.6 100m and 21.2 200m in the 100th Oxford v Cambridge match and his 7.19m long jump for the Southern Counties. STEVE WHITE~10.6/21.2! Superfast times came from Steve White in the 100th Oxford v Cambridge match on May 16th at West London, and it was nice to read in the paper next morning: "White is Oxford's hero". Unfortunately a strong following wind made the times invalid for record purposes but he surely must be on the verge of reducing his legal personal bests. He took the 100m in 10.6, the 200m in 21.2, the Long Jump with a leap of 5.82 and was a member of the winning 4 x 100m team. On Sunday 2nd June, the day after he had turned out for Belgrave in four events in a league match, he improved his best Long Jump for the year with 7.19m whilst representing the Southern Counties. items.s: O'Hara wins Club 10,000m Report and result of the Belgrave 10,000m club championship at Battersea Park on May 22nd 1974, won again by Laurie O'Hara from Lionel Mann, with Leo Coy taking bronze. O'Hara wins Club 10,000m MAY 22nd 1974 - BATTERSEA PARK - 10,000m CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP. It's easy to say that once again Laurie O'Hara beat Lionel Mann to retain the Club Championship over 10,000m but that statement simply does not do justice to either man. Nor does it tell of the pain that both suffer as one tries to break the other until, as usual on that 25th lap, Laurie's final burst prevails. The battle for the bronze was most interesting. It was a four way contest between Dougs. Jardine and Maughan, Leo Coy and Clive Shippen. They kept within a couple of yards of each other until half-way when Leo, suffering from stitch, dropped back by some 30 - 40 metres. Doug. Jardine now took up the running from Doug. Maughan and the laps gradually reeled off. Suddenly, Leo was catching them again and with six to go they were all together once more. Now Doug. Jardine tailed back for good and as the last few circuits were approached an exciting finish was promised. The pace slowly rose but Leo clung on to the other two until at the classic 300m mark he was away. It was a good run to celebrate his birthday but that third place medal was no gift, he had to work for it. 1st Class Standards: O'Hara, Mann. 2nd Class Standards: Coy, Shippen, Maughan. 1. items.label: June 1974
items.sum: Humorous boxed anecdote about starter Ron Langheim's troubled afternoon starting the Boys' races at Wimbledon, ending when he shot himself in the hand.
items.s: Humorous boxed anecdote about starter Ron Langheim's troubled afternoon starting the Boys' races at Wimbledon, ending when he shot himself in the hand. After a dismal debut at the "Dukes" Ron Langheim turned up at Wimbledon to start the Boys' races. His initial "To your marks - Get set" was followed by, well, nothing. The guns hadn't been cocked or something. And when the judges did hear his whistle, the timekeepers didn't. However, after a while the whole thing began to gel and Ron was improving all the time. Until the last race, when for some reason or other he shot himself. Looking at his pretty wife I couldn't see the logic in this, and as he made his crimson way to the stand someone shouted,"Get off the track!". His own comment after two injections and twelve stitches in his hand, "I'll be the laughing stock of Belgrave", which of course is nonsense. As someone pointed out, he can always use the other hand. C.E.M. Ron Langheim Ron Langheim starter for Boys' races at Wimbledon; injured his hand with the starting pistol Ron Langheim Ron C.E.M. C.E.M. initials match the President, C. E. Manning Wimbledon

items.s: TOUGH GOING IN ESSEX Report and A and B string results of the second Southern League meeting at Mayesbrook Park, Essex, on June 1st 1974, where Belgrave finished second to Essex Beagles. TOUGH GOING IN ESSEX JUNE 1st 1974 - MAYESBROOK PARK.,ESSEX. Our team for the second league meeting was stronger than the one we took to Sutcliffe Park so there was every hope of another win. Unfortunately the opposition was stronger too and instead of winning we were pushed down into second place by Essex Beagles. Even our ever reliable Steve White was forced to accept a couple of second places, a most unusual occurrence, and this in spite of producing a noteworthy 10.9/21.9 . Two welcome newcomers to the team were Peter Crosbie and Paul Whitby. Peter, a Youth, produced some good throwing in the Javelin and with 45.47m reached 3rd place in the 'A' event. Paul, who comes from Sussex and has only just joined the Club, clocked a snappy 16.3 in the high hurdles, a time which he will almost certainly be trimming down some more this summer. The 4 x 100m relay squad chalked up an impressive win in 43.4, beating the second team by well over 10 metres and running in a way that augurs well for the championship relays later in the season. Another good point for us was the form shown by Cliff Brooks (wearing his hair in fashionable braids), gradually returning to peak fitness. We had two double wins in the Long Jump and the 400m. With Steve White and Martin Scott in the Long Jump we have a duo capable of taking on anyone, and Martin also figured in the other double, this time with Philip Gee as a partner. But with only two other winners, Charlie Gillett and Mick Marshall, we were not good enough to hold the Essex Club. We can only pride ourselves on seeing how obviously pleased these clubs are when they do manage to defeat Belgrave. Match Result: 1. Essex Beagles 136pts; 2. BELGRAVE H 118pts; 3. items.s: Boxed note on Belgravians at the Inter-Regional Championships at Crystal Palace on May 26th/27th 1974, including wins for Carl Lawton and John Bicourt for Surrey and 2nd-claim member Chris Barber's illness-hit mile. We were well represented in the Inter-Regional Championships at Crystal Palace on May 26th/27th. Carl Lawton (46:07.8) in the 10,000m walk and John Bicourt (8:36.6) in the Steeplechase both won for Surrey. Now representing Berkshire Steve White ran in the 100m heats (11.1) and was 6th in the 200m final (22.2). In the Long Jump Martin Scott (6.76) finished 10th for the North Eastern Counties. We also had an interest in the 1mile where Chris Barber, one of our 2nd-claim members qualified for the final with 4:05.5, beating the eventual winner Dave Black in the process. Suffering from a bad cold he was forced to pull out in the final, and finished the day up in bed. Incidentally, Chris has clocked 1:53.6 for 800m this season as well - couldn't we do with that talent. items.s: WALKING Carl Lawton's walking notes marking Allan Callow's departure for New Zealand, lamenting weak turn-outs by younger walkers, and noting the regaining of the National 10 miles and Met. 20 kilos titles. WALKING Where have all the flowers gone? This issue of the "Belgravian" coincides with the departure of Allan Callow for New Zealand, to the land that attracted him a few months ago. Since his arrival from the Isle of Man in 1971 Allan has been prominent in many of our competitions including our winning National teams and we regret that he is to leave us at a time when we are slightly on the weak side Our weakness at present appears to be based on the failure of our younger members to persevere when the going is a bit hard. Success will seldom if ever come immediately but a little sustained effort could well produce the results in time. There is also the problem that Walking is very much an individual sport in the sense that members are spaced over wide areas and find it difficult to get together for training. However, with the arrival of the summer one hopes that the tide will turn and that those in hibernation will reappear. Some of our turn-outs in races over the past few months have been disappointing especially in the 10k and 20mile Club championships. The lighter side of the issue has been the regaining of both the National 10 miles, on which Harry Shields reports, and the Met. 20 kilos. Johnathan Dunsford has been continuing his consistant performances including a win in Eire in an inter-club meeting. Our schoolboys have all succeeded in reaching the All-England Schools meeting, results of which will appear later. items.s: BELS. WIN NATIONAL '10' Harry Shields' report of Belgrave winning the team title at the R.W.A. National 10 mile walk championship at Whetstone, Leicester, on March 16th 1974, led home by Allan Callow, with Belgrave results. BELS. WIN NATIONAL '10' MARCH 16th 1974 - WHETSTONE, LEICESTER - R.W.A. NATIONAL 10 MILE CHAMP. When I arrived home at midnight, I was greeted by my wife with the time hallowed words, " What sort of day have you had?" There is only one answer. A day spent with Jack and Joan Goswell, the company of our walkers, the knowledge that Belgrave had played its full part, administratively and in active participation, adds up to one thing - complete satisfaction. What an amazing record we have in this Championship since its inception 28 years ago. Champions 11 times and placed 11 times. No other club nears this unique performance and again this was to prove no exception While watching the race my impression was we had been beaten, so imagine my elation when working out the results to hear Jack suddenly say, "We have won!". Reviewing the result sheet shows "superb packing again bore its fruit" Too much praise cannot be given to Allan Callow for leading our team to victory, ably supported by his team mates John Moullin, Ray Middleton and Carl Lawton. Carl, the captain, had recently had leg trouble and it was his determination over the last two miles that ultimately gave victory. The forward walking of John Hall must give him great satisfaction while Dave McMullen, who took part in the first Championship, can only be described as a phenomenon. HARRY SHIELDS Teams:1. items.sum: J. V. Baker's point-by-point reply to Bill Laws' article on widening membership, rebuilding, an appeal fund and council support, urging members to show club spirit.
items.s: In Reply To Bill Laws J. V. Baker's point-by-point reply to Bill Laws' article on widening membership, rebuilding, an appeal fund and council support, urging members to show club spirit. In Reply To Bill Laws No doubt some members who read Bill Laws' article will have said to themselves, "He's right you know". I would suggest that Bill attends Belgrave Hall for training sessions and involves himself in Club affairs. I will comment on the main points of the article. 1. Widen the membership. To encourage new membership, Gordon Biscoe and myself this winter alone have officiated at the City Police Relay, Police and Inter-Services C.C. Race and a cross country race for cyclists. Others also help and we had good support at the Ravensbury Park and Merton Shows. I might add it is no good encouraging people to join the Club if they should arrive at Belgrave Hall for training and find only a few old members like myself present. Members must be prepared to show Club spirit and help youngsters and new-comers. 2. Re-build. I doubt if we could afford a larger site at todays prices. We do own the freehold of our present site and can improve our premises which are already better than any other club owned HQ I have visited round the country. 3. Finance through an appeal fund. This financial year already the sum of £129 has been donated and this does not include the President's Appeal Fund. 4. Get support from the Council. What negative thinking. It's just as well past members did not sit back and wait for something to fall into their laps. Unfortunately there are a number of Bill Laws in the Club, continually saying, "If only THEY would do so and so!" J.V.BAKER J. V. Baker J.V.BAKER Hon.
