items.s: NATIONAL 20 MILES Report and results of the National 20 miles walk at Redditch on 15 June 1974, run in oppressive heat and won by R.Thorpe of Sheffield, with Belgrave 6th team; it recalls Belgrave's 13 team wins in the championship and the Nijmegen Shield. JUNE 15th 1974 - REDDITCH. The day was oppressively warm with the sun breaking through to full strength for the last 90 minutes of the race, making it wonderful for supporters but one of extreme difficulty for the competitors. The strength sapping humidity and deceivingly difficult course lured many to over-reach and fall by the wayside, including our own Carl Lawton from whom we have come to expect so much. Ray Middleton with his vast experience gave his usual sterling performance while Ray Hall, but a shadow of his old self, showed it was possible to work through the field and achieve a respectable position. John Moullin, John Dunsford and Dave King who made up our scoring team deserve praise but to win the 'Blue Riband', the oldest of the Road Walking Championships requires an utter dedication to training and team work. It is a subject for discussion and reflection on 'How best achieved under present conditions'. It is possibly nostalgia but I recall we have won this team championship 13 times and placed 26 times since the inception 55 years ago of this 20 miles National competition and my feelings yearn for a return to the fitness and comradeship which resulted from the Saturday training sessions round Richmond Park, the laps of the Bridges from Battersea Park, during the mid-week and all-day strolls on a Sunday. In addition to the four-a-side Championship the 'Nijmegen Shield' for the first club to finish eight men is an important feature of this National 20 miles Championship continued ..... event and for many years it was a foregone conclusion that we would win this coveted award. Alas, it is many years since we were able to argue who would take it home, or finish a complete team. Enough of looking back. Sincere thanks to the Midland Counties for an extremely well organised Championship and to our own officials who travelled to Redditch and played a major role as recorders and judges. Teams: 1. items.s: NATIONAL 50km - BELS. 2nd Report and results of the R.W.A. National 50 km walk at Hendon on 20 July 1974 on a course devised by Ray Middleton from Copthall Stadium, with Belgrave second team behind Sheffield. JULY 20th 1974 - HENDON - R.W.A. NATIONAL 50 Km. The Championship was the responsibility of the Southern Area of the R.W.A., and any who have ever assisted in finding a good, safe, sporting course with easy travelling facilities for competitors from all parts of the country, with all the refreshments and other needs required for a race of over 30 miles, will know how formidible was the task. In no small part the original thinking of Ray Middleton devised a 10 lap course from Copthall Stadium, Hendon which amply met these requirements and enabled spectators, attendants and competitors to give of their best to achieve individual and team honours. My own observation is that the venue has great possibilities for events of a similar nature. The day was warm and Carl Lawton sensible to his responsibilities started steadily, moving in that immaculate easy style that at 20 miles one could picture him going to the front. This was not to be, fatigue suddenly struck him and the last two laps were an illustration of his doggedness to finish and complete our team. As for so many years Ray Middleton came through to lead our team home and with John Moullin and Dave King we finished an honourable second. The energy of the whole Middleton family must be commented on. Their name is synonymous with "Belgrave Harriers". Jean and her daughters organised raffles which I understand more or less covered the costs of the championship and few people realise the work they do. Congratulations. Teams: 1. Sheffield 43pts; 2. items.s: Ray Middleton wins Hastings to Brighton Report and results of the Hastings to Brighton 38-mile walk on 10 August 1974, walked through storms, in which Ray Middleton overtook Carl Lawton to win and Belgrave won the team race; the byline is the credit line printed on page 18. AUGUST 10th 1974 - HASTINGS. The weather forecast was showers or longer outbreaks of rain, thunder at times, gale force gusts of winds from the West, with sunny intervals. How right they were. The fight of competitors along Hastings front to start the 38 miles trek. Thunder, lightning, torrential rain at about 14 miles, then in line with the famous nursery rhyme, "Out came the sunshine", when the South Downs and the countryside displayed all the beauty and lushness which makes one say "This England". Through-out our men fought the elements and at 20 miles had clearly established themselves, leading in the individual and team championship. A further check between Lewes and Falmer showed Carl Lawton with an 100 yards advantage over Ray Middleton, with Carl Walking with fine style and and confidence of the champion that we know he is. Both had a five minutes lead over the next man. Our team was well placed. How surprised on arriving at Brighton to find Ray had beaten Carl by over two minutes. Ray's record over the past 10 - 20 years is awesome, astounding and must be unsurpassed in Club history. Congratulations to the remainder of the team. Teams: 1. BELGRAVE H 13pts; 2. items.s: A word from your Treasurer- The Hon. Treasurer thanks prompt subscription payers, chases those still owing, asks for help with fund raising, warns of a possible £6 minimum subscription and urges members to attend the A.G.M. This issue may not appear until after the A.G.M. so it is impossible to forecast whether I will still be treasurer. I would like to thank those who pay their subscriptions promptly and I hope the members who still owed last year's have now paid up as this will save my time and club money in sending out reminders. The subscription rate is low despite increases in everything we use. I hope members remembered this and responded well to the request for bottles for the stall at the Merton Show on August Bank Holiday Monday. If you did forget, try to sell as many A.A.A. draw tickets as you can. Should fund raising come to a stop I will ask the Committee to consider £6 per year as a minimum subscription so it's up to you. If you do not attend the A.G.M. it will be no use moaning to me about any decisions which are taken. Your voice can be heard at the A.G.M. so use it there, not in the pub afterwards. John Baker JOHN BAKER Hon. Treasurer Belgrave Harriers A.G.M. Merton Show Merton

items.label: September 1974
items.h: from the 'belgravian' 25 years ago ... and 40 years ago
items.sum: Reprints from the magazine 25 and 40 years earlier: the 1949 London to Brighton walk, where Jack Bidgood finished 9th to become club long-distance champion, and the November 1934 'Crazy Cabaret' social with Tom Cotton and the 'Seven Belgrave Sisters'.
items.s: from the 'belgravian' 25 years ago ... and 40 years ago Reprints from the magazine 25 and 40 years earlier: the 1949 London to Brighton walk, where Jack Bidgood finished 9th to become club long-distance champion, and the November 1934 'Crazy Cabaret' social with Tom Cotton and the 'Seven Belgrave Sisters'. SEPTEMBER 10th 1949 In the London to Brighton walk on September 10th, eleven of our walkers started off on the stroke of Big Ben at seven o'clock, to be joined later by a number of supporters. In the early stages, Jack Bidgood Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away. Gordon Doubleday, F.Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at Chequers Horley was in 9th position. A check at Crawley (29¾ miles) showed that our men had held their positions with the exception of Jack Wakeley who had stopped for a massage. By the time Bolney was reached, Jack Bidgood had improved his position to 7th, Clayton was 16th, Baker 21st and Wilson 27th. With the retirement of Bert Martineau from the Surrey team there seemed a chance that our team would be placed and although Jack Bidgood dropped a couple of places to go back to 9th, Joe Wilson moved up to 23rd and at the finish our positions were: Jack Bidgood 9th; Bert Clayton 16th; Joe Wilson 21st; Jack Baker 23rd making a score of 62 points and just losing us the third position. So Jack Bidgood became our long-distance champion as well as holder of the 20 miles Championship. He's a champion to be proud of. His judgement of pace and unflagging stamina throughout the race set a fine example. Bert Clayton was a worthy second and showed his grit in overcoming tiredness in the last few miles. Joe Wilson walked his best Brighton to date and came along in fine style in the latter half to finish remarkably fresh. Jack Baker pluckily stuck it out over the last half to complete the team. and 40 years ago NOVEMBER 1934 - CRAZY CABARET. The second Social of the Season was held on November 3rd, and was well supported by our guests, Croydon H., Epsom H., and Mitcham A.C., supplemented by the ladies who had been running from the Windmill during the afternoon. No doubt the advertised Crazy Cabaret, produced by Tom Cotton and trained by Miss Jo Parsons, was one of the attractions, and accounted for the really fine crowd which assembled. The versatile talent among the Bels. is outstanding! Among the performers were several who have delighted us before, including Tom Cotton, Florrie Footer (once again in the role of Princess Charming), and our old friends Castor and Oil, who again left us without a leg to stand on. The curtain rose at 9 pm with Miss Gladys Bailey singing "Over My Shoulder", which served to introduce us to "The Seven Belgrave Sisters" (including sylph-like Sidney and Harley, the original Harlequin) in a singing and dancing act which was well received. Then followed Castor and Oil (alias T.Carter and P.Donnelly, or vice versa. Which is vice and vich is versa, I'll leave you to guess). Their act was very moving. Tom, girlishly garbed in a shimmering creation of russet and gold which displayed her form (or that which he used in lieu of) to advantage, and with lovelight in her eyes, although a trifle haughty as becomes such a queenly figure, was soon swept off her feet by the advances of Paddy, all sackcloth and gnashes. Eventually her feminine charm, plus a half-nelson, brought the debonair swain grovelling at her feet, only to be left flat for his pains! Curtain, amidst tremendous applause. The ballet opened with Tom Cotton singing....... .....Love in Bloom appeared from the flower pot in the form of Footer in a blonde wig, garlanded with yellow pansies and little else. Around the hall he scampered, followed by the corps-de-ballet, spraying the audience with sweet scents and Mitcham Lavender........ Altogether a most successful show! items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Report on the club's Youths Medal Competition, won by Peter Crosbie with maximum points, and the Boys Competition for the Mrs. L. Ryan Cup, won narrowly by Simon Shanks from Martin Munro, with points tables for both. The Youths Medal Competition was neatly sewn up by Peter Crosbie who warily steered clear of the long track races but scored heavily in the field and sprint events to pick up the maximum 100 points for five events. Paul Warren and Danny Richards provided the other medallists with Adrian Cook and David Didino not competing in the necessary five events but nevertheless putting up some good performances. This year's Boys Competition for the Mrs. L. Ryan Cup turned out to be the most exciting on record. With no less than 45 boys taking part it was a major achievement to score in the necessary five events. When the day for the last three events arrived everything was set for a close finish. Mark Shippen, the leader after five events, was unable to improve any more as he was away on holiday; Martin Munro who scored max. points on the first two events and was then unable to attend for the next three was back in contention; Simon Shanks had scored well in three events but now desperately needed two more good scores; Ivan Beaumont, older than most of the others and therefore suffering with a lot less handicap allowance; all were pushing for the lead. The 1,500 metres was Simon's strong point and he scored well, finishing just behind Tony Pilcher and new member J.Heath. Ivan Beaumont leapt a tremendous 15'10" to win the long jump outright and also gained 2nd in the high jump but was it enough? All the time Martin Munro was creeping up with really solid all-round performances. Working out all the scores for such a close competition was a real headache and after checking and re-checking, Simon Shanks was declared the winner, only 1½ points ahead of Martin Munro who was in turn 5½ up on Ivan Beaumont. The medal for the best score outside the first three in all eight events was won by Stephen Fletcher with a tough all-round performance and not so far behind him came Andrew Byrne who won a special medal. Andrew has improved dramatically in the last twelve months, proving that no matter how far behind you are now, determination plus the strength you gain each year can make all the difference. The losers today can be tomorrow's winners. A final word of congratulation must go to those mighty "micro-colts" who competed so doggedly against boys considerably older than themselves - David Hicks, David Worley, Andrew Vallance and not forgetting Philip Headley who at eight years old and with only the same allowance as twelve year olds finished a magnificent 4th in the 1,500 metres with an actual time of 5 minutes 48 seconds! 1. items.s: MEET ANTHONY PILCHER Profile of 12-year-old new member Tony Pilcher, who set a new junior boys 800 metres club record and equalled the 1,500 metre record within months of joining, with a photograph of him winning. A youngster who has started his athletics with a bang is 12 year old Tony Pilcher. Tony has only been running for a couple of months, having joined the Club after a visit to one of our jumble sales, but already he has set new figures for the junior boys 800 metres and has equalled the 1,500 metre record. His best 800 metre run came in the Brighton young athletes meeting where he burst from the pack with well over half a lap to go and then kept it up to the finish to win in 2:31.4. This scorching finish has become his trademark and it is a surprise to hear him say, "I don't like 800 metres, it's too far. I really like the 100 metres." Tony goes to Bushey School at Raynes Park. He gets plenty of sporting encouragement at home from his father, Reg., a keen veteran cyclist who competes for the 29th Wheelers based in Tooting. Reg. has become a most welcome helper when it comes to measuring long jumps etc. At the moment Tony trains once a week on Sundays at Wimbledon Park. This coming winter he hopes to attend the Friday night sessions at Belgrave Hall as well as continuing his other sporting interest - football. He plays little league football for the Barclay Savers and Oakway teams. items.s: 5 STAR AWARDS Notice on the AAA 5 star award scheme for the club's boys, with six five-star members this season, how to order badges from Leo Coy, and the star ratings by age group (the Under 14 list is printed twice, the first incomplete). Once again the track season draws to a close, and as last year times and distances have been checked against the magic 5 star chart and converted to points. Last year we had two 5 star members. This year, with months of training behind them, the improvement in our lads' performances is apparent and we can boast six who have gained the coveted five star badge. It should be remembered that the points are scored by taking a boy's best three events during the season (one field event and two track or vice versa) Metal coat badges or cloth badges suitable for sewing on to a track suit (as shown above) are available at 25 pence each, and whether you have attained a 1 star badge or a 5 star badge Belgrave is proud of you. Keep at it through the winter and maybe you can achieve the next grade up in 1975. Write to Leo Coy and enclose a 25 pence postal order if you wish to obtain your badge and if you just want the free certificate that goes with it, or you have any enquiries, write to him anyway. Leo's address is 40, JEDBURGH STREET, LONDON S.W.11. He looks forward to hearing from you. items.sum: Report on the Belgrave Club Championships back at Battersea Park, with its new all-weather jumping surfaces, covering boys', colts' and senior events and records by Ivan Beaumont, Philip Clay and Stephen W. Crosbie.
items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report on the Belgrave Club Championships back at Battersea Park, with its new all-weather jumping surfaces, covering boys', colts' and senior events and records by Ivan Beaumont, Philip Clay and Stephen W. Crosbie. The return of the Belgrave Club Championships to their historical home of Battersea Park coincided with the all-weather jumping surfaces at that venue becoming available for the first time. A fair number of senior athletes took part, but the most pleasing thing was to see the ranks of youngsters who keenly contested the boys and colts events with heats necessary in both age groups for the 100 metres. So often boys events are held separately from senior competitions, but mixing with the old'ns and simply competing at the same track on the same afternoon seemed to raise their enjoyment of the proceedings. The organisation ran as sweetly as ever and we must thank our visiting officials - Harry Hathway, 'Tommy' Thomas, Mrs Nightingale and Mr and Mrs Long - who did great work in the timekeeping department. The jumping events produced some excellent performances. Outstanding was the triple jumping of 14 year old Ivan Beaumont who gained 2nd in the senior competition with a distance that beat his own boys record. (Here it must be noted that the following week at Battersea he pulverised the long jump record as well. It had stood since 1961!) Reg. Hopkins, having spent a fortune by entering practically every event, had an exciting duel in the long jump with Snowy Brooks, with the former just getting the verdict with a personal best leap. He also won the high jump, a mere centimetre below the championship best. The junior high jump gave David Didino the chance to launch himself to a new height of 1.67m and Richard Danpure, a new signing, set a championship best in winning the boys event. Philip Clay smashed the previous junior boys club record by 7 centimetres in this event. Richard completed an unusual double by taking his 800 metre race as well. Yes, those jumping areas are going to be a real boon. Colin Pearson seems to be the eternal runner-up. He has run in Club Championships from 800 metres to 20 miles, always giving his all, but he has never quite managed to make off with the winners "pot". This year's 800 metres was reckoned to be wide open, although Peter Carton, simply on past performances, was favourite. Could Colin do it? Well, he certainly tried, and maybe he was a shade ahead as he attacked Pete down the final straight but as they crossed the line with Colin wildly lunging forward it was Peter who got the decision. Colin turned the tables on him in the 1,500 metres by producing a do or die burst with a full lap to go. Peter had to give way but Laurie O'Hara was clearly untroubled by such tactics. Alan Black was in a class of his own in the steeplechase although Leo Coy, reducing his week old best by another 30 seconds, is improving fast these days and looks certain to produce a sub - 10 minute run in the not so distant future. Mark Shippen won a close boys javelin competition with 3rd placer Stephen W. Crosbie setting a new junior boys record. A titanic struggle took place in the senior javelin between John Martin, the holder, and Snowy Brooks. John must have been fairly sure of keeping his hold on the trophy because he hadn't bothered to clean it up. Snowy managed to wrest it away but John had the last laugh when he won the discus after Snowy produced six no throws! Snowy admitted later that his start was "a bit naughty" in the 100 metres. He held Charlie Gillett off by a tenth with young Reg. breaking new ground with an 11.6 for third. Charlie later stamped his authority on the 200 and 400 metre fields with a couple of good times considering the dusty condition of the track. Philip Gee added a worthy 2nd in the one lap sprint to his earlier 800 metre third place, and Paul Williamson reaped some of the benefits of consistant training with his effort in the 400 metres. At the start of this season, his first, he clocked 56.6 for the event. He is now down to 52.6. As shown on this issue's cover, David Bailey led home the field in the senior boys' sprint with some hot opposition breathing down his neck. New member James Heath took the colts' race. items.label: September 1974
items.sum: Track Secretary Philip Gee's review of a disappointing 1974 Southern League season, in which Belgrave fell to 11th of 25 clubs, praising reliable and newly emerging team members.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track Secretary Philip Gee's review of a disappointing 1974 Southern League season, in which Belgrave fell to 11th of 25 clubs, praising reliable and newly emerging team members. What a let down! After finishing 3rd and 4th in the Southern League in 1972 and 1973 respectively, our final place this year was a mediocre 11th (out of 25 clubs). We won our opening fixture but the results of the next three meetings looked like we were aiming for arithmetic progression (or perhaps I mean regression!) - we finished 2nd, 3rd and 4th. Our decline was partly arrested by gaining third place in the penultimate fixture but we finished the season at Wimbledon Park with a 4th place. In common with many other clubs we do not have an unlimited depth of talent, especially in middle distance events and, therefore, injuries to one or two key men (which has happened this year) are really felt. Life is not made easier by a number of members whose variety of excuses never cease to amaze and depress me. I only hope that 1974 was a bad year and that everyone will make an effort to support whoever takes on the mantle of Track Secretary in 1975. Division 1 of the Southern League is extremely competitive and it would not take much more of a decline to make Division 2 a real possibility in 1976. After all that I would like to thank those who have made my job easier by their reliability and willingness to compete. Unfortunately space does not permit me to list them all but Steve White (who travels from Oxford to compete for the club) and Charlie Gillett deserve a mention for their efforts; neither ever seems to have a bad run. New names have, of course, been seen in the Belgrave team this year; Martin Scott, who after competing very successfully at the beginning of the season unfortunately pulled a muscle (see you next season), Paul Williamson, who has steadily improved his 400 metres time and is now almost a regular in the 4 x 400 metres relay team, Leo Coy, who has found his niche in the team at 3,000 metres Steeplechase. He has only run this event three times but has improved from 10m.44secs. to 10m.5.8secs., and finally, Michael Manning, who although still a Junior has turned out in a couple of 5,000 metres league races and has run very well. items.sum: Note that Leo Coy found himself running with world record holder Brendan Foster from Clapham to Wimbledon, and improved his 3,000 metres and steeplechase times the following week.
items.s: Note that Leo Coy found himself running with world record holder Brendan Foster from Clapham to Wimbledon, and improved his 3,000 metres and steeplechase times the following week. It's no wonder Leo Coy has been chopping down his best times when one considers his training companions. Why, the other week, when setting out to run up to Wimbledon Common from his home at Clapham, who should fall in alongside him but world record holder Brendan Foster. Brendan was staying with friends in Clapham whilst visiting London for the Emsley Carr mile and had got himself lost while out for a run. The two ran together to Wimbledon and back - and the following week Leo was down to 9:08 for 3,000 metres and 10:05.8 for the steeplechase! items.s: 'SNOWY' 3rd IN A.A.A. Report on the AAA Decathlon Championship at Aldersley on 8-9 June 1974, where Snowy (C.) Brooks improved his club record to finish 3rd with 6642 points and Reg Hopkins was 10th with 5537. JUNE 8th/9th 1974 - ALDERSLEY. Snowy Brooks once again improved his Club record decathlon score, this time by 73 points, when he and Reg Hopkins made the journey to Aldersley to take part in the AAA Decathlon Championship. Reg also increased his best score by 175 points with his finest effort coming in the long jump. With many areas in his scoring open to enormous improvement when compared to his individual performances, he has an exciting future ahead of him in this event. Taking an early lead in the championship Snowy set up fastest time in the 100 metres, and when he followed this with 2nd in the long jump, 1st in the shot and equal 1st in the 400 metres, it was not surprising that the Belgravian found himself leading the competition at the end of the first day. The second day includes his weaker events and he slipped to 2nd overall, 17 points behind the leader, after the hurdles and discus. A best ever vault of 3.50 metres took him temporarily back into the lead and although he lost ground again in the final two contests he was more than proud of his 3rd place in the AAA Championship with a score that moved him to 7th in the United Kingdom for 1974. 1. items.s: WE SINK TO 3rd IN LEAGUE Report and results of the third Southern League match at Sutcliffe Park on 29 June 1974, where Belgrave finished 3rd behind Cambridge Harriers and Shaftesbury Harriers, with spectator Gerry North pressed into running the 1,500 metres. JUNE 29th 1974 - SUTCLIFFE PARK. Our field events section was boosted for the third match of the series by the appearance of Eric Barker, and with Cliff Brooks reaching top form we gained a double win in the shot putt. Unfortunately only four other individual wins came our way and in some events we were hard pushed to even turn out a team. Gerry North arrived to watch and was pressed into running an unaccustomed 1,500 metres in a pair of borrowed spikes with Lionel Mann, who had already run the 5,000 metres, to keep him company. Charlie Gillett enjoyed his elevation to 'A' string status, equalling his best 100 metre time and winning the 200 metres. This gave Steve White the chance to have a rest from the short events and tackle the one lap race for a change. The net result was the same as usual with Steve crossing the line first in a most comfortable looking 50.6 seconds. Both short hurdle races provided easy wins for Belgrave with Paul Whitby aggressively taking the 'A' field apart for a clear 1 second margin of victory and Reg Hopkins doing a similar demolition job in the 'B' race. Brothers Steve and Peter Crosbie again proved their worth by scoring some useful points in the triple jump and javelin. Overall, however, it was very disappointing to finish behind Cambridge Harriers, who are not so strong these days, and Shaftesbury Harriers who are new arrivals from division two. Even our regular relay wins at the meeting's close did little to salvage our pride. Match Result: 1. Cambridge H 140pts; 2. Shaftesbury H 134pts; 3. BELGRAVE 119pts; 4. Portsmouth 93pts; 5. items.s: OUR WORST S.LEAGUE EVER Report and results of the Southern League match at Clifton Park, Exeter on 6 July 1974, where an under-strength Belgrave team finished 4th, their lowest ever Southern League placing. JULY 6th 1974 - CLIFTON PARK, EXETER. If the previous week's performance was bad, this effort was a disaster. A crop of injuries and other commitments reduced the Belgrave team to shreds and although those who did go enjoyed themselves, we sank to our lowest ever placing in the Southern League of 4th. To rub salt into the wound even our local rivals Hercules Wimbledon managed to beat us. But let us not dwell on the gloomy side. As already mentioned our team was out to enjoy itself and the shortage of men gave most the chance to double up on events or tackle something new. Our hurdlers were in top shape. Reg Hopkins set up a personal best time to win the opening track event, the 400 metre hurdles, and Paul Whitby followed this with a magnificent first ever attempt at the event in 59.4 after a blistering start. They both went on to win their short hurdle races with Paul reducing his seasonal best to 16.2. The 800 metres gave us more points than of late with both our men ducking under two minutes for the first time this year and John Stow later followed this with an impressive win in the 1,500 metres. Charlie Gillett and Philip Gee covered the shorter sprints quite successfully and Paul Williamson made his league debut in the 'B' 400 metres with a good 2nd place. Two youngsters also making promising first appearances were David Didino who reached 3rd in the 'B' high jump, and Michael Manning who gained a similar position in the 5,000 metres. Yet another new face was that of Stephen Hartley who has a lot more triple jumping in him when he gets fitter. In the pole vault Alan Mead started out to 'get a point' and ended up by only narrowly failing at 2.60m. Covering all the throws between them, Bill Couzens and John Martin still had enough energy to compete with Bob Taylor when it came to repetition beer drinking on the train home to London. items.s: Championship wins by Whitby and Stow Report and results of the club 5000 metres and 110m hurdles championships at Battersea Park on 10 July 1974, won by John Stow (J. Stow) by a whisker from Laurie O'Hara and by Paul Whitby. JULY 10th 1974 - BATTERSEA PARK. After a day of intermittent rain and beneath a sombre and humid sky, 19 runners moved off to cover the 12½ laps of our annual 5000 metre championship. Following a brisk, bunched first lap the race soon formed into a pattern of small groups: Black, O'Hara, Stow and Carton in the first group were leading a second of North, Pearson and Mann; while further back a grimacing Clive Shippen was giving his younger rivals Coy, Jardine and Maughan a hard time. Five laps from home the leading group broke up with Stow and O'Hara leaving Peter Carton and a tiring Alan Black. And with less than a mile to go Gerry North ventured from group two and moved into 4th position. At the bell Stow and O'Hara were still locked together, their nimble feet almost stride for stride. Only a final last gasp dash in the home straight by the younger man prevented Laurie from annexing the 5000 metres title to the 10,000m he earned in May. Further back Peter Carton held the bronze position; Clive Shippen reversed his 10,000m position over Leo Coy, as did Doug Jardine over Doug Maughan; Fred Paget finished in a lung-busting dead heat with Derek Crookes and our gallant President brought up the rear. In the 110m Hurdles Paul Whitby ran in devastating fashion to put up a particularly good time on the Battersea Park cinders and take the championship at his first attempt. Decathlon man Reg Hopkins was 2nd and Ronnie McCrossen snatched a narrow margin over Steve Crosbie for 3rd. First Class Standard: 1st to 7th. Second Class Standard: 8th to 10th. 1. J.Stow 14:50.0 11. items.s: A. A. A. Championships Note on the four Belgravians at the AAA Championships at Crystal Palace: Steve White, Carl Lawton, John Hall, John Bicourt and second-claimer Chris Barber. Four Belgravians competed in this year's A.A.A. Championships at the Crystal Palace. Steve White, not jumping at his best, was 14th in the long jump with 6.75m whilst on the track Carl Lawton and John Hall distinguished themselves in the 3,000 metres Walk with 5th and 11th positions, both setting up new personal records. Over the same distance but with a few 'barriers' in the way John Bicourt got up to 4th (2nd U.K.athlete) after a sluggish start. Another to find foreign athletes ahead of him was our second-claimer Chris Barber. In his heat of the 1,500 metres he crossed the line 6th in 3:46.9 behind four overseas competitors. items.s: BROCKMAN TROPHY Report and Belgrave results from the Brockman Trophy meeting at Wimbledon Park on 20 July 1974, where Belgrave were 2nd of twelve clubs behind Southampton. JULY 20th 1974 - WIMBLEDON PARK. Belgrave '20' day, traditionally one of the hottest of the year, turned out to be quite a successful day for the Club. Whilst our road runners up at the Common toiled their way beneath the sun to a team victory and our walkers gained 2nd place in the National R.W.A. 50km, our track and field team reached a creditable 2nd amongst the twelve clubs contesting the 'Brockman Trophy'. Trophy meetings generally do not have the atmosphere that they once generated but the 'Brockman', organised slickly by Herne Hill Harriers is still one of the best track meetings of the summer. A personal best by Paul Whitby in the high hurdles event took him to just one tenth of a second behind our club record, although he was rather disgruntled with his 2nd place. Paul's progress in the few months we have known him has made him one of the key members of our team. Five times Charlie Gillett stepped onto the track to race and his record at the end of the day was remarkable. He won both his sprint heats in good times, improved on them again in the finals and then helped our relay team on it's way to 2nd place. Other highlights included Cliff Brooks' throwing and easy 400 metre hurdles win, Arnold Bentt's triple jump of bang on 13 metres, and a determined recovery by Alan Black after he had fallen very heavily at one of the barriers in the steeplechase whilst starting to pull away from the field. 100m: 3. items.sum: Ron Langheim urges members to sell tickets for the 1974 AAA Draw, half of whose proceeds go to the club.
items.s: AAA Draw 1974 Ron Langheim urges members to sell tickets for the 1974 AAA Draw, half of whose proceeds go to the club. Very soon you will be receiving books of tickets to sell for the above mentioned draw. Before you put them back in an envelope and return them to me with a note saying that the chaps at work will not buy any, or your family are against gambling, just bear in mind the following points. First of all, for every ticket you sell, 50% goes to the A.A.A. and we as a club get the other 50%. This is a tremendous chance to get some easy money for our Club funds. In the not so distant future big decisions will have to be made as to which road Belgrave Harriers as a club will take if we are to remain a force to be reckoned with. Whatever decision is made, it will cost money. Now that you are ready to go and sell your tickets, remember to ask everybody at work, especially people who you think are not interested. You will in many cases be surprised and pleased with the support they show. Also, presuming that the tickets are 5p each, use a salesman's ploy and suggest two for 10p (you can always climb down to one ticket if they show any doubts) Remember, it's easy money for our Club and you will get the benefits. I am certain I can count on all you Belgravians to give this venture 100% support. Ron Langheim RON LANGHEIM AAA Draw

items.s: ANOTHER LEAGUE 3rd Report and results of the Southern League match at Mayesbrook Park on 27 July 1974, where Belgrave finished 3rd behind Met. Police and Ilford. JULY 27th 1974 - MAYESBROOK PARK. This was a much better team performance than in the previous two league matches but we still had to give way to strong Met. Police and Ilford sides. Steve White led the way with another fine sprint double and later anchored both our relay teams. Cliff Brooks won his first ever pole vault competition and Philip Gee provided our only other points maximum in the 400 metres 'B'. It was nice to see Gerry North back in action over 5000 metres, in fact our middle distance section looked a lot stronger than of late. Leo Coy, in his first attempt at the event, improved every time he took a barrier in the steeplechase and had enough go in him to raise a spirited sprint at the end. items.label: September 1974
items.h: The proposed 'Alf. Harley' club honours board John Walker writes:-
items.sum: Letter from John Walker opposing the proposed 'Alf. Harley' memorial honours board and suggesting the money go on youngsters, a printed club history, advertising and fewer medals.
items.s: The proposed 'Alf. Harley' club honours board John Walker writes:- Letter from John Walker opposing the proposed 'Alf. Harley' memorial honours board and suggesting the money go on youngsters, a printed club history, advertising and fewer medals. Dear Editor, Belgrave Harriers. Quo vadis. Is Belgrave Harriers dying? No. Then why the proposed memorial board? I have seen the cap in hand circular and I believe the sum mentioned, 350 nicker (minimum!) should be spent in a much wiser fashion. Now, contrary to what some wildly deranged Belgravian may think I aint no lecturer! Either in Big Hall or Belgrave Hall! I feel that something should be done to shove some plasma back into the Bels and that can be done only one way. Not with a board, but with flesh and blood. Youngsters. Here I must pay tribute to men who since the Bels formation have done great work administratively. If it is felt by some that one such person should be especially remembered what better than that his name and memory be given to an event - close to his heart - the tribute being no less sincere than as I understand is being contemplated, by a memorial board. There is another way to remember the history of Belgrave. How about printing, say, 500 copies of the Bels history, with photos, and selling them? In this way a permanent reference could always be to hand in many homes. I realise a lot of work would be involved but it surely is practical and when the books are sold the club would benefit. Another venture which I'd support would be to encourage youngsters - early teenagers for example by taking parties of lads on regular training weekends by coach somewhere. Also, I believe, as I understand Bill Laws does, that Belgrave should advertise more than at present. Space should be bought in various newspapers and other media. Getting back to saving money. Why have medals? Incidentally this aint sour grapes! I know I aint won many. I am serious in the medals suggestion. Today engraving and medals are very expensive. One other thing. I don't believe our Treasurer is that old that he can't take out several novices on a training run. Naturally I mean male novice runners. John Walker JOHN WALKER John Walker JOHN WALKER Alf. Harley Alf. Harley proposed club honours board to be named after him Bill Laws Bill Laws said to favour Belgrave advertising more Big Hall Belgrave Hall

items.label: September 1974
items.sum: Past President Clive Shippen, organiser of the Club Honours Board scheme, replies to John Walker: the board's cost, Alf Harley's unfinished club history, and the state of the young membership.
items.s: ...and Clive Shippen replies Past President Clive Shippen, organiser of the Club Honours Board scheme, replies to John Walker: the board's cost, Alf Harley's unfinished club history, and the state of the young membership. As our Past President Clive Shippen has been responsible for organising the Club Honours Board scheme, and is well qualified to comment on John's other suggestions, we felt it would be of interest to hear his views too. My first reaction on reading John's letter was, "This is just the sort of man we need on our Committee". Ideas are always welcome and, although many come in for quite a buffeting, it is always of benefit to the Club that they should be debated by a lively Committee. I believe our present Committee to be a lively one and, under Charlie Manning's chairmanship, it has had a good year. Unfortunately, the large amount of investigation and sub-committee work which precedes a decision is not always common knowledge, but I can assure John that several alternative memorial schemes were discussed at great length over a period of months before a final decision was reached. It may interest him to know that his suggestion was one of those considered. .... continued on following page As for the Club Honours Board itself, the cost is now expected to be £80 less than the estimated sum and it is my hope that Club funds will not have to find any of the anticipated £270. The response from Past Presidents, Vice-Presidents and Life Members to my request for them to launch this fund was marvellous and well over half sent in letters applauding the decision. In the course of a year several hundreds of visitors from all spheres come to our Headquarters and on many occasions I have noticed individuals studying with interest the Ken O'Kell boards listing Past Presidents and Internationals. We cannot expect all outsiders to be fully aware of our history but there is a good chance that many future visitors will leave Belgrave Hall with a better knowledge of our great record. And it is of that great record that Alf Harley was terribly proud. So much so that he spent a great deal of time collecting together all the information he could find, with a view to writing the book that John Walker would like to see. It was never started, but we discussed it and pooled our researches. I hope to make that book reality, but if it took Blackheath six years to write theirs, ours can hardly be done quicker! As for selling 500 copies and making some money for the Club, my own experience of "The Belgravian" and "Veteris" leads me to doubt whether this could be regarded as a money spinning venture. Now to the youngsters. John suggests that we shove some plasma back into the Bels. Surely he must have seen the Young Athletes section of the June "Belgravian"? There seemed to be plenty of plasma amongst the 50-odd colts, boys and youths photographed or mentioned in that issue - and as our coach trip to Brighton showed, they can produce some useful results in open competition too. Reg Hopkins and Bill Couzens are principally responsible for the healthy state of our young membership, and although they get some help they could do with a lot more. I am sure that they will both be delighted to hear that John supports this type of venture. Perhaps they will hear from you John. Oh! And by the way - see you at the A.G.M.! Clive Shippen CLIVE SHIPPEN Past President; organised the Club Honours Board scheme Clive Shippen CLIVE SHIPPEN John Walker John writer of the letter being answered John John Walker Charlie Manning Charlie Manning chairman of the Committee Ken O'Kell Ken O'Kell the Ken O'Kell boards listing Past Presidents and Internationals at Belgrave Hall Alf Harley Alf Harley was collecting information for a club history book Reg Hopkins Reg Hopkins principally responsible, with Bill Couzens, for the young membership Bill Couzens Bill Couzens principally responsible, with Reg Hopkins, for the young membership Belgrave Hall Brighton Blackheath

items.sum: John Blair-Fish's 1974 fell-running season in Scotland and Wales, including the Camethy Hill Race, Manx Mountain Marathon and Ben Lomond, ahead of the Ben Nevis race.
items.s: Bel's king of the mountains John Blair-Fish's 1974 fell-running season in Scotland and Wales, including the Camethy Hill Race, Manx Mountain Marathon and Ben Lomond, ahead of the Ben Nevis race. John Blair-Fish is still running well over the fells up North. Early season efforts included the Camethy Hill Race where he finished 19th out of 98 competitors over the 9 mile/1,600 feet course in 57 mins. 6 secs., and the Manx Mountain Marathon - which sounds a real killer as it traverses 30 miles/9,000feet - in which he was 12th from 51 in 6hrs. 15mins. in spite of losing three-quarters of an hour and climbing an extra 1,000 feet through an error in navigation. During the summer he tackled eight more of these 'superman events' in Wales and Scotland, gradually improving his average position, over distances varying from 3 to 17 miles, with climbs being as much as 7,500 feet. (Makes the 'kiss of death' on our 5¾ mile race look a bit weak doesn't it.) A particularly good performance was his 4th in the Ben Lomond 9miles/3,000feet where he crossed the line 4th in 1hr. 15mins. John has cut back in training in the last few weeks to concentrate on the Ben Nevis race on September 7th. He was 40th last year and looks forward to improving on that. Good luck to you John. We hope to see you running down South again some day. John Blair-Fish John Blair-Fish fell runner; 19th Camethy Hill Race 57:06; 12th Manx Mountain Marathon 6hrs 15mins; 4th Ben Lomond 1hr 15mins; 40th Ben Nevis race the previous year John Blair-Fish John Camethy Hill Race Manx Mountain Marathon Ben Lomond race Ben Nevis race Wales Scotland Ben Lomond Ben Nevis

items.label: December 1974
items.sum: Editorial congratulating Ray Middleton on his five world best performances at Haringey, explaining why the magazine has been cut back to save costs, and noting that women joggers may now use the ladies room at Belgrave Hall as a base for runs.
items.s: COMMENT Editorial congratulating Ray Middleton on his five world best performances at Haringey, explaining why the magazine has been cut back to save costs, and noting that women joggers may now use the ladies room at Belgrave Hall as a base for runs. All members will undoubtedly wish to offer their congratulations to Ray Middleton whose record breaking spree at Haringey on Sept 29th reaped him five new world best performances. This magnificent feat once again reminds us of Ray's stature; one of the all-time "greats" of the walking world. Unfortunately his deeds seemed to be almost totally ignored at the time by the national press who, it appears, would rather report "hooliganism on the terraces". Slowly, however, and due in no small part to the efforts of Press Secretary George Piddington, news of his achievement began to spread; and an interview on LBC one evening was followed by a visit to his home by the BBC, and a 20 minute recording was subsequently made for broadcasting from American and Canadian stations. Once again the size of the "Belgravian" has been reduced and the photographs limited to just one on the front cover, a measure which will regrettably have to be continued. Lately each copy has been costing the Club around 20p. When one remembers that we have approaching 500 members and four issues per year, it does not take much to realise that important a link as it is, the Club's gazette is a luxury which must be kept in check. First lady bus drivers, then the Stock Exchange and now... could the exclusively male facade of Belgrave Harriers be beginning to crumble. Of course we all know that there are many jobs in our club which would not be done without the assistance of our ladies. Now it seems their presence is gradually being admitted. Some months back two women joined as Honorary Members and at our October Committee meeting it was stated that it would be perfectly acceptable for ladies to use the ladies room at the Hall as a base from which to commence a road or country run. Immediately the chance was taken, and now it is not uncommon to see two "Belles" setting out from our HQ on training nights in the week and on Sunday mornings. Any other female joggers who wish to join them must remember to use the stairway OUTSIDE the Hall at the end of the side-alley, otherwise there are going to be some nasty shocks all round. Ray Middleton Ray Middleton five world best performances at Haringey, 29 Sept 1974 Ray Middleton Ray George Piddington George Piddington Press Secretary Haringey Belgrave Hall

items.label: December 1974
items.sum: The General Hon. Secretary Peter Hilliar's review of the 1973/74 season covering the walkers, the cross-country and road relay teams, the track season, Charlie Manning's fund raising as President, the junior section and coaching, ending with thanks to the club's officials.
items.s: Hon. Secretary's Report for 1973/74 The General Hon. Secretary Peter Hilliar's review of the 1973/74 season covering the walkers, the cross-country and road relay teams, the track season, Charlie Manning's fund raising as President, the junior section and coaching, ending with thanks to the club's officials. And so we come to the end of another season. 1973/74 has been a funny sort of season. It seemed to promise so much in terms of athletic achievements in all our fields of interest but in the last analysis events did not live up to expectations. To plot the main milestones during the year, the most consistently successful section was the walking section as has been the case in the last few years. But even the walkers have had a relatively disappointing season by their own exceptionally high standards. After all, the days when National Championships were automatically assumed to be Belgrave's own preserve are not so far distant (almost beyond living memory in other fields!). Possibly this is because the standard of top walking is getting higher or on the other hand a reflection that most of our leading walkers are getting older. Nevertheless there was a notable turn-out at last January's Commonwealth Games in New Zealand with four representatives, Carl Lawton for England, Len Duquemin and John Moullin for Guernsey and Allan Callow for the Isle of Man. Nationally we won the 10 mile Championship, were 2nd in the 50 kilometres event but were otherwise unplaced. Carl Lawton has regularly appeared in GB colours over the past year. Once again the important point proved by the walking section is that team-work does count for a great deal. If only the same were always true of our cross-country teams. Admittedly competition is very fierce at top levels but I can't believe that our performances, particularly at National and Area level reflects the relative strength of our middle and long distance running talent. This point seems to be proved again and again by our road relay results which are consistently better than our winter form promises. Our performance in the Southern Road Relay, where our team finished 5th, only 16 seconds behind the 3rd placed team confirmed this. However, the standard of road running in the country as a whole was confirmed by the result of the National Road Relay, where the international standard of performances underlined the relative mediocrity of the Southern teams. On the track an excellent start to the season gave way to a gradual deterioration in our results. It was really the year of the individual rather than that of the team. Strangely enough many of our best individuals are also marvellous team members, particularly Steve White and the ever-reliable Cliff Brooks whose Decathlon points are still improving. However, Philip Gee and his other hard working helpers invariably confessed their inability to get the best teams to the starting lines of various meetings due to a multitude of reasons of varying complexity. On the track side we should not leave out John Bicourt our only current British international, who went to both the Commonwealth Games and the European Games in Rome. I think John would admit that 1974 was a disappointing year which did not live up to the early promise of the Commonwealth race. 1973/74 was also the year of controversy, much of it surrounding the genial features of Charlie Manning the President for the year. Charlie's fund raising activities will go down into Belgrave history whereas he confesses that the same is not necessarily true of his athletic achievements. He has apparently raised something over £1,000 for the Club in the past year by various methods which haven't always met with universal sympathy. But I consider that his ability to shock us out of our general complacency is a valuable asset. Looking to the future it is encouraging to note the strength of the junior section. Talking in stock-market terms this is the life-blood of Belgrave's future strength - our investment in the present. However it is arguable that the strength of this influx of youthful talent could be too much for our coaching system to accomodate - it has shown signs of being under severe strain on several occasions in the past. Undoubtedly talent will perform to its best ability if directed correctly and it is here that coaching comes in. We have in the past printed a long list of coaches in .... continued on page 10. HON. SECRETARY'S REPORT continued... our handbooks but how many do we see from week to week during the season. How many do our athletes recognise. I think this a terrific challenge and one which the present day senior athlete could undertake to replace his training - to put something back into the sport that has given him so much pleasure. Think about it - it is rewarding. Looking through past copies of the 'Belgravian', that excellent chronicle of our activities, one has noticed the Belgrave Evening of Culture, the Bazaar and other such novelties. I feel all departures from the straight and narrow are rewarding as long as they are profitable and the proceeds can be used to benefit our sport. It could be that our ambitions will grow ever wider, even though I am sure we will not lose sight of the essential objective, which is to encourage all facets of athletics. Finally I'd like to put in a word of thanks to all officials. They all do it in their own time, for their own reasons but again for the benefit of athletics. Support your committee. It's doing a good job and if you have any ideas please transmit them to a committee member rather than complain that nothing is ever done in Belgrave's name. PETER HILLIAR GENERAL HON. items.label: December 1974
items.sum: Harry Shields' account of the unveiling of the A.A. Harley Club Honours Board at Belgrave Hall by Mrs. Harley on 5 October 1974, a memorial to Alf Harley designed with Clive Shippen's help.
items.s: A.A.HARLEY CLUB HONOURS BOARD Harry Shields' account of the unveiling of the A.A. Harley Club Honours Board at Belgrave Hall by Mrs. Harley on 5 October 1974, a memorial to Alf Harley designed with Clive Shippen's help. Unveiled at Belgrave Hall on Saturday, October 5th 1974 by Mrs. Harley. The people of nations and of any organisations from earliest times have instinctive desire to record with pride the achievements they have accomplished in a tangible form. It provides a tradition and sets the standard for the future. In the same way Belgravians have the same instinct for history and that the Club, whose existence is spread over more that 80 years, should have a permanent record of its unique and unparallelled achievements, unequalled by any other club in the land. Not until the death of Alf. Harley, whose service over 44 years, 26 as General Secretary, could sufficient reason be found to raise the sum of money needed to provide a fit and proper momento, something pleasing to us all. Alf, with his great personality and unique qualities of athlete, companion, administrator, his lasting and deep interest in all facets of club life, made the occasion for such an appeal possible. Clive Shippen, whose efforts and major role in the design of the 'Honours Board', a magnificent addition to our Headquarters, referred to this in his preamble to the unveiling ceremony, in which he said, "Without other great Belgravians, internationals and solid club workers there would be no honours to record" The board is something in which we have all played our part. Any description from me of the 'Honours Board' would be inadequate. It is there for all to see. The unveiling ceremony was splendidly arranged. Mrs. Harley carried it out with the dignity we have come to expect from her. The whole of her family attended, son, three daughters, son-in-law, and grandson, who I am sure is a split image of Alf as a baby. Afterwards Mrs. Harley told me how deeply she felt and how impressed with the thought that had gone into making the occasion so simple and sincere. In her view the 'Honours Board' typified Alf completely - grand in design, modern and fitting in every way to a great club. She was sure he would have been absolutely thrilled. Others will comment on how pleasing it was to see such a gathering of Belgravians at the Hall. Many had travelled long distances to be present. Thanks to Clive Shippen and all those who have made the fulfilment of such a dream possible. HARRY SHIELDS Harry Shields HARRY SHIELDS Alf. Harley Alf. Harley served the club over 44 years, 26 as General Secretary; the Honours Board is his memorial Alf. items.s: Dear Belgravians, Letter from Clive Shippen thanking members for funding the Honours Board, which cost £284.70 against £304.35 raised, with a list of the donors. Dear Belgravians, With a successful Honours Board Unveiling Ceremony behind us, and the fund now closed, may I thank you on behalf of the Committee for the wonderful response to our appeal. The total cost of the project was £284.70 and the magnificent sum of £304.35 was raised. The surplus will be allocated for updating the board in future years. items.label: December 1974
items.sum: Club gossip notes: Joe Scammell senior retiring from walking, Terry Lewins' US mountain race and marathon, Jack Fletcher at the Brighton finish, Jean Middleton's sponsored walk, Keith Angus winning the Kosice Marathon, Glen Haszard's Two Bridges race, news of George Chantler, Ben Knifton, Ben Lulham, Clive Shippen and Gordon Biscoe, Martin Scott's Surrey junior trophy, Syd James, Gordon Doubleday, the McMullens and Gerry North's charity soccer match.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip notes: Joe Scammell senior retiring from walking, Terry Lewins' US mountain race and marathon, Jack Fletcher at the Brighton finish, Jean Middleton's sponsored walk, Keith Angus winning the Kosice Marathon, Glen Haszard's Two Bridges race, news of George Chantler, Ben Knifton, Ben Lulham, Clive Shippen and Gordon Biscoe, Martin Scott's Surrey junior trophy, Syd James, Gordon Doubleday, the McMullens and Gerry North's charity soccer match. We are sorry to learn that JOE SCAMMELL (senior) has had to retire from his walking activities owing to illness. Joe has carried our colours for FIFTY YEARS (can anybody recall having seen him not wearing Club colours?) and in his early days he was a regular team man. Although his speed dropped over the years he nevertheless maintained a fine upright style. His son Joe (junior) visits him regularly to give him news of how we are doing. Our best wishes to you, Joe. TERRY LEWINS and two other RAF athletes serving in Nebraska, USA, competed in the annual Pikes Peak Mountain Marathon in Colorado in August. The race takes in a 13.4 mile climb from 6,500 feet above sea level to 14,100 feet followed by a return down the same route. Terry finished 19th in 4hrs 40mins losing nine places by going off course three miles from the finish. The temperature was 87F. In the Mid-Western AAU Marathon at Omaha, Terry was 10th in 2hrs 46mins. Go to a fixture on the Brighton Road and the chances are that you will bump into JACK "NOBBY" FLETCHER. For many years he was a member of our cross-country packs and has probably seen more "Brightons" than any other member. This year was a special occasion, he was right on the finishing post to cheer in RAY MIDDLETON. Ray is not the only one in his family to be pacing out the miles recently. JEAN MIDDLETON took part in a sponsored walk at Peckham Rye Park to raise funds for Leukemia Research, in memory of Phil Embleton. She raised over £60, a mighty effort, and sends thanks to all those who so generously sponsored her. A popular member of the Bels whilst domiciled in London in 1964 was KEITH ANGUS from Sheffield. Steadily, over the years, his performances have been improving and his latest success was a win in the Czechoslovakian Kosice Marathon classic. Conditions were appalling but he clocked 2hrs 29mins. 09secs. to beat a star studded field that included New Zealander Jack Foster, Commonwealth Games silver medallist. And talking of Kiwis, on August 24th our own member from the land of the silver fern, GLEN HASZARD, competed in the Scottish Two Bridges Road Race (Kincardine - Forth), a distance of 36 miles 158 yards. He finished 43rd of the 65 starters in 4hrs 34mins 52secs. It is good to see GEORGE CHANTLER about again. Last winter he had a serious illness and more recently his wife was ill. We congratulate him on being elected President of his local club Feltham AC. One who would no doubt have been at the unveiling of the Alf Harley memorial were he not know living in Portugal is BEN KNIFTON. He writes of the pleasant climate and of enjoying a daily swim. He is a former Editor of the "Belgravian". It's nice to see BEN LULHAM around again after a few years absence. It was 1965 when Ben coached his magnificent relay squad to a AAA Junior 4 x 110 yards victory at Hurlingham in 42.8. CLIVE SHIPPEN has been made Vice-President of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association whilst GORDON BISCOE has been elected to that body's committee. MARTIN SCOTT is back in circulation again and we hear he is raring to go! At the Surrey Supper, held in November, Martin was presented with a trophy for the most outstanding Junior performance of the Surrey County Championships - his long jump of 7.17 metres. Another old walker still active is Syd James, former Surrey Champion. He is engaged in activities with the physically handicapped in his locality. GORDON DOUBLEDAY is now recovered from last years's illness we are are pleased to say, and is now regularly on duty with his stop watch although advised by his doctor to avoid strenuous activity. Gordon was on hand at the 30 mile race at Walton a few weeks back when Mick Molloy set a new World Best time. That well known veteran walker DAVE McMULLEN tells us that his father BOB McMULLEN, now over 80, is still active and well and enjoys a game of golf at Mitcham. Bob was a stalwart of our walking teams in the '20s. GERRY NORTH was selected to play in the International Athletes soccer side in a match against Radio London and Radio Medway. Playing for the radio team was none other than CHARLIE GILLETT and we understand he had a pretty good game too. Final result - seven all! items.sum: Notes on the members who came to, or sent apologies for, the unveiling of the Alf Harley Memorial at Belgrave Hall, with recollections of their running, walking and club service.
items.s: grapevine extra Notes on the members who came to, or sent apologies for, the unveiling of the Alf Harley Memorial at Belgrave Hall, with recollections of their running, walking and club service. The occasion of the unveiling of the Alf Harley Memorial brought to Belgrave Hall a number of members who were great friends of Alf and our reporter was soon mixing with them with notebook and pen. Here they are as they were spotted. Perhaps first of all a mention should be made of those unable to attend and who sent apologies. Letters were read out from our Senior Past President, Harry Hare, a member of our walking teams who willingly turned his hand to any job that needed doing. Len Coleman, now living in N. Ireland. Charlie Smart, slowly recovering after a long illness. Ed. Donovan, our Vice President from the U.S.A. who has vivid memories of running with the club in his early days at Battersea. F.M.(Rodney) Stone, the only Belgravian to be the subject of the "This is Your Life" TV programme. When he was a policeman he performed many acts of bravery and courage which was the theme of his appearance. Naturally the subject of his walking was brought up and we had the pleasure of seeing on our screens the late Harry Evans. In addition to the letters read out, a number of members had let us know that they could not attend. Bert Mitchell, one of our earliest marathon runners who now lives in Deal. Ken Miller, one of our Hon. Auditors. Chas. McLennan, said to be,"Out on a demo." Cliff Brooks, the best ten-man-team we have. Ray Plummer, a supporter of Belgrave for many years. Jim Rimmer, our holder of the Macher Shield, who, we hope, is going to have a horde after him eager to take the title. Arthur Welling, still active in performing and helping with the Veterans AC. Bernard Eglington, who still shows the Claret and Gold on the beaches and roads of N.Wales, and of course pops down for the odd race. Frank Simmons, always full of training advice. Double Olympian Eric Hall (50km 1956 and 20km 1960) and past winner of the hardest of all to win - the RWA 20 miles. Harry Hathway, not a member, but one who has helped as a timekeeper for many years. We learn that he has recently had an operation and wish him a speedy recovery. Track international Tommy Scrimshaw, who represented Great Britain on a number of occasions in the '30s. Going round the Hall it was a pleasure to meet so many old friends. Alf Taylor, member of our first winning E.C.C.U. team title at Beaconsfield in ..continued on following page GRAPEVINE EXTRA continued .... 1935, London - Brighton relay teams and winning Middlesex C.C. teams, he made the journey from Wellington, Somerset, where he now lives. Tom Cotton, former Trustee and Hon. Auditor, and one of the prime movers of the building fund which enabled us to buy Belgrave Hall. Jack Williams, accompanied by his wife, came up from Brighton - he still competes in veteran sprint races. Syd King, a former Hon Treasurer and regular member of our walking training packs and teams; he too was accompanied by his wife, daughter of a former club stalwart the late Bill Redgrave. Percy Wright journeyed up from Southampton and conveyed verbal apology from our 1932 Olympic 50km champion Tommy Green (he was over 40 when he won the title). Alf Harley often used to visit Eastleigh as his firm had a branch nearby, and he would usually pop in and see Tommy. Percy still judges walking events in his area. We cannot imagine him "pulling" a competitor by calling out what was the finish for him in a certain race in the '30s, "Aht! Git on aht!" Charlie Munro has officiated at cross country and track events longer than most can remember, now still going strong in his eighties. He is a Past President of the E.C.C.U. Denis Brickwood, whose sensational victory on the line in a London - Brighton relay was front page news in the "News of the World" and brought victory to Mitcham over the Bels. He later transferred to to us and served as cross country captain. Looking very fit, he attributes this to playing squash. Bill True is another who was a regular with the walkers, he knew everyone's form down to the last yard or second and served as Hon Handicapper for a good many years. Ken O'Kell knew Alf right from his early days in the club and they enjoyed many runs together and built up a lasting friendship. Len Marchant, one of the greatest all round runners we have had, he represented the A.A.A. and narrowly missed international selection. He now lives at Basildon but travels daily to the City. Mrs. Savage, and of course Win, were there. Mrs. Savage had a serious illness last winter, from which we hope she has recovered and will not recur. Win, in the Savage tradition, still puts in plenty of work for Selsonia and ladies athletics. Bill Ashford, still working in Holland, made one of his week-end trips coincide with the function. Syd Spencer is often seen judging walking events. When he was a policeman at Chelsea he gained us many new members. He was a good long distance man and became a Centurion by walking from Bath to London in 1952. Charlie Speechley, our oldest member, was involved in sport before World War I and took part in the trial for the 1908 Olympic Games at Diving! He still turns out in veteran events. Jack Bidgood, now 70 and looking well, gets a double mention as he had been seen on the Brighton Road at Bolney (where else!). A member of winning London - Brighton teams, past winner of our own long distance championship and the police Barking to Southend walk. As our "Grapevine" reporter prepares to rest, a bicycle bell is heard. Yes, it is Past President Bill Webb who has recently celebrated his 80th birthday. We close with a question, "has anybody seen a fitter and less likely octogenarian?." No mention has been made of the bulk of the people present - they are those who are generally present at any Belgrave meeting and we all know who they are. If, of course, somebody has been left out - our apologies. items.s: ERNIE JARVIS Death notice for Ernie Jarvis, former club sprint champion and member of the famous Belgrave medley relay team around 40 years earlier. We must sadly record the death of Ernie Jarvis, one time Club Champion over 100y, 220y and 440y. He was generally regarded as one of the fastest starters in the country during the late 1920s, and was a member of that famous Belgrave medley relay team some 40 years ago. items.label: December 1974
items.sum: Personal tribute introducing Ray Hall, the club's new President, recalling his walking records, club service and Sunday strolls with friends.
items.s: RAY HALL ~ PRESIDENT Personal tribute introducing Ray Hall, the club's new President, recalling his walking records, club service and Sunday strolls with friends. To follow the pattern of election jargon, balderdash, gibberish, slang, etc., used to introduce political candidates appears a fashionable way to introduce our new President. It has the merit of being concise, again a word of many meanings, but here I proclaim and laud:- Raymond Hall, 41 years old, married to a beautiful brunette, nee Pauline Norriss, a "Selsonian" and member of the 1954 Womens 4 x 110 yards relay team, with two young children - 10 year old Timothy and Geraldine who is five. Ray hails from East Dulwich, has a long record of Public Service, is a respected Stock Exchange man and is buying a house in Surrey, the purchase of which he hopes to complete in the next 50 or if he becomes a bus driver in the next 10 years. He does admit to making boobs. He joined Herne Hill Harriers as a runner, then Surrey Walking Club before becoming a "Belgravian" in 1953, which proved the soil in which he could blossom to full stature. For the Club he has been a continuous inspiration by his enthusiasm and has encouraged all to give their best. When living at Bexley, in spite of the inconvenience of travel, he could be relied on to be in constant attendance at Wimbledon and Battersea Park for training and club matches. He has always taken new and young members under his wing and to undertake any job that required doing. The inspiration of his own performances and unobtrusive generosity of time and assistance to those having financial problems are corner-stones of his character. For a long period of years he has been Walking Captain, Handicapper, Committee Member and all the unofficial posts of coach, transport manager, and propaganda chief, that crop up. He holds the Club record for the London - Brighton Walk of 7hrs 58 minutes 23 seconds, has the record for the Stock Exchange 25 mile walk with 3hrs 39 minutes 06 seconds, occasions which bring to mind many stories showing his character, while I have pushed a bicycle in attending him. His replies to my urges during his record breaking London - Brighton walk, particularly at the top of Dale Hill, cannot be printed. In addition he has been a member of many of our winning National Walk teams, the highlight probably being 3rd in the R.W.A. 50 Km Walk. My feelings towards Ray are beyond expression. As a companion on strolls over many years my feelings are deep. We have never had a cross word. In times of adversity he comes to the fore. Commencing from his early days in the Club with Stan Vickers, Jack Goswell George Beecham and others, Sunday strolls through the Kent and Surrey countryside were the order of the day and are full of sparkle and anecdotes. Three typical occasions that readily come to mind are:- 1. On holiday in Cornwall with Alf Harley. After a hard days walk, an unexpected magnificent tea in a monastery, sitting on the banks of a tributary of the river Fal, waiting for the ferry to take us across. Ray idly throwing stones into the water, Alf snoozing away. Beautifully warm, the lap of the water, the gradual setting of the sun. The place that passeth all understanding. 2. A day with the temperature well into the eighties. Towards the end of a 40 mile slog round Kent lanes, the road ahead giving the mirage of water, the final gasp at Godstone and the salvation of the London Transport canteen which we drank dry. The remarks of Ray and George Beecham when we boarded the train at Caterham on the wonder of moving without the torment of tired legs and sore feet. 3. Another, even hotter, summers day when Ray and myself staggered into Kemsing Station, glad to drink water and wet our handkerchiefs from the ..... continued on page 10 RAY HALL - PRESIDENT continued.... tap in the lavatory. My pleasure after some eight hours in eventually seeing Ray wilt, to get my own back on the long slog home via Eynsford and Farningham. Never can one expect to again enjoy the comradeship of such a companion or a greater test to find the calibre of a man. I recommend Ray as a man full of ideas for the future of the Club, a person commanding respect, of great personal integrity, a wonderful friend and companion worthy to be included in the Roll of great "Belgravians". H.S. items.label: December 1974
items.sum: Outgoing President Chas. Manning's farewell message on his fund-raising year, which raised £1,162.27 against a £500 target, handing over to Ray Hall.
items.s: £1,162.27 Outgoing President Chas. Manning's farewell message on his fund-raising year, which raised £1,162.27 against a £500 target, handing over to Ray Hall. We've come to the end of the year of the fast buck and the end of my year of Presidency. I thank you all for being so tolerant of my bullying ways - it has produced results! Consider when I declared that we should aim to make £500 and now look at the record behind you. Thank you all, and in particular that small hard core who've made it possible - Gordon Biscoe, John Baker, Evelyn Stimpson and my daughter Linda, who have done more for this office than I have. I would like to make these points:- 1) Don't imagine that I don't appreciate that there are those amongst us who want to belong to Belgrave Harriers to come up on a Saturday, have a run, and beyond that remain totally uninvolved. I do not condemn this thinking and wish it were possible for all of us to do the same but it is a luxury that we cannot afford on our present income. 2) Don't be overawed by the money we have made this year. With our potential it should be firmly put in its place - peanuts! 3) Don't let the searching questions your committee have been asking be obscured (i) our role in athletics at national level, (ii) the real future of Belgrave Hall, (iii) the promotion of all sections, (iv) expansion of facilities both indoors and out, (v) strengthening the club by concentrating on the wasteful dilution of local talent. It is my final, pleasant task to hand over to your new President for 1974-75. The overwhelming choice - Ray Hall. CHAS. MANNING Chas. Manning CHAS.
