items.s: S.R.W.A. Track League Final John Keown's report of the Southern Race Walking Association Track League final at East London Stadium on 26 July 1975, where Belgrave finished second to Brighton & Hove; as printed, Brighton 'led Belgrave by five points (101 to 106)' with one race to go. S.R.W.A. Track League Final Back in 1972 the Southern Race Walking Association decided to hold annually a competition with the object of encouraging clubs to support track walking and produce teams comprising walkers of all age groups. The competition is held in two stages; a qualifying round and a final. Each consists of four races; three for walkers over the age of 16 and one for walkers under the age of 16. Each club is entitled to start three walkers in each race, two to score. This year's final was held at East London Stadium on the 26th July 1975. Amongst the ten teams who had qualified for the final were Belgrave Harriers. The Club walkers were anxious to atone for their poor showing in the 1974 final when after winning the competition in 1972 and 1973 they failed to finish in the first three. In the first race of the afternoon, the 3,000 metres, Carl Lawton our hard working Walking Secretary began the fight for top honours when he finished 1st in 13:40. Newcomers Tim Thorogood and Steve Sharp finished in 5th and 10th places with times of 14:03 and 15:17. The next race, the 10,000 metres saw John Bromley complete his preparation for the World Veteran's Championships in Canada by finishing 3rd to British Internationals Amos Seddon (Enfield) and Stuart Maidment (Yeovil Olympiads). His time was 51:15. He was supported by Les Dicks and Martin Lewin who finished in 7th and 8th places with 53:42 and 54:26. The leading team positions at the half-way stage were Belgrave with 68pts, Brighton & Hove with 64pts and Enfield with 60pts. The third race on the programme was the 2,000 metres for walkers under 16 years of age. Our competitors in this race were Stephen Humphries and Desmond Bennett. Both gave of their best but failed to hold the much more experienced Brighton pair of O'Shea and Buchanan who finished 2nd and 3rd. Our pair, with times of 11:01 and 12:31, finished 5th and 10th. With one race to go Brighton led Belgrave by five points (101 to 106). Although John Hall, Ray Middleton and John Dunsford fought hard in the last race the 5,000 metres to close the gap, Brighton's Scottish International Alan Buchanan kept his club in first place by winning the race. Our three finished 3rd, 4th and 6th with times of 24:36, 24:46, and 25:11 respectively. The top three teams were Brighton and Hove 135pts, Belgrave 131 pts and Enfield with 108pts. Five Belgravians finished in an all-comers 5,000 metres race which did not form part of the competition. They were 6th Dave McMullen with 26:03, 9th Doug. Fotheringham with 26:30, 10th John Hall with 26:42, 13th Martin Bennett with 28:21 and 18th Joe Scamell with 30:14. Helping to run the meeting as she has done for the last three years was Mrs Dunsford, who ensured that full details of each race were available within 15 minutes of the end of each race. items.sum: John Baker reports on the club's bottle stall at the Merton Show in August 1975, which sold 3,047 tickets and raised £165 for club funds, and thanks the helpers.
items.s: The Merton Show John Baker reports on the club's bottle stall at the Merton Show in August 1975, which sold 3,047 tickets and raised £165 for club funds, and thanks the helpers. The Merton Show As the last bottles were put on the shelves and the numbered straws set out on the counter, the Merton Show opened on Sunday August 24th - very quietly. Luckily Monday saw the crowds flocking in and altogether 3,047 tickets were sold. This was the culmination of weeks of preparation by the team of willing members putting tickets in straws, arranging posters, shelving and scaffolding. I would like to thank all those members who donated bottles and also the following who made up the team: Ray and Pauline Hall Carl and Barbara Lawton Ron and Stephanie Langheim Gordon Biscoe John Morris George Piddington George, by the way, travelled up from Hayling Island to give a hand. My thanks also to Tom Carter and Arthur Penny for their invaluable help. The total raised altogether for Club funds was £165. Repeating Charlie Manning's words of last year, a great team effort just think what the Club could do. items.label: November 1975
items.sum: Gordon Doubleday's report of the 50th London to Brighton walk on 6 September 1975, won by Ray Middleton with Belgrave also winning the team race, with club statistics, results and a farewell to the landlord of the Queen's Head, Bolney.
items.s: Cock of the walk ! Gordon Doubleday's report of the 50th London to Brighton walk on 6 September 1975, won by Ray Middleton with Belgrave also winning the team race, with club statistics, results and a farewell to the landlord of the Queen's Head, Bolney. Cock of the walk ! SEPTEMBER 6th 1975 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON WALK. I have never been able to relate roads with numbers, the notable exception being the Brighton Road (A23). This year saw the 50th Annual Open Walk promoted by Surrey W.C. and as Big Ben boomed out six o'clock on 6th September some 98 walkers ( 9 teams and individuals) including 9 Belgravians set off. At the first check (5mls) Ray Middleton and Joe Toehill (Yorks W.C) led the way. On to about 15 miles and the race was beginning to take shape, the leaders were hammering away and Carl Lawton was a short distance away in third place. Dave King, John Moullin and John Dunsford soon followed giving us a strong position teamwise, and it wasn't long before the rest were through. Shortly after 20 miles Ray forged ahead and as Toehill weakened Carl came up into second place. John Moullin didn't look too comfortable, he has been having back trouble and it was good to see him in action again. John Dunsford, on his first Brighton, was steadily making headway. By Bolney (38 mls) Ray was well in command with Carl strongly behind him. Dave King and John Dunsford were still going well, particularly the latter. With about nine miles to go disaster struck. Carl was suddenly afflicted with leg cramp and in spite of roadside treatment was unable to continue and retired. So over Dale Hill and the six odd miles into Brighton Ray again led the field home. This repeated last year's double of winning the Hastings to Brighton as well. He was followed home by veteran Ken Harding of Royal Sutton Coldfield and Dave Boxall, the 100 miles specialist, of Brighton. In 9th place came John Dunsford, and this must rank as his best ever performance. We hope to see him again in action at what seems to be his best event. Another solid performance by Dave King brought him home in 19th place. At this stage we had the edge over Surrey W.C. for the team race, a few more crossed the line and then somebody called out, "It's Moullin" and John came in 26th to clinch the team race. So, for the 50th "Brighton" the Bels provided both individual and team winners, Cock of the Walk indeed! In 36½ place came the other two Johnnies, inside second class standard (try telling either of them that the other was 36th!) Our other two starters John Hall and Bob Picton unfortunately were among the non-finishers. It was good to see some of our younger walkers on the road as attendants. According to our statistician on the A23, Bels have won the team race no less than 21 times against 19 wins by Surrey W.C. Two clubs have won twice and six clubs once. We have provided individual winners in Tommy Green (four times), N.Guilment (once) and Ray Middleton (twice). John Keown has completed 17 successive Brightons, and of those in this year's race Dave King and John Morris have notched up 11. Dave King now has six winning team medals (between 1965-75) and is chasing George Beecham's seven winning team medals (1956-68). This year's field was the largest since 1956 when 106 started. 1. R.Middleton 8:10:21 (best performance 7:50:47/2nd 1970); 9. J.Dunsford 8:53:50 (no previous performance); 19. D.King 9:22:47 (8:46:01/3rd 1964); 26. J.Moullin 9:31:19 (8:22:35/4th 1969); =36. J.Keown 9:47:20 (9:24:26 18th 1960) =36. J.Morris 9:47:20 (9:20:38/16th 1960); Teams: 1. BELGRAVE H 36pts; 2. Surrey W.C. 45pts; 3. Verlea. "Regulars" on the Brighton Road will be sorry to learn that the landlord of the "Queen's Head", Bolney is leaving. This place has been a timing, feeding and sponging point for many years and has been run by the same family for 94 years. So we join in thanking Mr. Dollamore for his kind and cheerful service over the years and give him our best wishes. items.s: Maxwell stars Shaun Maxwell won the National Youths 3 miles walk title at Coventry on 18 October 1975, with Belgrave juniors 3rd team in the Junior 5 miles. Maxwell stars OCTOBER 18th 1975 - COVENTRY - NATIONAL JUNIOR & YOUTH CHAMPIONSHIPS. A great race by Shaun Maxwell gained him the National Youths title over 3 miles in 23:37 ahead of C.Hope (Steyning) 23:40. With Jonathon Dunsford backing up magnificently in 23:43 for 4th, we only needed one more starter to have been up in the medals. Steyning won the team race with 16pts D.Cotton of Holloway Polytechnic won the Junior race over 5 miles in 36:38 with Richard Tanner our first man home in 9th spot with 39:14. Martin Lewin was close behind in 12th position with 39:41 with Tim Thorogood 13th in 39:56 and Steve Sharp 22nd 41:40. The team race was an extremely closely fought affair. Our third and final scorer finished ahead of any other teams' third man but we still had to be satisfied with 3rd place and 31pts. Sheffield won and Holloway Poly were 2nd, both with 28pts. items.sum: Extracts from The Belgravian of 1950 (LCC Track Championships, Surrey County Road Relay win for the Underwood Trophy) and 1935 (club 3 miles track championship, subscription increase).
items.s: from the Belgravian ... 25 years ago ... and 40 years ago Extracts from The Belgravian of 1950 (LCC Track Championships, Surrey County Road Relay win for the Underwood Trophy) and 1935 (club 3 miles track championship, subscription increase). from the Belgravian ... ... 25 years ago SEPTEMBER 1950 - LCC TRACK CHAMPIONSHIPS ..... Gordon Lowers retained his 100 yards title in the good time of 10.6 secs on a very heavy track, and then Ches. Walker won the mile in 4 mins 28.8 secs. with Bob Taylor in second place. Jack Braggington was third in the 3 miles run which was won in a new record time, while in the Junior events we had D.G.McLean 2nd in the 1 mile with Ray Tooby, now in the Army, finishing 3rd. Maurice Jones, perhaps better known as "Glimpy", finished 3rd in the Junior 880 yards with his usual strong burst down the straight and should do well next season. SEPTEMBER 23rd 1950 - SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAY........ At Old Woking on September 23rd once again our team proved too good for the opposition and thus we won the "Underwood" Trophy for the third year running. Ches. Walker went off first for us and he beat Stone of Dorking and Martin of Walton AC to give Jack Braggington a useful lead, and his time of 14:12 beat the previous course record. Braggington did 14:38 to further increase our lead and then Len Adams returned 14:48 and when he handed over to Stan Davies the next team was not in sight. Stan did 15:16 but can feel very satisfied with the thought that he is our only runner to have been in all three of our winning teams. Archie Bedford was our next runner and he returned a time of 14:26 which beat the old record of 14:30 and then Bill Lucas took over for the final leg and he did 14:11 which was only beaten by Chataway of Walton, who put up a new record time of 14:02 for this course of 2.94 miles. ... and 40 years ago SEPTEMBER 14th 1935 - BATTERSEA PARK ....... ..... We also held our Club 3 miles Track Championship at this meeting and in winning for the first time, C.T. (Tom) Carter ran one of his best races to date. Unlike the 1 mile championship, he wisely let J.Parker go and worked up to his man gradually. When he did catch his rival he soon went in front, and Pat was well beaten long before the finish. He managed to retain his hold on second place, and Arthur Allum and Syd Ring had a fine tussle for third position, with Allum proving the speedier when they reached the home straight. Arthur Penny, our Empire Games 6 Miles Champion, made his first appearance of the season after his long enforced rest, and ran very wisely in qualifying for 2nd Class Standard. ...... items.label: November 1975
items.h: ROAD AND COUNTRY: Arise, awake, or be forever fallen!
items.sum: Gordon Biscoe reproduces his circular to Belgrave's cross-country and road runners setting out a plan to rebuild club spirit through pack training runs from Belgrave Hall under new captain Colin Pearson (succeeding Gerry North), with targets for the season and an encouraging progress report five weeks on.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY: Arise, awake, or be forever fallen! Gordon Biscoe reproduces his circular to Belgrave's cross-country and road runners setting out a plan to rebuild club spirit through pack training runs from Belgrave Hall under new captain Colin Pearson (succeeding Gerry North), with targets for the season and an encouraging progress report five weeks on. ROAD AND COUNTRY ARISE, AWAKE, OR BE FOREVER FALLEN! Shakespeare probably did not have Belgrave in mind when he originally penned the above words but broadly this was the basic message of a circular letter recently distributed to all our cross-country and road runners. To allow for anyone who may have been inadvertantly omitted in this circulation and because of its considered importance to our future successes I make no apology for reproducing the contents in part again now for general information, as follows:- Much has been said and written via the "Belgravian" etc. in recent years about our performances, and many comparisons drawn with the teams and triumphs of former years. However even the most loyal clubman must now admit that due to lack of talent, the ageing and loss of former stars, the lack of spirit or just plain apathy or whatever the reason, our performances and fortunes on the road and country during the last few seasons have been taking a downward trend and the end of last season saw us at a fairly low ebb. The fortunes of all clubs of course fluctuate from time to time but it is equally obvious that to put ourselves on the upward trend again a concerted effort is needed to rebuild our teams and just as important, team and club spirit, the basis of success. With these facts in mind certain plans have been made for the coming year which it is hoped (and in fact expected!!) that all active runners will support. These are best outlined as follows. THE OBJECT is to re-establish a club spirit by means of pack training runs centred around Belgrave Hall. This has been the basis of our (and other clubs) successes in the past and is currently working wonders for 'Gateshead' as those who saw a recent TV programme will have observed. The emphasis will be on 'youth' in an attempt to mould and integrate the youths and juniors which we have already got (with ability!) in with the senior members. As well as give guidance and assistance where necessary with a proper training programme. THE PLAN is, with Gerry North having expressed the desire to stand down as Cross Country Captain, that Colin Pearson will be nominated in his place at the A.G.M. with John Stow and Leo Coy as Vice Captains. A training programme will then subsequently commence as follows: TUESDAY EVENINGS LEAVE BELGRAVE HALL 6.20 P.M. SUNDAY MORNINGS LEAVE BELGRAVE HALL 10.45 A.M. Packs will be divided into the 'A' (or fast) pack led by Messrs. Pearson, Coy and Stow and a 'B' (medium) pack led by Messrs. Bruce, Biscoe and Mead. Provision will be made for a 'C' (slow) pack as the occasion arises. It is intended that all packs will leave the Hall together and then subdivide as necessary, therefore whilst it is appreciated that many runners already have their own established times and training programme it is emphasised that it is only planned to 'organise' you for two sessions per week and it is hoped that all will co-operate in order to achieve a united effort. For too long we have had too many odd groups going off at various times 'doing their own thing'. Flexibility will the keyword in the organising of the training runs with the emphasis on training so it is not envisaged, or expected to turn them into races. I would therefore stress that everyone is wanted to join in. You may not be planning to make the 'National' or Road Relay Teams, but all can play a role in encouraging and advising younger members or just helping with that aforementioned club spirit - as well as getting fit of course! Eccentrics and drop-outs we're not interested in! Generally no ambitious claims are being made or imposed, like winning the 'National' next year , that will follow! But a more realistic approach is to start with events we can improve in. Two targets we will therefore be aiming for is to improve our overall position in the N.S. League from 5th place last year (so a maximum turn out on these occasions please!) and a 'place' in the South of Thames Senior (we could win this one with the right support). Finally success will breed success, we have the facilities and organisational ability second to none, and a depth in numbers still the envy of many; the right combination of these will attract the brighter talents we need - so lets have a show of strength all round on 1975/76. I know everyone can't train from Belgrave Hall but if you can get there please do. The 'Points Competition' will operate again, and considerable effort has already gone into laying these and other plans - the rest is up to you to make these efforts worthwhile. For any information, comments or criticism (constructive please!) on the above or any other points contact any of those mentioned above. • • • At the time of writing some 5 weeks after having put these plans into operation (and with Messrs. Pearson, Stow and Coy having been duly elected at the A.G.M.) it is very pleasing to report that we have had a very encouraging response to this 'Call to Arms' (or should it be Legs!). Packs of runners, some 20 to 30 or more strong, are now regularly going out from the Hall. It's good to see Peter Carton and Richard Langley back in training on a Sunday morning together with Adrian Cook, whose talents we haven't had the benefit of yet due to the claims of his school; or Doug Maughan on a Tuesday evening 'mixing it' with Colin and Brian Gorman. Whilst in the medium pack Peter Gardner, Simon Williamson, Peter North and Brian Marmion have shown great improvement and enthusiasm. Having hopefully sounded a note of encouragement may I quickly add that this is, of course, only just the start and there is a long way to go. So I would like to express thanks to those who have already made an effort and request that they keep up the good work. To those who have not yet joined in - please get involved whenever you can. We do realise that there will be 'teething troubles' with some of our plans but given the chance we will sort them out. However as already stated, any suggestions, ideas or constructive comments are welcome - but please do make them constructive, in the right place and at the right time! In lighter vein, it is interesting to note the other ways in which the abovementioned plans have had an effect. Already this season Brian Gorman has bought a new Belgrave vest and raced three times. Already in the Walton Relay John V. Baker was seen to pass another runner on the fifth stage. This almost brought him a press interview with Tom Pollak until John mumbled something about Tom not having paid his subs! On another page can also be seen some typical Charlie Manning ramblings on his impression of the situation. Needless to say he's got the various packs and pack leaders all mixed up - but then if you can make an impact on anyone as thick as Charlie, it must mean something!!! items.s: We win our own '20' again D. R. Crookes's report and results of the Belgrave 20 mile road race at Wimbledon on 19 July 1975, won by Tim Johnston, with Belgrave winning the open team race but losing the Surrey Championship to SLH on a tie-break, and an appeal for prizes for the 25th race. We win our own '20' again JULY 19th 1975 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 20 MILE ROAD RACE. One hundred runners started in the Open 20 mile road race and of these 81 finished. The race was fairly comfortably won by Tim Johnston who, after the first five miles, was out in front in splendid isolation. Don Faircloth and our own Bill Weller had good runs to finish 2nd and 3rd. Good backing by Pat O'Connor and Lionel Mann ensured we won the open team race for the second year running. By the narrowest of margins we just failed to retain the Surrey Championship held in conjunction. Although equal on points to SLH their 3rd scorer was better placed. Thirteen of the fourteen Belgrave runners finished. These included Martin Best and John Wasbrough making their 20 miling debut and Geoff Pearson - still going well. Next year's race will be the 25th and to mark the occasion it would be an idea to give the first 25 finishers a prize. To cut down cost to the Club, however, I would ask that if anyone has a "redundant" prize or present at home they let either myself or a member of the Club Committee have it. This will enable you to get rid of unwanted objects and alleviate the need for asking for donations. 1. T.Johnston (Portsmouth) 1:44:33; 2. D.Faircloth 1:46:15; 3. W.Weller 1:48:50; 7. items.s: It's Stow again Report and full result of the club's autumn 5¾ mile road race at Wimbledon on 20 September 1975, won by John Stow from Pat O'Connor. SEPTEMBER 20th 1975 - WIMBLEDON-THE AUTUMN 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE. The first race of the 'winter season', the non-championship 5¾ mile road race, took place in sunny and warm conditions and although the majority of our top men gave this one a miss no fewer than 48 runners took part. After the customary rush around the initial circuits of the top part of the Common, the field settled down and before heading off down the dip towards the "Crooked Billett" O'Connor and Stow had begun their relentless push away from the rest. Colin Pearson found himself alone in 3rd spot and as the race took its course down Copse Hill and back up the steep Cambridge Road, leading positions were static. A brief pause at the top of the "kiss of death" enabled Colin to bring up the contents of his stomach but at least he was able to suffer in private for the leading pair, still shoulder to shoulder, were well over one minute ahead. At the War Memorial with half a mile to go John Stow tried to surge away into a decisive lead but was unable to bring it off. Pat O'Connor was still close on his tail as the final turn into Lauriston Road came up and the track man was forced to turn on another fierce burst to ensure his win was beyond doubt. Both turned in times considerably faster than their spring performances in the championship race. Michael Manning continued his progress towards the top and two other youngsters to run well were Simon Williamson and Pete Gardner. Messrs. Gorman and Maughan were locked in combat as the finish approached and the timekeepers were unable to split them although the former's "Rollerball" tactics got him the judges'verdict. Handicap: 1. items.s: Surrey C. C. League - Race 1 Report and Belgrave results from the first Surrey League match of 1975-76 on Wimbledon Common on 25 October 1975, where 41 Belgravians ran and the team finished 4th. Surrey C. C. League - Race 1 OCTOBER 25th 1975 - WIMBLEDON COMMON. A marvellous turn out of 41 Belgravians (including some of our walkers doing a spot of legal lifting) for the opening Surrey League Race gave Messrs. Biscoe and Pearson the first indication that their training scheme is bearing fruit. If as many toe the line for the away matches we will really be getting somewhere. Teamwise things were not quite as good as they could have been - just two more men in the 30's would have placed us right up within range of SLH and Aldershot. As it was we finished 4th but the result was fairly close and there are three matches to go yet. John Stow underlined the fact that he is the man of the moment by leading home the claret and gold vests in spite of the welcome presence of Dick Piotrowski and Bob Richardson. John Bicourt sportingly ran even though he was suffering from a twisted ankle and this worthy effort saved us from 5th team place. Colin Pearson had his work cut out to get in front of Leo Coy who is running better and better these days and particularly good runs came from Brian Gorman, closing in the Belgrave team in 60th place, and youngsters Simon Williamson and Pete Hardwick. Charlie Gillett always gives all he's got and it must have surprised many to see this 22.9/200 metre man breathing down Comrades Marathoner Arthur Bruce's neck. 1. P.Standing (Walton) 27:37; 2. items.sum: Leo Coy's notes on the club's 88th AGM at Belgrave Hall on 17 September 1975: officer changes, life-members and W. Couzens as new President.
items.s: A.G.M. NOTES Leo Coy's notes on the club's 88th AGM at Belgrave Hall on 17 September 1975: officer changes, life-members and W. Couzens as new President. A.G.M. NOTES SEPTEMBER 17th 1975 - BELGRAVE HALL. The 88th A.G.M. was the best attended for many years. Over 60 members were present to hear P.Hilliar deliver his last report as General Hon. Secretary, a position he has held for five years. J.Baker explained the new style balance sheet and commented that if all those miserable ----s had paid their subs we would have broken even for the year. Instead we made a large loss. A.Bruce and C.Lawton were elected life-members for their tremendous services to the Club. R.Hall relinquished the role of President and became General Hon. Secretary. R.Hopkins, for many years a popular Junior Hon. Secretary, resigned and Clive Shippen offered to take his place. R.Wyld took over the new position of Junior Team Manager. The Track Secretary's job became vacant* as A.Mead resigned after leading us through our best season for some years. G.Biscoe presented his plans to re-vitalise our road and cross country sections by holding regular pack runs from the Hall throughout the winter. It seems fitting that at a time when we are at last doing something to get Belgrave back to the top, we should have W. Couzens as President. This man is always involved in Belgrave activities - weight training in the winter, hammer throwing and coaching in the summer, not to mention jumble sales and barn dances. With R.Hall beside him as Gen. Hon. Sec. we have the right men at the top. Throughout this A.G.M. there was an air of optimism in Belgrave Hall. Perhaps it was because with people like W.Couzens, R.Hall, G.Biscoe, C.Shippen, R.Wyld, C.Lawton and J.Baker guiding us we cannot fail. Watch out you southern clubs we are on the way back. LEO COY * This situation was subsequently resolved in the following manner: John Martin to take on the new post of Track & Field Fixtures Secretary, Arthur Penny to become Officials Secretary - another new post, Ray Hall to look after the general Track Secretary's job, and Alan Mead to become Track Captain. items.sum: Ray Hall's farewell as President and first notes as General Hon. Secretary, with dates of 1975-76 meetings and 1976 championships.
items.s: Ray Hall writes ~ Ray Hall's farewell as President and first notes as General Hon. Secretary, with dates of 1975-76 meetings and 1976 championships. Ray Hall writes ~ The end comes so quickly, and my year as President has disappeared into history. First I must thank all my officials for their great help and tolerance during the past year. It's wonderful to be able to write that not one of my Club Officers let me down. Thankyou, gentlemen. My further education was assisted and enlightened by trips to the Isle of Man and Kirkby, Liverpool (with its defunct ski-run), and many other parts of the athletic scene. I must make special mention of the track and field section with its wonderful team spirit, led by the never complaining Alan Mead, well assisted by Pat. I then started to mention individual members of the team but quickly stopped because so many came to mind. I'll always remember them as great people, not just numbers and times. So another facet is added to my athletic outlook. My advice to all Belgravians is get involved in all parts and sections of the Club, the motto being "Get involved and get your money's worth." Congratulations to our new President Bill Couzens. I only hope he gets as much pleasure in his Presidential Year as I did. Good luck. Now, in my new appointment as General Hon. Secretary, I'm feeling my way, so I'll give you some dates of interest:- Southern Counties Meetings at Crystal Palace - December 10th, January 14th, February 11th. Championships 1976. May 15th recommended for County Champs. June 19th Southern Senior Champs at Crystal Palace. July 17th/18th Southern Junior & Youth Champs (venue not decided). August 6th/7th AAA under 20 Champs, Warley. August 13th/14th AAA Champs, Crystal Palace. continued over page continued from previous page Anyone interested in written tests for track and field event officials at Poly, January 9th - further information from Ted Stimpson our able Middlesex County Representative. items.s: YOUR ENTERTAINMENT LINE UP Social Secretary Bill Couzens' programme of club social events for winter 1975-76: jumble sale, dinner and dance, darts, jazz, the Jaguars, a barn dance and a riverboat shuffle. YOUR ENTERTAINMENT LINE UP SATURDAY 1st NOVEMBER - JUMBLE SALE Can we have your best jumble up at the Hall by Friday 31st October? Help will be greatly appreciated on the Friday night and, most important, selling on the Saturday morning between 10.30 am and noon. SATURDAY 22nd NOVEMBER - CLUB DINNER AND DANCE At the 'Worcester' (opposite Worcester Park Station). For only £4 you can enjoy a good meal and dancing. Music provided by a dance band until midnight and then a disco until 2am. Phone Bill Laws 337 7215 for further details but you'd better be quick, tickets are going like hot cakes! SATURDAY 13th DECEMBER - BELGRAVE DARTS CHAMPIONSHIP The 'Denmark Pot' will again be at stake at the Denmark Public House on Saturday 13th December at 7.30 pm. Entrance fee to be decided on the night. Enter your name on the list in Belgrave Hall or phone me. SATURDAY 20th DECEMBER - KEN COLYER 'LIVE' AT BELGRAVE HALL Another visit from Ken Colyer's All Star Jazz Band. Tickets 75 pence. Don't miss this pre-Christmas 'hoot'. SATURDAY 7th FEBRUARY - THE JAGUARS ROCK GROUP Remember the last time the Jaguars came to Belgrave Hall. If you were there you'll never forget it. Make sure you don't miss this chance to see and hear one of London's top semi-pro groups. Tickets 75p. FRIDAY 9th APRIL - BARN DANCE The Country Dance Band return again. Tickets 75p. BELGRAVE RIVERBOAT SHUFFLE Watch out for details of this exciting event coming up early next summer. Date to be decided. BILL COUZENS SOCIAL SECRETARY. Telephone 01-946 7490. It used to be "Scramble" (1) then "Red leader to angels one five" (1). A dozen years later it was, "10-4" (2), and half a decade further on we became familiar with, "Zero - we have lift off!" (3) Now we hear, "It's 6.20 let's go!" as the eloquent Colin Pearson gently persuades twenty three and a half (Bernard Merry) runners out of the doors of Belgrave Hall. Colin is very delicate at delivering his instructions because Brian Gorman is a bit sensitive. Other members of the pack well know the captain's kindly orders and the understanding way he cajoles them to attend fixtures. That his boss, Gordon Biscoe, in the Boffins department drafting out the master plan, secretly refers to him as "the Fuhrer" and the pack themselves are getting him an Iron Cross for Christmas, in no way reflects on this warm, human person. After the mass start, that sweeps majestically past the trickle of athletic flotsam from the cottage, the mighty Belgrave Harriers Racing Machine divides with fantastic precision into three. The leader for the premier pack is John Stow, who was nurtured at the Belgrave Breast and is now honed to a dangerous sharpness. A Titan of awe inspiring potential and putting it back in as, fast pack, leader. The second line of attack is spearheaded by Leo Coy (4) who is Battersea's answer to Anthony Quinn. His rumbustious bearing hides the mean streak of dedication that has superior runners stretched to breaking point. Don't be taken in by this man of few words - he's a killer underneath and built out of whipcord. The third pack is led by a contradiction - he runs beyond the pain barrier, the nerves of his brain obviously switch off yet he is an intellect. He looks like a shire horse but goes like Nijinsky - he can discourse on Alfred Shrubb, Yuri Gagarin, Grandma Moses, Christine Keeler or Socrates, usually does, and probably at 49 miles in a 54 mile race. You may not end up the best runner in the world but stick with Arthur Bruce and you'll know the displacement of every soldier at Waterloo and what the captain had for breakfast on all the second line frigates of the Japanese Navy on Pearl Harbour Day. Alan Mead. I can't say anything about him without being rude but he fits into the pattern by taking out specialist packs - that's the rubbish that cannot get into the three proper' packs. Ignore the selfish sods like Arthur Penny, Ted Stimpson, Charlie Manning and John Baker who do their own thing - badly. They are rebels, renegades and obviously don't believe in pack running. Treat with contempt Berry - always looking for an easy run - Richard Danpure surprise ????? winner of the Yacht '3' and Bob (Clean Air Duct) Glover, they have tired blood. The men to watch, to train with, to win with, are Colin Pearson, John Stow, Leo Coy, Arthur Bruce and Alan Mead. (1) R.A.F. Battle of Britain language. (2) Broderick Crawford in Highway Patrol (3) Saturn Rocket Launch. (4) His wife has beautiful hair. CHAS. items.label: March 1976
items.sum: The president announces that, after a members' questionnaire, a Ladies Section of Belgrave Harriers will be formed from 1st July 1976 and that talks are under way to bring in Selsonia Ladies Athletic Club.
items.s: The president announces that, after a members' questionnaire, a Ladies Section of Belgrave Harriers will be formed from 1st July 1976 and that talks are under way to bring in Selsonia Ladies Athletic Club. The questionnaire forwarded with the last Belgravian resulted in a substantial majority of club members in favour of a Ladies Section. After lengthy discussions, and bearing this result in mind, the committee decided that a Ladies Section should be formed within Belgrave Harriers taking effect from 1st July 1976. This decision was not taken lightly and when viewed objectively without the sentiment of our all male heritage there is no doubt that the future of club athletics lies in mixed clubs. This is endorsed by the attitude of local authorities who feel far more sympathetic to financially assisting mixed clubs in any immediate projects such as, in our case, upgrading Belgrave Hall and future ideas of a track headquarters of our own and the best possible track facilities. The financial aspect, however, was only a small issue compared with the general belief that ladies in Belgrave will assist in the recruitment of athletes, especially the higher teenage group who will be needed for future senior teams, therefore the hope of recruiting a ready made good senior to strengthen our teams would only be a bonus and not a necessity. As for the ladies, the intention is not to have a second rate Ladies Section but to build a strong section that will cater for all aspects of womens athletics with the future view of overall club strength. You may wonder how this can be achieved, where will the ladies officials, coaches and athletes come from. In this respect I can report that negotiations are going on between ourselves and Selsonia Ladies Athletic Club with a view to their incorporation within Belgrave Harriers. I might add that should our hope for a local authority grant fall through, or should our negotiations with our friends Selsonia fail, it will only make us more determined that our Ladies Section will succeed. Ladies, welcome! BILL COUZENS, President Bill Couzens BILL COUZENS President Belgrave Hall Selsonia Ladies Athletic Club Selsonia

items.sum: Club gossip column: membership figures, Charlie Gillett's radio show, the 88th Annual Dinner, a new A.A.A. club-colours rule, Ranjit Bhatia's visit, Duncan MacLean on television and the officials and helpers at the Belgrave Open '7' walk.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: membership figures, Charlie Gillett's radio show, the 88th Annual Dinner, a new A.A.A. club-colours rule, Ranjit Bhatia's visit, Duncan MacLean on television and the officials and helpers at the Belgrave Open '7' walk. grapevine Our total membership as at December 31st was 496, made up of 289 seniors, 27 juniors, 28 youths, 100 boys, 37 Honorary/Associate members and 15 2nd-Claim members. CHARLIE GILLETT, one of our leading track men, continues to grow more popular on Radio London. His rock 'n' roll programme 'Honky Tonk' is now extended from 11.30am till 1.00pm on Sundays and on Friday nights at 10pm he now presents a review of the best popular music of the week with 'Singles File'. It is a coincidence that BILL COUZENS and his wife GWEN share the same birthday - but even more remarkable is the fact that this date fell on the very day of the Club Dinner when Bill was installed as Club President. The 88th Annual Dinner was again a night to remember and ran so smoothly that one would not have guessed that the organisation of the function had passed from TED STIMPSON (who has done it so well for around ten years) to BILL LAWS for the first time. The new format of dance band until midnight and then disco through until 2.00 am was greatly enjoyed by all. Bill thanks all those who helped him in this his first year - in particular GORDON BISCOE. The jazz evening organised by GORDON was another great success and KEN COLYER and his band enjoyed themselves as much as the revellers. Instead of halting the festivities at midnight, the band played on for an extra hour. If you finished further down the field than 11th in the Club 10 mile cross country championship you will not thank the 'Grapevine' authors for reminding you that DENNIS JONES has been a grandfather for the past 18 months! Of course that makes BILL JONES a great-grandfather - doesn't seem possible does it. The A.A.A. General Committee have amended the rule regarding the wearing of club vests. From January 1st 1977 club colours MUST be worn by competitors in all open team and relay competitions unless the referee gives his permission for a change to be made. Colours will be registered during 1976 and of course ours will go on the books as 'Claret with Gold Hoop'. So if you bought your last club vest in the early fifties and it is now one of the pale pink variety with off-white hoop, faded after a quarter of a century of action on the roads, tracks and country of Britain, get a new one now. TOM CARTER ([phone number withheld]) is sure to have one in your size, aswell as shorts and track suits all in club colours. As the 1976 Belgrave 20 miles road race will be the 25th such promotion, it is race secretary DEREK CROOKES' intention to make it a bumper affair and have prizes for the first 25 runners to finish. So if you have any unwanted Christmas presents or prizes that you would like to donate, please contact Derek ([phone number withheld]). He did mention this in the last magazine and of course was overwhelmed with the response - in fact he only has about 23 prizes to find now! JOHN DUDMAN only appeared on the Belgrave scene just over a year ago but has soon become a popular member of the Duke's Joggers. He is off now for a spell in Australia but hopes to return before the end of the summer. The JAGUARS must be one of the best semi-pro rock groups in London and when they visit Belgrave Hall we are always pleased to see and hear them. Their last appearance on February 7th surely was the best yet. Tickets were sold out during the preceding week and on the night 200 Belgravians and their friends packed themselves into the Hall and danced with complete abandon until midnight. Over £120 worth of beer was downed and the crowd ripped like locusts through the refreshments, supplied by CARL and BARBARA LAWTON and RICHARD TANNER. Our thanks to MARTIN BEST for providing his 'Shambles Disco' during the interval; to the barmen, bless 'em; and of course to COLIN PEARSON for getting it all together. RON WYLD has been doing some calculating and reckons that the space gained by the Club in the national press during the last couple of months regarding the Boys 50 x 1 mile relay and the Club's donation towards the expenses of JOHN BICOURT's training trip across the Atlantic, would have cost any advertiser around £6,000. Apart from this there was coverage on Radio London and on radio and TV in Liverpool. Looking forward to that great feast of athletics this summer, the Olympic Games, you may like to be reminded of the actual dates of the athletic competitions:- July 23rd to 26th and 28th to 31st. RANJIT BHATIA who ran regularly for us some 15 years ago before returning to India, will be visiting the United Kingdom this summer. We look forward to renewing our acquaintance with him and in the meantime Ranjit sends his best wishes to all Belgravians. Two former members of winning 'National' C.C. teams have been to our fixtures. On Boxing Day we had DICK TOBIN eyeing the field and FRANK ABBERTON was at the Surrey C.C. Championships. It is learned that the Belgrave team of arena stewards has been asked to perform again this year at the Crystal Palace. Our veteran veteran runner DUNCAN MacLEAN was recently seen on television on a programme devoted to health and fitness in old age. We saw this remarkable nonagenarian running, dancing, singing and talking. He attributed his vitality to having a very energetic mother, and told the interviewer that he hopes to run a lap at the Palace on his hundredth birthday! ...at the Belgrave Open '7' Any open event promoted by Belgrave always attracts a good number of members, many of whom have their alloted jobs which they do faithfully year after year. Perhaps a mention of those around at this year's Open Walk will not come amiss. We had, of course, a number of active members whose performances can be seen in the result shown elsewhere. The field of 135 starters was got under way by our President BILL COUZENS - he is hoping to have to walk a bit farther this summer to retrieve some of those impedimenta which he projects so efficiently. Chief Judge was our own GEORGE BENTLEY and amongst those judging were FRED DENNY - happily recovered from his operation, FRANK JARVIS who has also had a bout in hospital, evergreen HAROLD KING with SYD SPENCER, HARRY SHIELDS and BILL TRUE to cast their eagle eyes on the proceedings. JOE WILSON was unfortunately unable to appear A hearty welcome to the Judges list to Mrs. BARBARA DUNSFORD. With a family so devoted to walking it would be hard to keep mum out. Congratulations Barbara upon gaining your initial grading. We hope that you will progress to the higher Grades in due course. At the corner of the Common was a figure in bright orange keeping the competitors sorted out from the traffic - it was JOHN DUNSFORD. He looked remarkably fit - a fortnight in a sunnier climate had obviously done him a world of good. John's illness gave cause for anxiety and a big factor in his excellent recovery was his supreme fitness. Our immediate Past President, RAY HALL, seemed to be everywhere and with that past master of the result sheet, JACK GOSWELL, was soon dispatched to a lonely place once the competitors started coming in. After the event competitors and officials alike need some refreshment and once again BRIAN GORMAN and his helpers were busy upstairs. The Grapevine memory is indebted to the programme for help in the foregoing, and these well produced documents were on sale before the event by JEAN MIDDLETON and JOHN KEOWN. It was good to see MICKEY PYER around again. CHARLIE CHURCHER was seen talking to old friends, whilst CHARLIE JONES, FRANK WEBB, NORMAN DEWBERRY and CHARLIE MacLENNAN were about doing various jobs around the course. JACK FLETCHER is obviously fit again and goes for a morning swim at Tooting Bec Open Bath! continued over page .... GRAPEVINE continued ..... We often get somebody turning up whom we havn't seen for years. This year saw DON HEATH - a member of our walking teams in the thirties, forties and fifties. For many years he has been living in Cornwall and is now back nearer to London. Amongst those of his contemporaries he was asking after BERT EAST - he was pleasantly surprised to be directed to a corner where Bert was preparing himself for another Open Seven. It's good to see JOE COLEMAN around again after a recent operation, he can't keep away from doing a lap or two of the hills even if only on a motorbike! Congratulations to JEAN and STEVE WHITE on the arrival of baby THOMAS. PETER NORTH has qualified for the gold award in the Duke of Edinburgh's Award Scheme - well done! It seems that Peter is the first Belgravian to have gained this award. From The Treasurer At the time of writing a great many members still owe their subscriptions for the current year. Surely it is not necessary for reminders to be sent so if you are in default pay up now. We must thank Ron Langheim for his effort in raising the sale of A.A.A. Draw tickets to 1368 books. Thanks also to the 120 members who took the trouble to sell the books but it is of note that six people sold one third of the total. A further fifty-eight sold more than ten books and fifty-six sold less than ten. You will see that there is further room for improvement so let Ron know your requirements for the next one and he will then order enough books. I notice that in the A.G.M. notes printed in the last issue it was not mentioned that John Plummer has taken over the medals and trophies from Tom Morrell. Tom did a good job over the years and I am certain all sectional secretaries will give John the help required to ensure the medals are engraved and ready for presentation. There are still a few small size club T-Shirts suitable for training in. Price £1.10. Designed by Charlie Manning, obviously they do not help you to run faster but you feel good when making your successes. John Baker Honorary Treasurer. items.s: FURTHER HONOURS FOR ED. LACEY Report on an exhibition of sports photography by club member Ed Lacey at the Kodak building in High Holborn, with a sketch of his career as a freelance photographer. FURTHER HONOURS FOR ED. LACEY An exhibition of sports photography, the work of our own ED. LACEY, was held recently in the Kodak building in High Holborn. Ed. is now acknowledged to be one of the world's leading sports photographers and his pictures are held in enormous esteem by sportsmen, sports fans - and his fellow photographers. It was just twelve years ago that Ed - then in his mid forties - gave up his "safe" job with Cable and Wireless Ltd to become a freelance photographer. From then on he doggedly pursued his chosen career - on many occasions bluffing his way into arenas and sporting events, including the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, to get the pictures he wanted. These days as an honoured member of his profession, such desperate tactics are no longer necessary, but the single-mindedness and determination are as much in evidence as when he first became an eager freelance. His work is particularly sought after for its dramatic composition and his ability to catch the climax of any event. Ed Lacey ED. LACEY leading sports photographer; exhibition at the Kodak building, High Holborn; left Cable and Wireless Ltd to go freelance about twelve years earlier ED. LACEY Ed. items.sum: History of the Haig & Haig Challenge Cup, Belgrave's first trophy, presented in 1897 by George Ogilvie Haig, won outright by Sam Sherrington and returned in 1974 by his son Lionel; the text says Sherrington's third win came 'by 1920' yet also 'after only six years'.
items.s: THE HAIG & HAIG CUP History of the Haig & Haig Challenge Cup, Belgrave's first trophy, presented in 1897 by George Ogilvie Haig, won outright by Sam Sherrington and returned in 1974 by his son Lionel; the text says Sherrington's third win came 'by 1920' yet also 'after only six years'. THE HAIG & HAIG CUP Clive Shippen writes Belgrave Harriers' annual dinner is always a very special occasion, but the 88th event held at the Worcester Hotel in November last was of extra-special significance. It was on that evening that Belgrave's first ever trophy, the HAIG & HAIG CHALLENGE CUP, reappeared in public and, in addition a renewed association was made with the whisky company itself, now John Haig & Company Limited. It was back in 1897 that the first association began. The Club had been founded only 10 years earlier and had recently moved from its first headquarters at "The Kings Arms", Ranelagh Road, Pimlico, to the "William the Fourth" in Grosvenor Road. This was the start of a pub-crawl which ended 24 years later at "The Swan" near our present headquarters. But it was not unusual for sports clubs to be attached to public houses in those days; there were very few sports facilities in Victorian times and public houses were popular meeting places. The publican was no doubt very pleased to let out a room to an athletic club whose growing membership (70), plus many supporters, all made good custom - particularly after a run or walk! Boxing gloves and punch bags were kept in the club room and Belgrave Harriers' boxing section worked up a thirst on the premises while the runners and walkers were out on the road heading for Battersea Park and the sprinters were at Lillie Bridge athletic ground being coached by the international dash man, Harry Hutchings. The boxing section did particularly well, eventually producing several leading amateurs, including Alex Lambert, A.B.A. Featherweight Champion in 1913. It was in 1897 that George Ogilvie Haig, a vice-President of the Club, presented the HAIG & HAIG CHALLENGE CUP. This, our first ever trophy, was presented each year to the member scoring most points in club handicap events (nearly all races were run on the handicap system). This beautiful ornate solid silver cup was formerly a rowing trophy and portrayed a coxless four at full stretch. Apart from being manufactured in 1843 its history is unknown. Rowers, boxers and athletes were closely allied in those days and it was not unusual for trophies to be interchanged. The cup was additionally engraved for Belgrave and dated 1897. The following year George Ogilvie Haig became our second president and had pleasure in presenting the trophy to the first winner, C.E. Lofts - especially pleasurable for Lofts as the award was accompanied by a case of the real stuff! G.O. Haig held the Presidency for five years and was reckoned in his time to be a good sport. During his term of office the Club laid on a boxing show at the "William", but at the last minute the police got to hear of the unauthorised promotion and it was rapidly turned into a smoking concert. Fortunately the Bels then, as now, were well equipped with 'entertainers'! In 1898, Sam Sherrington, the Club Captain, became the second winner of the trophy and by 1920 had run up two more victories, thus entitling him to retain the cup as his own. So, after only six years the HAIG & HAIG CHALLENGE CUP was lost to the club. It was another 8 years before the next trophy appeared - the Blackstaff Shield for the 7 miles cross-country championship of 1910. Seventy-two years of Belgrave history passed by after Sam Sherrington's outright win of that long lost trophy. Seventy-two years which saw events that those early stalwarts could not have dreamed possible.....our own freehold headquarters; national champions at running and walking; the production of 10 international runners from just 12 cross-country 'Nationals'; Olympic, European and Commonwealth medals; and many many other achievements. The HAIG hiatus ended in 1974 when Mr. Lionel Sherrington, Sam's son, contacted the Club to let us know that while those momentous years were rolling by the HAIG cup had been proudly displayed on the family sideboard. On being acquainted with the story behind the cup and its very special meaning to the Club, Mr. Sherrington most generously offered it back to us on the understanding that it would be well looked after. To ensure that this would be so our first ever trophy will be on display at each club dinner where it will be presented each year to the incoming president. A new plinth has been made which records the Cup's history, its return by Lionel Sherrington and its first new award to W. Couzens, our President. The HAIG cup had found its way home again and the Club is most grateful to Mr. & Mrs. Sherrington for their generosity. One other thing needed to be done - the renewal of our association with the original donors, now incorporated in John Haig & Company Limited. ... continued on page 11 THE HAIG & HAIG CUP continued ...... Following a series of meetings, the Company offered to sponsor the Belgrave 12-stage Relay for Southern Clubs this coming April. To mark our renewed association we were delighted to welcome to our Dinner Mr. Michael Henderson, the Company's Managing Director, who was able to meet our other honoured guests, Mr. & Mrs. Lionel Sherrington. The arrival of the HAIG Cup in 1897 marked the beginning of an unrivalled half century of Club history. Let us hope that its re-appearance will signal the start of another era of achievement. items.label: March 1976
items.h: High jinks and high hopes at the 88th ANNUAL DINNER and DANCE
items.sum: Report on the 88th Annual Dinner and Dance, the first organised by Bill Laws, with speeches, the presentation of the returned Haig Cup, Haig's sponsorship of the 1976 Twelve Stage Relay, the raffle and the disco.
items.s: High jinks and high hopes at the 88th ANNUAL DINNER and DANCE Report on the 88th Annual Dinner and Dance, the first organised by Bill Laws, with speeches, the presentation of the returned Haig Cup, Haig's sponsorship of the 1976 Twelve Stage Relay, the raffle and the disco. High jinks and high hopes at the 88th ANNUAL DINNER and DANCE Last year, following ten years of stirling service Ted Stimpson finally stepped down from managing the Belgrave Annual Dinner and Dance and Bill Laws took over responsibility for organising this, Belgrave's major social event of the year. Your Committee believing that the format developed over preceeding years would be adhered to were startled to learn of Bill's plans for major changes including a disco and extending dancing past the witching hour to 2 a.m. Small groups could be seen huddled together in Belgrave Hall and it soon became clear that there was support both for the new and old formats. What to do when the tickets and menus were already printed? As usual the experience and wisdom of your management team prevailed and Bill's compromise proposal for dancing to the Florida Band until Midnight followed by a disco until 2 a.m. was widely acclaimed as combining the best of the new and old. And so to the night. With tickets at £4 (the same price as 1974) a maximum number of 211 attended and what a night they had! A witty speech by our President ("the jumpers are jumping higher, the throwers throwing further, the walkers walking faster - and we're expecting the runners any minute now" - howls of derision from G. Biscoe and his cohorts on tables A B & C), insight into future plans and the possibility of a Ladies Section, ("the ladies would help Belgrave to lead out front" - who wrote your script Bill Couzens?) and generous undertakings from our guest. Frank Beckett, of the G.L.C. Parks Department, confided that Belgrave's home track at Battersea is next in line for the full treatment including tartan track, but naturally timing is doubtful in the present economic climate. Michael Henderson, Managing Director of the Haig Whisky Company presented Bill Couzens with the recently re-discovered Haig Cup which it's owner Lionel Sherrington has kindly re-donated to the club, some 90 years after its original presentation to Belgrave by the Haig Whisky Company. (In future the new Club President will be presented with this cup at each Annual Dinner & Dance). Michael Henderson was roundly applauded when he announced his Company's intention to finance the 1976 Belgrave Twelve Stage Relay which in the past has been used by the S.C.A.A.A. as a selection race for the National Championships. Other official guests welcomed to the Dinner & Dance were Mr. & Mrs. Frank Evans of the G.L.C. and Peter Barson of the Sports Council. With the official ceremonies over the evening moved on to dancing to the Florida Band and then on to the raffle; and what a raffle! Twenty prizes totalling over £100 in value, the majority of which had been generously donated by members. Many thanks to all those who donated prizes but particular mention of Gerry North for the fantastic supply of sports goods, including footballs, shooting stick, various rackets and holdalls. Colin Pearson won one of Gerry's donations, a pewter drinking mug and many of the Sunday pack felt this was his only chance of winning one! A huge piece of rolled beef was eagerly snapped up by a certain city jobber who shall remain nameless but Maggie Thatcher's advice seems to be getting home. Things must be tough! The draw was undertaken by 'Emu' Lawton ably assisted by Charlie Manning in a large box - later seen also to include a lady who also shall remain nameless. Half an hour in that box and Charlies dancing seemed to go to pot! At twelve o'clock the traditional circle, Auld Lang Syne and cheers for the President. The Florida Band disappeared, the bar stayed open and ten minutes later Peter Gurd sprang to life on the disco. And wonders to behold, no-one left. 211 people stayed on and had a whale of a time. There is one sight the writer, well lubricated by this time, will remember for a long time - Bill Merrimen doing his thing, a kind of combination of shimmy, palais glide, charleston with a splash of rock. The younger members were overawed; Bill revelling in the admiration proceeded to dish out his complete repertoire. His taxi had to wait for over an hour outside the Worcester Hotel until he was finally dragged away protesting, by a very patient wife, into the darkness. And after it was all over we sought reactions! An unqualified success .......... Chas. Manning Bloody splendid! .......... Tom Carter I only liked the first half, I can't remember the second.... Colin Pearson What dinner? .......... items.sum: Notice opening the Road and Country section: with the Poly. Marathon gone, the 1976 club marathon championship will go to the member with the fastest time in any RRC-recognised UK marathon between 1 April and 31 October.
items.s: BELGRAVE MARATHON CHAMPIONSHIP Notice opening the Road and Country section: with the Poly. Marathon gone, the 1976 club marathon championship will go to the member with the fastest time in any RRC-recognised UK marathon between 1 April and 31 October. ROAD AND COUNTRY BELGRAVE MARATHON CHAMPIONSHIP With the regrettable demise of the Poly. Marathon it has become increasingly awkward each year to designate a suitable and convenient marathon for the purpose of the Belgrave Championship. For example this year the AAA Marathon is being held in Rotherham on May 8th whilst the RRC Marathon (our choice last year) falls only two weeks before our own 20 miles road race. With a view to seeking a solution opinions were solicited from a selection of those most likely to be involved, with the expected result that you get as many opinions as people asked but no overall favourite. However, as an outcome from one suggestion made, the Committee have now agreed that this year as a trial case the Club Championship will be awarded to the Club Member achieving the fastest time in any marathon officially recognised by the Road Runners Club, within the U.K. and during the period 1st April to 31st October. Place medals will be awarded in a similar fashion. So road runners, the choice of race is yours and the'spin off' from such a scheme is that you can have more than one crack at the championship, although it is not anticipated that many will be intending to run a marathon every other week - apart from Lionel Mann that is. If you do have any other queries or comments (constructive please!) please let me know, but it is hoped that this will prove to be a practical solution to the problem. Gordon Biscoe Cross Country and Road Running Secretary. Gordon Biscoe Gordon Biscoe Cross Country and Road Running Secretary Lionel Mann Lionel Mann Belgrave Marathon Championship Poly. items.label: March 1976
items.sum: Road and Country notes on Belgrave runners' road and cross-country performances in late 1975.
items.s: Road and Country notes on Belgrave runners' road and cross-country performances in late 1975. John Davies became Vets AC Marathon Champion when he recorded 2:47:35 for 70th place in the Unigate Marathon last October. He was not the first Belgravian to finish,however. John Jackson, carving a niche for himself in the Belgrave road team, placed 31st in 2:33:00. Doug Maughan ran in a late season 5,000 metres at Crystal Palace on Nov.12th to clock 16:38, and he followed this a couple of weeks later with a trip to Gateshead for the 'Jackson The Tailor' international race : 1. B.Foster (GB) 2. J.Hermans (Netherlands); 3. A.Simmons (GB).... 91. D.Maughan (Belgrave). We are used to seeing Bill Weller leading home our team of ten-milers - as he did in November at Bracknell and Epsom, but just to prove that he's not afraid of getting his feet dirty, he has featured in several of our cross country teams this season and has even gone to the lengths of purchasing a pair of 'studs'. Inspired running came from Colin Pearson in the Hogs Back '10' when he recorded 53:18, less than 20 seconds behind John Jackson. But when it came to the Mitcham 25km he went one better and had the audacity to beat John by over 2 minutes. We lost our hold on the team race at Mitcham this year in spite of good running from Bill Weller, Pat O'Connor and Laurie O'Hara. Laurie was 1st veteran home for the 3rd successive year and placed 8th in the veterans' handicap held in conjunction. Running off scratch, he was giving away 66 minutes to the winner. Laurie was also in good form for the City of London Veterans 10 mile road race on New Year's day. He won in 52:57. items.s: Humorous boxed piece with a photo of Joseph McDonald modelling the Belgrave running kit of around 1951. Our model Joseph McDonald displays what the better dressed runner was wearing around 1951 - a charming ensemble of claret short sleeved jersey, hooped in gold with cross keys and portcullis motif over the heart, matched with a delightful pair of slinky 'off the knee' white cotton shorts. Those who know "our Joe" will have some difficulty in believing that as a lad he was a choir boy at St. Mary's, Kensington and was trained to serve at the altar. County Championships JANUARY 3rd 1976 - GUILDFORD - SURREY. John Bicourt rounded up his training for the week to 100 miles by leading the Belgrave team home in 4th place on the usual rutted Guildford course. But in spite of vociferous encouragement from our Boys and Colts (easily the noisiest on the course) our runners were not quite forward enough to get into the team medals. John Jackson showed up pretty well in 40th place but at the time was not able to count as a scoring team member. Charlie Walker took a nostalgic trip into the past as he toured the course in 121st place, back 25 years to that glorious day when he romped home to win the event. In the Junior race Pete Gardner managed for the first time to get narrowly ahead of Simon Williamson, and Michael Manning also ran well up in 14th position. We were unable to complete a team but these three, together with Adrian Cook in this age group next year, should bring home a set of medals. 1. B.Ford (Aldershot) 35:38; 2. items.s: Bicourt and Mann battle for Macher Shield Report and results of the Belgrave 10 miles cross country championship (Macher Shield) at Wimbledon on 10 January 1976, won by John Bicourt from Lionel Mann, with the handicap and the junior 5 miles championship, and two photos by Martin Best. Bicourt and Mann battle for Macher Shield JANUARY 10th 1976 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 10 MILES CROSS COUNTRY CHAMP. An unfortunate clash with the Mitcham 25km road race resulted in this year's Club '10' being a little short on 'star performers'. In cold and damp conditions Lionel Mann and John Bicourt, attired in full tracksuit, immediately went away from the field. They ran more or less together for the first of the four laps but then Lionel decided that the time had come to test the mettle of our Olympian. He raised the pace to such an extent during lap two that at times they were virtually sprinting and Bicourt later admitted that at that stage he was prepared to fall back and run for second place. But Lionel was feeling the pace too and by five miles John had gained the advantage only to be attacked again as they ran down the horseride on the far side of the course. On the last circuit, however, he got right away for a 43 second victory. Can this really be only his first senior Club cross country title? Brian Gorman ran the entire race on his own for try as he might, Doug. Maughan just could not get on terms with him on this occasion. It was Brian's third Club medal, his first over the country. Pete Hardwick is progressing nicely these days and it surely will not be long before the more seasoned campaigners are struggling to hold this youngster back. 1. J.Bicourt 63:53; 2. L.Mann 64:36; 3. LEAGUE - Race 4 Report and Belgrave placings from the fourth and final Surrey Cross Country League race of 1975/76 at Petersham on 21 February 1976, where Belgrave were sixth, with the final league table showing Belgrave fifth overall. SURREY C. C. LEAGUE - Race 4 FEBRUARY 21st 1976 - PETERSHAM. In the final Surrey Cross Country League race, held in Richmond Park from Ranelagh's headquarters, the Bels slumped to 6th team place after the previous race's sparkling 2nd. It was not surprising really. Although we turned out 28 runners we were missing over 50% of our more forward placers. Bill Weller led us home with a good 16th place over a course considerably shorter than those he normally traverses. Next home was Pat O'Connor, as reliable as usual, and Leo Coy had a great afternoon getting the better of Lionel Mann and John Jackson. In a short space of time John has become one of our most dependable team men. Revelation of the race was the running of Peter Hardwick. A year in athletics has seen him come on nicely; not the instant success of "here today and gone tomorrow" but the gradual, solid progress borne of hard graft. It was the first time he has made the scoring team - it is unlikely to be the last. ...5th Again Overall We finally placed 5th in the league for 1975/76, the same as last year but with 77 points less. Aldershot, Croydon and Hercules Wimbledon also remained steady in 1st, 2nd and 4th places but Walton shot up to 3rd in only their second season after gaining re-entry to division one. South London H dropped from 3rd to 6th and Ranelagh, after a solitary year in the premier division, were relegated. Ranelagh's place will be taken by Herne Hill H. 1. Commanding lead for Pat O'Connor CROSS COUNTRY AND ROAD POINTS COMPETITION. Leo Coy is keeping the scores this season in the points competition which seems to be lacking some of the wild speculation of last year - could it be that this time Alan Mead is now well clear of Charlie Manning who has only been able to amass an abysmal score of 3 points! items.s: Short note about young Belgravians playing football in Richmond Park before a North Surrey League race and then cheering on the team. Seen in Richmond Park before the start of the N.Surrey League Cross-Country Race was a group of young Belgravians, in full Belgrave colours, playing football. Football indeed!. yes, our youngsters very wisely do not restrict themselves to sheer running, participation in different activities is a sound basis on which to build one's athletics. When the race started they vanished into thin air to give vocal support to our team. They are discovering that life with the Bels is not only activity but comradeship and fun. items.label: March 1976
items.sum: Feature on John Bicourt taking unpaid leave from teaching to prepare for the 1976 Olympic steeplechase, with the club committee donating £250 towards his training costs, plus his facts, figures and annual progression.
items.s: Bicourt's Bid Feature on John Bicourt taking unpaid leave from teaching to prepare for the 1976 Olympic steeplechase, with the club committee donating £250 towards his training costs, plus his facts, figures and annual progression. Bicourt's Bid As many members will already know, John Bicourt has taken unpaid leave from his teaching post from the end of February through to the Olympics in a do or die effort to prepare in a "professional manner". He will spend six weeks in Mexico City training at high altitude with the Polish steeplechasers, at the invitation of one of the favourites for the event in Montreal, Bronislaw Malinowski, and following this he will move on to the United States to stay with Olympic Marathon champion Frank Shorter. By that time John intends being racing fit and will compete in the 'chase at the Kansas Relays, Texas Relays and Drake Relays. He will then return to Britain with the aim of making the international team v. East Germany. The British Olympic Trials will be held on the first two weekends in June and by the time they are over, if all has gone to plan, John will hold a best time for the season of well under 8:30. The Olympic Qualifying Standard is 8:32 but it is not John's intention to qualify with the minimum required and if fate is with him he will be around 8:20 by the time the Games come along. John broke through to international level on a steady 70 miles per week and this has got him below 8:30 but he has found that he cannot handle any more mileage than this AND carry out his duties as a housemaster and head of two departments at school. 100 miles per week including sessions of 10 x 1,000 metres over barriers requires extra sleep and the avoidance of the tensions and frustrations of school life. John has also included "hill work" this winter for the first time since his junior days, in an effort to drag out that extra speed needed during the last two laps of a race - his weakest point. So many times in the past he has felt good as the race finish approaches but has found it impossible to accelerate. Last season was intended to be low key with no steeplechases but urgent requests from the British Board had him turning out in spite of the fact that he had made his intentions clear beforehand. Nevertheless, without any preparation over the barriers he reached 8:33.2 and was rated 4th in the country at the end of the season. Of course anything could happen and with rivals of the calibre of Davies, Staynings and Coates he will have to be in top form to make the team but he has plenty of determination. In the Munich Olympics he went out as 50th best performer in a field of 51 yet came away 22nd fastest. John says: "At 30 years of age this is almost certainly my last chance at the Olympics and I intend to make it coincide with the realisation of the absolute maximum of my potential." Bold words and bold plans by John Bicourt; but the Belgrave Committee too have taken a bold, controversial and exciting decision in backing up their top runner and donating £250 towards the £600 - £800 it is going to cost him in training expenses this summer. ARM FACTS AND FIGURES: Born Putney 25.10.45. Height 1.77/5'10. Weight 68kg/150lb. Occupation - teacher. An international since 1972, having represented Great Britain about 17 times. 4th in Commonwealth Games 1974. Best times: 1,500m/3:48.6, 3,000m/7:59.6, 5,000m/13:57.6, 3,000mSC/8:26.6. items.s: SCAAA COACHING COURSE Brian Marmion's account of the S.C.A.A.A. coaching course at Crystal Palace in December 1975 attended by seven young Belgravians, thanking the club for paying half the cost. SCAAA COACHING COURSE DECEMBER 1975 - CRYSTAL PALACE. There were 150 people at the S.C.A.A.A. Coaching Course, amongst them seven Belgravians:- Stephen Sampson, Richard Danpure, Peter Crosbie, Paul Churchley, David Bailey, Peter Gardner and myself. I am sure we all found it hard work but enjoyed ourselves immensely. We all learnt a lot and will change our training programmes accordingly. In the 'Superstars Competition' held there, Peter Crosbie was the only Belgravian to win his group. Unfortunately David Bailey had to miss the last day of the course. I would like to take this opportunity on behalf of my friends and myself to thank the Club for putting 50% towards the cost of the course, which will help us to beat the so called 'stars', e.g. Brian Gorman, in the very near future. items.h: World Best for Belgrave Boys 50 x 1 mile
items.sum: Report of the 50 x 1 mile relay by Belgrave young athletes at Battersea Park on 8 February 1976, a claimed world best that raised £106 towards John Bicourt's Olympic training, with every leg's time.
items.s: World Best for Belgrave Boys 50 x 1 mile Report of the 50 x 1 mile relay by Belgrave young athletes at Battersea Park on 8 February 1976, a claimed world best that raised £106 towards John Bicourt's Olympic training, with every leg's time. World Best for Belgrave Boys 50 x 1 mile FEBRUARY 8th 1976 - BATTERSEA PARK. All right, so far as we know no club has attempted it before. And yes, no doubt when they do they will beat our time, for of our 50 young athletes the vast majority were-boys, colts, even "micro-colts". Nevertheless it was a stirring sight to see so many youngsters clad in claret and gold and doing Belgrave proud. The idea was for each boy to get sponsors who for a 5p stake could make a guess at the final overall time. The closest would win a £5 prize donated by Chas. Manning and the profits were to go towards John Bicourt's expenses in getting to Mexico City to train at high altitude for the Olympics. John started the run at 10am and for the next 5¾hrs-odd as each lad took his turn in the pouring rain he seemed to be transformed into a superstar. He wasn't just running around Battersea track carrying a baton, he was carrying the Olympic spirit, bearing a little of the effort that it takes to get to the "Games". Of course some blasted it from the start and paid for it. Some ran fiercely all the way while others made their big effort on the last lap - but they all ran themselves out. If John Bicourt does make it to Montreal there will be 50 lads glued to their TV sets this July knowing that they helped put him there, for when the sponsors dues were collected and counted there was a handsome profit of £106 to add to the £250 already donated by the Club. Gordon Doubleday and Tom Reynolds did a marathon job in the bitter weather, sitting throughout the entire event to time each boy. Anne Wyld did similar service as recorder whilst Brian Pritchard and his wife, themselves ridden with flu, dashed about phoning up reserves that were needed due to the flu bug decimating our team at the last minute. As for Ron who put it together - what can you say about a bloke who this time last year had nothing to do with athletics. He's got a few more grey hairs! ARM Final Time: 5hrs. 46mins. 39.8secs. items.s: Short note on the high standard of UK boy athletes in 1975, with Mark Shippen ranked sixth in the country in the pole vault. It is staggering to read the performances of the top Boy athletes in the United Kingdom for 1975. Performances like 10.8 for 100 metres and 1:56.8 for 800 metres - thats right, fifteen year old boys! Nevertheless, even at this exalted standard we have a representative. Mark Shippen was rated at number six in the country with his 3.15 metre pole vault. items.s: Around the schools.... Notes on Belgrave boys' school cross country results, including Brian Marmion qualifying for the Middlesex Schools race and Pete Gardner retaining the Wilson's School championship. Around the schools.... Brian Marmion qualified for the Middlesex Schools cross country race by placing 4th in the Richmond district race at Petersham. He was actually lying 2nd when, with the leader, he was mis-directed. He made up ground again once he was back on course but the end of the race came too quickly and at the finish there were still 15 metres between himself and the 3rd placer. In the Middlesex race at Harrow he placed 62nd and was second Richmond scorer. Pete Gardner retained his hold on the Wilson's School championship, reducing still further the record that he set last year. In the Surrey Schools race at Coulsdon on February 14th he was the first Belgravian home in 24th place. Adrian Cook and Simon Williamson, both suffering the after effects of colds, were 34th and 37th. In the junior boys race Mark Sinclair was 36th , John Fernee was 58th and Mark Sharp was 70th in a field of 140. items.s: Late news.... Late news notes on Jane Pritchard's first walk, John Blair-Fish's Fell Runner of the Year placing, Barbara Lawton's recovery from knee surgery, and Belgrave veterans at the Veterans National Cross Country Championships. Late news.... Jane Pritchard, walking her first race in Belgrave colours, placed 11th in the Southern Junior Ladies 2,500 metres race recently. She was in fact 4th Southern girl home, the others being guests. John Blair-Fish finished a worthy 6th overall in the 1975 Fell Runner of the Year competition, scores being calculated on each participants best 12 runs out of a possible 23 category 'A' fell races. Barbara Lawton seems to be recovering well from her recent knee operation. Her chances of competing this season were almost nil after the op. but are now reckoned to be fifty-fifty and on those odds she could still make it to Montreal. Our best wishes for a continued fast recovery go to her. At Parliament Hill Fields on February 22nd six Belgrave veterans were in action in the Veterans National Cross Country Championships. The over 40 race was won by Roy Fowler (Stoke) and John Davies was 61st in 37:10, Chas. Walker 112th in 39:31 and Don Bonsor 139th in 40:39. The team were 21st with 253 points. In the over 50 event 2nd claim member Jack Brown (Cambridge H) was the winner in 36:13. The Belgrave team scored 61pts for 7th place with E.Young 23rd in 41:23, Joe McDonald 31st in 42:26 and John Baker 44th in 43:47.
