items.label: October 1977
items.h: 1976 BRITISH HOGGAR MOUNTAINS AND BILMA SANDS EXPEDITION
items.sum: George Flanagan's account, as leader, of the 1976 British Hoggar Mountains and Bilma Sands Expedition, a first unguided crossing of the Sahara northwards from Lake Chad.
items.s: 1976 BRITISH HOGGAR MOUNTAINS AND BILMA SANDS EXPEDITION George Flanagan's account, as leader, of the 1976 British Hoggar Mountains and Bilma Sands Expedition, a first unguided crossing of the Sahara northwards from Lake Chad. GEORGE FLANAGAN writes of his experiences as leader of the 1976 BRITISH HOGGAR MOUNTAINS AND BILMA SANDS EXPEDITION The purpose of the expedition was to make a first ever crossing of the Sahara Desert from Lake Chad travelling due North using no local guides but relying solely on our own navigational aids and to explore the remote area of the Hoggar Mountains in the Sahara Desert known as the Tahifet Region and climb in the Atakor Region. On October 9th, 1976 six people in two specially equipped Land Rovers left Dover travelling through France and Italy to Tunisia and Algeria. The route planned going south was an easy one through the Sahara Desert via The Tademait Plateau, In Salah, Tamanrasset Agadez reaching Kano in Nigeria where final preparations were made for the formidable task of crossing the Grande Erg De Bilma from Nguigmi in Niger just to the north west of Lake Chad. To reach this point we had to make a long detour due to the river Komodougan being in flood. In this region just to the north of Abadam we found small villages where many had not seen white people before. A tremendous amount of preparation had gone into the proposed crossing northwards from Nguigmi. Our choice of two prepared routes was reduced to one due to the activities of the Taubau and the Frolinat Forces infamous for their kidnapping of M. Claustre. They had extended their activities to include a point where our firstly proposed route was due to emerge at the northern side and no one in the party fancied taking their chances with an encounter similar to the one reported several months earlier when the occupants of two Land Rovers were killed for their vehicles. The route we plumped for went almost due north and had only been previously attempted using local guides to lead the way. We were crossing using our own system of Dead Reckoning with a Sestrel Compass and using Stars and Planets at night to fix our position ready for the next days navigation. The first three days were fairly easy going in which we made good progress not having to deviate much from a straight line and using a track of sorts for about half the distance. The fourth day took us into the complex dune areas proper and we were constantly changing course, sometimes as much as every few hundred yards. The system used was for the lead vehicle to find a route through the dune field as near to our approximate direction as was possible to travel, weaving through the dunes and climbing when necessary, using the magnetic compass. The other vehicle would follow and keep an accurate Dead Reckoning Plot on the progress which would be plotted onto the large scale map at the end of the day. This worked very well but the nights would often be late by the time this plus sightings of stars had been taken to obtain the astronomical fixes. By now we were right in the middle of The Grand Erg which when translated means large sea of sand and this was a perfect description. As far as one could see in all directions there was nothing but a maze of endless rolling dunes. These constantly gave the impression of absolute obstacles but we always eventually managed to weave a way through or climb over when no way seemed possible. On one day we registered forty miles but only progressed little more than ten in the true direction of our goal. This continued for three days during which we sometimes had to travel away from our goal to avoid particularly difficult ranges of dunes which blocked our way. Driving through such terrain was a new experience. Often it was impossible to tell whether we were going uphill, downhill or on the flat due to having no datum point. Only the engine gave an indication and this often lied due to passing through particularly soft sections of sand. It was necessary to run fast at a dune face to reach the top in one attempt and there was always the risk of not stopping and sliding in a precarious manner down the steep face on the other side. On one occasion a vehicle was driven straight into a dune face which caused it to shed its ladders. It had been just impossible to see it as the horizon and dunes often merged and everything between became a brown matrix with no contrasts from which to pick out any detail. When vehicles became stuck it was a case of hard struggling usually managing to get an alloy ladder below the wheels to drive off only to have to repeat the process a few yards further on in many cases. It was certainly no difficult task to sleep at night! For three and a half days we lived in another world where all was sand and sky and where the adrenalin would often flow fast. It is perhaps put into perspective by a verse taken from one members diary as follows...... Moonlit dunes that stretch As far as imagination will allow Dunes and sand: valleys of hard "flying" sand as Vehicles sing along the packed Granules. Throw over the wheel and luckily The soft grey 'cement' is missed Yet again. Mind bending Expanses of sand that flow to The earth's curvature. Ridge Dunes with flying 'spray' Coming off the Cornices and Making driving more difficult Down wind where you've Found a col to lurch the Vehicle through. A ridge ahead - scream up To the top and hopefully the drop On the other side isn't too bad. A quick brake, and then slide - Pulses quicken - adrenalin flowing The vehicle dips, nose into Oblivion, Sky disappears over the roof Line - and your gone, down the Slope - second gear - metal and cogs Racing, finishing, bending - foot on the Throttle and you're down the slope And away fighting the steering Wheel as the drive wants to go Its own way. And then a mile away Its another ridge and more hard Work and sweat and tears and swearing And cursing as vehicles refuse to go where the drivers want them. Bilma Sands - an experience to end All. Something to always remember, to Relive, but most difficult to Recount. Having completed this vehicle section of the expedition we rendezvoused with three climbers back at Tamanrasset from which one vehicle with three non-climbing members returned to U.K. The remaining vehicle with six members drove towards the Tahifet Region, being a very remote point to the south east of Tamanrasset, and drove into the area as far as was possible going cross country with the vehicle. Here we set up vehicle base camp and then trecked in a further 9 miles on foot to set up our advance base camp from where we explored the mountain range. We had to carry all water from a point three miles short of advance camp and it took us four days to stock up the camp with equipment and food. Having spent time in some of the most beautiful mountains imaginable, we returned to the main Hoggar circuit where, notably, the French and Italians have put up a series of classic climbs. We repeated almost all of these and added three particularly good new routes. Practically all of the fortyone existing routes we did were first time British Ascents. items.sum: Note of the club officials chosen at the 1977 AGM, with Derek Crookes succeeding Ray Hall as General Secretary, Leo Coy taking over the Young Athletes Section, two new Life Members and two new Vice-Presidents.
items.s: NEW OFFICIALS TO THE FORE Note of the club officials chosen at the 1977 AGM, with Derek Crookes succeeding Ray Hall as General Secretary, Leo Coy taking over the Young Athletes Section, two new Life Members and two new Vice-Presidents. NEW OFFICIALS TO THE FORE Surely our line-up of officials has never been so youthful. At the 1977 A.G.M. Simon Holmes, Anna Matthews and Sheik Wahab were voted onto the Committee while Stephen Crosbie assumed the roles of Assistant General Secretary and Coaching Secretary. Ray Hall has given all but blood as General Secretary for the past two years and stepping down from that post he now takes on responsibility for our Ladies Section. Thanks Ray, for all your hard work, and good luck with our newest and fastest growing section. Taking over from Ray is Rutlish schoolmaster Derek Crookes, a quiet but dedicated man of athletics who already handles the jobs of Secretary of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association and Surrey Road Running Secretary. Another who deserves our thanks is the unflappable Brian Pritchard who has held our Young Athletes Section together for the last couple of seasons. This is a fifty-two weeks a year job and Leo Coy, who is taking over, will need a lot of support. While quite happy to take on the administration of this section, Leo will obviously not be able to do all the organisation on the day at each event due to being a key member of our senior team. Peter Hilliar and Bill Merryman are now Life Members of the Club. Peter has given sterling service as Track Captain, General Secretary and Assistant Secretary in spite of living away from our normal circle of activities. As for Bill Merryman, well, a member and official of 48 years standing and he still has a cheery word to say to everyone at our committee meetings - that takes some doing! Those worthy fellows John Martin and Brian Gorman have both been raised to the august status of Vice-President. items.s: from the Belgravian ... 25 years ago ... and 40 years ago Reprinted items from the Belgravian of 1952 on the first Road Runners Club London to Brighton run and of 1937 on the A.A.A. Championships, including the relay team's bronze medals. from the Belgravian ... ... 25 years ago LONDON TO BRIGHTON RUN......1952. Yet another chapter in the Club's long and successful connection with the Brighton road opened on the 27th August when five of our road runners were among the fifty odd starters in the first Annual London to Brighton run sponsored by the newly formed Road Runners Club founded by our Vice-President Ernest Neville...... From the start our new member Wally Wortley ran extremely strongly and in finishing so high up in such a distinguished field put up a really remarkable show. Our Marathon champion, Macdonald, despite a bad spell at about forty miles when he was nearly caught by George Chantler, finished very strongly, and George running his usual steady race also did very well indeed to finish inside seven hours. Arthur Whitehead after running with George to over 35 miles faded badly but managed to complete the course to make up our team which did very well to close in in such an exacting race at the first attempt. Arthur Penstone, suffering from an atrocious cold, did well to reach the 35 mile mark, but was soon afterwards forced to retire. Positions: 10.W.Wortley 6:28:34; 16.J.Macdonald 6:38:20; 17.G.Chantler 6:50:18; 21.A.Whitehead 7:14:58. ... and 40 years ago A.A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS......1937. Heartiest congratulations to our team placed third in the Amateur Athletic Association's 4 x 440 yards Relay Championship. This is the first time we have ever been placed and Messrs. Pack, Michael, Herbert and Bird will value their bronze medals. In the A.A.A. Championships proper, a week later, our representatives acquitted themselves well. Pat Parker was placed third in the 3 miles and earned selection against France the following week. Don Brown was third and Percy Wright fourth in the 2 miles walk, and Eddie Pack finished fourth in the final of the 440 yards championship. His time was 49 and one fifth seconds. We were also glad to see J.Dodd, representing the Northern Counties A.A., win the Pole Vault. The "Sporting Life" compiled a table giving winners six points down to one point for sixth place. This table took into consideration the distance championships decided earlier in the year, and was as follows:- 1.Achilles AC 41½pts; 2.Germany 35pts; 3.London AC 28½pts; 4.Hungary 24pts; = 5.Belgrave H and Greece 18pts; = 7.Milocarian AC and Blackheath H 17pts; = 9.Irish Free State and Salford AC 14pts. This shows us in a deservedly favourable position, and if E.H. Pack and J.Dodd had appeared on the programme in the club name, our tally would have been even more impressive. items.label: October 1977
items.sum: Letter from George Piddington complaining that members who failed to turn up cost the club's veterans team a full finish in the Crystal Palace Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay.
items.s: GEORGE IS UPSET ! Letter from George Piddington complaining that members who failed to turn up cost the club's veterans team a full finish in the Crystal Palace Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay. GEORGE IS UPSET ! Dear Editor, I would like to write through the medium of the Belgravian about my feelings and disgust at those who let the side down by not bothering to turn up at the Crystal Palace Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay on Sunday June 19th. As you know I ran in the Vets. team and it really hurt me and I was very upset for days afterwards to learn that had we finished a complete team of 25 (I think we only managed 22) we would have been the fastest vets. team in the country beating our nearest rivals by over 8 minutes. I think the persons concerned know who they are so I will not embarrass them by having their names mentioned, but they can be sure of feeling guilty next time they line up for the start of a club race. I feel very sorry for the officials in our club who put in a great deal of hard work to get teams together for this great event which can only come once in a lifetime. It does not require much effort to either phone or drop a line to those concerned to say if they could not make it, so a replacement can be nominated. I worked as usual in a night club (following a full days work) on the Friday evening arriving home 3.30a.m. Saturday morning. I did a 10 miles training run on the Saturday afternoon and was back in the club during the evening arriving home at 3.30a.m. Sunday morning, to catch a few hours sleep before getting up at 8 o'clock. I then drove up to Crystal Palace (from Hayling Island) very proud of the fact that I was taking part in such an event and wearing the colours of such a great club as the Bels. One of those who did not turn up had the excuse that he was tired while another was seen to be training that very day elsewhere, not far from Crystal Palace. Another who was supposed to be injured still went out training. Are they ashamed to wear club colours, or even run for the club? I feel that if a fine of some sort was imposed for everyone that does not notify the officials when they cannot run after having entered for an event they would soon think twice before doing it again. It cost the club £35 to enter the teams for the race. I think that I have made my point clear and what was to have been an event which I could look back on in future years as a proud participant has now been shattered by a mindless few who also let down 20 odd other runners in their team and the hardworking officials. George Piddington. George Piddington George Piddington ran in the club veterans team in the Crystal Palace Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay, June 1977 Crystal Palace Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay Crystal Palace Hayling Island

items.s: Eggbound Report of the 63rd Poly Marathon from Windsor on 11 June 1977, where Bill Weller led the Belgrave men home in ninth and the team placed third, every competitor receiving eggs. JUNE 11th 1977 - WINDSOR - POLY MARATHON. Eggbound The 63rd Poly Marathon, held on 11th June, was again sponsored by Goldenlay and started by tradition in the private grounds of Windsor Castle, and at a signal for Sir Roger Bannister 120 odd runners were bound for the finish at the Windsor, Slough and Eton Track. There was a little rain, virtually no sun, so nobody could complain of the heat. An added incentive to Belgrave competitors was that times would be considered for the Club Championship (to be decided on a similar basis to last year). Our first man in was Bill Weller in ninth position, Bill has had a busy season and it had made him fit. As usual Mr. and Mrs. Weller were there to give support. Our next was lion-hearted Lionel (how else can you describe a chap who however busy his job has kept him will turn out at any distance and fight all the way). Lionel was 61st at 20 miles and picked up 18 places over the last six odd miles. Doug. Brew revealed before the race that he had injured his ribs, but he showed his mettle by finishing a little way ahead of John Davies who had pursued him for many miles. John too had family support for Pam and the boys were at the track to welcome him in. It was good to see another Davies family supporting the lads, Stan (up to town from Suffolk) and Dai. Paul Pringle was unlucky to finish a few seconds over the 3 hours mark. Welcome to newcomer L. Collingwood who gamely stayed the course, and with more training and experience should be bringing his time down. In addition to the usual prizes associated with this classic event all competitors received two dozen eggs, which, according to the programme, were presented not thrown! The first ten finishers were to receive five dozen eggs, nice work Bill! items.s: Belgrave '20' Derek Crookes's report and results of the 26th Belgrave '20' on the Kingston By-pass, Wimbledon, on 16 July 1977, won for the fourth time by Don Faircloth of Croydon, with Geoff Pearson taking the over-50 veterans prize. JULY 16th 1977 - WIMBLEDON. Belgrave '20' The 26th Belgrave '20' on 16th July resulted, for the fourth time, in a win for Don Faircloth of Croydon in the fast time of 1hr.42min.53 secs. This year's race was of a higher quality 'up front' with 7 inside 1hr.50min. (as against 2 last year) and 26 inside 2 hours (as against 20 last year). T.V.H. ran out winners of the open team race, beating Croydon by 2pts. whilst Croydon easily won the Surrey Team race (the Surrey Championship once again being held in conjunction). Belgrave narrowly missed the Surrey 3rd team medals but there was one Belgrave prize - Geoff. Pearson won the 'Over 50' Vets. prize with a time of 2hrs.34min.23 secs. - not bad at nearly sixty years of age! Once again I would like to thank all the timekeepers, recorders, marksmen etc. for their assistance - it's no joke being stuck out on the Kingston By-pass for 3 hours and without their help the race would be impossible. In the 5,000 metres Alonso of Spain had the measure of him by 1.8 seconds - 15:15.0 to 15:16.8 - and in the 10 10,000 metre event the order was the same but the result was just as close - 32:08.9 to 32:10.3. items.sum: Bill Laws's report on Blackheath Harriers' Silver Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 19 June 1977, where non-appearances forced Belgrave runners to double up but youngsters ran promising times, with the full stage-by-stage times of the A, B, Vets. and Under 17 teams.
items.s: SILVER JUBILEE RELAY Bill Laws's report on Blackheath Harriers' Silver Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 19 June 1977, where non-appearances forced Belgrave runners to double up but youngsters ran promising times, with the full stage-by-stage times of the A, B, Vets. and Under 17 teams. JUNE 19th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE. SILVER JUBILEE RELAY Departing from the popular 100 x 1 mile format Blackheath Harriers celebrated Silver Jubilee year by reducing all teams to 25 stages of 1 mile each. The correspondingly large increase in the number of teams meant more runners on the track at any particular time and at Crystal Palace 24 teams took to the tartan in the morning and 20 of the faster teams in the afternoon. Belgrave entered a Vets. and Under 17 team in the morning and an A & B team in the afternoon. Due to the non-appearance of 25 runners several people competed twice, sometimes in 2 teams, to enable final times to be gained. Perhaps the bigger disappointment was in the Vets. team where, due to the non-appearance of 3 vets. doubling up became necessary. The final time of 2 hrs.22min.22secs. easily beat the winning vets. time of 2 hrs.30min.9.6secs. set by Sale Harriers and with 3 more of our better vets. 2 hrs.20mins. would have been on the cards. The running of two teams at a time put a strain on the handful of Belgrave officials who turned up to help out and it was almost inevitable that something would go wrong. Steve Williams was the unfortunate one - he hadn't stripped off ready to take stage 14 for the A team and his time represents some kind of record for running to the change-over point and doing a striptease while running the first 2 laps. There were however some very encouraging performances. In the A team Jamie Stevenson ran a stalwart first leg and Robin Brown confirmed Gordon Biscoe's predictions by running an immaculate 10th stage. John Bicourt ran a relaxed 4.20 before being rushed to Victoria Coach Station by Tom Carter to join the England team travelling to Turin. The most promising signs came from the Boys, Colts and Youths all of whom thoroughly enjoyed their racing. Checking on last year's times shows that all of them substantially improved their previous bests and some times were very good indeed. John Searle ran 5:04 and 5:05, Alan Perriam 5:07 and 5:00 but pride of place must go to 13 year old Matthew Cannon who confirmed that some of his reported timings at school were not way-out by running 5:03. Miss Baker became the first young lady to run for Belgrave in the event and Miss Pritchard the second - albeit as a protesting reserve but enabling the U.17 team to finish. Incidentally it is worth noting that the U.17 team's average age was 14 and if the youngsters keep up progress Belgrave's hopes for the future are high. Organisation of the teams proved once again how many of our active members fall out of circulation each year. This year, of the 110 runners entered, only 39 had run in 1976 and only 22 in 1975! Let's hope more people stay with it for next year. Finally my thanks to those who once again helped to make it all possible; especially Bill Couzens and Keith Sinclair on time recording. Brian Pritchard and John Baker on booking in arrivals and Gordon Doubleday on stopwatch. Bill Laws. SILVER JUBILEE RELAY 143 complete teams finished. Stage A B Vets. Under 17. 1. items.s: Quiz filler asking where the 'Olympic Games' were held between 1636 and 1850, answered on page 53: Robert Dover's Cotswold Games, until Dr. Penny Brooke founded the Much Wenlock Olympian Society. Do you know where the 'Olympic Games' were held between the years 1636 and 1850? Turn to page 53 for the answer. THE 1636 OLYMPICS After the death of the ancient Olympic Games in 393 AD there was a lapse in sporting activities but at the Renaissance, naturally, there was renewed interest. It was in the heart of the Cotswolds that Robert Dover held his Games in 1636, and they continued until 1850 when Dr. Penny Brooke founded the Much Wenlock Olympian Society. items.sum: Track and field notes for summer 1977: Gerry Deegan's club 3,000m best and Irish 5,000m win, Glyn Ratcliffe's discus club record, Cliff Brooks's decathlon, Mark Shippen's pole vault and Ernie Obeng's sprint records.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and field notes for summer 1977: Gerry Deegan's club 3,000m best and Irish 5,000m win, Glyn Ratcliffe's discus club record, Cliff Brooks's decathlon, Mark Shippen's pole vault and Ernie Obeng's sprint records. TRACK AND FIELD Gerry Deegan became the fastest ever Belgravian over 3,000 metres at Crystal Palace on May 18th. In the Philips Silver Jubilee Night of Athletics, he placed 7th in 7:59.1. At Limerick on June 2nd he took Eire's colours past the post first in the 5,000 m. with 13:57.0 in the Ireland v Greece international. John Bicourt gained selection for Britain in the GB v Italy v USA meeting at Turin on June 21st but was well down on his times of the past few years with 8:53.1 for 6th. John Stow, in Surrey's side for the SCAAA v Surrey v Wales v Police match on May 29th was unplaced in the 1500m. but nevertheless clocked 3:56.0 - a promising early season time. May 28/29th saw Cliff Brooks reaching his second best ever score in the inter-area decathlon at Southampton, adding 195 points to his A.A.A. Champs. 7th place tally earlier in the month. Among the ten events were two equal personal bests for Cliff - a 1.89m high jump and a 15.6 hurdles - and his final score of 6,695 was just 12 points shy of his own Barbados National and Belgrave record. Glyn Ratcliffe was in fine form at Aldershot on 15/16th June where the Army Championships were being held. He took the discus title with 50.42m - a new Club record - and also managed 14.04m for 3rd in the shot. Other important wins have gone to Glyn in the Inter-Services Championship (47.72m) and Surrey v Hants v Army (48.88m). Representing Surrey in this latter meeting Cliff Brooks placed 2nd over the 400m hurdles in 56.0 and Ernie Obeng again had the beating of Danny Laing but was in turn beaten by the Army's S.Hall - both recorded 10.8 for the 100m. Pride of place however, must go to our Super-youth Mark Shippen, clearing 4 metres yet again to take 3rd in this senior pole-vault competition. Going back again to the Army Champs at Aldershot, second over 400m hurdles was Mel Ford who we have not seen for a few years but was a regular in our league teams a while back. His time of 55.6 was not too far down on the winner, Walcot Taylor, and just to underline his current fitness Mel raced to victory in the Midland Counties A.A.A. Champs a few days later with 54.6. Ernie Obeng was our only finallist in the Southern Champs. with his 6th place in the 200m - 21.83. He was an unlucky non-qualifier in the short sprint with 10.76, as was Paul Whitby with his 15.69 high hurdles. Just four days after his record breaking exploit at Haringey in our fourth league match, Ernie was back again at the same track, exploding to two more outstanding sprint times. He equalled his new Club 100m mark of 10.6 and also shaved a tenth off Steve White's 200m record with 21.5. He has not left things to rest there however, for in August in an Open Meeting at West London he cut that 100m time again - to 10.5. items.s: APRIL 30th/MAY 1st 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY A.A.A. CHAMPS. PART I. Report on the first part of the Surrey County AAA Championships at Motspur Park, 30 April-1 May 1977, where Peter Crosbie won the junior pentathlon with a club record 2,598 points. APRIL 30th/MAY 1st 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY A.A.A. CHAMPS. PART I. Peter Crosbie added yet another county championship to his tally when he opened the 1977 season with a clear win in the junior pentathlon. In spite of actually winning only one of the five events, his speciality the javelin, his overall victory was by a convincing 100 points and his score of 2,598 constituted a new Club Record. Peter's individual performances were LJ 5.80, JT 53.66, 200 26.3, DT 30.78, 1500 4:59.0. Our senior relay squad had been tipped for a possible win but in their first outing of the year together the change-overs were a bit "rusty" and they were beaten by a slick Croydon team, 43.2 to 42.7. Both were inside the old championship best. Leo Coy placed 6th in the steeplechase with 10:30.2, Pete Gardner ran to a PB of 9:45.0 in the junior 3,000 metres and over the two days Reg. Hopkins piled up 5,581 points for 2nd in the decathlon. items.s: League starts with a win Report and results of Southern League match 1 at Wimbledon Park on 7 May 1977, won by Belgrave from Hercules Wimbledon thanks to Charlie Gillett's last leg in the 4 x 400 metres. MAY 7th 1977 - WIMBLEDON PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 1. League starts with a win Belgrave took the lead early in the afternoon but never had any chance of breaking away completely and as the relays came up Hercules Wimbledon were well within striking distance. In the final event, the 4 x 400 metres, they needed to beat us by three places to take the match and were doing just that before Charlie Gillett unleashed his full fury on the opposition on the last leg to save the day. Our winning points tally was enough to place the Club second overall in the league - a fine start. New member Jim Preston made a sparkling debut in winning both his hurdle races and Reg. Hopkins confirmed that he was in good shape by being our highest points scorer of the match. A fighting Jamie Stevenson boosted our middle distance points, running a personal best 800 metres in his first 1977 track race and in fact each of the middle distance events gave us at least 6 points, an improvement on how things stood at the end of last season. Stretching their unbeaten series of league sprints from one year to the next, Ernest Obeng and Jim Evans looked superb, with Ernie drawing gasps from the spectators each time he went into action. His first leg in the sprint relay seemed unbelievable as he rocketed past the opposing teams in the staggered lanes outside him, putting the Bels ahead after 100 metres with the advantage of the second bend still to come. An event as exciting as any was the pole vault where young Mark Shippen came up against ex-international Jeff Fenge of H.W. items.s: MAY 14th 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY AAA CHAMPS. PART II. Report and results of the second part of the Surrey AAA Championships at Motspur Park on 14 May 1977, where Ernest Obeng won the 100m in 10.9 and was second to Danny Laing in the 200m, and juniors Peter Crosbie (javelin) and Mark Shippen (pole vault) won titles. MAY 14th 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY AAA CHAMPS. PART II. Our double champion from last year's meeting, Jim Evans, has been finding things tough recently with injuries, moving home, etc. but Belgrave's colours were kept to the fore in the sprints thanks to Ernest Obeng, competing in his first "Surrey". He qualified for the 100m final with the fastest time and then sped to a 10.9 victory over South London's Danny Laing, 11.1. In the 200m Ernie impressively took his heat in 21.9, six metres clear of Croydon's ace sprinter Bob Benn, but come the final which was the last event in the nine hour programme, Danny Laing got his revenge with a 21.7 to Ernie's 22.3. No other senior medals came our way although there were a good sprinkling of 4ths. Cliff Brooks was cock-a-hoop with his 40.34m discus throw, beating a ten year old pb. On a brief holiday in the old country, John Thresher was our sole representative in the 5000m and we had no-one out at all in the 1,500m. Our junior athletes provided two winners in Peter Crosbie - his 6th successive javelin title - and youth Mark Shippen who collected the pole vault with no opposition. 100: 1.E.Obeng 10.9. 4.J.Evans 11.3. 200: 2.E.Obeng 22.3. 5.J.Evans 22.7. 400: 4.C.Gillett 52.8 (52.5ht). 800: C.Gillett 2:02.3(Ht). 5000: 17.J.Thresher 16:14.0. 110H: 4.P.Whitby 16.0. 5.C.Brooks 16.2. items.s: Bedford Blues Report and results of Southern League match 2 at Bedford on 28 May 1977, where a makeshift Belgrave team without Cliff Brooks and Ernest Obeng finished fourth and fell to 9th overall. MAY 28th 1977 - BEDFORD - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 2. Bedford Blues Our win in match 1 had placed us in second spot in the league and ready for great things but match 2 was where it all started to go wrong. With Cliff Brooks down at Southampton busy putting together a fine decathlon and Ernest Obeng suffering a pulled thigh muscle, our league team was suddenly a very makeshift outfit. Hot competition came from the up and coming Bedford and Chelmsford teams and with our older rivals Cambridge H. and Windsor also present the Bels. had an uphill battle keeping out of last place. Jim Preston suffering from "the night before" did not enjoy his 400m hurdles at all but by the time his high hurdles race came up he had recovered to give us one of our few wins. The other first places came from Reg Hopkins and Arnold Bentt in the jumps and Jamie Stevenson in the 800m. Reg also set his best ever time in the 200m. Young David Bailey who seems to have been around for years but is still only a first year junior impressed all with his very relaxed 4 x 400 relay run, coming on strong at the end of his lap. Surely his place in the team will now be a standard booking. Les Davies made his debut in Belgrave colours with 2nd in the triple and long jumps and is a most welcome addition to our ranks, whilst David Bradford came close to his best in the 1500m. So, fourth place it was in the end - sending us plummetting down to 9th overall. 100: 4.J.Evans 11.3. 4.C.Gillett 11.3. 200: 4.J.Evans 23.2. 3.R. items.s: O'Hara again Report and result of the club 10,000 metres championship at Battersea Park on 8 June 1977, Laurie O'Hara's seventh consecutive win and eighth Tom Carter Cup, ahead of Colin Pearson and Lionel Mann. JUNE 8th 1977 - BATTERSEA PARK - CLUB 10,000M CHAMPIONSHIP. O'Hara again Ten days short of his 45th birthday the remarkable Laurie O'Hara gained his seventh consecutive win in the Club 10Km championship and has now taken home the 'Tom Carter' cup on eight occasions all told. As the years go by the margin of his superiority remains as great as ever and he appears to be in no danger of being caught by any of our current members. This time his win was by over a minute and the entire field, barring Colin Pearson, was lapped at least once. The only flaw in Laurie's astounding record is the fact that he has not as yet gained the championship best time, his fastest in this race being 30:57.6 in '72 compared to Bob Smith's 30:31.2 in 1969 when the race first went metric. Overshadowed but not going unnoticed, Lionel Mann picked up his eighth place medal from the last ten races, having won in 1970. A second class standard medal went to Brian Gorman as a reward for turning in his fastest time for some years and Jamie Stevenson impressed onlookers by keeping well up the field throughout; no need for surprise, however, for Jamie seems to be a natural at any distance that he cares to tackle from 400 metres upwards. 1.L.O'Hara 32:07.0; 2.C.Pearson 33.15.4; 3.L.Mann 34:00.6; 4.B.Gorman 34:05.4; 5.L.Coy 34:39.6; 6.J.Stevenson 34:44.8; 7.P.Roche 35:11.2; 8.S.Masterson 35:55.6; 9.S.Williams 37:09.2 (1 lap extra); 10.K. items.s: Bouncing Bentt Report and results of Southern League match 3 at Croydon on 25 June 1977, where Belgrave were second to Blackheath, with Arnold Bentt's 13.99m triple jump and two junior records for Matthew King. JUNE 25th 1977 - CROYDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 3. Bouncing Bentt Finishing as second team kept us from slipping further down the league. We might have hoped to beat Blackheath H. before the event but their new member, international Mike Winch, not surprisingly made them a gift of the discus, shot and hammer and of course this also made their previous 'A' thrower a mighty powerful 'B' man; the 'Heathens' were therefore unstoppable on this occasion. Star of the Belgrave team for the afternoon was Arnold Bentt who suddenly and for no apparent reason added a "Beamon-like" improvement to his previous best triple jump. In 1973 Arnie was pleased to record a 13.30m effort but had not improved since, so this day's leap of 13.99m left him and others of our team astounded. On the cinders a track-suited Ernest Obeng guarding his injured leg against the cold still kept ahead of all others in the sprints. Paul Whitby and James Preston gave us maximum points in the high hurdles while Cliff Brooks broke new ground with a 52 metre javelin throw and succeeded in making Peter Crosbie a winning 'B' man for the day. Young Matthew King made a welcome first appearance for us and in picking up 1st in the 'B' discus and 2nd in the 'B' shot established two new junior records. It appears that our overall strength in jumps and throws is now leaving our middle distance men behind in points gathering and will soon be challenging our sprinters and hurdlers. 100: 1.E.Obeng 11.1; 4.M.Smith 12.2. 200: 1.E.Obeng 23.0; 2.M.Smith 23.9. 400: 3.C.Gillett 51.5; no 'B' competitor. 800: 4.J.Stevenson 1:59.7; 5.C.Pearson 2:01.1. 1500: 4.R.Brown 4:12.2; 5.D.Bradford 4:33.5. 5000: 4.J.Stow 15:20.4; 4.P.O'Connor 15:43.4. 110H: 1.P.Whitby 15.7; 1.J.Preston 16.1. 400H: 4.P.Whitby 63.6; 3.J.Preston 59.8. 3000SC: 4.A.Black 9:59.6; 4.L.Coy 10:22.8. 4 x 100: 1.Belgrave (R. items.s: Four records smashed Report and results of Southern League match 4 at Haringey on 2 July 1977, where Belgrave were second to Haringey & Southgate, with Ernest Obeng's 10.6 100m, a 42.3 club 4x100 relay record and Mark Shippen's 4.15m pole vault (the heading says four records, the text three). JULY 2nd 1977 - HARINGEY - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 4. Four records smashed So often we seem to rise to the occasion when the opposition is at its greatest. A win against the very strong Haringey & Southgate club was never on the cards but our boys did us proud with fine performances all round and three new Club records. Our sprinters were superb. Ernest Obeng swept away our complicated 100 metres list with a devastating 10.6 seconds and then started our 4 x 100 metres relay squad off to another Belgrave best - 42.3 secs - thus erasing that 1954 A.A.A. winning time from the record books. With our sprinters faster than any who have competed in claret and gold before, Mark Shippen now set about making himself highest ever Belgravian by tackling 4.21 metres in the pole vault. He had already smashed by 15 centimetres his own junior and youth marks of 4.00 metres to win the event but now some doubt existed as to the height of our senior record. Was it 4.19m.....4.20m perhaps? No one seemed to know for sure so Mark had the bar set at 4.21m. He wasn't too far away and it will not be long before he does beat that senior best of 4.18 metres. Nice running came from another of our youngsters Dave Bailey. His 400 metres showed just a hint of what this boy could be capable of with regular training. 100: 1.E.Obeng 10.6; 1.J.Evans 11.2. 200: 1.E.Obeng 21.9; 5.M.Smith 23.9. 400: 3.C.Gillett 51.0; 5.D.Bailey 53.8. 800: 4.C.Pearson 2:01.6; 2.R.Brown 2:01.1. 1500: 3.L.O'Hara 4:06.5; 3.S.Holmes 4:16.4. 5000: 2.J.Stow 15:37.4; 2.L.Mann 15.51.4. 110H: 2.P.Whitby 15.7; 1. items.s: A day to forget Report and results of Southern League match 5 at Croydon on 30 July 1977, a day of dropped batons and dropouts in which Belgrave finished fourth, stayed 8th overall, and Ernest Obeng's unbeaten league run ended in the 200m. JULY 30th 1977 - CROYDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 5. A day to forget This was the day when everything went wrong for the Bels. Dropped relay batons, runners pulling out in mid race, members turning up to support and finding themselves toeing the starting line - it all happened for our penultimate match. Luckily the clubs placed behind us in the league table were some points down so even with only two match points gained after a couple of hours of trials and tribulations our overall league position remained unchanged - 8th. The appearance of Glyn Ratcliffe's huge frame gave the Bels something to enthuse over but surprisingly even he, the Army Champion, was beaten in the discus. It just goes to show the standard of competition these days. At long last Ernest Obeng's unbeaten run came to an end. He took the 100 metres for his 19th consecutive league win but his young North London opponent had pressed him hard and in the longer sprint the decision was reversed. 100: 1.E.Obeng 11.0; 5.P.Halliday 12.1. 200: 2.E.Obeng 22.1; 5.P. items.label: October 1977
items.sum: Report and results of Southern League match 6 at Battersea Park on 20 August 1977, won by Belgrave on newly equipped grounds, lifting the club over Blackheath to a final 7th in Division 1.
items.s: Bels finish with a flourish Report and results of Southern League match 6 at Battersea Park on 20 August 1977, won by Belgrave on newly equipped grounds, lifting the club over Blackheath to a final 7th in Division 1. AUGUST 20th 1977 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 6. Bels finish with a flourish "We start as we mean to go on and we finish as well as we start but something always seems to go wrong in the middle of the season." Our Field Events Secretary has never said truer words than these, spoken after our exciting win in the final match. Battersea Park, not previously known for its fine athletic facilities had never looked better. Brand new equipment was on show everywhere: pole vault stands and landing beds, a hammer/discus cage, new high jump stands, all-weather javelin run-up, a cleaned up shot putt area and even a proper "laps-to-go" sign, all were there for our use thanks to the G.L.C. Parks Dept. (and the regular harrassment of the Parks Dept. by our Committee). The javelin run-up gave Peter Crosbie a boost as he launched his second longest throw ever and another to take full advantage of the new equipment was Mark Shippen. After winning at 4 metres Mark had the bar set at 4.20m in another attempt to make the Belgrave Senior Club Record his own. He cleared on his third try....only to dislodge the bar with his arm on the way down. The trackmen, of course, were still competing on the sluggish Battersea cinders but Ernest Obeng does not seem to worry what surface he runs on. He zipped to 10.9 in the 100 metres and with a winning lead of four tenths one could easily understand how he clocked 10.5 during the week on an all-weather track. Jim Evans backed up as reliably as ever in the 'B' sprints. John Bicourt turned out to give us a 5000m/1500m double and Ian Duncan, fitting into our team very nicely, scored well in the 'B' 1500, but again the most exciting race was the 4 x 400 metres relay. With our team looking for a fourth member, Ernest Obeng was cajoled into running his first ever 400. Jamie Stevenson, suffering from a cold, handed over near the front but soon Ernie was loping along in the rear, coolly taking his pace from the other runners. When they hit the straight he exploded into action and gave Reg Hopkins a slight lead. While Ernie recovered from "rubbery legs" the race see-sawed back and forth until Charlie Gillett again took the claret and gold to the front of the tightly bunched group with only 50 metres left. Ilford's man pipped him on the line to finally win the race, as thrilling as any international. This team victory leap-frogged us over Blackheath H in the league chart for a final 7th place among the 25 clubs in Division 1. 100: 1.E.Obeng 10.9; 1.J.Evans 11.3. 200: 1.E.Obeng 22.1; 1.J.Evans 22.9. 400: 5.C.Gillett 53.1; 5.C.Pearson 60.0. 800: 4.J.Stevenson 2:00.9; 3. items.sum: Report of the London A.A. (GLC) Championships at West London Stadium on 3 September 1977, where Ernie Obeng won the 100m in 10.6 and tied Les Hoyte at 21.7 in the 200m, and Belgrave were third for the Club Trophy.
items.s: SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - LONDON A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the London A.A. (GLC) Championships at West London Stadium on 3 September 1977, where Ernie Obeng won the 100m in 10.6 and tied Les Hoyte at 21.7 in the 200m, and Belgrave were third for the Club Trophy. SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - LONDON A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS In the GLC Championships our ace sprinters were again to the fore. Ernie Obeng was a clear winner of the 100 metres in 10.6, two tenths clear of a "blanket-finish" for second place. International Les Hoyte (Thames Valley) was awarded the silver medal with our Jim Evans in 5th place but sharing the same time, 10.8, as Hoyte. It was an equal personal best for Jim. Ernie handed another defeat to Hoyte in the 200m although this time they were both given the same time of 21.7, whilst 5th place again went to Jim with 22.6. Jamie Stevenson placed 6th over 800m in 1:58.8 and Belgrave finished up third for the Club Trophy with 12 points to Thames Valley's 32 and Shaftesbury's 23. Back Page: Walker Graham Seatter en-route to a fine 2nd place in the A.A.A. 3,000 metre championship. Photo by Paul Dong. Graham has had a remarkable year, clocking up a couple of fast mile races against Ilford's Roger Mills at the Crystal Palace, winning the Club 3,000 metre championship in 12:31.8 and following this time with a lightning 12:14.9 for 2nd in the A.A.A. Victor in the G.L.C. Championships in 12:33.2, breaking Paul Nihill's record by seven seconds, he has also led the field to the finish in the Enfield 20km (91:01), the Ilford 10km (43:09) and the Lambeth 10km (44:43). 1977 has seen Graham emerge as one of the main contenders for the Commonwealth Games in Edmonton, Canada next year. items.label: April 1978
items.sum: Editorial praising the club's young athletes - the girls' walking team, Joann Warnett, Richard Dorman, the Youth cross country team and Mark Shippen - and the three men who organise them, Carl Lawton, Ray Hall and Leo Coy, urging members to take an interest in the youngsters.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial praising the club's young athletes - the girls' walking team, Joann Warnett, Richard Dorman, the Youth cross country team and Mark Shippen - and the three men who organise them, Carl Lawton, Ray Hall and Leo Coy, urging members to take an interest in the youngsters. How heartening it is to see our youngsters pushing the name of our Club to the fore. Only eighteen months after the first girls joined Belgrave Harriers the signs are that we have the fastest improving ladies walking team in the country. The great thing is that they become stronger with every week that passes and all have youth on their side. Whilst most of our lady walkers have already made their names well known to us through their deeds on road and track it must be mentioned that another lass, fourteen year old Joann Warnett, is also making a name for herself in the world of cross country running, winning the Wandsworth Schools event, finishing highly placed in the Greater London Schools race and gaining selection to run in the All England Schools Championship. Do not imagine, however, that our young men are letting the ladies have the stage to themselves. Junior Captain Richard Dorman leads by example and this past winter season has seen him develop into a fine walker, already making his presence felt among the seniors, and as our leading Youth cross country runner has brought the Bels to victory in their Surrey C.C. League events. The cross country team that followed Richard is being viewed with great interest as well, for all still remain Youths next winter. With the summer season now approaching it will be interesting to see how Mark Shippen continues his progress in the pole vault. Last year while still a youth he ranked =22nd in the Nation's Senior list and 5th among the Juniors. And of course there are quite a few others - jumpers, throwers and runners - who have also already made their mark in Senior competition while still teenagers and who should be ready to improve again with another winter under their belts. This progress has not come about by pure chance. Three men have put a great deal of their time and energy into organising our young teams' training and competition - Carl Lawton (walking), Ray Hall (Ladies cross country, track and field) and Leo Coy (Youths and Boys). Their tasks can be counted perhaps the most rewarding in our sport; continued at the foot of page 5. EDITORIAL .... continued from page 3. helping the development of young athletes on the way up. On the other hand they are most certainly at the same time the most heartbreaking when things are not going well and when the general membership shows little or no interest in what they are trying to do and offering them no help with their efforts. Need we say more! One way in which all members can help is simply by taking notice. Ask our youngsters how their training is going, when will they be competing next, how did they get on last time. It means a great deal to be noticed by those who "matter". items.sum: Grapevine club news column: members abroad (Stuart Masterson, Graham Seatter, Allan Callow, John Knifton), births, Charlie Speechley's 90th birthday, Bernard Eglington's retirement, Cyril Gittins' R.W.A. presidency, Don Maclean's darts win, the club's 1977 membership figures and other notes.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine club news column: members abroad (Stuart Masterson, Graham Seatter, Allan Callow, John Knifton), births, Charlie Speechley's 90th birthday, Bernard Eglington's retirement, Cyril Gittins' R.W.A. presidency, Don Maclean's darts win, the club's 1977 membership figures and other notes. grapevine Stuart Masterson has returned to Australian for a couple of years; let us hope that we have not seen the last of this friendly road runner. Stuart would be more than pleased to hear how his old colleagues are getting on so why not drop him a line - 56 Birtwistle Plac[illegible] Poleystone 6111, Western Australia. We are also very sad to see the return to New Zealand of Graham Seatter but hopefully we will be able to see him in action later this year via our TV screens when the Commonwealth Games at Edmonton, Canada, take place. Graham made many friends while over here - walke[illegible] and road runners - and this is one of the great things about our spor[illegible] our common interest in athletics that serves as a basis to meet and enjoy the company of folk of all nationalities, from all walks of life However, another Belgravian is planning to return to the UK this summer - Allan Callow. Allan, a past committee member of our club has enjoyed a deal of success while in New Zealand. On October 8th he won an over distance 20 mile Walk at Dunedin beating the NZ 50Km Champion John Rayner in the process, having set a pb of 36:03 for 5 miles the previous week. Many congratulations to Carl and Barbara Lawton on the birth of son Colin, who arrived on October 23rd weighing 7lb 12oz. And while on the subject of prospective members we must also welcome Faye, daughter of Bernard and Margaret Merry, who was born in December Charlie Speechley recently received a 90th Birthday Card signed by the President and a number of members. He also received a presentation plaque from the Veterans A.C. He was at the Murphy Shield (10 miles walk) Race and was soon chatting to old friends. He also made the acquaintance of our youngest member, Colin Lawton - 90 years between them! Surrey County Womens' A.A.A. soon took advantage of our facilities for the ladies. They held their cross country championships there in December. In charge of the proceedings was Win. Shepherd with a number of members helping in the background. We were pleased to hear that Past President of the Assn., Mrs Savage (Win's mother) is still about and enjoying life at eighty plus. The Boxing Day Meeting usually attracts the odd older member and this year it was F.A. (Mick) Walker, cross country and road runner of the thirties and forties. He scored in a number of Surrey County Championship wins, but he was perhaps best known for his runs at 20 miles and the marathon (nothing longer in those days). During World War II he won the Finchley '20'. He has lived in Cornwall for a number of years. John Knifton writes from Austin (Texas) where it is much hotter than it is here. Because of the heat he trains late in the evening but even so it is still too hot for speed work. Consequently when he goes to a cooler place for a race (some hundreds of miles away in many cases) the lack of speed work plus Anno Domini begins to tell. However it is good to see his name occasionally in the U.S.A. results. He hopes to visit the U.K. in 1979 - give him a number Carl! Bernard Eglington informs us that he is retiring this year. He will be cutting down on his forays into Lancashire for the occasional spin. He plans to keep his tracksuit aired regularly on the front at Colwyn Bay. When he first joined us he was a runner with the R.A.F. (he also sported a Derby & County Vest). He switched to walking and soon became a regular member of our teams at all distances gaining a number of winning and place medals. Merton Schools' have a nice muddy cross country course from their sports ground at Beverley Meads (hard by Beverley Brook and the woods at the foot of Wimbledon Common). A number of Belgravians were representing their schools at this year's championships; star of the meeting was Richard Dorman, Raynes Park High School, who not only won the race for the oldest age group but set a new course record. Warmest congratulations to our Q.P.H. member, Cyril Gittins, upon being elected President of the Southern Area of the R.W.A. Cyril has also had a spell in the Chair, is a Grade I Timekeeper, and is a regular official at our Battersea Park meetings. A "back-room boy" whose continued service makes our sport possible. You should have seen them ... past champions Arthur Penny and Tom Carter showing each other their pensioners bus passes while waiting for the runners to reappear after the first lap of our cross country course. We won't insult them by saying how spritely and fit they look, as we know full well that the only reason they don't don a pair of shorts each and set out with the competitors is that they might embarrass the Club by getting among the scorers again! Meanwhile, one of their peers, Harry Shields, always searching for another cultural pursuit, has taught himself to paint by attending evening classes, and we are pleased to say that some of Harry's work was recently on exhibition. What talent we have in the Club. Well done Don Maclean, who has managed to get his name on the "Denmark Pot" by winning our Darts Championship. It is particularly appropriate that Don should win this event at last for he was one of its instigators some dozen or so years ago. At the end of 1977 the total strength of Belgrave Harriers stood at 563 members - 494 men (278 Seniors, 30 Juniors, 26 Youths, 107 Boys, 25 Associate Members, 7 Honorary Members and 21 Second-claim Members) and 69 women (9 Seniors, 6 Juniors, 49 Girls, 2 Associate Members and 3 Second-claim Members). items.label: April 1978
items.sum: Walking secretary's review: the ladies' team fifth in the National Women's 5Km, new recruits Shirley Rook and Linda Nicholls, the men's teams in the National rankings and junior championships, and tributes to Graham Seatter, Ray Middleton and John Hall.
items.s: WALKING Walking secretary's review: the ladies' team fifth in the National Women's 5Km, new recruits Shirley Rook and Linda Nicholls, the men's teams in the National rankings and junior championships, and tributes to Graham Seatter, Ray Middleton and John Hall. WALKING National Medals for a Belgrave Ladies Team. - Not an impossible dream but almost a reality. In the National Women's 5Kms walk championship at Birmingham in December we finished 5th only 7 points from 2nd place and that was with the misfortune of a disqualification without which we would have been placed. Since the last edition we have increased our ladies section by a sufficient number to give us a team to be reckoned with. It took eighteen months to gently suggest to Shirley Rook that it would be the best policy for her to join us and eventually she made her decision and is now our number 1. Also joining us recently was Linda Nicholls who will be able to compete in the team in a few months. (She was quickly followed by her brother Michael). As to the men - 2nd overall in the National rankings - we would have won it had we started a Youths team in '76. But this year we have already started off on the wrong foot. The National, Junior, Youths and Boys at Wimbledon, was the first time that the Boys championship was to be included in the tables. Fortunately we just started a boy[illegible] team but not the team it should have been and we finished last. In the Youths we did not start a team although one was entered. Fourth in the Juniors was the best we could do with what we had but if..... Thanks are extended to all who turned up to help make the event a success. Graham Seatter has returned home and will leave a gap difficult to fill. He managed to fit into 12 months what most of us would do in three years. He arrived as a "useful" walker, he went through bad spells, foot injury, anaemia, a hospital operation, had holidays in Scotland, Ireland, Cornwall and the Isle of Man but still managed to win the National Junior, Leicester 7, Lambeth 10Kms, Enfield 20Km[illegible] and finally his parting triumph the Belgrave 7 and of course he was part of the many Belgrave team victories during the year. One of the dangers of signing a new walker who will immediately fill a team place is that he will push out one of the old brigade. This method has been tried for years but Ray Middleton still comes back!! Always a stalwart, always there in the Open team wins, and first man in the National 50Kms, Hastings and Brighton. John Hall is a hard worker who arrived on the Belgrave scene in 1971 as an average mid field man. Over the years he trained, he raced and slowly improved, then '77 was the year that he made the grade. Six years to get there but now, in the first 10 in the opens, an equivalent of sub 52 minutes for 7 miles in the 11Kms at Imber Court, a sub 70 minutes 15Kms and then the Sussex 10 miles title in '78. He also did the Hastings and beat a few notable distance men. Looking to 1978, well by the time you read this the National 10 will have passed by. National Titles are not impossible but............ There is always a team placed to be filled - Bob Picton at Highgate, Jon Dunsford at Luton, Richard Dorman (in his first outing as a team member) at Imber Court. We have a few new faces in the club and the future is rosy if the backing can be provided - a turn out of four starters in the 50 kilos will not win the team of eight! Carl Lawton, Walking Hon. items.s: Walking reports from August 1977: Belgrave team wins in the Hastings to Brighton and the Lambeth Festival of Race Walking, Carl Lawton's South Western Counties 10Km win, and Graham Seatter's records at the London Vidarians 5 miles and the Enfield 20Km. On August 6th Belgrave again took the Hastings to Brighton event thanks to the trio of Ray Middleton (4th 5:42:37), John Hall (8th 6:03:33) and Carl Lawton (15th 6:16:19). Alain Moulinet of France won the event, the 40th time it has been held, in 5:34:54. The pace had been fast throughout with 50Km coming up for our men in 4:34:55, 4:52:55 and 5:54:24. Dave King and John Keown also competed for the Bels whose score of 17 points was 6 points too good for second placers Brighton & Hove. One week later came a sparkling 1 - 2 from Graham Seatter and Carl Lawton in the Lambeth Festival of Race Walking at Brockwell Park. Graham had just over half a minute on Carl at the finish of the 10Km. 44:43 to 45:15, with Amos Seddon (BoE) a further five seconds down. Other Belgrave placings were: 10.J.Hall 48:06; 15.R.Middleton 48:59; 26.J.Dunsford 53:08; 34.R.Day 54:36; 37.D.Fotheringham 55:31; 42.S. Bennett 56:32; 52.J.Morris 59:59. Once again the team race went to the Bels with 12 points to Brighton & Hove's 23 and Boro' of Enfield's 24. In the Youth's 5Km at Lambeth Richard Dorman placed 6th in 25:49 with T.McDermot and P.Morris also competing. Diane Cook was third home in the Women's 10Km and Jane Pritchard was in action in the intermediate girls 5Km. August 20th saw Carl successfully tackling the South Western Counties 10Km at Weymouth, winning in 46:46, while over the London Vidarians 5 mile course Graham Seatter zipped to a record 34:59. The fearsome conditions did not deter Graham Seatter from blazing from start to finish to win the Enfield 20Km on August 28th. At 10Km he was timed at 44:30, over a minute up on Seddon, and in torrential rain he drew even further away to set a new personal best of 91:01. Ray Middleton was 15th in 100:37 with Doug. Fotheringham also in the field but Carl had to retire due to back trouble. In the womens 5Km Anna Matthews placed 5th in 30:53 and Jane Pritchard 7th in 32:40. items.h: SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON. LEICESTER'S TURN!
items.sum: Report by G.S.D. of the 1977 London to Brighton walk, won by John Lees of Brighton & Hove, with Leicester taking the team title and Belgrave second (Ray Middleton fourth), plus a Belgrave 1-2-3 in the G.L.C. Championships 3Km.
items.s: SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON. LEICESTER'S TURN! Report by G.S.D. of the 1977 London to Brighton walk, won by John Lees of Brighton & Hove, with Leicester taking the team title and Belgrave second (Ray Middleton fourth), plus a Belgrave 1-2-3 in the G.L.C. Championships 3Km. SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON. LEICESTER'S TURN! This year saw 69 starters in the Open London to Brighton Walk, five of whom were ours. The weather was kind, a little breeze and a little sun but no rain. In the early stages Ray was with the leaders with Dave and Ron walking together not too far down the field. The two Johns completed our team and, if all went well, one of these would be our fourth scorer. By twenty miles Ray had lost a few minutes on the leaders who were moving very well. About halfway John Morris retired; our remaining four were still going strong. Dave was able to open up a gap on Ron (suffering the effects of a recent cold) but Ron always had Dave in sight on the long stretches - it's always good to have someone in view on these long efforts! Thus the race had developed and history was made when John Lees became the first Brighton walker to win this event, his time of 7h.54m. 52s being very good indeed. He was well ahead of Alan Moulinet the Frenchman who had won the Hastings to Brighton a few weeks earlier. Ray was beaten into fourth place by Ken Harding (Royal Sutton Coldfield) who this year broke Pat Duncan's Manchester to Blackpool record. Soon the blue vests of Leicester came rolling in and they had three men home before our second man, Dave, came in and before Ron came in a fourth Leicester man appeared to give them the team title. Congratulations to Leicester who won the race thirty years ago. The battle for placings in the team race was now on, Ron soon came in followed by a Brighton man and with three men home from each team Brighton had a two points advantage. A stolid John Keown arrived four places ahead of our rivals and so we took second medals. This was John's 17th consecutive Brighton! Thanks again to the usual band of helpers, particularly Richard Dorman who cycled down. items.s: SEPTEMBER 10th 1977 - SOUTHWICK - SOUTHERN R.W.A. CHAMPS. Report by G.S.D. of the Southern RWA Juniors, Youths and Boys walking championships at Southwick, with Richard Dorman second in the Youths 5,000m, followed by a note on John Hall's 3,000m pb in the Southern 3Km championship at Crystal Palace. SEPTEMBER 10th 1977 - SOUTHWICK - SOUTHERN R.W.A. CHAMPS. A week after the London to Brighton Walk a small band of Belgravians made the trip to Southwick on the Western suburbs of Brighton for the Southern RWA Juniors, Youths and Boys Championship. The course was based on the Green which is almost exactly 1,000 metres around. Our sole representative in the Boys 3,000m was Kevin McDermot, a newcomer who clocked a creditable 17:11 for 17th. Kevin and his brother Trevor look tough and strong and are training with Ray Middleton who lives nearby - those Hendon roads will soon need re-surfacing. The Youth's 5,000m gave us our best result with Richard Dorman taking second place to Gordon Vale (Surrey W.C.) in 25:13. The aforementioned Trevor was 11th in 26:44 with Peter Morris 18th in 28:37. When Richard becomes eligible to represent us we should have a good team. In the 10,000m Junior Nigel Morris 20th in 56:06 and Stu Bennett 11th in 57:38 were obviously not at their best but worked hard against the odds. G.S.D. John Hall's pb for 3,000 metres took another dive on September 14th at Crystal Palace when he clocked 13:04 for 5th. The event was the Southern 3Km championship won by Lightman (Met WC) in 12:40, although first to cross the line was guest Canadian Marcel Jobin in 12:23.6. Carl Lawton placed 3rd in the championship with 12:45.0 while Jonathon Dunsford 14:05 and Ron Day 14:28 also competed. items.s: OCTOBER 15th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - R.W.A. JUNIOR,YOUTHS & BOYS CHAMPS. R.W.A. under-21 champs Report of the R.W.A. Junior, Youths and Boys walking championships held from Belgrave Hall, where Belgrave's Junior 10Km team came fourth. OCTOBER 15th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - R.W.A. JUNIOR,YOUTHS & BOYS CHAMPS. R.W.A. under-21 champs This was only the second time these championships have been held and of course, the first time from Belgrave Hall. We had competitors out in each of the age groups, closing in teams in the Boys and Juniors races. Over 3,000 metres our boys team placed 12th with 96 points - K.McDermot 19th in 16:50, G.Sexton 36th in 17:54 and S. Pritchard 59th in 22:19. Richard Dorman was well up the field in the Youths 5,000 metres, placing 6th in 24:33 with 23rd T.McDermot in 27:00 and 31st P.Morris 27:44. It was in the Junior 10Km, however, that we came closest to the medals, our team of J.Dunsford 16th 16:28, S.Bennett 22nd 52:46, N.Morris 27th 53:39 and S.Sharp 33rd 54:17 reaching 4th out of the 9 teams with 50 points. items.s: Note that no Belgrave men were in the Great Britain team for the 1977 Lugano Trophy, listing the Belgravians among the officials and recalling past Belgrave placings by George Williams (1961) and Ray Middleton (1963). Unfortunately there were no Belgrave men in the Great Britain team for the Lugano Trophy. Carl Lawton narrowly missed selection as did Ray Middleton (who competed in 1961,63,65,67,70 and 73 a feat no other walker has equalled). However a number of Belgravians were on the Officials List, and looking at the programme we find Fred Denny (Recorder) Jack and Joan Goswell (Results) John Keown (Judges Recorder) Ray Middleton (Chief Steward Refreshment Station) and Jean Middleton (Sales and Programmes). Glancing at previous results we find two Belgrave names in the Individual placings, George Williams third in the 20 Kilos in 1961 and Ray Middleton second in the 50 Kilos in 1963. items.s: NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - ENFIELD. DOUBLE EVENT Report and results of the Enfield Open 7 miles walk meeting, where Belgrave won the men's team race and the girls won the senior women's 5,000 metres team race. NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - ENFIELD. DOUBLE EVENT On November 12th Club history was made at Enfield for not only did we notch up another scratch team in their 54th Open 7 miles walk but our girls won the team race in the Senior over fifteen 5,000 metres. The meeting comprised five events and we were represented in four of them. Taking the afternoon's events in order, first the Girls (11-15)2,500m and amongst those lined up was Tracey McDermot. This was her first race and wisely she let the more experienced ones go away, nevertheless she persevered with a fine style and with more experience is going to be challenging the others. Next the Senior Women's 5,000m which turned out to be between Epsom and ourselves. Anna soon established herself with the leaders with Diane not too far behind and Jane putting up her usual fight to keep us in contention. With vocal support our trio maintained their positions to give us a one point victory. Congratulations to them - may this be the first of many. Meanwhile the Boys (13-15) 5,000, had got under way and Kevin McDermot was already making his presence felt, but as the race progressed some of his speedier rivals pulled away, but he showed his fighting qualities to bring out a personal best. The main event, the 7 miles saw the Mexican E.Vera in action, for two of the three laps he led Bob Dobson (Southend), but on the third lap he was away on his own to finish in 48:44 with Dobson second. Easily the best of the remainder was Graham, whilst Carl was showing young Colin what its' all about (he slept through the proceedings). John was in good form and soon appeared and it was not long before Ray came in to give us another team win. Shortly before the hour was up Trevor McDermott crossed the line - only 16 years of age and '7 in the hour' in his first season. Trevor and Kevin are both strong with good styles and are training under the eye of the old master himself, Ray Middleton. Another improving youngster showing his paces was Peter Morris who is showing some of the Seniors a clean pair of heels. G.S.D. items.sum: Report and results of the 58th Belgrave Open Seven Miles Walk at Wimbledon, won by New Zealander Graham Seatter in his last walk before returning home, with notes on the club officials and on Havering AC's walks the next day.
items.s: NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN '7'. BON VOYAGE ! Report and results of the 58th Belgrave Open Seven Miles Walk at Wimbledon, won by New Zealander Graham Seatter in his last walk before returning home, with notes on the club officials and on Havering AC's walks the next day. NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN '7'. BON VOYAGE ! The 58th Open Seven Miles Walk was once again a triumph of Belgrave organisation and Belgrave walking tinged however with some regret as our popular New Zealander, Graham Seatter was due to leave for home the following Monday. There was general pleasure that his last walk for us (for a while) brought him a fine win over the Sheffield 50 Kilos specialist, Jake Warhurst. With Carl and John (who nearly caught him) finishing in good positions and with Ray giving his usual support we held off a strong challenge from Steyning, now a strong force to be reckoned with. We had the usual backing of non-scorers and for the first time four of our ladies took to the road (unofficially of course!) and Shirley, Anna, Diane and Jane impressed us all by their determined walking. There was the usual crowd of Bels doing their jobs, headed by our President who was Starter and Referee. Amongst the Judges were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Syd Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson. Ray Hall together with Fred and Bill were logging them in, the sheets going in to Jack Goswell and Frank Jarvis, assisted by their wives to get out the results. Also seen on the course were Charlie Churcher, Charlie Jones, Tommy Scrimshaw, Frank Webb, Norman Dewberry and Charlie MacLennan. Tommy Cook's wife, assisted by other ladies dealt with refreshments. The whole of the proceedings were masterminded by Carl and once again our thanks and full marks to him. It is fitting to close by wishing Graham and the charming Rosemary "Au Revoir" we hope that you enjoyed your visit to the U.K. as much as we enjoyed your company. Good Luck with your walking in New Zealand and may you soon be back in the Claret and Gold of Belgrave. items.s: DECEMBER 11th 1977 - BIRMINGHAM - NATIONAL WOMENS 5km CHAMP. OUR GIRLS JUST MISS NATIONAL MEDALS Report and results of the National Women's 5km walking championship at Birmingham, the first time a Belgrave ladies team ran in a senior national championship, finishing 5th, four points off the medals. DECEMBER 11th 1977 - BIRMINGHAM - NATIONAL WOMENS 5km CHAMP. OUR GIRLS JUST MISS NATIONAL MEDALS On this, the first occasion that a team of Belgrave Ladies turned out in a Senior National Championship, our girls did us proud by coming within 4 points of a set of National medals. The race was held over five laps and the entry was the largest ever received for this championship. The team was greatly strengthened by the inclusion of a new Belgravian, Shirley Rook, a budding policewoman. Unfortunately on the first lap our other policewoman, Diane Cook, who had incidentally been on night duty all week, came under the judges ban - giving our team hopes a bit of a blow. However, Shirley and Anna Matthews started steadily and worked their way slowly through the field together to finish 11th and 12th and with young Jane Pritchard backing up well to place 24th our team closed in a pleasing 5th 1.C.Tyson (Lakeland) 24:02; 11.S.Rook 28:06; 12.A.Matthews 28:24; 24. items.h: DECEMBER 31st 1977 - WIMBLEDON - HORWOOD CUP '7'. AGONY CORNER
items.sum: Report and results of the Horwood Cup seven miles walk on a new hilly Wimbledon course planned by Carl, won by Richard Dorman, with matches against the Metropolitan Police and Combined Clubs.
items.s: DECEMBER 31st 1977 - WIMBLEDON - HORWOOD CUP '7'. AGONY CORNER Report and results of the Horwood Cup seven miles walk on a new hilly Wimbledon course planned by Carl, won by Richard Dorman, with matches against the Metropolitan Police and Combined Clubs. DECEMBER 31st 1977 - WIMBLEDON - HORWOOD CUP '7'. AGONY CORNER Does such a place exist? Ask any of those who competed in our Seven Miles Walk on December 31st using a new course, where a sharp hill up Cottenham Drive had to be climbed three times. The villain of the piece, the chap who planned it, was Carl, seeking out an alternative for the traditional Open Seven course which is getting dangerous in parts. It was agreed that the new course was better from the safety angle, and, in retrospect, the competitors liked it. Being the Season of Goodwill we welcomed a number of walkers from other Clubs and we were able to provide matches against the Metropolitan Police and against Combined Clubs. Carl was directing the competitors round an innocent looking corner where the climbing began. Sweeping round in fine style Adrian James (Enfield) led them home to set a course record of 54:21. Our main interest was in the Horwood Cup for those not barred from the Garnet Trophy and Richard Dorman, improving every time won from Trevor Mc Dermot, also making good progress. (These two gave further evidence of their prowess the following week-end at Imber Court). We beat the M.P. by a narrow margin, but the Combined Clubs were too strong for us. Many will look forward to improving these times, whilst others will be anxious to have a go on the new course. G.S.D. items.sum: Report and results of the Metropolitan Police Open 11Km walk at Imber Court, where sixteen-year-old Richard Dorman made a fine open debut and Belgrave placed second team to Steyning.
items.s: JANUARY 8th 1978 - IMBER COURT - MET. POLICE OPEN 11KM. RICHARD'S FINE DEBUT Report and results of the Metropolitan Police Open 11Km walk at Imber Court, where sixteen-year-old Richard Dorman made a fine open debut and Belgrave placed second team to Steyning. JANUARY 8th 1978 - IMBER COURT - MET. POLICE OPEN 11KM. RICHARD'S FINE DEBUT With the departure of Graham Seatter back to New Zealand, who would fill the gap in our team? The answer came in the Metropolitan Police Open 11 Kilos walk. Sixteen years old Richard Dorman, who the previous day had run so well in the Surrey County C.C. Championships gave us an unprecedented performance. In his first Open race at this distance he was fourth scorer in our team which placed second to the much improved Steyning A.C. John led the team home with what was probably his best open placing to date, he was near the leaders right from the start. Carl soon followed with Ray, who had had Richard for company in the early stages, hammering his way home. It wasn't long before Richard obliged with a performance which, had the course been seven miles, must have brought him home under the hour. Young Trevor too, who has already done seven miles in the hour, consolidated his position as one of our good prospects. There were many Belgravians in the field and those trying to make the team can't relax! We welcomed Len Duquemin back to the fray, his style is still very impressive, and a few more outings should bring the speed back. The event was once again efficiently organised by Doug Fotheringham (who also competed) and it is an event where one often meets old friends. Usually helping at this event is Mrs. Bonnie Yescombe, and she asked after many Club members. Many will recall her late husband Cyril's purposeful walking for Club and Police teams. One of his greatest performances was when in almost continuous raid he walked from Brighton to London and back step for step with Bernard Eglinton G.S.D. 1.S.Lightman (Met.WC) 49:07; 6.J.Hall 50:27; 8.C.Lawton 50:51; 34.R. items.sum: Report and results of the G.L.C. 10 miles walking championship at Battersea Park, won by G. Nibre of Ilford, where Belgrave finished second team by one point between Ilford and Enfield.
items.s: FEBRUARY 11th, 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - G.L.C. 10 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP. 34-35-36 Report and results of the G.L.C. 10 miles walking championship at Battersea Park, won by G. Nibre of Ilford, where Belgrave finished second team by one point between Ilford and Enfield. FEBRUARY 11th, 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - G.L.C. 10 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP. 34—35—36 These were the team scores in this year's G.L.C. 10 miles Walking Championship of Ilford AC (without Roger Mills), Belgrave and Enfield (without Amos Seddon), with Surrey WC not far behind with 42 points. The event was held at Battersea Park on the 11th February over the usual five lap course; it was dry but cold. Carl and John Hall were prominent in the early stages and Surrey WC seemed to have the edge over us for the team title, but Ray and John Bromley were moving well. The winner, who led for most of the way, was G. Nibre of Ilford - one of the country's promising young walkers. With a lap to go Carl and S. Elms (Sutton) were in hot pursuit, but over the last lap the diminutive Brighton man put in some fast work to drop Carl. John kept up the pressure and recorded a time equivalent to eight m.p.h. Ray and John were picking up places and it was good to see how their judgment and experience got them really moving over that part of the race which matters. The closeness of the result shows how tight team races are these days, actually we were the first club to finish its four scorers. It was good to see John Dunsford and Ron Day getting back to form. The proceedings were presided over by Cyril Gittins, adorned with the Chain and Badge of the President of the S.R.W.A. G.S.D. 1.G.Nibre (Ilford AC) 73:10; 3.C.Lawton 73:44; 5.J.Hall 74:58; 15.R. items.s: Notice of the death of Arthur Welling, aged 69, general secretary of Vets AC from 1952 and a long-serving race organiser. We are sorry to have to announce the death of Arthur Welling on December 8th at the age of 69. Arthur never excelled as walker or runner but veteran competitors far and wide have a great deal to thank him for - races organised, handicap marks paced out, pins and numbers dispensed and all with a cheery word or two to each contestant. He became a member of Vets AC in 1949 and took over as general secretary in 1952, a post he held until the end. Arthur Welling Arthur Welling died December 8th aged 69; joined Vets AC 1949, general secretary from 1952 Arthur Welling Arthur Vets AC
