items.sum: Ladies Section news from the Ladies Hon. Secretary covering winter training, the women walkers' three championships, the ladies' cross country championships and the new women's captain.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Section news from the Ladies Hon. Secretary covering winter training, the women walkers' three championships, the ladies' cross country championships and the new women's captain. WITH THE LADIES The Ladies Section, from the point of competition, goes into hibernation for the Winter at present, but the track training with 18-20 youngsters still goes on at Battersea Park every Sunday morning throughout the Winter, and every Wednesday evening at Belgrave Hall with circuit training and games. Our Walkers, however, have competed in three major championships, the first being the National Junior 5000m at Milksham in November, where Diane Cook finished 6th in her first championship race for the Club and Anna Matthews was unfortunately disqualified while fighting out for 3rd place. The National Championships came next, and were held at Birmingham on a Sunday early in December, where Belgrave fielded a full team in the Senior section for the first time in history. The last championship was the Southern Counties at Maidstone and this race saw the first appearance of Linda Nicholls, the Kent Champion, in Belgrave colours. Welcome Linda, you've got your worst race out of your system, and it was a horrid day. Looking further forward it can only be a matter of months before our walking team gains Championship medals, and my thanks go to Carl Lawton for providing transport and support for the Birmingham trip. ★★★ For full details of walking events see under The Walking Section. We held our Cross Country Championships at Wimbledon on January 21st. The Junior race had eight competitors and Joann Warnett won comfortably with the Taylor sisters second and third. Rebecca Augustine and Alison Jones surprised with their forward running. The Senior race saw Shirley Rook winning easily, her first Club Championship, from Anna Matthews. Congratulations to Joann Warnett on being picked to represent Greater London in the All England Schools Cross-Country Championships at Lincoln. She won the Wandsworth Schools, finished 3rd in the Inner London and then 5th in the Greater London Championships. It is nice to see Alison Bethwaite back in training after illness at Christmas. Wendy Dunsford will be the Womens Captain for the coming year, and my Assistant Secretary will be Derrick Jones, who comes to help every Sunday. Please come and support us when we compete at Battersea Park in the Southern League, Mid-Week League, and the youngsters in the Lily 'B' League. Your support means much to us, so please bring your Mums and Dads. Ray Hall, Ladies Hon. items.label: April 1978
items.sum: Co-Auditor Ken Miller's A.G.M. statement on the club's finances, reporting a loss for the year to June 1977 and warning that Belgrave Harriers must improve its position by at least £1,000 a year.
items.s: MONEY MATTERS £ Co-Auditor Ken Miller's A.G.M. statement on the club's finances, reporting a loss for the year to June 1977 and warning that Belgrave Harriers must improve its position by at least £1,000 a year. MONEY MATTERS £ At the A.G.M. last September Ken Miller, one of our co-Auditors incisively outlined the Club's financial position. The Committee regards it as important that all our members should be aware of the constant struggle to make ends meet and we therefore reproduce below Ken's comments. "The Accounts for the year to 30th June 1977 show a loss of £663 of which £246 represents a provision for depreciation. There was thus a cash loss of £417. Apart from a very small deficit in 1975, this is the only occasion since before 1970 that the Club has suffered an outflow of cash. As explained by the Treasurer, the reason in part for this outflow, has been the restricted use of the Hall for social activities during the building programme. The Balance Sheet at 30th June 1977 shows that after meeting our immediate liabilities, we have surplus cash of £867. Please remember this figure. But what of the future? If we assume that for the year to June 1978, expenditure will increase by 10%; subs. will be static[illegible] Building Society interest will reduce to a small figure; other income (football scheme, hire of hall, socials, etc.) will increase by £500 - the Club will have a cash loss of £500 for the year. But the position is worse than this, for we have already received £400 advance subscriptions. Thus our cash position will deteriorate by £900 during the current year on these assumptions. If we refer back to the fact that we had at June 1977 £867 surplus cash, we could find that the money has run out by next June. But the problems do not stop at June 1978 for we have already received and effectively spent £400 of subscriptions for the year 1978/79. A Club with the responsibility of a building such as Belgrave Hall, must in my view have some reserves upon which to fall back for major repairs. We have therefore not just to seek to cover our cash outgoings but also to cover a charge for depreciation to provide a build up of cash for this purpose. A sensible depreciation charge each year on the improved Belgrave Hall would be in the region of £350-£400. To summarise, we need to improve the financial position of Belgrave Harriers by at least £1,000 per annum. This can only be achieved in two ways - (1) Cutting costs (marginal scope) (2) Increasing income - from socials, hire of hall, etc. - from subscriptions. Under the Rules of the Club, subscriptions cannot be increased until 1st July 1978 but it is interesting to note that currently subs. only just cover the cost of printing, stationery and postage (including the "Belgravian"). It is the Auditors' prime function to report on the past but my co-Auditor and I felt we would be failing in our duty if we did not underline this evening the potentially serious financial future facing the Club." K.W. Miller. Ken Miller Ken Miller co-Auditor; K.W. Miller Ken Miller Ken K.W. Miller. Belgrave Harriers A.G.M. Belgrave Hall

items.sum: Youths and Boys secretary Leo Coy reviews a strong cross country season including the team's Surrey League victory, and outlines track plans in the Rosenheim and Ebbisham Leagues, an appeal for helpers and training times.
items.s: YOUTHS AND BOYS Youths and Boys secretary Leo Coy reviews a strong cross country season including the team's Surrey League victory, and outlines track plans in the Rosenheim and Ebbisham Leagues, an appeal for helpers and training times. YOUTHS AND BOYS Cross Country Season. After an initial shock over the resignation of Alan Perriam, who has moved north, the season proved to be one of our best for some years. Alan has already been greatly missed and we hope that he will return in the not too distant future. The highlight of the season was our team victory in the Surrey League Our result at Wimbledon, like the Seniors, set us up for the rest of the season. This was our first win in any cross country race for a number of years and is an encouraging sign for the future. Of our scoring teams in the league only Richard Dorman won't be eligible for next year. So we intend to show the seniors again how it should be done by winning Div. I in 1978/9. Another achievement was our good turnout in the Surrey Championships where we completed a team, despite a number of absentees in every age group. Next year with David North eligible to run for us we stand a great chance of being in the medals in the Youths race. Our turnout in the HHH league at Brockwell Park was very disappointing. We could have won this if everybody had turned out. Hopefully we can improve next year. Track Season. The coming track season has a new feature in that we shall be competing in the Rosenheim League for the first time. There is a separate section for a youths team, with one scoring in each event and any number of non-scorers. The league is held over five matches with the first three teams going into the final. The Boys/Colts will again be competing in the Ebbisham League but included for the first time are second year boys. If any young athletes want to take part in the above leagues please see me at Battersea Park or give me a ring. Note to older Members and Parents. I still need help to run this section of the club. If you feel that you can help in any way please get in touch with me. The club has a better gathering of young athletes now than at any time before so it is up to everyone to make sure that they become the seniors of the future. Training. Club training sessions will be held on Sunday morning, Tuesday and Thursday evenings throughout the spring and early summer for all events. items.sum: Report and results of the second youths' Surrey League race at Petersham, where a weakened Belgrave team finished second to Guildford but extended its league lead, with 12-year-old Gary Williscroft 14th.
items.s: NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - PETERSHAM - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE. THE MAGNIFICENT EIGHT Report and results of the second youths' Surrey League race at Petersham, where a weakened Belgrave team finished second to Guildford but extended its league lead, with 12-year-old Gary Williscroft 14th. NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - PETERSHAM - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE. THE MAGNIFICENT EIGHT After our convincing win in the first race we were short of our first three scorers for this second race. Mark Waller and David North were injured and Richard Dorman was on a training weekend. But there was no need to worry, for although we finished second behind Guildford we pulled further ahead in the league after a magnificent team display. Mark Sinclair returned to his best form to finish 4th and next came John Searle in 7th place. John Gladwin, having run for his school in the morning, showed us a touch of his class by finishing 10th. Then came the best run by a young Belgrave athlete for many years - Gary Williscroft, 12 years of age and competing against Boys and Youths, came home in 14th position. Gerry Sexton fought all the way to complete our team and with Paul Thorp, David Whisson and Pat Lyttle also on hand to cover our scoring five it was a great result. 1.A.Cunningham (Ranelagh H) 14:14; 4.M.Sinclair 15:22; 7.J.Searle 15:42; 10.J.Gladwin 16:05; 14.G.Williscroft 16:39; 23.G.Sexton 17:20 28.P.Thorp 18:22; 29.D.Whisson 18:45; 34.P.Lyttle 21:33; 35 finished Teams: 1.Guildford & Godalming AC 54; 2.Belgrave H 56; 3.Mitcham AC 63; 4.Ranelagh H 76; 5.Surrey AC 77. DECEMBER 10th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE. LEAGUE VICTORS ! Beaten again by Guildford & Godalming even though we finished our scoring five by 14th place. items.sum: Reprint from 1953 on the Surrey and Middlesex county cross country championships, where Belgrave lost the Surrey team title by five points and its Middlesex men ran as Cadogan AC.
items.s: from the Belgravian... ... 25 years ago: COUNTY SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS......1953 Reprint from 1953 on the Surrey and Middlesex county cross country championships, where Belgrave lost the Surrey team title by five points and its Middlesex men ran as Cadogan AC. from the Belgravian... ... 25 years ago COUNTY SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS......1953 These were held on 3rd January, and the Surrey event was in Richmond Park, which was more or less familiar ground to our team. We were not at full strength.....and did not expect to retain our team title, which we had held for the past two seasons. Our team, however, all ran well and we only lost first place by five points and second place by one point. Chas. Walker was our first man home in 5th position, then came Bill Lucas, 12th, and Bill only came into the team in order to make up the number, as he says he has retired from serious competition and declined an invitation to run in the Inter-Counties race. (Other members: 14.E.A. Short; 14.E.Herbert; 16.D.Brickwood; 21.J. Masters; 36.D.Briggs; 44.A.H.Bishop; 53.J.Bromley; 55.E.M.Bishop; 63.S.Davies; 67.L.C.Bishop; 74.G.J.Stace). The Middlesex event was held at Trent Park and here again Cadogan AC were weakened.....and eventually placed 6th. Bob Taylor ran well to finish 20th, and Mick Porter 27th also did well. (Other members: 63.E.Stimpson; 70.J.McDonald; 73.R.W.Tobin; 85.R.J.Wolton; 127.A. Penstone; Ken Stimpson did not finish). Ed: a club was only allowed to compete in one county championship in those days so our Middlesex men had to run under the name of Cadogan AC - a second claim club whose membership was restricted to Belgravians. items.sum: Reprint from 1938 celebrating Belgrave walkers' unprecedented treble of R.W.A. 'Junior' 10 miles, 20 miles and 50 km team titles, led by Colin Sutton, with the club holding all five R.W.A. trophies.
items.s: ... and 40 years ago: R.W.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS.......1938 Reprint from 1938 celebrating Belgrave walkers' unprecedented treble of R.W.A. 'Junior' 10 miles, 20 miles and 50 km team titles, led by Colin Sutton, with the club holding all five R.W.A. trophies. ... and 40 years ago R.W.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS.......1938. The accomplishment which must command our attention above all other matters, and merits our sincerest congratulation, is that of our walkers in winning the R.W.A. 10 miles "Junior" Championship, R.W.A. 20 Miles Championship and R.W.A. 50 Kilos. Championship. No other club has ever at any time won all three championships and to do so in the space of three months is almost miraculous. This record of success is one that may never again be approached by any club, and we most heartily congratulate and thank the members of the winning teams. The performance of Colin Sutton in appearing in all three championship teams is one that may never be equalled. He was sixth in the "Junior", fourth in the 20 Miles Championship, and fifth in the 50 Kilos.Championship - a trio of performances that reflect the greatest credit on Colin's conscientious training and determined efforts to help the Club to a treble victory. Others deserving our congratulations are Fred Bentley, who was placed second in both 20 Miles and 50 Kilos events; and Joe Coleman and Len Coleman, who dead-heated in the "Junior" Championship for first place. It is interesting to note that as a result of the Winter season's activities, all five trophies which the Road Walking Association offer for competition (the "National" Shield, "Garnett" Cup, "Horlick" Cup, "Nijmegan" Shield and "Berman" Cup) are in the possession of Belgrave Harriers! ROAD AND COUNTRY At the World Veterans' Championships, Gothenburg, back in August 197[illegible] the O'Hara running machine tackled something new - the marathon. Our Laurie placed 36th in the Class 1B event with 2hrs.43minutes 15secon[illegible] and in his own words "It was a fairly comfortable run." Who says you can't teach an old dog new tricks? September 3rd saw Steve Jones (RAF Lyneham) fly to a course record in the Witney '12' road race with 61:42. Only 112 of the 137 starters could finish the undulating course in the beautiful grounds of Blenheim Palace. Bill Weller ran his usual strong race and was well backed up by Pat O'Connor and Lionel Mann to make the team bronze medallists. 8.W.Weller 65:07; 21.P.O'Connor 67:17; 23.L.Mann 67:52; 35.S.Masterson 71:11; 58.D.Maughan 74:16. items.s: OCTOBER 1st 1977 - NORTHWOOD -'PHILIPS' HALF-MARATHON. Bels ~ by a close shave! Belgrave win the team race at the Philips half-marathon at Northwood through Bill Weller, Pat O'Connor and Doug Maughan, on a course 6/10ths of a mile short. OCTOBER 1st 1977 - NORTHWOOD -'PHILIPS' HALF-MARATHON. Bels ~ by a close shave! Everyone must run well and finish and we might be in the medals, was the feeling before the start. So with this constantly in mind, coupled with unbelievable five and ten mile times and a very strong headwind, the race was run. Pat O'Connor ran a well judged race and was only 1:22 behind sixth man Bill Weller while Doug. Maughan pulled through in the latter stages to make up the winning team. OCTOBER 22nd 1977 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2) THE CLIMB BACK BEGINS Ten in twenty-two and the captain fails to score! items.s: NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SOUTH OF THE THAMES JUNIOR CC Belgrave host the South of the Thames Junior cross country on Wimbledon Common with a record 394 finishers; Colin Pearson was first Belgrave man in 58th. NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SOUTH OF THE THAMES JUNIOR CC Our improved facilities were tested to the full with a huge field, nearly 50% up on the previous year, using Belgrave Hall for changing accommodation - 37 clubs had entered no fewer than 92 teams. One snag did arise when with 394 finishers, runners had to queue up down the course, the "funnel" being unable to take the strain but all was straightened out satisfactorily in the end. Unfortunately we were unable to celebrate Clive Shippen's term as President of the South of the Thames C.C. Division I of the Surrey Cross Country League for 1977/78 was won yet again by Aldershot, Farnham & Dist AC, their sixth win in a row. items.sum: Laurie O'Hara wins the Belgrave 7 mile cross country championship and Blackstaffe Shield, while Brian Marmion takes the handicap prize.
items.s: DECEMBER 3rd 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 7 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. IT'S THAT MAN AGAIN Laurie O'Hara wins the Belgrave 7 mile cross country championship and Blackstaffe Shield, while Brian Marmion takes the handicap prize. DECEMBER 3rd 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 7 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. IT'S THAT MAN AGAIN Having scored a double during the summer with the 5,000 and 10,000 championships Laurie set about the first leg of the Club's winter championships with a fine Blackstaffe Shield victory. Our old Heathen friend and guest Bob Richardson scored over Colin Pearson and coming into form nicely to take the 'bronze' came Lionel Mann. If there was ever a vote for the youngster most Belgrave distance runn[illegible] would like to see succeed, Brian Marmion could well come out on top. Not endowed with a great deal in the way of natural ability he has stuck at it over the past few years, more often than not getting a hammering in the process. Brian successfully negotiated three laps of our course at a faster pace than he has usually taken in the past for just one circuit and in the process stormed off with the handicap prize. 1.L.O'Hara 45:18; 2.R.Richardson 45:39; 3.C.Pearson 46:08; 4.L.Mann 46:43; 5.P.O'Connor 46:51; 6.S.Holmes 48:03; 7.L.Coy 48:39; 8.P.Roche 48:59; 9.J.Stevenson 49:40; 10.D.Maughan 50:08; 11.M.Riley 51:02; 12.W.Laws 51:20; 13.L.Morris 52:51; 14.B.Taylor 53:28; 15.C.Lawton 54:31; 16.J.Golling 54:33; 17.B.Marmion 56:44; 18.J.Davies 56:45; 19.N.Morris 57:43; 20.G.Piddington 58:41; 21.W.Harvey 59:22; 22. .Devitt 59:24; 23.J.V.Baker 60:00; 24.G.Pearson 60:10; 25.C.Manning 60:18;26.J.Plummer 61:06; 27.D.Gordon 62:30; 28.D.Hurd 63:11; 29.E.Thorp 63:30. items.h: DECEMBER 10th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2). BEATEN AT THE PALACE
items.sum: Ranelagh beat Belgrave in the third Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 match at Crystal Palace, but Belgrave's second place keeps an 80-point overall lead.
items.s: DECEMBER 10th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2). BEATEN AT THE PALACE Ranelagh beat Belgrave in the third Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 match at Crystal Palace, but Belgrave's second place keeps an 80-point overall lead. DECEMBER 10th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2). BEATEN AT THE PALACE A totally new course to us this one, with a much smaller lap than usual due to the fact that TV coverage was being given to the international race held on the same afternoon. With John Bicourt racing on the Continent it fell to Bob Richardson's lot to lead the Bels home. Our packing was not quite what it had been in the earlier two races. Ian Duncan was also absent, competing successfully in a University race, while Jim Rimmer seemed to have more than a little difficulty keeping his shorts on and even with second-claimer John Abberton of Poly H in our colours Ranelagh had no difficulty in beating us to the line. In fact half the first twenty men home were Ranelagh Harriers with only five Belgravians finished at that point. Luckily our next five runners were soon in and we still placed a comfortable second, maintaining an 80 point lead overall. Pat O'Connor had the measure of Bill Weller on this occasion and it was good to see Bob Smith scoring for us again. Peter Gardner crept ever nearer the scorers being our 11th man and only 7 seconds down on Lionel Mann. Laurie O'Hara, meanwhile, finished with a personal score of 14 points after three races - just two down on the overall leader, Hutchin of Met. items.sum: Report of the City of London New Year 10 mile road race, where Laurie O'Hara won the veteran's prize in ninth and Belgrave took third team prizes on aggregate time.
items.s: JANUARY 1st 1978 - CITY OF LONDON - 10 MILE ROAD RACE. A Fine Start .... Report of the City of London New Year 10 mile road race, where Laurie O'Hara won the veteran's prize in ninth and Belgrave took third team prizes on aggregate time. JANUARY 1st 1978 - CITY OF LONDON - 10 MILE ROAD RACE. A Fine Start .... .... was made to 1978. At 1.00 p.m. on New Year's Day in the City of London five Belgravians lined up for the seven lap course (starting and finishing in London Wall) for the Ten Miles Road Race, the first event of the City of London New Year Road Races. There were over 170 starters (including four ladies) and the team race was decided on aggregate times instead of positions, so every second was vital. With this in mind all of our team came roaring through the finish on all cylinders. Laurie was our first home in ninth position, this won him the veteran's prize. Doug and Lionel were never far apart and finished close together. New member Alan Painter gave us a promising performance with John Wasbrough not far behind. The team race was won by R.A.F. (Wattesham) who also provided the Individual Winner. Ranelagh H. took second awards whilst our trio snatched third prizes by a few seconds from Southend who were just ahead of S.L.H. by the narrowest of margins. items.sum: Laurie O'Hara beats Ian Duncan to win the Belgrave 10 mile cross country championship and complete the winter double; Alan Painter wins the handicap and Peter Gardner the juniors' 'Savage Shield'.
items.s: JANUARY 14th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 10 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. LAURIE'S WINTER DOUBLE Laurie O'Hara beats Ian Duncan to win the Belgrave 10 mile cross country championship and complete the winter double; Alan Painter wins the handicap and Peter Gardner the juniors' 'Savage Shield'. JANUARY 14th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 10 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. LAURIE'S WINTER DOUBLE At last it appeared that Laurie's time might be drawing to a close as Ian Duncan, less than half the master's age, stuck to him like glue for two laps and even ventured to match strides side by side on occasion. But Laurie was only toying with his young adversary and at the crucial stage on the third lap he put his foot down and it was all over; the winter 'double' was his. Colin Pearson, in dogging these two's footsteps early on, seemed to have the third spot sewn up but from about seven miles Bill Weller and then Leo Coy and Paul Roche seemed to be making ground on him. A hard fought last lap was to no avail and Bill came home 11 seconds ahead. Alan Painter was the deserving handicap winner but Steve Williams must also get a mention, finishing as he did cut, bruised and muddied from a very heavy fall on the horseride. 1.L.O'Hara 63:09; 2.I.Duncan 64:21; 3.W.Weller 64:35; 4.C.Pearson 64:46; 5.L.Coy 66:41; 6.P.Roche 67:11; 7.M.Kortenray 69:05; 8.D.Maughan 69:06; 9.A.Painter 70:07; 10.S.Williams 70:07; 11.P.Hardwick 70:5[illegible] 12.J.Wasbrough 72:59; 13.S.Holmes 74:16; 14.L.Morris 74:35; 15.J.Angus 75:01; 16.D.Searle 76:17; 17.H.Satchell 76:46; 18.A.Stroud 78:01; 19.K.Duckett 79:35; 20.D.Wooll 81:45; 21.G.Piddington 82:30; 22.P.Staples 83:03; 23.C.Manning 83:14; 24.C.Cross 83:36; 25.A.Vosper 85:34; 26.R.Day 86:18; 27.G.Pearson 86:41; 28.P.Wooll 86:48; 29.J.V.Baker 87:39. He hammered home his advantage over Simon Williamson to the tune of half a minute but something in Simon's countenance as he came home second gave a hint that this race might have been lost but there are many more ahea[illegible] Nigel Morris is a young man with determination. items.h: FEBRUARY 18th 1978 - MILFORD - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE DIV.2. GOING UP!
items.sum: Report of the final Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 fixture at Milford, where Ranelagh won on the day but Belgrave won the division overall (final result table) and promotion back to Division I, with the Youths also winning their section.
items.s: FEBRUARY 18th 1978 - MILFORD - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE DIV.2. GOING UP! Report of the final Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 fixture at Milford, where Ranelagh won on the day but Belgrave won the division overall (final result table) and promotion back to Division I, with the Youths also winning their section. FEBRUARY 18th 1978 - MILFORD - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE DIV.2. GOING UP! A year ago we were bemoaning the fact that we had finished bottom of Division I of the N.Surrey League and would be relegated. "Only for a year" we said. On February 18th we travelled to Milford for the final fixture of the season. We were 80 points up on Ranelagh H and we knew that they were fielding a very strong team, so a keen race was expected. The course was over sandy paths over heathland; the recent weather had covered them with snow, making them slippery in places. Our Youths had already shown their views on being in Division II by winning their section (they do not have as many races as the Seniors) Our hosts, Guildford & Godalming A.C.) had put on a race for them. David North scored a convincing win, with the improving Mark Sinclair fourth and in eighth position the diminutive Gary Williscroft. Later a blood-stained Ray McCann (he had had a fall) stormed in. Scoring three a side we won from the local club. Great running from great prospects, keep it up! The Senior race, being over three laps, gave us a chance to assess our chances. Right from the first lap we had Ranelagh vests prominent in the first half dozen or so, with John Abberton in second place. Then Belgrave vests came through thick and fast and the necessary ten scorers, with a few to spare, were soon through. Second time round showed our team to be holding their positions, and so to the finish. Ranelagh provided the winner, and with about a hundred yards to go John and another Ranelagh runner were neck and neck, but our man out sprinted his rival to gain a valuable place. The next three were solid Ranelagh, then Pat O'Connor led in a group containing many Belgrave vests. Particular mention for a newcomer from New Zealand (actually born in Britain), Lyn Jones whose forceful running split Lionel Mann and Jim Rimmer. Our scoring men, mostly "the old gang" were anchored by Steve Williams with Peter Hardwick and Simon Holmes hot on his heels - these three are soon going to worry our established seniors. It was pleasing to see Brian Marmion further up the field - let's hope he's on his way to showing his true potential. A quick tot-up showed Ranelagh to have beaten us on the day's event, but they were well short of wiping out our initial advantage. So, next year it's Division I again, let's stay there! There was general elation as we got into the cars which sped us back home. Finally, our thanks to the man whose efforts were largely responsible for our prowess - no, he didn't actually run, but he wrote to you, 'phoned you and conveyed some of you to the venue and got you to the start. Yes! Thank you Gordon Biscoe! items.sum: Report of the National Cross Country Championships at Leeds, highlighting John Bicourt's 17th place from 1536 starters, with Belgrave senior and junior placings.
items.s: MARCH 4th 1978 - LEEDS - E.C.C.U. CHAMPIONSHIPS. A BICOURT "BLINDER" Report of the National Cross Country Championships at Leeds, highlighting John Bicourt's 17th place from 1536 starters, with Belgrave senior and junior placings. MARCH 4th 1978 - LEEDS - E.C.C.U. CHAMPIONSHIPS. A BICOURT "BLINDER" It's Commonwealth Games and European Games year again and one may well have expected our most capped international John Bicourt to start to raise his game with a view to gaining selection for these championships later on this year. An early and promising result will have been noted by those who read every line of their "AWs" - February 2nd, Draguignan (France) 1.Boxberger, 2.J.Bicourt - but nobody could have forseen John's "blinder" of a run in this year's National. He travelled up to Leeds the day before the race in an effort to produce the most exciting cross country race of his career and succeeded magnificently. We have all heard how in the old days Belgrave used to pack them in, "all our team home in the first 30", etc. but let us remember that John's marvellous 17th place was from a field of 1536 starters, not the one or two hundred of the nineteen thirties. Runners finishing after him read like a list of who's who in English cross country: 18.A.Holden; 19.P.Standing; 22.R.Wilde; 23.D.Bedford; 27.K.Steer.....Crabb, Cannon, Beevor, Tagg....What a great pity that we did not turn out our best side to back him up and give ourselves a more respectable team place. items.s: MARCH 11th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE CHAMPIONSHIP. A NEW CHAMPION Report and results of the club 5¾ mile road championship at Wimbledon, won by Ian Duncan from Bill Weller, with handicap placings. MARCH 11th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE CHAMPIONSHIP A NEW CHAMPION It was a pleasant afternoon for the opening of our Spring road running season and by the end of the afternoon Team Manager Gordon Bisc[illegible] could at least pick out the likely candidates for "long-legs" in our Belgrave Road Relay. After two miles Bill Weller and Ian Duncan, with Colin Pearson in their slipstream, had broken clear of the field and as they took the dip past the "Crooked Billet" Laurie O'Hara was a full 20 metres astern. Ian Duncan does not normally reckon to be a good hill runn[illegible] but as the field came into view again by the church after the mile long haul up Cambridge, Pepys and Cottenham Park Roads, he appeared to be edging ahead of Bill. Colin had gone back and although Lauri[illegible] appeared to be moving quite well it was obvious that on this day he was out of the hunt for victory. Past the "Crooked Billet" again, and Bill Weller forced his way back to Ian's side; a mile round the top of the Common and still the issu[illegible] was not resolved. As the leading pair entered Lauriston Road for t[illegible] final straight an approaching car forced them to part, one on eithe[illegible] side, and at this point the younger man made his final effort to shake off our road running specialist, Bill Weller. Ian broke clear at last, thereby gaining his first Club Championship less than a year inside becoming a member - congratulations! 1.I.Duncan 28:46; 2.W.Weller 28:51; 3.L.O'Hara 29:29; 4.C.Pearson 29:43; 5.P.O'Connor 29:49; 6.L.Mann 30:09; 7.J.Stow 30:11; 8.L.Coy 30:45; 9.S.Holmes 31:07; 10.P.Gardner 31:30; 11.P.Hardwick 31:43; 12.D.Maughan 32:03; 13.S.Barrett 32:19; 14.J.Jackson 33:01; 15.C.Walker 33:16; 16.D.Crookes 33:20; 17.S.White 34:19; 18.J.Gosling 34:39; 19.R.Bale 34:46; 20.R.Coombs 34:53; 21.J.Angus 35:09; 22.L.Jones 35:14; 23.M.Head 35:37; 24.P.Joseph 35:50; 25.G.Collins 36:10[illegible] 26.B.Taylor 36:24; 27.E.Thorp 37:12; 28.M.Best 37:16; 29.C.Henn 37:[illegible] 30.B.Marmion 37:30; 31.D.Jones 37:37; 32.A.Vosper 38:06; 33.G.Pears[illegible] 38:54; 34.C.Manning 39:32; 35.D.Gordon 39:53; 36.J.McDonald 41:02. items.sum: Humorous essay by Eric Hall, a former competitor and official now watching on television, on the growth of officials, commentators' clichés and support staff in athletics.
items.s: ATHLETICS: A GROWTH INDUSTRY Humorous essay by Eric Hall, a former competitor and official now watching on television, on the growth of officials, commentators' clichés and support staff in athletics. ATHLETICS: A GROWTH INDUSTRY As one who has competed, officiated and spectated but is now, alas confined by distance to tele bashing I have noticed some changes in the sport over the years. All my early experience of meetings was, I now realise, giving a surface impression. Now it is possible to see things in depth. Some years ago at a fairly important meeting the centre of the arena was crowded with athletes, officials and hangers on - mainly the latter. The referee appealed for all non-essential personnel to leave the arena - no one moved. He repeated the appeal with the same result, he cajoled, he threatened but still after an hour or so it was the same - packed. It was the usual thing then. Get out in the middle and look important. However, during the mile the rains came. A cloudburst in fact and the result was just what the referee wanted - all but essential personnel left the arena. Not only left but rath[illegible] fled! Drowned! Only the scorers and timekeepers remained. The Almighty supported the referee. Now all is different. A 22" picture (in colour naturally) of Crysta[illegible] Palace, Meadowbank or Cosford shows the crowds and we hear them described by Ron P., Stuart S., or Barry D., and next year ??? "The crowd numbers X thousand". "The crowd is knowledgeable" - that mea[illegible] they know how to get to Crystal Palace etc. "They are enthusiastic" that means not all have been able to get complimentary tickets. "They are right behind the team" or "the world record holder" or their "favourite" etc., and now "they are boosting them" or "lifting them" - that means the crowd are looking into the possibility of shipping them out by using man powered flight. Another source of fun is to try to spot the commentators word for the year. We have had "adrenalin" followed by "pain barrier" then came "fight back" and "long ha[illegible] season" but this year it has been "above themselves" and "world beaters" with the mind boggling "surpassing themselves" - this means you meet yourself coming back never having been. Enough of the media and we have all had that I am sure. What about the centre of the arena? On a 22" screen it is still crowded. At times it outnumbers the crowd in the stands but in contrast to my earlier picture this time they are all essential. We now have carefully groomed, white trousered, white haired or balding officials carrying out a wide range of duties. I now spend some of the viewing time spotting old friends - Theo, Julian, Brutus - not their real names of course I have no wish to be sued! One we saw recently didn[illegible] move for well over an hour - he was either playing "Statues" or Madame Tussauds had done a damn good job! I digress, back to the officials - each man has his set duties, computer prepared and each vital to the success of the whole. To name them all would make for a paper shortage but I have selected those concerned with starting a race. We have spotted the starter, the deputy starter, the ammunition keeper, the assistant starter, the gun holder and deputy, the microphone holder, electrician and assistant plus deputies; the lane marshals, generals, majors and sergeants; the block carriers, but alas I have noticed the passing of the nail carriers and that most important official - the hammer holder - Tartan meant redundancy. The proliferation of officials is not restricted to the meeting itself. Athletes need coaches, advisers, technical assistants, to say nothing of psychiatrists, psychologists, masseurs etc.etc. I have yet to actually see the jock strap carrier but there was a bloke with Litesome on his tracksuit at a recent meeting! In my day we had one piece of soap for the whole team but now I assume they each have their own and have a gold plated container. The big question for the future is where will it end? You will recall that London hosts the Olympics every forty years and 1988 is not too far away. What the hell is the connection you ask? It should be apparent. By 1988 given the growth in the number of officials needed for a meeting and the decline in the population of London there will not be enough people in the area in 1988 to provide officials. On a much more serious note though, they don't seem to need the same number of officials at foreign venues and they know when a world record has been broken too! Eric Hall Eric Hall Eric Hall former competitor and official, now 'confined by distance' Ron P. Ron P. television commentator Stuart S. Stuart S. television commentator Barry D. items.label: October 1978
items.sum: Editorial congratulating Graham Seatter, Allan Callow and Ernest Obeng on Commonwealth Games selection at Edmonton, noting Obeng's Tommy Green Cup award, Cliff Brooks' near miss on decathlon selection and promotions for the ladies and the boys and colts teams.
items.s: Editorial congratulating Graham Seatter, Allan Callow and Ernest Obeng on Commonwealth Games selection at Edmonton, noting Obeng's Tommy Green Cup award, Cliff Brooks' near miss on decathlon selection and promotions for the ladies and the boys and colts teams. Congratulations to our three members who gained selection for the Commonwealth Games at Edmonton, Canada in August. In the 30 kilometre walk, held in blistering conditions, Graham Seatter placed 7th for New Zealand while Allan Callow, representing the Isle of Man, was numbered among those who failed to finish. Graham's best performance of the year was without a doubt that magnificent display he put up at Stretford when he pulverised a selected field over 20 kilometres, winning by three minutes to record 87:37. A successful summer campaign by the outstanding sprinter Ernest Obeng eventually gained him recognition from Ghana. Ernie has raced many of the best in the World this year and has not had a poor run in a season stretching back to March. After following his progress through the preliminary rounds of the Commonwealth 100 metres it was a thrill for all Belgravians to see him line up against two Olympic Champions. Ernie placed 8th in the final and then came home to run an electrifying 10.29 at Crystal Palace for his sixth Club Record of 1978. For this latter performance the Committee have awarded Ernest the "Tommy Green" Cup for the most meritorious performance by a Belgravian in 1978. (Last year he shared that honour with Graham Seatter.) We must also remember the summer of 1978 for Cliff Brooks' narrow failure to earn selection for the Games. Setting his best ever decathlon score of 6,727 points (with veteran status not that many seasons away over the horizon), he was just short of the qualifying mark that would have enabled him to compete for Barbados. Teamwise it was not such a good season but we must give recognition to our ladies section who gained promotion from their division of the Lily B League, and our boys and colts who did likewise in the Ebbisham League. All credit to the teams and their organisers. Graham Seatter Graham Seatter 7th for New Zealand in the Commonwealth Games 30 kilometre walk, Edmonton; won 20 kilometres at Stretford in 87:37; shared Tommy Green Cup in 1977 Graham Seatter Graham Allan Callow Allan Callow represented the Isle of Man in the Commonwealth Games 30 kilometre walk; did not finish Ernest Obeng Ernest Obeng selected by Ghana; 8th in Commonwealth Games 100 metres final; 10.29 at Crystal Palace, his sixth club record of 1978; awarded Tommy Green Cup for 1978 Ernest Obeng Ernie Ernest Cliff Brooks Cliff Brooks best ever decathlon score 6,727 points; just short of qualifying mark for Barbados at the Commonwealth Games Commonwealth Games Tommy Green Cup Lily B League Ebbisham League Edmonton Canada New Zealand Isle of Man Stretford Ghana Crystal Palace Barbados

items.label: October 1978
items.sum: Feature comparing the collapse of the fictional marathon hero in the film "The Games" with the real 1948 Olympic Marathon, where former Belgravian Etienne Gailly entered Wembley first but finished third, and recalling other Belgravians at the 1948 Games.
items.s: MARATHON AGONIES Feature comparing the collapse of the fictional marathon hero in the film "The Games" with the real 1948 Olympic Marathon, where former Belgravian Etienne Gailly entered Wembley first but finished third, and recalling other Belgravians at the 1948 Games. MARATHON AGONIES "I suppose you will want to see this" said my wife switching the T.V. to the film "The Games". This is about the Olympic Games and the climax is the marathon, and is set in Rome. The hero is a British Runner, Harry Hayes, played by Michael Crawford. When preparing for the part Michael joined the Bels and a 1968 magazine shows a picture of him training on Wimbledon Common. In the film he is the favourite for the marathon and his trainer wants him to run the first sub. two hours marathon! The event is held on a very hot day and our hero draws away running at a fantastic pace, the half-way mark being reached in just under the hour. He is first to enter the stadium, but he has run himself out and he staggers round the track to be passed by six others and to collapse just after finishing. A similar fate actually befell a former Belgravian in another Olympic Marathon - True or false? True! In the 1948 Olympic Marathon E'tienne Gailly (Belgium) was first into Wembley Stadium only to stagger round and be passed by D. Cabrera (Argentine) and our old friend, Tom Richards of S.L.H. On crossing the line for the bronze medal E'tienne was whipped on to a stretcher. During the war he had escaped to Britain from occupied Belgium, and as a keen runner he joined us and trained with and competed for the Bels. "Steve" Gailly was well liked and when he returned to Belgium it was predicted in the "Belgravian" that he would make his mark. A few years later he was tragically killed in a car accident. A marathon is held annually in Belgium in his honour. Also competing at Wembley in 1948 was Belgravian Bill Lucas (5,000m), Harry Churcher (10,000m Walk) and Bill Nankeville (1,500m). The fastest marathon on record stands to the credit of Derek Clayton (Australia), who, in 1969, clocked 2h.8mins.34secs. at Antwerp. So the two hour barrier is still some way off - a tantalising and agonising one and threequarters of a mile. items.s: compute your collapse point Illustrated piece reprinted via the Highgate Harriers journal explaining the 'Collapse Point Theory' that a runner slows at about three times their average daily distance, with a table of weekly mileage against suggested maximum race distance. compute your collapse point You might like to experiment with this Collapse Point Theory. It works as follows: ~ You will stop or slow down dramatically at a point about three times your average daily distance for the past six to eight weeks. ~ Say you've averaged 35 miles a week during that time. That's five miles a day. Your projected collapse point is 15 miles. Your maximum race distance should, therefore, be a little less than 15 miles. (Taken fom 'Step Up To Racing' by K. From the President As your President for this year I should like to take this opportunity of wishing you much success in the coming season. Over the past years I have been inspired by great team spirit and enthusiasm with Belgrave, now older and slower the same spirit is still as strong but it should be remembered that you only get out of sport what you put into it. I should also like to remind members that the Club and our sport cannot run without its officials. Do not take them for granted give them the support they deserve. Yours in sport, Ray Middleton Ray Middleton Ray Middleton club President for the year

items.s: Graham Seatter 7th in Edmonton Report of the Commonwealth Games 30 kilometre walk at Edmonton in great heat, where Graham Seatter (New Zealand) placed 7th and Allan Callow (Isle of Man) did not finish, with the top eight results. Graham Seatter 7th in Edmonton The conditions could probably not have been much worse for the Commonwealth Games 30 Kilometre walk at Edmonton, in which two Belgravians were competing. The sun scorched the sixteen starters unmercifully and it is not surprising that four men failed to finish including our own Allan Callow representing the Isle of Man. The Australians Sawall and Erikson blasted off, followed by Jobin the Canadian record holder while Belgrave's Graham Seatter (New Zealand) took things a little steadier. At 5KM Jobin led in 22:14 with Sawall 22:16 and then a gap until England's Olly Flynn passed the checkpoint with Erikson in 22:37 and Graham 22:54. Sawall pushed hard to lead at 10Km in 45:12, 11 seconds up on Jobin but Olly Flynn had closed up with 45:29 with our man still 5th in 46:15. By 15Km Sawall led in 1:08:37 but Flynn had him in his sights, 13 seconds down. Jobin passed by in 1:09:27 and Graham was up to 4th in 1:10:05, 24 seconds clear of Brian Adams with Erikson apparently fading. Adams took Graham (1:35:55) in the next 5Km stretch and then up front Flynn moved into a lead he was to maintain to the end. By 25 kilometres Erikson stormed back into medal contention but Graham was in bad trouble as was Jobin and it must have been a desperate effort to keep going in the 26°C (80°F) temperature. Adams, Seddon (England) and Boeck (Canada) came past and eventually he crossed the line 7th in 2:31:48.9. 1.O.Flynn (England) 2:22:03.7; 2.W.Sawall (Australia) 2:22:58.6; 3.T. items.label: October 1978
items.sum: Profile of new club President Ray Middleton by John Keown, covering his race walking career from 1951, National 50Kms titles, Commonwealth silver, London to Brighton club record and 1974 world best track walks, his work as an official, and his family's support, with two photographs.
items.s: OUR PRESIDENT RAY C. MIDDLETON Profile of new club President Ray Middleton by John Keown, covering his race walking career from 1951, National 50Kms titles, Commonwealth silver, London to Brighton club record and 1974 world best track walks, his work as an official, and his family's support, with two photographs. OUR PRESIDENT RAY C. MIDDLETON by John Keown Ray places 2nd over 30km in a match v German clubs at Frankfurt What qualities do we look for in a President? We expect him to be a person who is a leader; one who will inspire others to give of their best; one who has down the years clearly demonstrated his loyalty to his club and his fellow members. In Ray Middleton, Belgrave Harriers have found such a person. Ray was born in London on 9th August 1936. At school he competed in the high jump and 880 yards but not being too successful in these events, in 1951 he tried his hand at race walking. Despite finishing third out of three in a one mile novice walk he discovered that he enjoyed the sport and so joined Belgrave Harriers. Progress was slow but steady for Ray. In the R.W.A. Junior 5 Miles Championship in 1956 he finished sixth with a time of 41m.21s. The following year he began to win Club championships, and in 1959 at Wembley he won his first major race, the Southern "Garnet". He gained his first Surrey County vest the same year. In 1961, ten years after taking up race walking, Ray established himself as one of the top middle distance walkers in the United Kingdom. He finished third in the National 20 Miles, second in the Leicester Mercury 20 miles and second in the National 50 Kms when he split the two Thompson brothers, Don and Nigel. He gained his first international vest that year when he represented Great Britain over 50Kms in the Lugano Trophy Competition. At Baddesley Colliery, Warwickshire in 1963 Ray gave one of the best walking performances of his long career when at his third attempt he won the National 50Kms with a world-class time of 4h.16m.43s. Two years later at Bolton he again won the National 50Kms. Ray has represented his country on numerous occasions. Besides taking part in six Lugano Trophy finals he has competed in three European Championships, one Olympic Games and a Commonwealth Games. In the latter event at Kingston, Jamaica, Ray won the silver medal in the inaugural 20 Miles Walk. During the present decade Ray has turned his attention to such established "classics" as the Hastings to Brighton and London to Brighton. In 1970 he won the Hastings to Brighton and when finishing second to Shaul Ladany (Israel) in the London to Brighton established a new Club Record of 7h.50m.47s. for the 53 miles journey from Big Ben to Brighton seafront. Just a month after winning the 1974 "Brighton" in an International 8 Hour track walking race at White Hart Lane, London, Ray crowned all his previous performances by establishing new World Best distances and times for 6, 7 and 8 hours, 40 and 50 miles. During the last 20 years Ray has been a scoring member of practically all Belgrave walking teams at every distance from 5 miles to 53 miles The fact that he is the proud owner of nearly 50 National team medals clearly demonstrates his loyalty to the Club and his ability to inspire other members to bring top honours to Belgrave. His consistency over all distances will almost certainly see him go down in history as one of the all-time greats of British Race Walking. Ray's activities have not been confined to racing. He has for a number of years been an elected member of the Southern R.W.A. Committee. Besides competing in National Championships he has successfully acted as local organiser of the longer championships. His knowledge of the competitors and their requirements made him a natural choice as chief steward in charge of the feeding stations at last year's Lugano Trophy final at Milton Keynes. In all his endeavours Ray has always had the whole-hearted support of his wife Jean and his daughters, Debra and Lesley. Jean has, down the years, been an ardent and vocal supporter of Belgrave. Her ability to sell programmes, tickets, etc. to even the most reluctant athlete has gained her the grateful thanks of many a race organiser. The election of Ray Middleton as President of Belgrave Harriers cannot do other than increase the Club's standing in athletic circles because his pleasing personality, high sense of sportsmanship and cheery cockney humour will quickly enable him to gain the friendship and respect of everyone he meets. Before his year in office is over some members may forget his surname but, as in race walking circles. his popularity will be noted by the frequent reference to "Ray" in conversation about Belgrave affairs. items.label: October 1978
items.sum: Feature on Ernest Obeng's 1978 sprint season: club records at 100 and 200 metres, victory over Don Quarrie at the Philips International Games, Inter-Counties and SCAAA titles, 8th in the Commonwealth Games 100 metres final at Edmonton for Ghana, and 10.29 at the Rotary Watches International Games.
items.s: Great sprinting from Ernest Obeng Feature on Ernest Obeng's 1978 sprint season: club records at 100 and 200 metres, victory over Don Quarrie at the Philips International Games, Inter-Counties and SCAAA titles, 8th in the Commonwealth Games 100 metres final at Edmonton for Ghana, and 10.29 at the Rotary Watches International Games. Great sprinting from Ernest Obeng Those interested in track athletics will remember 1978 as the year in which Scotland's Allan Wells rose from obscurity to the highest levels of world class sprinting. In Belgrave, however, we have another reason to mark the '78 season as a special one - Ernest Obeng's equally meteoric rise to very nearly the same standard. In 1977 Ernest, a chemistry student at Chelsea College, University of London, had taken our Club Record for 100 metres down from 10.7 to 10.5 and also set new figures for the 200 metres of 21.5. His best fully automatic timing over the shorter race was 10.74 and it is interesting to note that the difference of .24 seconds between his best "auto" and "manual" times is exactly the conversion factor applied by track statisticians when measuring one against the other. A winter of hard work with coach Martin Coomber ironed out the wrinkles in Ernie's technique and as early as March in indoor competition he posted a warning to his rivals by winning three 60 metre races on the same day, all in 6.8 seconds; then in the Blackheath H[illegible] Winter Meeting he scored his first outdoor success of the season - 1st over 100 metres in 10.8. Representing the Southern Counties on April 26th he streaked to a resounding win with a new Club Record of 10.4 with the second man a full five metres behind and back on the same track, Crystal Palace, a week later, he proved the former run was no fluke by clocking 10.5 and also reducing our 200 metre best to 21.4. Now came his sweetest victory to date and one which earned him respect far beyond Crystal Palace, the scene of his triumph. Lined up for the start of the Philips International Games 100 metres on May 24th were two fairly highly rated Americans, Britain's number two sprinter Mike McFarlane and the Olympic 200 metre champion Don Quarrie of Jamaica. Ernie stormed down the straight heading the field all the way to defeat Quarrie - 10.3 to 10.4 (photo-electric timing not in use). The Inter-Counties Championships came and racing in Surrey's colours Ernie gave Belgrave their first champion in this meeting since 1966 when Geoff North took the 3 miles. His 10.46, without wind aid, was a Championship Best Performance. Likewise the SCAAA Champs, where a windy 10.34 kept him well clear of the field for another CBP, and where for good measure he also gained 3rd in the 200 metres and our Club Record for the longer event took another dive to 21.36. Far from being unranked back in April among the top Commonwealth contenders, Ernie, who packs more power into his five foot six frame than many another six footer, was now being tipped to reach the semi-finals at Edmonton if only he could gain recognition in his native Ghana. Having met some of the best in the world in 1978 he was still unbeaten over his speciality, the 100 metres. However, after clocking 10.58 twice in the preliminary rounds of the AAA Champs on July 24th he suffered his first defeat at the hands of Sanford (USA) and Abrahams (Panama) in the final where a headwind kept them down to 10.42, 10.53 and 10.67 respectively. Now Ernie left the scene for a short while to compete in the African Games where Ghana at last recognised his talent and put him on their list of entries for the Commonwealth Games. And so to Edmonton, Canada, and the XI Commonwealth Games..... On August 6th the first round of the 100 metres took place and into a slight breeze Ernie won his heat just 1/100th outside his best time with 10.47. The second round had him matched against Quarrie again who this time got the better of the battle - 10.36 to 10.44 and Ernie's 5th Club Record of the season. A swirling wind the following day made things difficult for all the runners. The first semi was taken impressively by Wells (Scotland) in 10.31 but in the second race Quarrie hit his best form at the crucial time, equalling the Games Record with 10.19 ahead of Haseley Crawford (Trinidad) the Olympic 100 metre champion in 10.24. Gilkes (Guyana) placed 3rd in 10.31 and right on his tail came Ernie with 10.32 and a place in the final. By now the wind was gusting dramatically and the final got under way with a following blast of nearly four times the legal limit At 50 metres Crawford showed just ahead of Wells but as the line was approached Quarrie came through to take his 6th Commonwealth Games "Gold". Ernie placed 5th or 6th at 70 metres but faded at the very end for 8th. 1. D.Quarrie (Jamaica) 10.03 Games Record; 2. A.Wells (Scotland) 10.07; 3. H.Crawford (Trinidad) 10.09; 4. J.Gilkes (Guyana) 10.15; 5. M.McFarlane (England) 10.29; 6. P.Narracott (Australia) 10.31; 7. C.Braithwaite (Trinidad) 10.32; 8. E.Obeng (Ghana) 10.34. Good running on the lead-off leg for Ghana's 4 x 100 metre squad enabled Ernie to share in a 39.74 timing for 5th place in the final. One might have thought that this was a fine note on which to end the season but our member still had his best run yet to come. The Rotary Watches International Games saw one of the best 100 metre line-ups seen in the United Kingdom: Silvio Leonard (Cuba) - the world's fastest in 1977 with an incredible 9.98, Osvaldo Lara (Cuba) - a best of 10.11, Charlie Wells (USA), Allan Wells, Haseley Crawford and Ernest Obeng. The race was a cracker, producing the tightest of finishes. Leonard was judged the winner in 10.26 from Crawford 10.26 and .... Obeng 10.29! Scotland's Wells was 4th 10.33 with Lara and Charlie Wells back down the field in 5th and 6th. A tremendous time by Ernie and with the wind OK he claimed his 6th improvement on his own and Club's best performances during the '78 season. One more run was to come. The Coca-Cola meeting 100 metres was run into a cool evening breeze and did not produce spectacular times but Ernie was still in form and obviously delighted with his 3rd place behind Crawford and Gilkes but ahead of Clancy Edwards of the USA (owner of one of the fastest times in the world for 1978) and our old friend Don Quarrie. A remarkable season by our Ghanaian member. Footnote: The African Games results were late coming in but reveal that Ernie placed 5th in the 100m final in 10.58 after a 10.42 heat (wind readings unknown). He also reached the semi-final of the 200m with a 21.46 heat but was then eliminated. items.sum: Introduction by Ray Hall to the ladies' section's second full track season in two leagues, noting the need for middle-distance runners, coaches and officials and listing the venues visited.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Introduction by Ray Hall to the ladies' section's second full track season in two leagues, noting the need for middle-distance runners, coaches and officials and listing the venues visited. WITH THE LADIES We have not won any great honours in our second full track season but we have competed with credit and gained much experience, participating in two different leagues giving competition for 11 years old and upwards. I intend to write about each league separately. You will see we lack competitors in the middle distance events and we need assistance in all quarters concerning coaches and officials. We have travelled like a mini "Cooks Tour" competing at Portsmouth next to the harbour, Hastings where we did battle, Dorking in the shadow of Box Hill, Erith next to the marshes, Redhill in sight of the Fullers Earth quarries... plus our own home matches. Now say athletics is not educational! reports by Ray Hall Ray Hall Ray Hall Portsmouth Hastings Dorking Box Hill Erith Redhill

items.s: Southern League Division 4 Ray Hall's report on the Belgrave ladies' three matches in Southern League Division 4 (Portsmouth, Wimbledon Park and Erith), with junior and senior club records and full results of all three matches. Southern League Division 4 In this section we competed against five clubs (Portsmouth B, Hastings AC, Hercules Wimbledon, Bexley Borough and Dartford B) in three matches. All these matches were closely fought especially in the middle order where you will note we lost a place by one point in two competitions. The first match meant a coach trip to Portsmouth where we had few winners but some fine performances from Shirley Rook (800m/1500m senior), Anne Slattery (senior javelin), Marjorie Woodward (3000m) and the 4 x 400m team made up of 3 field events girls Karen Smith, Wendy Dunsford, Anne Slattery and Valerie Bridges who ran the fastest leg. Of the juniors, the Taylor sisters Pam and Angela, Tina Couzens Barbara Dunsford and M[illegible] Sexton competed with success on the field whilst on the track Lorna Brown and Celia Estwick ran well in the 200m. The next match, our home match at Wimbledon Park, was notable for Junior Club Records by Glenda Mahoney (100/200m) Angela Taylor (75m hurdles) and Veronica St. Ange (Javelin). Senior Shirley Rook gained club records in the 800m and 3000m and Dawn McNeil worked hard by competing in no less than five events. Our Captain Wendy Dunsford had two seconds and a third in the field. After holding high hopes for this match we were disappointed to only finish 5th but just five more points would have placed us 3rd, so closely contested was this match. The last competition in the Southern League for us this year was at Erith. Our only win came in the Senior Shot thanks to Wendy Dunsford in the 'A' string and the ever present Anne Slattery, 'B' string. The meeting was notable for the help from our walkers, Jane Pritchard Linda Nicolls and Anna Matthews who ran in the 800m 1500m and 3000m to help the team. New names appeared in Belgrave colours, with the seniors Ruth Johnson (Dawn's sister), Angela Sharp (a converted sprinter from Durham) and Sarah Laing, who all competed in events they had not done before. We must mention a word about the courage shown by Dawn MacNeil who was injured in the high jump and had to retire, but came back later to anchor the relay team with a great run for their second fastest time of the season. You should have seen her later attempting to walk down the stairs at Clapham Junction. APRIL 22ND 1978 - PORTSMOUTH - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. items.sum: Light-hearted account by 'An Onlooker' of the walking section turning out in force at the AGM to elect Ray Middleton President.
items.s: The Night of the A.G.M. Light-hearted account by 'An Onlooker' of the walking section turning out in force at the AGM to elect Ray Middleton President. The Night of the A.G.M. They came in small groups of twos and threes, making their way toward the canteen. Who were these people I wondered. Could they be the K.G.B. I waited with bated breath. When the meeting started they showed their strength by grouping on the right side facing the chair. It was some time before we were enlightened. They proved to be the walking section of whom we hear quite a lot but rarely see. They had come to promote one of their top men to be President. I gave a sigh of relief. Good luck during your term of office Ray Middleton. I am sure you will do a good job. An Onlooker. Ray Middleton Ray Middleton elected President at the AGM Annual General Meeting

items.sum: Ray Hall's report on the Belgrave girls and juniors in the Lily B League, with matches at Battersea Park and Battlebridge, Redhill, and results of the Battersea Park and Redhill matches.
items.s: Lily B League Ray Hall's report on the Belgrave girls and juniors in the Lily B League, with matches at Battersea Park and Battlebridge, Redhill, and results of the Battersea Park and Redhill matches. Lily B League This league is for girls 11-12 years old and juniors 13-14 years old and we competed against Aldershot & Farnham "B", Camberley & District Dorking St. Pauls and Redhill & Reigate. First of the three matches took place at Battersea Park on May 28th on one of those few pleasant days we have had this summer. In the girls events we lacked competitors in some of the field events and this without a doubt cost us important points in the final classification. In the sprints Pam St. Ange and Janet Bridges ran well to win their events and they were also members of the winning relay team. Bernadette Sexton had a busy afternoon with a second place in the walk, third in the "B" 800 metres and second in the "B" javelin. Antonia Ugbade won the "B" 75 metre hurdles and Alison Jones was second in the "B" long jump, both these girls competing for the "Belles" for the first time. In the junior section we found a javelin thrower in Veronica St. Ange who finished with 19.30m. Glenda Mohoney won the 100 metres and placed second in the high jump, whilst Caroline Khan had a hard afternoon with second in the 1,600 metre walk and third in the 1,500 metres with a personal best. Barbara gained three firsts, the 1,600 metre walk, the "B" shot and the "A" discus. Not far behind came Karen Norris with two firsts - the "A" shot and the "B" javelin. Pam and Angela Taylor had successful afternoons and Joanna Warnett raced well to finish 2nd in the "A" 800m in a personal best. In the end we failed by four points to gain second place over Dorking St. Pauls. On a Sunday afternoon we travelled to Battlebridge, Redhill to renew our battle with Dorking St. Pauls, and both teams ended up closer to Aldershot than in the first match. Aldershot, Dorking and Belgrave each took a turn in the lead during the second half of the match. Our winners in the girls were Antonia Ugbade, who took the "B" 75m hurdles and also placed second in the "B" 200 metres, Jackie Weldin, who won the shot and discus in her first outing for Belgrave, Bernadette Sexton, who took part in three events including her winning 1,000 metre walk, and Janet Bridges - the "B" 100 metres. Much better all round performances in this section. Our junior sprinters did us proud with three wins and a second place. Glenda Mohoney took the "A" 100 metres, equalling her best of 12.9, and in the "B" events Lorna Brown won the 100 metres and Celia Estwick the 200 metres. The 1,600 metre walk saw Caroline Khan doing well for second place and a personal best, being very well supported by Rosalind Morris who won the "B" string. items.s: Seven Club Records Report and results of the Belgrave ladies' first trophy match, the inter-club trophy meeting at Hastings, where seven club records were set and Belgrave Harriers placed third. JULY 29th 1978 - HASTINGS - INTER-CLUB TROPHY MEETING. Seven Club Records We gave the away day tickets a try for our Sussex by the sea trip. This meeting was the first trophy match our ladies team had been invited to - an historical event. The match was also notable for the fact that no fewer than seven new Club records were set in the three different age groups. We travelled without any hurdlers and so we asked four people to compete in events they had never done before and, remarkably, we finished with one first and three second places because their rivals fell or failed to finish. The girls and juniors broke their relay records and now the junior team is faster than the seniors! A special word of praise for Claudette Jackson for her courage after being injured in the 100 metres. After being taken to hospital for patching up and injections, she came back to compete in the 200 metres, 400 metres, high jump and relay. items.sum: Bill Laws's report on the 100 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 4 June 1978, where Laurie O'Hara's last-stage chase left Belgrave 3 metres behind Cambridge Harriers, 3rd at the Palace and 7th nationally, with a photograph of a baton change, the 100 Belgrave stage times (total 9:00:58) and the leading team results.
items.s: 100x1 mile relay Bill Laws's report on the 100 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 4 June 1978, where Laurie O'Hara's last-stage chase left Belgrave 3 metres behind Cambridge Harriers, 3rd at the Palace and 7th nationally, with a photograph of a baton change, the 100 Belgrave stage times (total 9:00:58) and the leading team results. JUNE 4th 1978 - CRYSTAL PALACE. 100x1 mile relay For the many supporters who stayed to watch the closing stages of the 100 x 1 mile relay at the Crystal Palace the close finish between Belgrave and Cambridge Harriers provided the most exciting racing seen so far in this event. After 100 miles only three metres or half a second separated Laurie O'Hara from Cambridge's last stage runner. The story started at 10am in perfect weather conditions when 11 teams at the Palace together with a further 29 teams at other venues began this marathon team event. The Bels. made a steady start placing 17th nationally and 7th at the Palace after the first 10 miles. Hopes for a rapid rise through the field were not realised as several of our middle distance runners failed to appear. It was fortunate that 18 reserves had turned up and as it turned out each of them was needed - the last being our President John Baker who had spent the day booking in team members (and chasing those who had not paid their subs). By 80 miles Bels. had moved to 5th place at the Palace and 11th nationally. Everyone was confident that our last ten scheduled runners - all of them track specialists - would move through the field. So it was that at the 93rd mile Bels. passed Croydon and on stage 95 passed Hercules Wimbledon who had run out of senior runners. Cambridge, who were 1½ miles ahead, looked out of reach but a series of good runs meant that Laurie O'Hara took over the last stage some 600 metres down on the Cambridge President. A first lap by our remarkable veteran in 64 seconds rapidly cut into the lead and by now all the spectators were cheering, fully anticipating the prospect of a close finish. And so to the last lap. Laurie entered the finishing straight in a sustained sprint some 50 metres down and despite all his efforts failed by a mere 3 metres. Belgrave finally placed 3rd at Crystal Palace and 7th nationally. The time was slower than in recent years, the only Belgrave record being set by Bill Couzens who once again sat through the whole day recording individual lap and mile times. Other faithful stalwarts also worked flat out all day and special thanks are due to Brian Pritchard, Gordon Doubleday, Tom Carter and John Baker. It was good to see how many of our boys and youths are progressing and special mention should be made of Mark Waller's, Matthew Cannon's David North's and John Searle's fine runs. Several old faces made a welcome re-appearance and rumour has it that old 'TK' will be battling it out with Tony Fairclough this winter. John Stow made a welcome return to clock fastest of the day Bill Laws. (It would be remiss of us not to mention Bill's own contribution to our day's competition, co-ordinating the Belgrave effort as usual.) 100 x 1 MILE RELAY continued. 1. Sale 8:01:03.5; 2. items.label: October 1978
items.sum: Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's review of the summer: 34 men and 8 girls registered, the remarkable season of new member Derek Howie, a virtually blind Scot, Graham Seatter's club records, John Knifton's 50Km run, the girls' Lily B League placings and a 6th place in the McSweeney Trophy.
items.s: WALKING Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's review of the summer: 34 men and 8 girls registered, the remarkable season of new member Derek Howie, a virtually blind Scot, Graham Seatter's club records, John Knifton's 50Km run, the girls' Lily B League placings and a 6th place in the McSweeney Trophy. WALKING The summer season is now past and there are not many trophies in the cupboard. We have tried and although we managed it sometimes, on many occasions we failed to be there first. Looking down the list of registered competitors, i.e. those that replied to the circular sent out towards the end of last year, we have 34 competing walkers on the mens' side and 8 girls. This is the largest number we have had for some years and maybe this is a good sign for the future but with such a number, some of us should not become disinterested and expect someone else to turn out all the time. Each individual should feel part of the team whether or not he actually picks up the prizes or medals. Over the last few months we have had a few more useful additions to our numbers. The most prominent of these is Derek Howie. Having competed in three Nationals this year any doubts as to his authenticity to compete have been completely dispelled. In December last year the Club was contacted with regards to his application for membership. A Scotsman, living in Scotland, he was partially coached by Bob Coates and wanted to join Belgrave but there was one small problem (to us not to him) for he is virtually blind. This is obviously something that has to be considered as regards competing on the roads but the Club took the bull by the horns and accepted his membership. Derek had never raced on the roads until January of this year although he had done a few track races with credit. Since then Derek's performances have been astounding. In the National '10' he was 14th, in the Brighton to Steyning over one of the most arduous and difficult road courses he was 8th, and he was selected to compete for Scotland against Greece in Athens. To top this he then placed 12th in the National 30Km to win the Sidney Bayliss Cup for Belgrave's first man and also gained a Club honours badge. In the National 50Km he was second Belgravian home and in the Hastings to Brighton event he led our team to victory with an individual 5th place! Graham Seatter made a short stop off to England in June en route for Canada and the Commonwealth Games. He competed for us on a few occasions including 4th in the A.A.A. 3Km. Since his return to New Zealand last November he has notched up two club records - these being for 10 and 3 kilometres. John Knifton, on tour with the U.S.A. Olympic squad, competed in the National 50Km at Stretford and was our first man to finish. On the Girls' side we have had rather a quiet summer with nothing outstanding to report. Exams and other commitments have rather restricted progress but with these now out of the way for most of them, we can look forward to a hard and successful winter with full team turn outs now that Linda Nicholls has become eligible for team events. On the lesser known side of walking is the Lily B League for Girls under 15. As with last year we have been able to produce some placings in the two walks that are held in these meetings and Barbara Dunsford, Bernadette Sexton and newcomer Caroline Carne have been able to keep up the same standard this year. Overall the Club can look forward to some good results during the coming season if everyone pulls together. We start off with the National Junior, Youths and Boys Championships and although we may struggle a bit in the latter championship there should be no excuse in the other two. On the Girls side we very nearly got medals last year so we look forward to some good results. As a result of the National 50Km in which we could only finish 6th our final National placing in the McSweeney Trophy was 6th, our lowest for years. Although it looks disastrous at first, a closer look and some quick calculations show that had we started a Youths team in the championship we could well have been placed 2nd if not 1st. So, next year an all out effort and ....... items.s: A lesson in packing Gordon Doubleday's report and results of the Southern Counties Ten Miles walk championship in Battersea Park, won by Bill Wright of Southampton, where Steyning A.C.'s team packing beat Belgrave into second place, with Belgrave placings in the supporting 5Km walks. MARCH 4th 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN R.W.A. 10 MILES CHAMPS. A lesson in packing With our long history of team wins we naturally appreciate good team packing and Steyning A.C. gave us a fine demonstration in the Southern Counties Ten Miles Championship. Steyning is a village nestling under the Northern slopes of the South Downs which has a walking tradition extending over many decades and has indeed produced one Olympic Champion, Norman Read, who won the 50 kilos walk in 1960 wearing the colours of New Zealand. The Individual winner was Bill Wright (Southampton), his first win in a race of this class. His performances in 'Opens' have been improving for some time and he took control of the race right from the start. He was followed closely by Carl with the third man hot on his heels. John Hall gave us another fine well-judged performance and then came the Steyning team. Our third and fourth scorers did well to bring us second place - not bad for Ray and John Bromley who, between them have carried the Bels colours for over fifty years! As befits a race in Battersea Park there were plenty more familiar Belgrave faces in the field. At the same time there were supporting events on the track and our younger members, including the ladies, gave their usual encouraging performances. 1.W.Wright (Soton) 73:22; 2.C.Lawton 74:02; 5.J.Hall 75:15; 22.R.
