items.sum: Gordon Doubleday's report on the 32nd National Ten Miles walk championship at Crystal Palace on 18 March 1978 (won by Olly Flynn on a short course, Belgrave third team, Derek Howie 14th; the text gives his time as 71m.53s and the results as 71:52), opening with a history of Belgrave's record in the event since 1947 and a year-by-year list of Belgrave placings.
items.s: The R.W.A. 10 Gordon Doubleday's report on the 32nd National Ten Miles walk championship at Crystal Palace on 18 March 1978 (won by Olly Flynn on a short course, Belgrave third team, Derek Howie 14th; the text gives his time as 71m.53s and the results as 71:52), opening with a history of Belgrave's record in the event since 1947 and a year-by-year list of Belgrave placings. MARCH 18th 1978 - CRYSTAL PALACE. The R.W.A. 10 With race programmes diminishing in size and detail the programme for the 32nd Annual National Ten Miles Championship was excellent value at tenpence. Not only did it give the names of officials and competitors but it was the first occasion upon which walkers individual numbers were worn (i.e. permanent ones issued to them by the R.W.A. through their clubs and to be worn at all open events). Then came lists of the first 3 to finish and first three teams since the first race in 1947. Here, it may be recalled that immediately prior to World War II the Bels had been unbeatable in team races over the seven to ten miles range but unfortunately there was no National Championship. After the war our walkers soon got down to things at Belgrave Hall and our winning ways continued and it is no surprise that we won the first National 10 held at Sheffield with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland taking the first two places. Charlie Churcher was 8th and didn't get a team medal! Looking down over the years we find that Sheffield and ourselves have won the title eleven times each, with ourselves claiming eight seconds to their four and three thirds to their six. Prior to the war the Inter-Counties Walk had been held annually since 1934 as a separate event and in 1948 it was held in conjunction with the National Title. Naturally a number of Belgravians have helped their counties. It is perhaps worth while going back over the years and recalling the Belgravians who have served us so well in this event, the most popular of the National Walking Championships. Composition of winning teams given: Incidentally the first Belgravian to finish holds the Frank Thomson Trophy for a year. Frank was a Past President of the Club and the R.W.A. (of which he was also an elected Life-Member). A great Battersea Park man, he also judged and coached Track and Field Events. Allan's Back It was good to see the cheery figure of Allan Callow on arrival at the Crystal Palace for this years R.W.A. '10'. He was already in his tracksuit ready to battle for the Bels. again. There was some sunshine but a decided nip in the air. The start had been delayed as news had come through that most of the Sheffield team (the holders) were still on the road having been delayed on the motorway. Unfortunately they didn't arrive until after the "field" was off. In fact it was over six minutes after the "off" that they were able to pin on their numbers and get going - a gap that no aspiring winners could hope to close. Another hitch was that due to a landslip the original course of seven laps couldn't be used owing to mud and water on the course, an alternative course of four laps (out and home) had been quickly planned. At the end of the first lap (covered in less than 17 minutes) Olly Flynn (Basildon) had opened up a gap on Brian Adams (Leicester) who was clear of the rest of the field. Carl was in the leading group with John well placed and it wasn't long before Allan came through with Ray moving strongly to complete our four. At halfway the leader was just inside 33 minutes, clearly a fast time was in view - or was the course suspect? Olly and Brian kept their places to the finish with very fast times - it turned out that the course was short so fast times and personal bests were in plenty. A good race for third place resulted in the bronze going to young Graham Morris (Steyning A.C.). Carl led the team home again and John maintained the fine form he has been showing. Allan celebrated his return home with a good turn of speed and Ray, dependable as ever, closed the team in. The team positions were difficult to assess so it was wait and see! As things turned out Ilford A.C. were clear winners with Leicester W.C. (who started only the minimum of four) a few points ahead of us. So, once again, our walkers rose to the occasion to gain third team medals. Congratulations to our walkers for adding to our many past successes in this race. We must not overlook the great performance of our new member Derek Howie. Making his first appearance in a National Championship he competed as an individual and finished in 14th place in 71m.53s. What is remarkable is that this was only his third road race and he is almost completely blind. He is a student at Stirling University and should be a strong contender for a Scotland vest. 1.O.Flynn (Bas) 67:29; 2.B.Adams (Leics) 68:13; 3.G.Morris 69:08; 7. Acting as a track judge at the Ministry of Defence Sports, held at Motspur Park, was former Club sprint champion S.C.Botwright. Just before World War II started Stan was triple champion, holding our 100, 220 and 440 yards titles. He was also prominent in Civil Service and Middlesex County Championships as well as a regular in inter-club matches. Naturally he was asking after old friends and talked of Boxing Day Handicaps and Club socials. APRIL 29th 1978 - CROYDON - ENGLISH SCHOOLS CHAMPIONSHIPS Five Years Old The fifth English Schools Athletic Association Race Walking Champs were held from Monks' Hill Sports Centre, South Croydon. Testing courses had been planned over undulating laps with the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. providing key officials. The first event, Junior Girls 2,500m, had Tracy McDermot (Mddx.) lining up for her fifth race and in clocking 14:55 to finish 31st she showed the improvement predicted in the report on her first effort at Enfield in November. We also had a representative in the Boys' 3,000m, P.Porter who finished 36th. The Intermediate Girls' 3,000m saw two of our girls in action. Linda Nicholls (Kent) finished 9th in 17:22 and was unlucky not to get a team medal. Kent tied with Hereford and Worcester for 3rd place but were placed fourth under A.A.A. Laws. Jane Pritchard was London's only representative; a great team walker, she finished 19th in 18:25. For the complete programme of six events London could only muster six competitors, for most of the capital's walkers came from the outer boroughs and so represented various home counties. The Intermediate Boys' 5,000m saw three of ours in action. Michael Nicholls did well to finish 8th in 24:54 and collected a winning team medal for Kent. This gave particular pleasure to Harold King, himself a Kent County Champion in the 'thirties. Kevin McDermot (Mddx.) put up a PB to finish 20th in 26:05, whilst S.Sethi did a creditable 27:03 to finish 29th. Peter Morris was on the sidelines as a reserve for Surrey, unfortunately he had an "off-day" on the day of the trial; had he walked he would have gained a good placing. Anna Matthews lined up for London in the Senior Girls 5,000m and soon settled down in 4th place, a position she held to the finish where the watches showed 29:02. She had made a great effort and seemed distressed afterwards but soon recovered. The Senior Boys 10,000m had quite a "classy" line up, many of the competitors having done well against Seniors in open races. After the first of the seven laps Richard Dorman (Surrey) and Trevor McDermot (Mddx.) were in a group in 4th position. As the laps went by our two pulled away and it looked like 4th and 5th for us. Coming into the finish Richard had a short lead but Trevor put in a great effort to catch him. However, Richard found sufficient speed to keep him away. Great stuff from these two which highly pleased Club supporters, their times were 49:59 and 50:05 respectively. These championships, now five years old, look like being here to stay - they get fine support from the R.W.A. Some great walking from Britain's stars of the future - it was good to see ten Belgravians carrying their county colours with such credit. items.s: Coventry - Unlucky City Report and result of the R.W.A. 20Km championship at Coventry on 13 May 1978, won by Olly Flynn, where John Hall's disqualification left Belgrave 7th team, with a list of Belgrave's team record in the event since 1965. MAY 13th 1978 - COVENTRY - R.W.A. 20Km CHAMPIONSHIP. Coventry - Unlucky City Not a very fitting description of this famous Midlands city which, in addition to many fine institutions, has great sporting traditions. However, last year we tied for 3rd place in the R.W.A. National '10' only to be placed 4th under the A.A.A. Rules covering such eventualities. This year we went there for the 20 kilo's championship and fared even worse! John Hall was disqualified on the last of the three laps and so we had to go back to Len Duquemin in 44th scoring position to complete the team. At halfway the team position looked very open, Sheffield, Steyning, Ilford, Coventry and ourselves were doing well and the holders, Sheffield, didn't seem to have a stranglehold on the title as they did last year. Olly Flynn (Basildon) scored his fifth consecutive individual win with Brian Adams (Leicester) passing Roger Mills (Ilford) for second place. Carl walked well for 6th place and then came a flush of Steyning and Sheffield vests. Allan was our next man then Ray - but where was John Hall? Alas he had been disqualified and obviously it was no medals this time. Mike Scamell, now first-claim, finished a creditable 32nd and when he is eligible for us he will be strong addition to our teams. We sincerely congratulate Steyning A.C. on their team win, beating strong teams from Sheffield and Ilford. 1. O.Flynn (Basildon) 88:44; 2. B.Adams (Leicester) 89:47; 3. R. Mills (Ilford) 90:42; 6. items.s: Boxed note on John Hall's Sussex championship hat-trick at 3Km, 10Km and 20Km and his 5th and 4th places at the Inter-Counties walks at Cwmbran. Not one to let a dubious disqualification in the National 20Km upset him, John Hall bounced back the following day, May 14th, to win the Sussex 3Km in 13:18. This made a hat-trick of Sussex championships for John: on January 21st he took the 20Km title and on May 7th the 10Km in 46:05 Representing his county in the Inter-Counties meeting at Cwmbran on May 28th/29th, John took 5th over 10Km in 47:37 and in the 3Km scored 4th with yet another PB - 12:57. John Hall John Hall won Sussex 3Km (13:18), 10Km (46:05) and 20Km walk titles 1978; Inter-Counties 5th 10Km 47:37, 4th 3Km 12:57 PB John Hall John Sussex Walking Championships Inter-Counties National 20Km walk Cwmbran

items.s: JULY 15th 1978 - STRETFORD - R.W.A. NATIONAL 50KM CHAMPIONSHIP. Club Trophy Goes West Report and result of the R.W.A. National 50Km championship at Stretford on 15 July 1978, where John Knifton, home from the U.S.A., won the Belchamber trophy as first Belgravian and the club finished 6th in the team race won by Sheffield United Harriers; a paragraph is typed twice, first unfinished then in full. JULY 15th 1978 - STRETFORD - R.W.A. NATIONAL 50KM CHAMPIONSHIP. Club Trophy Goes West The late Jimmy Belchamber did much for the Club in the years between the two World Wars, particularly with regard towards the walkers. He was no mean performer himself over the longer distances and was also one of the Club's Hon. Auditors for many years. After he died we were presented with a trophy to perpetuate his memory, to be awarded to the first Belgrave man home in the R.W.A. 50 Km Championship. For many years past the trophy has had pride of place at a certain house in Hendon. This year, alas, Ray Middleton had to miss the race because of injury (he has competed in every 50 kilos since 1961). The Club's performance was a below par one, we were down to 6th place in the team championship with the winners being Sheffield United Harriers who must be congratulated on finishing their team in 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th positions - perfect packing. They also took the Milan Trophy with their eighth walker in 42nd position. Making a welcome re-appearance in our team was John Knifton, home on holiday from the U.S.A. where he now lives. He celebrated his return by being our first to finish over the seven lap course; so the Club trophy goes to the United States where John has won A.A.U. Walking titles. He was closely followed by Derek Howie, walking as an individual, with John Hall taking 3rd place in the Club Championship. Carl Lawton and Bob Picton completed the team. 1978 will not go down as a good year for us regarding the Championships. Our record in this event is unapproached by any other club. Of the forty team championships held to date Although 1978 will not go down as a good year for us regarding team championships our record in this event is unapproached by any other club. Of the forty team championships held to date we have won 17, with 11 and 6 second and third placings respectively. Definitely an "off" year. John's journey from Texas must be the farthest ever mad to win a Club Championship. Congratulations John once again. 1.D.Cotton (Holloway) 4:14:25; 2. I.Richards (Coventry) 4:18:32; 3. Report and result of the R.W.A. invitation 20Km road walk at Stretford on 16 July 1978, won by Graham Seatter in a new club record of 87:37. JULY 16th 1978 - STRETFORD - R.W.A. INVITATION 20 KM ROAD WALK. The Morning After! Over the same course at Stretford the R.W.A. held an invitation 20 kilos walk the following morning. A select field of 18 started. The result was a great win for Graham Seatter who finished nearly three minutes ahead of his old rivals Roger Mills (Ilford) and Amos Seddon (Boro' of Enfield). At 5km he was one second ahead of Roger in 22:11 but by 10km he had a 39 second lead in 43:59. By 15km the lead was extended to 2 minutes 9 seconds and Graham sped over the last 5km in 22 minutes dead to win in 87:37. This is the fastest time by a British clubman for several years and is a new Club Record. Congratulations on some great walking Graham, its good to see you back in such great form - a great day. Allan Callow and Derek Howie (who had competed in the longer race the previous day) were our other representatives. 1. G.Seatter 87:37; 2. R.Mills (Ilford) 90:32; 3. items.sum: Boxed note, prompted by John Keown, on J.N. Thomas, the Belgrave walker who between 1921 and 1929 was the first to complete three London to Brighton and Back walks, and on John Keown's chance to equal him at Ewhurst.
items.s: Boxed note, prompted by John Keown, on J.N. Thomas, the Belgrave walker who between 1921 and 1929 was the first to complete three London to Brighton and Back walks, and on John Keown's chance to equal him at Ewhurst. John Keown has drawn our attention to the feats of a great Belgrave long-distance walker of the past. Between 1921 and 1929 J.N. Thomas became the first walker in history to successfully complete three successive London to Brighton and Back Walks (104 miles). He started walking as a novice at the age of 44 in 1919. Two years later he tackled his first B & B - 24h:23m.42s. In 1926 at 51 he did it again in 22h:28m.04s. In 1929 at 54 he put up his best performance of 21h:35m.07s and he figured prominently in several ' 'Brightons'. He died round about 1932. In 1971 Surrey W.C. decided to stop using the London to Brighton road for this race and instead a ten lap course at Ewhurst (Surrey) is used. John, having completed two Ewhurst 100's could well equal Thomas' feat when the race is held next year. John Keown John Keown completed two Ewhurst 100s; could equal Thomas' feat next year John Keown John J.N. Thomas J.N. items.h: MAY 8th - 13th 1978 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS. Pat Lyttle's County Double
items.sum: Report on Belgrave youths and boys at the Surrey County Championships at Motspur Park in May 1978, where Patrick Lyttle won the Boys 100 and 200 metres.
items.s: MAY 8th - 13th 1978 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS. Pat Lyttle's County Double Report on Belgrave youths and boys at the Surrey County Championships at Motspur Park in May 1978, where Patrick Lyttle won the Boys 100 and 200 metres. Reports by Leo Coy MAY 8th - 13th 1978 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS. Pat Lyttle's County Double Our youths and boys were a bit thin on the ground at this year's Surrey Championships but still managed to gain three medals. Patrick Lyttle was the star performer. First in his heat of the Boys 100 metres with the fastest heat time of 12.6, he went on to win the final in a time one tenth faster still. He was also unbeaten in the longer sprint, setting the fastest time of the championships with a heat time of 25 seconds dead and then maintaining his winning streak with a narrow victory in the final. Pat placed 4th in the long jump with 5.19 metres to round off a successful couple of days work. Chris Powley was clocked at 12.8 for 3rd in his preliminary round of the Youths 100 metres but did not quite make the final. On the field Stuart King heaved the Youth shot out to 13.01 metres for 2nd and just missed the medals in the discus with 37.74 metres and 4th spot. Our only middle distance man in action was John Searle whose 2:11.0 and 4:37.5 did not get him beyond the heats of the Youths 800 metres and 1,500 metres. Leo Coy Leo Coy Patrick Lyttle Patrick Lyttle won Surrey Boys 100m (12.5) and 200m (fastest heat 25.0); 4th long jump 5.19m Pat Lyttle Patrick Lyttle Pat Chris Powley Chris Powley 12.8, 3rd in preliminary round of Youths 100m Stuart King Stuart King 2nd Youth shot 13.01m; 4th discus 37.74m John Searle John Searle Youths 800m heats 2:11.0, 1,500m heats 4:37.5 Surrey County Championships Motspur Park

Hurdlers set the pace Report and results of Ebbisham League match 1 at Carshalton on 20 May 1978, won by Belgrave's boys and colts led by Pat Lyttle and Matt Cannon. MAY 20th 1978 - CARSHALTON - EBBISHAM LEAGUE MATCH 1 Hurdlers set the pace Belgrave started their league campaign with a visit to Carshalton track with a small team and not very much confidence. All changed after the first few events when the Bels. stormed into the lead after fine wins by R.Taylor and P.Thorp in the hurdles. For the rest of the afternoon we were never headed and ended up clear winners from Guildford & Godalming. Each member of the team showed great competitiveness and fought for every point. Pat Lyttle showed his class with three wins plus a relay victory and was ably supported by Matt Cannon who gained two wins and a 2nd. This great win set us up for the remaining two league matches and hopefully for promotion to division one next year. JUNE 3rd 1978 - WIMBLEDON PARK - EBBISHAM LEAGUE MATCH 2 Second Ebbisham win Again our hurdlers got us off to a flying start and we were never out of first place during the afternoon. With two new faces competing for the first time, Paul Gerhard and Simon Simpson, we were much stronger and won 14 events in all. With one match to go and Epsom and Guildford fighting it out for the second promotion spot, the last match was likely to be a formality. items.h: JULY 12th 1978 - WIMBLEDON PARK - H.A.C. MEMORIAL TROPHY. Matt Cannon (14) 2:05.1
items.sum: Report and results of the H.A.C. Memorial Trophy at Wimbledon Park on 12 July 1978, where an under-strength Belgrave finished third, their best ever position, with Mark Waller winning the Youths 800m and Matt Cannon (14) winning the Boys 800m in 2:05.1, just outside the 1961 club record.
items.s: JULY 12th 1978 - WIMBLEDON PARK - H.A.C. MEMORIAL TROPHY. Matt Cannon (14) 2:05.1 Report and results of the H.A.C. Memorial Trophy at Wimbledon Park on 12 July 1978, where an under-strength Belgrave finished third, their best ever position, with Mark Waller winning the Youths 800m and Matt Cannon (14) winning the Boys 800m in 2:05.1, just outside the 1961 club record. JULY 12th 1978 - WIMBLEDON PARK - H.A.C. MEMORIAL TROPHY Matt Cannon (14) 2:05.1 The HAC Trophy this year had a special significance for Belgrave. It was felt in some quarters that we could frighten the other clubs and surprise many by lifting this trophy. It turned out that we were not quite good enough on the night. With six members not bothering to turn out or tell anyone why they did not, too much was placed on the other team members. Despite these setbacks and with two of the new stars of Belgrave, J.Gladwin and D.North, watching from the stand we finished third overall with some great performances. It was our best ever position in this meeting. Chris Powley battled with English Schools runner-up Powell in the 200m and just finished 2nd. Stuart King, as dependable as ever, got two seconds in the shot and discus, and Phil Clay also took second in the 'B' shot. M.Gay made a good debut in the 400m and others to catch the eye were of course Pat Lyttle, John Searle, Kevin Clarke and Gary Wilson. Belgrave stars of the night were: Mark Waller, winning a classic 800m and just failing to catch the winner in the 1,500, and Matt Cannon, who having placed 2nd in the hurdles in a Club Record then proceeded to pulverise the field in the 800 metres with 2:05.1 (the Club Record stands at 2:05.0 set in 1961!). How nice to see Belgrave doing well on the track and field in all events. Those who watched the match noticed two important factors: a new spirit among all our young athletes the like of which we have not had before. items.h: JULY 15th 1978 - GUILDFORD - EBBISHAM LEAGUE MATCH 3. Boys and Colts top their league
items.sum: Report and results of Ebbisham League match 3 at Bannister Park, Guildford, on 15 July 1978, where Belgrave were 2nd to Aldershot but won the league and promotion to Division One.
items.s: JULY 15th 1978 - GUILDFORD - EBBISHAM LEAGUE MATCH 3. Boys and Colts top their league Report and results of Ebbisham League match 3 at Bannister Park, Guildford, on 15 July 1978, where Belgrave were 2nd to Aldershot but won the league and promotion to Division One. JULY 15th 1978 - GUILDFORD - EBBISHAM LEAGUE MATCH 3 Boys and Colts top their league We hired a mini-bus for the last match and with a depleted team of six colts and five boys travelled south to Bannister Park, confident of promotion to division one. With Dennis Blackburn making a timely first appearance in the league this year and two newcomers, Mark Williams and Ben Peel we were going to fight all the way for victory. At the end of the day we conceded first place to Aldershot, having been in the lead a number of times throughout the afternoon. Again everybody performed really well but perhaps a special mention should be made of Simon Simpson who took everybody on in the 800m and tried to do the same in the 1,500m but was knocked over by someone three times his size when he was going really well. Simon picked himself up to finish 4th and later ran a leg in the relay. A mention also for Mark Williams who recorded 14.7 for the 100m - he reaches the age of nine in November! Ben Peel filled in the two sprints but did not look too happy although his times were good. When Ben was asked to do the 1,500m he responded by running 5:40 and looked a natural. Our league win means next year we face the mighty Hercules in Division One. With the boys we now have in the Club we must have a promising future, but they still need looking after on a regular basis and by not doing so, the people in Belgrave who could have helped but didn't have let the lads down. items.s: Nineteen not out Correction and tribute listing John Keown's nineteen consecutive London to Brighton walks and his three 100-mile performances. Nineteen not out * * By the time this article is read it could well be twenty. Firstly an apology to John Keown (already kindly acknowledged and accepted). In the last Belgravian he was credited with seventeen London to Brighton Walks, in fact he has done nineteen in a row. John has still a way to go to reach Hugh Neilson's (Woodford Green) thirty-three, not to mention his twenty-one "hundreds". However, he has walked more "Brightons" than any other Belgravian, being followed by George Beecham, fifteen between 1954-72 and Dave King 1964-77, both of whom have won seven first team medals. To make amends we give a list of his performances. John also has three 100 miles performances to his credit and these are included for good measure. These performances would not have been possible without help on the road by others so a tribute to the selfless efforts of Charlie McLennan, Jack Goswell, Bob Barnes, Gerry Cameron, Bob Picton, Carl Lawton and Pat Duncan, and when not competing against him, John Morris. John will be lining up for this year's "Brighton" and next year's Ewhurst '100' - we wish him luck for these two events and subsequent super efforts. items.s: JULY 15th 1978 - WIMBLEDON. The `20' Report and results of the 27th Open Belgrave '20' at Wimbledon on 15 July 1978, won by Mike Hurd, with Lionel Mann retaining the Belgrave Championship and the Surrey Championship and women's race held in conjunction. JULY 15th 1978 - WIMBLEDON. The `20' 123 of the 163 entries started the 27th Open Belgrave '20' on 15th July and of these 100 finished. Conditions were good and at 5 miles there was a bunch of 8 runners together; Mike Hurd and Don Faircloth (Croydon H), Dave Patterson (TVH), Paul Earles (Windsor S & E), Colin Taylor (Airdale & Spen Valley), Ian Macintosh (Ranelagh), Tom Moore (Liverpool H) and Tom Roden (S.L.H.). These were timed through in 25:41. By ten miles Moore and Roden had dropped from the leading bunch, who were through in 51:42. Between 10 and 15 miles gaps opened up so that now Hurd (1:17:31) led from Earles (1:17:54), Patterson (1:18:01) Don Faircloth (1:18:04). The latter two both passed Earles before the end, however, but Mike Hurd ran out a clear winner by nearly a minute. Team honours went to Croydon from Ranelagh and T.V.H. The overall quality of the race was an improvement with the first 30 inside 2 hours and the first 8 inside 1hr.50mins. The Surrey Championship in conjunction was won by Don Faircloth from Paul Earles and Tom Roden with Epsom & Ewell Harriers easy Team winners. In the historic Women's race held in conjunction Lyn Billington (Feltham AC) did a very good 2hrs.10mins.16secs. with Bridget Cushen (Mitcham) 2:28:30 and Betty Norrish (Brighton & Hove) 2:30:00. All three times impressed those watching the race. BELGRAVE '20' continued....... Of the Bels, Lionel Mann retained the Belgrave Championship from Bill Laws (a silver medal at his first '20' attempt) and John Davies. Thanks as usual must go to all the regular marksmen, recorders, refreshment post stewards, timekeepers and results team who helped make the afternoon a success. items.s: AUGUST 5th 1978 - DARTFORD HALF MARATHON. Report and results of the Dartford Half Marathon on 5 August 1978, a disappointing race for Belgrave, who finished 13th team. AUGUST 5th 1978 - DARTFORD HALF MARATHON. Following last years inaugural race which Belgrave won, this year's Dartford Half Marathon attracted a considerably larger field and on a warm sunny day over 250 runners lined up for the off. Belgrave's team consisted of several men making their debuts at the distance. Of the seasoned campaigners both Lionel Mann and John Jackson were recovering from leg injuries and were content at finishing without undue strain. Of the other Belgravians David Searle pulled through over the later stages to claim the scalp of Peter Hardwick. Overall, however, the result was a poor one for Belgrave and the hoped for signs of a resurgance in distance running were not evident in this race. items.sum: Feature on John Walsh's 1977 British Marathon Ranking List, noting where Belgrave members and some former members are placed.
items.s: MARATHON RANK Feature on John Walsh's 1977 British Marathon Ranking List, noting where Belgrave members and some former members are placed. MARATHON RANK John Walsh of Cardiff A.A.C. is not only an enthusiastic Marathon Runner but he compiles a British Marathon Ranking List. The 1977 List makes interesting reading, 1441 athletes in all are ranked from the sub. 2.15 Internationals to performers who take over twice the time for this arduous event. This number includes veterans over forty and over fifty, and the ladies (31 of them) and covers forty events including those overseas where British athletes have run. Naturally the positions of our Club members are of interest. To get in the first hundred is no small feat and it is good to see Bill Weller ranked 84th. Laurie O'Hara's run in the World Veterans Championship at Gothenburg finds him in 329th place. You naturally expect to come across the name of Lionel Mann and there it is 411th. Doug. Brew and John Davies occupy 548th and 549th placings - separated by two seconds (but over different courses). Paul Pringle is on the right side of the three hours mark in 651st (689 beat three hours). Doug. Maughan is 881st and newcomer Len Collingwood 1092nd. Not such a newcomer, Geoff Pearson, listed as over 50 (he's over 60;) is 1128th Competing for other clubs we find Mike Kortenray 337th and, knowing of his performances at Fell Running, it was no surprise to see the name of John Blair Fish 512th. The compiling of this list is a marathon effort indeed,so many thanks John Walsh and congratulations upon your performance which enabled you to appear opposite position 193. APRIL 29th/30th, MAY 8th - 13th 1978 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY AAA. Seventh javelin title for Crosbie Only one winner came from the Belgrave stable at this year's County Championships. Peter Crosbie did not let the fact that he is in his first season as a senior stop him from continuing his winning ways as he took his seventh consecutive Surrey County Javelin title. It was no marginal victory either, his 64.12 metre cast being over 7 metres further than the best effort of the second man. items.sum: Report that Belgrave's opening Southern League Division I home match at Battersea Park on 6 May 1978 was rained off, and how points would be allocated.
items.s: MAY 6th 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV I. MATCH 1. League keenness dampened Report that Belgrave's opening Southern League Division I home match at Battersea Park on 6 May 1978 was rained off, and how points would be allocated. MAY 6th 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV I. MATCH 1. League keenness dampened With a fifth national league being formed next season all we had to do was finish near the top of this year's league table and we had an excellent chance of promotion. Our opening match was at home and all our top men had pledged their support. But then it rained....and it rained.... and on the Saturday morning the track was awash. The meeting was cancelled and under the league rules that means points for the match are not allocated until the end of the season. If we ended up ahead of the Clubs we would have met on this day we would be allocated the full five league points, if one of them was ahead of us we would get four...and so on down to one point if they were all ahead of us. Not a good start when one considers that this was our home match. Southern League Battersea Park

items.s: MAY 20th 1978 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.I MATCH 2. 25 points from Brooks Report and results of Southern League Division I match 2 at Crystal Palace on 20 May 1978, where Cliff Brooks won three events and Belgrave were narrowly 3rd. MAY 20th 1978 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.I MATCH 2. 25 points from Brooks Cliff Brooks was our outstanding competitor with three wins included in his usual attempt at a "one day decathlon". Perhaps his most outstanding effort was a 16 second hurdles victory - very snappy for this time of the season and exactly equal to the time set by Paul Whitby our 'A' string man. Jim Evans was also in good form with 10.9 and 22 second sprints, and Martin Scott celebrated his return to our league team by winning the long jump. Ian Duncan undertook a daunting double by turning out in the 5000 metres and steeplechase yet still clocked a couple of good times. Our younger members made their presence felt on both field and the track with Matt King picking up 6 points in the heavy events, Mark Shippen beating all other competitors in the pole vault by nearly half a metre, and an inspired Dave Bailey cut his best 400 metres down to 52.8 and then ran 51.6 in the relay. It was a close match but with just one or two weak events on the afternoon we were narrowly pushed into 3rd team place. 100m: 1.J.Evans 10.9; 2.M.Scott 11.4. 200m: 2.J.Evans 22.0; 4.S.Crosbie 25.2. 400m: 3.C.Gillett 52.0; 3.D.Bailey 52.8. 800m: 5.J.Stevenson 1:58.6; 2.S.Williams 2:02.4. 1500m: 3.J.Bicourt 3:58.4; 2.J Stow 4:05.6. 5000m: 4.L.O'Hara 15:05.8; 2.I.Duncan 15:14.2. 4x100m: 2.Belgrave 43.8. 4x400m: 3.Belgrave 3:31.1 (J.Stevenson 53.5, S.Williams 54.2, P.Whitby 51.8, D.Bailey 51.6). 110mH: 2.P.Whitby 16.0. 1.C.Brooks 16.0. 400mH: 3.P.Whitby 57.8; 2.M.Smith 60.9; 3000mSC: 4.I Duncan 9:54.0; 5.L.Coy 10:57.8. items.sum: Short historical note on the ancient Olympic Games, the stade race and the sacred truce.
items.s: Early Olympics Short historical note on the ancient Olympic Games, the stade race and the sacred truce. Early Olympics The first Olympic Games are believed to have been held as early as 1370BC. In 776BC Coroebus won the Stade race (192.27 metres) from which comes the word stadium. The Games were a bloodthirsty affair in those days although in 884BC King Ephitis of Elis spoiled the spectacle by introducing a sacred truce, banning legal disputes and the execution of death penalties during the Games. The terms of the truce were engraved on a discus and set out in five concentric rings which in modern times were used to symbolise the five continents of the world. Coroebus Coroebus won the Stade race in 776BC King Ephitis of Elis King Ephitis of Elis introduced the sacred truce in 884BC Olympic Games Elis

items.h: JULY 1st 1978 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. MATCH 4. ... and then disqualified...
items.sum: Report of Southern League Division I match 4 at Norbiton on 1 July 1978, where Belgrave were disqualified for fielding New Zealander Dennis Brown before his clearance was due.
items.s: JULY 1st 1978 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. MATCH 4. ... and then disqualified... Report of Southern League Division I match 4 at Norbiton on 1 July 1978, where Belgrave were disqualified for fielding New Zealander Dennis Brown before his clearance was due. JULY 1st 1978 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. MATCH 4. ... and then disqualified... Even worse than coming last, this time the Bels received no league points at all and after four matches our score was four points out of a possible twenty. There were some bright spots, particularly Simon Holmes' fine run in the 800m, but after the race an official from another club realised that we had run New Zealander Dennis Brown whose clearance to run in the league was apparently not due until a few days later. A complaint to the track referee soon followed and a simple oversight turned into a major disaster as we were disqualified One couldn't help feeling sorry for Dennis, in the centre of a difficult situation after a good run, but he will obviously be a tremendous asset to our side. Once again the full results have not been received but Bedford won with 143, followed by Epsom & Ewell 137, Hercules Wimbledon 93, Belgrave H 78 (but disqualified) and Surrey AC 75. Mark Shippen was 2nd in the pole vault with 3.80 metres and Martin Scott leapt 6.95 metres for 3rd in the long jump. Simon Holmes Simon Holmes fine run in the 800m Dennis Brown Dennis Brown New Zealander whose league clearance was not yet due, causing Belgrave's disqualification Dennis Brown Dennis Mark Shippen Mark Shippen 2nd pole vault, 3.80m Martin Scott Martin Scott 3rd long jump, 6.95m Southern League Norbiton Bedford Epsom & Ewell Hercules Wimbledon Surrey AC

items.sum: Report and Belgrave results of Southern League Division I match 5 at Bracknell on 22 July 1978, where Belgrave finished last (5th, 91 points) again, with John Bicourt disqualified in the 5,000m, all but ensuring relegation to division two for 1979.
items.s: JULY 22nd 1978 - BRACKNELL - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. I MATCH 5. ... then last again Report and Belgrave results of Southern League Division I match 5 at Bracknell on 22 July 1978, where Belgrave finished last (5th, 91 points) again, with John Bicourt disqualified in the 5,000m, all but ensuring relegation to division two for 1979. JULY 22nd 1978 - BRACKNELL - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. I MATCH 5. ... then last again A good result in the penultimate match and we would stave off relegation. Our team travelled to Berkshire in hope and with seven juniors and youths in the side at least our prospects for the future look bright.... But after an afternoon of fighting for third position we suddenly found ourselves trailing again as the final events took place Kunle Ashaye and Derrick Williams, both juniors, were terrific in the sprints and under the captaincy of Charlie Gillett and with Reg Hopkins, they managed to underline our track motto "Belgrave always win the relay". Dave Bailey put up another good performance in the one lap sprint and John Gladwin, a youth, came very close to the Club Record in the 800 metres. John also started our 4x400 metre squad who came close to victory, all recording very useful times. We did reasonably well on the field with 'A' string wins coming from Pole Vaulter Mark Shippen and javelin thrower Peter Crosbie but our middle distance and hurdling team members found the opposition tough. John Bicourt, running although suffering from a virus, stopped running in the 5,000 metres after having difficulty breathing and then on remembering how much we needed the points, he got going again to struggle for another six laps to the finish - only to be disqualified for stepping off the track! Such is our luck in 1978 and the net result of an afternoon's endeavour was one solitary league point almost certainly ensuring that we join division two in 1979. items.h: AUGUST 19th 1978 - NEW RIVER - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. I MATCH 6. We just hang on
items.sum: Report and Belgrave results of Southern League Division I match 6 at New River on 19 August 1978, where Belgrave finished 2nd and narrowly escaped relegation because four Southern League clubs qualified for the National League.
items.s: AUGUST 19th 1978 - NEW RIVER - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. I MATCH 6. We just hang on Report and Belgrave results of Southern League Division I match 6 at New River on 19 August 1978, where Belgrave finished 2nd and narrowly escaped relegation because four Southern League clubs qualified for the National League. AUGUST 19th 1978 - NEW RIVER - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV. I MATCH 6. We just hang on At last our team showed what they are capable of. Against very good opposition from Croydon and North London, solid performances all round left the Bels in 2nd position, almost doubling our points for the season. Once again our sprinters scored heavily with Jim Evans, Kunle Ashaye and Derrick Williams looking really good, when it came to the relay they scorched to a magnificent 42.6 for second fastest time ever in Belgrave history - and that without Ernest Obeng. Derrick also got the better of Martin Scott in the long jump but nevertheless Martin has had a reasonable season and looks far more comfortable concentrating on jumping these days. A marvellous run came from Mark Lindsey-Bayley in the high hurdles. Still a junior, he ran 15.8 to win the 'A' race just two tenths shy of Paul Whitby's Senior Club Record. Simon Holmes ran well under 2 minutes for the 800 metres yet again - what a good summer he has had - and Cliff Brooks notched up another big individual score of 23 points. As it turned out this final fling prior to expected relegation just did the trick. When the qualifying matches for the National League came around no fewer than four Southern League Clubs made the grade: Epsom & Ewell H, Windsor, Slough & Eton AC, Bedford & Cnty and Chelmsford. So with these clubs going out of the top of our league the number due to be relegated was fewer than expected and we kept up by the skin of our teeth. Surely we have now reached our nadir. Many of our team members now come from the 16 to 19 age group and they can only improve under the leadership of the experienced Charlie Gillett and Cliff Brooks. 100m: 1.J.Evans 10.9; 2.K.Ashaye 11.2; 200m: 2.J.Evans 22.2; 2.D. items.sum: Short note on the ancient Olympic Games and their five-day programme.
items.s: Early Olympics Short note on the ancient Olympic Games and their five-day programme. Early Olympics The ancient Games, before 393AD, grew from one race to a five day programme. Cheating was a serious crime and very respected judges were carefully appointed; an initiation rite marked the seriousness of their noble task. Athletes were sometimes beaten for false starts! The five days were as follows: 1st day - the opening ceremony. 2nd day - the pentathlon (discus, javelin, running, wrestling and jumping. 3rd day - running over a distance approaching 5,000 metres. 4th day - wrestling, boxing and pankration (involving gouging, strangling and limb breaking. 5th day - those still able mounted the pedestal. items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Editorial arguing that the club lacks team spirit outside the walkers, pointing to Linda Nicholls' Swedish trip and Arnold Bentt's jumpers as examples, and urging training trips and a continental holiday for the young athletes.
items.s: Editorial arguing that the club lacks team spirit outside the walkers, pointing to Linda Nicholls' Swedish trip and Arnold Bentt's jumpers as examples, and urging training trips and a continental holiday for the young athletes. "The team that trains together stays together": a statement that contains more than a little truth. Our walkers are small in numbers but they have a closely knit fraternity that goes hand in hand with success. Our runners, meanwhile, have not been successful since the 60's and although laudable attempts have been made to foster the pack training system, with due respect, it is not the 'A' team runners who have responded. Track and field tends to be even more individualistic and true to form, our track men rarely even see each other apart from match days; the social event of the year is a quick drink together after our single home league fixture. Not surprising then that when the result sheets are handed out Belgrave Harriers features a little lower down the list than we would like. We do have a problem in that our membership is drawn from a large catchment area and this is further aggravated by our head-quarters being ten miles from our track base but more could be done to engender a sense of togetherness or team spirit, call it what you will. Linda Nicholls writes in this issue of her stay with a Swedish club which regularly goes out into the countryside to camp and train together. Arnold Bentt, in "Spotlight", harks back to the days when we had a group of successful jumpers all working at their events together. The lesson seems obvious. At present we have a fine bunch of young athletes who should go far if we can only keep them together. So let's liven things up a bit, plan a few training trips, and what about an athletic holiday on the Continent next year. Or are we all too old and staid and unable to climb out of the rut? Linda Nicholls Linda Nicholls stayed with a Swedish club Arnold Bentt Arnold Bentt subject of Spotlight; one of a group of successful Belgrave jumpers Sweden

items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Grapevine column of club news and gossip.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine column of club news and gossip. We are sorry to report that Gordon Doubleday, a key member of the "Belgravian" team, has had a spell in Kingston Hospital thanks to a recurrence of the heart infection that laid him low in 1969. Apparently the trouble was caused by some decayed fragments of teeth left behind after extractions. Now on the mend and at home again, he will have to take it easy for a while but we look forward to seeing his familiar figure, stopwatch in hand, on the finish lines this summer. One thing that cheered him enormously during his incarceration was the sight on TV of Ernest Obeng bearing a Belgrave Club Honours Badge to the 60 metre finish line at Cosford ahead of Allan Wells. Our already busy General Hon. Secretary Derek Crookes was elected Secretary of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association at their AGM in October. He is obviously doing so well on the Surrey County Committee that his fame is spreading. An interested spectator at the Autumnal '5¾' was Charlie Smart and it was good to see him chatting away with old friends. Happily he still has some mobility and the fighting spirit which used to strike terror into our old rivals on the Brighton Relay is still evident by the way he tackled the stairs for welcome refreshment at Belgrave Hall. He was the darling of the crowds at the White City - they seemed to think that the balding Belgravian who was carving his way through the field was old enough to be the father of the others! Let's hope we see more of you, Charlie. In the 1978 Belgrave Draw, organised by Ron Langheim, there was a healthy profit of £275.18 for the Club coffers - £100 up on last year. Thanks and well done Ron! We hear that Bernard Eglington pulled off the biggest fiddle of his athletic career in October. He has been walking second-claim with Lancs. W.C. for about seven years and had twice won their "Alison Trophy" for a 10 kilometre handicap. When he turned up to compete on October 14th he was astounded to find only officials and himself there. Someone had blundered and no other walkers had turned up. Although he was all for postponing the race the officials insisted that he should set out on his own - which he did - to win the cup for the third time. One way of getting your name into the Club's minutes is to change your address and one change recently notified was Dick Towndrow who has moved from one address in Mere, Wiltshire, to another in that delightful village. Dick was a member of the old Ashcombe AC, and when they disbanded (they used to run in Richmond Park from Sheen) he came to us via the Poly. During Army service in the war he was stationed at Gillingham, Dorset, and married a local girl. Why mention this? - Some years later a lad from Gillingham came to London to seek fame and fortune and, amongst other things, joined Belgrave - his name - Carl Lawton. Dick was a fine cross-country and road runner and on one occasion won the now discontinued Wigmore '15'. Some years ago he left London to take up a teaching job in Wiltshire. The Southern Counties Cross Country Association have taken advantage of the tendencies of that compulsive committee member Derek Crookes, our General Hon. Secretary now being elected to that august body's committee. Good news for speedy tipplers! Haigs, distillers of fine whisky and sponsors of our Belgrave Road Relay (April 7th), have upped the size of the team prizes. In the past the first team has received a 1 gallon bottle of the 'hard stuff', second team half a gallon and third team one quarter of a gallon. This has done nothing to slow down clubs like Aldershot & Farnham and Thames Valley H, so let's see what the new measures can do - first team to receive one whole bottle each, second team half a bottle each and third team quarter of a bottle each. Congratulations to Doug. Fotheringham on being elected President of the Southern Area of the Race Walking Association. He has been walking for a quarter of a century and was a regular in our "Garnet" Cup teams until he scored in our winning team in 1977 to gain "senior" status. One of his greatest performances was in the 100 miles race promoted by the M.P.A.A. at Chigwell in 1965 when he covered the distance in the fine time of 21hrs. 31mins. 9secs. to become Centurion No. 373. More recently he has been Race Hon. Sec. for the popular M.P.A.A. Open 11 kilos. (formerly 7 miles) held from Imber Court. John Thresher has joined the ranks of the marathoners. Now 39 years old he lined up in a field of 205 at Regina, Saskatchewan, and finished 5th in 2hrs. 39mins. 25secs. Great stuff John! As a vet in 1980 he says he will be looking for Gorman and trying to avoid O'Hara. John has now moved to Winnipeg and we wish him, Mavis and their children the best of luck in their new home. If anyone wishes to write to John his new address is [address withheld]. Incidentally, John is still our Club Record holder for 1,500 metres and 1 mile with 3:44.6 and 4:02.1, dating from 1968 and 1964 respectively. We note that John Blair-Fish, now representing Edinburgh, was 37th in the Barnsley Marathon in 2hrs. 40mins. 22secs. There were 282 finishers. Poor old Charlie Speechley! At 91 years of age he was competing in the Highgate One Hour Walks, we hear, when someone had the nerve to disqualify him. He was most disappointed and is now said to be thinking of changing his style. Belated congratulations to two Belgravians who have taken the marital plunge. Howard Satchell (can he really be 20 years a member) has married Chris from Canada, and Arnold Bentt has married Pat. Best wishes to them all. In November Derek Crookes did not get voted onto the committee of any athletic organisation. When asked by our correspondent what she thought about Derek's "failure", Mrs. Mary Crookes replied, "Who is Derek Crookes?" It was good to see Len Marchant at the A.G.M. A Club stalwart of the 30's and 40's and a great middle-distance runner who has represented the A.A.A. (regarded by many as the stepping stone to an International Vest). He would probably have been at his best during World War II, when he served in the R.A.F. and picked us up many members. He was a good cross-country and road relay runner and on one occasion was second in the South of the Thames Junior - the winner being Bill Lucas. GRAPEVINE continued ..... An absentee from the A.G.M. was Frank Webb who has recently undergone an operation. However, you can't keep chaps like Frank away for long and it was good to see him at the '5¾' run. The Chief Judge at the Chippenham to Calne Walk was George Bentley now living at Portishead, Avon. He looked fit and well and told us that his brother Fred, one of our great long-distance walkers of the 30's and an international in 1938, was also fit and well. Also at the race was Percy Wright who is busy planning the English Schools Road Walking Championships due to be held in Southampton. We hope that many of our younger walkers will be there competing for their counties. A steering committee was formed in January by the London Borough of Merton to discuss the setting up of a Merton Sports Council. It is not yet resolved whether "steering committees" are allowed to count towards a record attempt but if so, Derek Crookes now needs only one more committee for a World Record and his own niche in the Guiness Book of Records! Fame at last. Peter Hardwick and Alan Painter were featured on the front page of "Athletics Weekly" for March 10th. Well, perhaps featured is overdoing it a bit, just their rear views being shown along with many other rear views tackling a hill in the 1978 National. One sees some funny snippets of information around. According to the financial columns "for the six months to July 31st the turnover of Belgrave (Blackheath) turned in at £1.39 million ..... Taxable profit for the last full year was £198,630." Does John Baker know something we don't? Or what about this one from the "AW": "Tiretta - removes unwanted hair from legs and body-assisting massage. An incredible discovery that acts quickly. No pain or smell, no hours of effort. Send now for this incredible hair remover ... to BELGRAVE DIRECT SUPPLIES LTD, Leicester!" OCTOBER 21st 1978 - WIMBLEDON - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE RACE 1. With Mark Sinclair, John Searle, John Gladwin and Mark Waller closing the scoring five in seventeen it was a great start to the Surrey League. items.s: The Disappearing Trick Report and results from the second Herne Hill Harriers cross-country league race at Brockwell Park on 18 November 1978, with few Belgrave Colts and Boys but the Youths going top of their league. NOVEMBER 18th 1978 - BROCKWELL PARK - H.H.H. C.C. LEAGUE RACE 2. The Disappearing Trick Race two of this league should have seen us move up the combined age group table. Instead, we only had two colts and two Boys in action apart from a good turn-out of Youths. Simon Simpson and Ray McCann were very disappointed with the other Colts who didn't turn up and it showed in the way they ran. If only we had a dozen more like these two - their enthusiasm and willingness to compete on every occasion puts the rest of the Club to shame. Our saving grace was the Youths team. A great run by John Searle gave him the beating of David North for the first time. We finished 3rd again but went top of the Youths league by one point. JANUARY 6th 1979 - LLOYD PARK - SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS. Two Bels. Win County Vests Magnificent running again by our runners in all age groups. FEBRUARY 24th 1979 - BROCKWELL PARK - H.H.H. C.C. LEAGUE RACE 4. Our chances of picking up a win in Herne Hill Harriers' cross country league were dashed when with only three runners in the Youths section of the final event we could only place fourth and thus were pushed down to second overall. Nevertheless it was a fine run by David North who placed 2nd in 22:59, with John Searle 9th and Mark Gay 22nd. Elliott AC's final score was 35 points to our own 37. items.sum: Article reprinted from "Sport In The USSR" on laser and optical measuring devices in field events and the rule that world records must still be measured with a tape measure.
items.s: TAPE MEASURES RULE! Article reprinted from "Sport In The USSR" on laser and optical measuring devices in field events and the rule that world records must still be measured with a tape measure. TAPE MEASURES RULE! (from "Sport In The USSR) In recent years science has provided sportsmen and trainers with a huge variety of technical gadgetry to help them hone their skills by flawlessly registering times. Competing with the noble tape measure are the latest technical devices, which make it possible to register information with degrees of precision which at the present are not even all that necessary. The tape measure is not always laid and stretched evenly, and is affected by temperature. Of course, its influence is not great enough to really affect the measuring of javelin or discus throws, but it does exist. Optical devices measure this distance with mathematical precision. This type of equipment was first used at the Olympic Games in Munich. The unusual-looking device was reminiscent of a movie camera sitting on a tripod. The official went over to the javelin, which had left a mark in the grass, stuck a reflector into the ground, and the scoreboard would light up, indicating the result. The work here is being done by a laser. An electronic optical tachometer makes it possible to measure simultaneously horizontal distance, curves and a host of other parameters. Of course no one forbids the use of optic laser devices at sports competitions. Curiously enough, however, they can be utilised only until a world record is set. In this case something rather comical takes place: the judges run for the tape measure and "check" the result measured by a laser device. As of now, the rules prohibit the registering of world records with anything other than a tape measure Olympic Games Munich

items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Cecil Gittins's obituary of Harry Hathway, the country's leading athletics timekeeper for some twenty years, who died after helping at a meeting.
items.s: HARRY HATHWAY Cecil Gittins's obituary of Harry Hathway, the country's leading athletics timekeeper for some twenty years, who died after helping at a meeting. HARRY HATHWAY A few weeks ago, as I understand it, Harry was (as so very often) helping out at an athletic event, and he felt not too good. Well, the weather had not been kind and Harry was in his seventies. When he was at home that evening he collapsed and when medical help arrived he was dead. Harry had been the country's top timekeeper for a long, long time - twenty years to my recollection. It was he who developed, organised and arranged proper testing for timekeepers - and those who have read his articles will appreciate the immaculate detail and assembly of factual data which backed up his plans. As an unsure novice timekeeper myself, he was one of those who gave me instruction and encouragement and for that I am grateful. Harry was always firmly and quietly confident in himself but never bombastic; indeed he was always willing to listen to what someone else had to say. Harry was always around with his multitude of watches at the top internationals but he never neglected the "small" meetings which are the basis of our sport. He was to be seen at Belgrave events often. He was a retired mathematics teacher and a bachelor, as well as a Roman Catholic of deep conviction. The timekeepers' stand will not be quite the same without Harry. Cecil Gittins Harry Hathway HARRY HATHWAY the country's top timekeeper for about twenty years; developed testing for timekeepers; retired mathematics teacher; died after collapsing at home HARRY HATHWAY Harry Cecil Gittins Cecil Gittins timekeeper

items.s: SEPTEMBER 23rd 1978 - WIMBLEDON - THE AUTUMNAL 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE. Report and full results of the club's Autumnal 5¾ mile road race at Wimbledon on 23 September 1978, won by new member Dennis Brown, with Steve Sharp winning the handicap; under the 'Road and Country' section banner. ROAD AND COUNTRY SEPTEMBER 23rd 1978 - WIMBLEDON - THE AUTUMNAL 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE. Once again the Belgrave Road and Country Organisation Machine came to life for the start of the winter season, producing a warm, sunny day for the race officials and some fairly slow times for the "athletes". As expected our new signing Dennis Brown soon took the lead followed by O'Hara, Jackson, Callow and Gorman. The rest of the 44 starters were soon strung out behind the leading runners. The chasing group of Coy, Mann, Williamson and Reilly were together around the Common and off down Copse - but not making any impression on the leaders. Dennis Brown was always making the pace - only having to wait for course directions from behind. Even so he managed to make a wrong turn and took Laurie O'Hara with him. Meanwhile, back in the field Mike Reilly was paying for a fast start and was dropped by the rest of the chasing bunch. The leaders got back on course and Dennis lengthened his lead around the final circuit of the top to come in 100 yards up on the fast finishing Laurie. It was good to see John Jackson in 3rd place coming back to form and Allan Callow in 4th embarassing quite a few 'A' team runners. These two earned 3rd and 2nd handicap places behind Steve Sharp who had the remarkable time of 26:01. 1. D.Brown 30:07; 2. L.O'Hara 30:19; 3. J.Jackson 31:07; 4. A.Callow 31:20; 5. B.Gorman 31:25; 6. items.s: SEPTEMBER 30th 1978 - WALTON - WALTON ROAD RELAY. Report and results of Belgrave's three teams in the Walton Road Relay on 30 September 1978, where the 'A' team finished 10th with Dennis Brown fastest in 15:43. SEPTEMBER 30th 1978 - WALTON - WALTON ROAD RELAY. This race was quite a contrast to the previous weeks run at Wimbledon. Not only was the weather bad but we had no 'A' team until five minutes after the start of the race. Some hurried rearrangements were made during which our 'C' team was disrupted and three people did not get a run. With the weather worsening, Belgrave seemed to be improving - after Supergorm on the first leg anything must be an improvement! Lionel Mann and Simon Holmes each made up one place putting us in 15th with our stronger runners to come. The 'B' team was having a variable race, dropping to 32nd and then pulling up to 26th with last week's "find" Allan Callow clocking the fastest 'B' team leg for Belgrave of 17:19. The 'A' team big guns of O'Hara, Rimmer and Brown came home strongly but were unable to make up more than four places due to being well behind the leading group. Once again Dennis Brown showed his form with our fastest time of the day - 15:43. OCTOBER 7th 1978 - WIMBLEDON. The Yacht Handicap As always a scorching hot day was arranged for this popular event over "the usual course" - out to the Windmill and back over the Common. With 46 starters including some notable track stars not usually associated with tarmac and mud it was bound to be another enjoyable race. The Hon. Handicapper again did a good job managing to get 34 finishers inside 2 minutes of the winner! Although so many were close, the first two were well clear of the rest of the field. Mark Gay, the pre-race favourite (if there ever is such a thing without Brian Gorman around) took the lead through Wimbledon Village and no-one looked likely to catch him as he finished six seconds clear of Reg. Bale. With Gerry Sexton in 3rd and Mark Sinclair 6th the youngsters had a good day auguring well for the rest of the season. Pat O'Connor, making a welcome and well-timed recovery from injury, recorded second fastest time of the day behind Leo Coy and in front of the in-form John Jackson ("I don't really like these sprint races") and our new Captain Tony Binda ("It's too cold to run here"). 1.M.Gay 18:06; 2.R.Bale 19:01; 3.G.Sexton 18:56; 4.J.Myddleton 18:40 5.C.Henn 18:16; 6.M.Sinclair 17:24; 7.K.Sinclair 18:46; 8.G.Collins 18:50; 9.C.Gillett 17:54; 10.D.Jones 19:37; 11.J.Angus 17:47; 12. items.sum: Account of the gathering at Belgrave Hall on 3 November 1978 where Tom Carter presented Joe McDonald with a plaque for forty years' membership.
items.s: A NIGHT OUT FOR JOE Account of the gathering at Belgrave Hall on 3 November 1978 where Tom Carter presented Joe McDonald with a plaque for forty years' membership. A NIGHT OUT FOR JOE Our well known and popular member, Joe McDonald, recently completed forty years membership of the Club, and there was a fine article about him in a recent "Belgravian". To celebrate the occasion a number of his Club friends gathered in Belgrave Hall on Friday, November 3rd for a "get together". A few old Club photographs in which Joe appeared where on display. Highlight of the evening was the presentation of a plaque, suitably inscribed and complete with the Club Badge. The inscription read: Presented to Joe McDonald by Belgrave Harriers In recognition of 40 Years Valued Service 2nd Nov. 1978 The presentation was made by Past President and former cross-country international Tom Carter who, in a witty speech, fittingly short enough for the occasion, paid tribute to Joe's fighting spirit as a member of Club teams for many years and for the unsung but greatly appreciated work he does regularly behind the scenes to help keep Belgrave Hall in good shape. Joe gratefully accepted the plaque with his usual modesty and to the applause of the gathering of members. Our President was unable to be present but he sent a cordial message which was read out. Everybody will join Ray in wishing him many more years of running and good fellowship with the Club which means so much to Joe. items.s: Low turn-out for 'South of Thames' Report and results of the South of Thames Junior cross-country championship at West Wickham on 11 November 1978, where only 13 of 36 Belgrave entries ran and Dennis Brown was 11th. NOVEMBER 11th 1978 - WEST WICKHAM - SOUTH OF THAMES "JUNIOR". Low turn-out for 'South of Thames' Lack of enthusiasm seemed to hit Belgrave early this season with only 13 of the 36 entries turning out on the day. If this continues we shall soon deservedly lose the support and organising efforts of our secretary. We must give him our support by turning out and performing well. Those who did compete ran encouragingly, particularly Dennis Brown who finished 11th of the 350 strong field - a great effort. Unfortunately he had no immediate back-up over the short, hilly five mile course until Simon Holmes in 87th place and Tony Binda in 93rd. There was another long gap until Tom Dowdall closed in the 'A' team in 189th. With the team 20th from 54 we were not too disappointed but could do so much better. 1.R.Hackney (Aldershot F&D) 23:42; 11.D.Brown 24:25; 87.S.Holmes 26:00; 93.A.Binda 26:03; 189.T.Dowdall 27:25; 207.D.Maughan 27:45; 218.P.Hardwick 27:52; 244.K.Duckett 28:46; 257.A.Grant 29:00; 266. items.s: An unexpected win Report and results of the cross-country match against Thames Valley Harriers and Walton AC at Wimbledon on 18 November 1978, which Belgrave won comfortably, led by Laurie O'Hara in 4th. NOVEMBER 18th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - C.C.MATCH v TVH v WALTON AC. An unexpected win Although on our home course, we were not expecting much against some good opposition but we had a good result - scoring 14-a-side - beating both our rivals quite comfortably over the still fast Wimbledon course. Laurie O'Hara led the team home in 4th just three places ahead of Dennis Brown. Simon Williamson was our 3rd scorer in 9th place, after some secret training in Birmingham and South Africa over the summer. Then came the rest of our 'A' team scrubbers led (inevitably!) by the arch-scrubber himself in yet another time of 31 mins. items.s: League position worsens Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League race 2 at Fleet on 25 November 1978, where Belgrave finished only 6th and stayed bottom of division one, led by Laurie O'Hara in 26th. NOVEMBER 25th 1978 - FLEET - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE RACE 2. League position worsens With a deficit of 79 points on South London H from the first race we needed a good result to keep in with a chance of remaining in division one next season. With 18 Belgravians in the field we felt we had a better chance than at Wimbledon. However, we still lacked one or two "stars" to finish in the first ten, so although we were 3rd team to close in we finished only 6th overall - and our nearest rivals SLH were 4th. Once more Laurie O'Hara led the team home in 26th position. He really does go well on any surface from tartan to muddy and stony country. Many people complain of the conditions while Laurie just gets on and runs the race. After Laurie there was a gap of about half a minute before Simon Holmes came in leading the rest of the scoring team who packed well in the 50s to 70s. Our team Captain was 52nd followed by Gerry North (making a very welcome appearance), Jim Rimmer and Leo Coy. With victory over Herne Hill by only 9 points we remained at the bottom of the league nearly 200 points adrift - requiring a really special effort from everyone to enable us to stay in the premier division for our Boys/Youths team who are doing so well in their races. 26. items.sum: Note, from the Road Runners Club newsletter, on Milton Keynes' plans for a traffic-free marathon course and stadium and its intended bid for the 1986 Commonwealth Games.
items.s: Milton Keynes to host 'Friendly Games'? Note, from the Road Runners Club newsletter, on Milton Keynes' plans for a traffic-free marathon course and stadium and its intended bid for the 1986 Commonwealth Games. Milton Keynes to host 'Friendly Games'? It was interesting to learn through the Road Runners Club newsletter for January 1979 that the town of Milton Keynes, fast becoming the home of road running and walking in this country, hopes to construct a permanent marathon course which will be completely traffic free and available for use by walkers, runners and joggers, for racing and training. The course will probably consist of a three lap circuit with the start and finish in the 30,000 spectator stadium also planned by the Milton Keynes Development Council. Such items as permanent distance markers, water hydrants and telephones at intermediate points have been discussed, as well as facilities for spectating. With an indoor sports complex already existing and a plan for an Olympic sized swimming pool on the drawing board, Milton Keynes intends to make a bid for the 1986 Commonwealth Games - last held in England in 1934. Good luck to them. Commonwealth Games Milton Keynes England Road Runners Club

items.s: The Master Mastered Report and results of the club 7-mile cross-country championship and handicap on Wimbledon Common on 2 December 1978, won by Ian Duncan from Laurie O'Hara, with Dave Searle winning the handicap. DECEMBER 2nd 1978 - WIMBLEDON - THE 7 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. The Master Mastered Thirtyseven foolhardy runners braved the December weather and three laps of the Common for this year's Club '7'. After a fast start the front of the field soon split up, led by last year's rivals Ian Duncan and Laurie O'Hara - meeting for the first time this season. Jim Rimmer was the only one to go with the two leaders but he was dropped after one lap and remained isolated in 3rd place. The second group of Gerry North, Lionel Mann, Colin Pearson and Simon Holmes were always falling back and the experience and fitness of Pat O'Connor and Tony Binda brought them through well at the end. Meanwhile, up at the front, battle was under weigh between the two 'big' names. It seems Ian has been doing some hard training away from the Club this year as he pushed the pace along at the front. The two were still together after one lap but by the halfway mark Ian had forced a gap of about ten metres which he extended over the third lap to finish 35 seconds ahead of Laurie. So we have a new name on the cup at last! The handicap was won by a much improved Dave Searle with Alan Painter, recovered from his marathon, in 2nd. Mr. Handicapper was fooled by Ian Duncan's absence and the race winner collected his second prize of the day in 3rd place. 1.I.Duncan 45:17; 2.L.O'Hara 45:52; 3.J.Rimmer 46:42; 4.S.Holmes 47:04; 5.A.Binda 47:23; 6.P.O'Connor 47:34; 7.R.Dickson 48:08; 8. items.s: 370 Points Adrift Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League race 3 at Epsom on 9 December 1978, where an under-strength Belgrave finished last of seven, some 370 points behind Herne Hill overall with one race left. DECEMBER 9th 1978 - EPSOM - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE RACE 3. 370 Points Adrift Belgrave's league fortunes were mirrored by the weather at this third race of the season on a bleak, windy day at Epsom. We needed a miracle to keep alive any hope of staying in division one but it was not to be. Once again we were unable to field our strongest team and never looked like being able to score well enough to improve our position. After a fast downhill start Jim Rimmer led the Belgrave team followed by Alan Black, Leo Coy, Simon Holmes and Tom Dowdall - having a real 'blinder'. Pat O'Connor, getting fitter every week, was moving through well and at the end of the lap took over from Jim as first scorer. We were packing well but about 30 places too low. On the second lap Tom Dowdall began to 'die' but the thought of beating Gorman kept him going. John Jackson was gradually working through and Simon Holmes moved up into 3rd scoring position ahead of Alan Black. At the end we were last team and overall tailed Herne Hill H by some 370 points with one race left. 1.M.Connelly (Walton) 25:40; 46.J.Rimmer 28:01; 47.P.O'Connor 28:02; 55.S.Holmes 28:24; 61.A.Black 28:38; 66.L.Coy 29:01; 69.J.Jackson 29:10; 72.T.Dowdall 29:18; 75.B.Gorman 29:32; 83.D.Searle 30:03; 84.L.Mann 30:03; 98.A.Painter 31:22; 101.D.Maughan 31:28; 105.R. JANUARY 6th 1979 - LLOYD PARK.- SURREY COUNTY 7½ MILES C.C. CHAMP. County Championships Lloyd Park on a good day is a difficult course - so three laps on a day with a biting wind and several inches of snow was no-ones idea of fun. However, our team was strengthened by the presence of John Abberton, John Bicourt and Simon Williamson and a better result than that in previous league races was hoped for. Our scoring six were soon apparent and although Bicourt and Rimmer were struggling in the snow, Abberton, O'Connor, Williamson and Holmes were running to form and we were packing inside 50. Abberton and Bicourt were always our first two, with the former getting home just 2 seconds ahead to score in 24th place. The other four seemed to be having a private race. Williamson led them through the first lap but once more O'Connor's experience showed as he came through on the second to be our third scorer in 37th. Holmes and Rimmer closed up on Williamson on the second lap but he kept going well and drew away on the last circuit. Further down the field Tom Dowdall proved his earlier victory over Brian Gorman was no fluke - but only by 2 seconds. Leo Coy seems to be having a rough patch at the moment but no doubt is holding back for the big races later in the season. Brian Marmion was our only Junior in action, completing the 5 mile course in 42nd place with 31:31. 1.R.Treadwell (S.Beagles) 36:13; 2.D.Clarke (Herc.Wimb) 37:00; 3. items.s: Duncan's Double Report and results of the club 10 miles cross-country championship on Wimbledon Common on 13 January 1979, Ian Duncan's second club title win of the season ahead of Laurie O'Hara and Jim Rimmer, who won the handicap; with photos of the medallists. JANUARY 13th 1979 - WIMBLEDON - THE 10 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. Duncan's Double Thirty Belgravians set off over the Common for this year's '10' but only two-thirds lasted the full four laps. The horse-rides, notoriously muddy after rain, were rock hard and caused several people to retire 'hurt'. The rivalry begun in the '7½' before Christmas continued over four laps as Duncan, O'Hara and Rimmer were joined by Williamson and soon broke away from the rest of the field. Ian Duncan looked as though he might pull away early on but suffered a bad fall and did not make his move until the third lap. By this time he and O'Hara had opened up a clear lead over Rimmer and Williamson who had started too fast and struggled to hang on for the second half of the race. Duncan now put on the pressure and got away from Laurie O'Hara to record his second win of the season. By now the rest of the field was well spread out - 4th placed Williamson finished over two minutes up on Lionel Mann in 5th and making a return to form over the longer distance. Leo Coy's training started to pay off as he finished 6th ahead of newcomer (!) Steve Williams having his first race for two months. The handicapper was seen surveying the scene with pleasure (glad he wasn't running perhaps!) and even pacing Peter Hardwick over the last lap while retrieving the flags!! 1.I.Duncan 62:21; 2.L.O'Hara 62:36; 3.J.Rimmer 63:10; 4.S.Williamson 65:41; 5.L.Mann 67:57; 6.L.Coy 69:03; 7.S.Williams 69:17; 8.A.Painter 69:48; 9.D.Searle 70:58; 10.C.Pearson 71:03; 11.D.Maughan 72:02; 12.J.Wasbrough 73:31; 13.K.Duckett 75:05; 14.J.Dooley 76:07; 15. items.s: ERNIE 'DUFFS UP' WELLS AGAIN Note on club record holder Ernest Obeng's winter form: 10.2 to win the African Students Championships and a 60 metres win in 6.73 over Allan Wells at Cosford. ERNIE 'DUFFS UP' WELLS AGAIN The summer should bring some exciting sprint results from our Club Record holder Ernest Obeng if his 'winter' form is anything to go by. Running in the African Students Championships 100 metres on a cinder track, he clocked 10.2 to win - his fastest ever time, although details of wind conditions etc. are not yet known. Soon after this victory he was in an invitational line-up at Cosford. Leading the field from gun to tape he scored a mighty win over British Record holder Allan Wells, who has himself been wintering in Australia, to record 6.73 for the 60 metres. JANUARY 27th 1979 - ALDERSHOT - SOUTH OF THAMES 'SENIOR'. O'Connor Undaunted By Icy Conditions With the weather continuing to be icy it was not surprising that only eight hardy Belgravians made the trip to Aldershot for this race; and all eight fervently wished that they hadn't bothered. The course was treacherously covered with ice and snow, and the ruts became worse as the race went on. The course was similar to that used in the Surrey league race only longer - about four times as long it seemed! Even the support of several of our officials could not raise the team and everyone had a "bad one" except Pat O'Connor who once again showed his form over the country by finishing 54th, two places ahead of last year and easily our best man of the day. Unfortunately the rest of the report is a tale of woe. Tony Binda was forced to stop and walk on the second lap with bad cramp in the stomach and Steve Williams, after a promising return in the '10', was forced to retire with the same diaphragm trouble that has dogged him since the summer. The others struggled round and were glad to have finished the course. Colin Pearson had to add two more names to his black-list and will soon have to resort to other means of eliminating them! 1.P.Standing (windsor) 40:46; 2.R.Treadwell (S.Beagles) 41:18; 54. FEBRUARY 10th 1979 - PARLIAMENT HILL - SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. The 'Southern' After the South of Thames, two weeks before, we thought we had experienced the worst of the weather and conditions but it was not to be. Parliament Hill has always been difficult and it was made doubly so this year by a bitterly cold wind and no changing accommodation! Some people had come changed but for the rest, dressing rooms were either the back seats of cars or out in the open. Nevertheless we managed to field a full team if not our strongest. It was also good to see an old friend in the person of John Stow, unfortunately for us wearing the colours of Woodford Green over his claret and gold. As usual the mass start up the hill was fast and Belgrave were soon prominent towards the back of the field. As the race wore on ... and on ... Pat O'Connor worked through steadily and passed Stow on the final circuit of the 9 mile course to finish 138th. Simon Holmes was also working through the field but was unable to make the first 200 finishers. Behind him but another 100 places back Lionel Mann ran steadily and only just got home in front of Colin Pearson, having a real 'blinder'. The scoring team was completed by Doug Maugnan, also having a good one and Brian Gorman. The only enjoyable thing about the afternoon was the warming tea and coffee dispensed at very little charge by Messrs. Carter and Biscoe - once more braving the weather to support the runners. 1.J.Davies (TVH) 44:44; 2.P.Standing (Windsor) 45:24; 3.D.Clarke (Hercules Wimb) 45:38; 138.P.O'Connor 50:51; 208.S.Holmes; 311.L.Mann; 319.C.Pearson; 321.D.Maughan; 352.B.Gorman; 401.A.
