FEBRUARY 17th 1979 - COULSDON - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE RACE 4. Here We Go Again The final league race of the year was run over three laps of a shortened Coulsdon course due to the snow and ice still covering the ground. Although certain to be relegated we managed to field one of our strongest teams this year - something we should have done in the first three races. There were some notable absences but those who braved the cold weather ran well and we salvaged some pride by beating Herne Hill by 60 points on the day. Ian Duncan took over from Pat O'Connor as our leading runner; he was well up the field for the whole race and finished 13th. Simon Holmes was our second scorer for most of the race but was tiring at the end and O'Connor, timing his run to perfection, just got home in front. The deep snow was making the course very slippery and Dennis Brown was further hampered by heavy shoes. He gradually worked through though (encouraging the rest of the team as he went!) and finished just inside the first forty. With four in forty and our next six evenly spread out up to 78th we scored better than in any of the previous races - but all too late. Next year will see us in Division 2 for the second time in three years - not a happy record and one which we must reverse next season. Once again our thanks to Gordon Biscoe for his untiring efforts as team secretary. It is doubted that we would even be in Division 2 if not for his work and encouragement. 1.B.Ford (Aldershot F & D) 26:43; 13.I.Duncan 29:07; 28.P.O'Connor 30:04; 29.S.Holmes 30:04; 37.D.Brown 30:41; 48.L.Coy 31:28; 59. items.s: MARCH 3rd 1979 - STOPSLEY PARK, LUTON - E.C.C.U. CHAMPIONSHIP. Report and results of the English Cross Country Union (National) senior championship at Stopsley Park, Luton, on 3 March 1979, won by Mike McLeod, with Belgrave 68th of 169 teams and Ian Duncan their first man in 217th. MARCH 3rd 1979 - STOPSLEY PARK, LUTON - E.C.C.U. CHAMPIONSHIP. With a record number of 1,672 starters, 1,555 of whom managed to complete the windswept course, it is becoming quite a challenge to finish in the first 1,000. Up front spectators were treated to one of the finest finishes ever with the result in doubt until Elswick's Mike McLeod burst away from Ford (Aldershot), Rose (Bristol) and Kenyon (Bolton) with only 150 metres to go. As far as Belgrave were concerned however, it was one of those "if only" races. If only Laurie O'Hara and Jim Rimmer could have made it... if only Dennis Brown, who was there, was qualified to run.... if only John Bicourt could have finished (he was 17th last year) .... if only Simon Williamson, running well but for Birmingham University as an individual, had been on our team .... our team score would have been about 1,600 points less and our position about 30th instead of 68th. But no doubt other teams could point to their own shortcomings on the day, and at least we had the consolation of beating other Surrey League clubs Herne Hill 98th, Walton 105th and Epsom & Ewell 141st. 1.M.McLeod (Elswick) 47:10; 2.B.Ford (Aldershot) 47:12; 3.N.Rose (Bristol) 47:13; 217.I.Duncan; 255.J.Abberton (2nd-claim); 434.P. BELGRAVE HARRY by Alan BELGRAVE OPEN 7 FINISH GO ON HARRY - PILE IT ON - ALL THE WAY NOW - KEEP IT GOING - EYEBALLS OUT - NOT FAR NOW ZOOM OH NO! POOR OLD HARRY'S LAST AGAIN (HARRY'S MUM) HARRY GOES THROUGH HIS ATHLETIC BOOKS THAT NIGHT... I MUST FIND SOME WAY OF IMPROVING GOT IT! THIS BLOKE GORDON PIRIE USED TO TRAIN IN ARMY BOOTS WEIGHTED WITH LEAD THIS'LL DO IT - SHOT, DISCUS, WEIGHTS, BRICKS.... AND SO .... GASP! ....TRAINING BEGINS. HARRY YOU CAN'T WEAR THAT LOT TO WORK GOT TO MUM. MY SCHEDULE SAYS I CAN'T TAKE 'EM OFF TILL NEXT YEAR'S RACE COPSE HILL HARRY STRUGGLES ON.. NIGHT AND DAY... WINTER AND SUMMER... UNTIL ONE DAY HE MANAGES TO STAY WITH THE PACK TO THE END OF DENMARK ROAD! AND THEN, FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE HE DONNED THE WEIGHTS, HE GETS BACK FROM A SESSION THE SAME NIGHT HE SET OUT!! RACE DAY COMETH...... POWER COR! I FEEL GREAT WITHOUT THOSE WEIGHTS HOLDING ME DOWN ON YOUR MARKS! BLAM! CAW! WATCH IT YOU'RE OUT HARRY - DISQUALIFIED FOR LIFTING! items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Look-back column recalling Ron Linstead's course-record win in the 1954 5¾ mile road race, Belgrave's team win in the 1954 National 20 miles walk, and the club's victory in the 1939 National Cross Country Championship at Manchester.
items.s: from the Belgravian ... 25 years ago Look-back column recalling Ron Linstead's course-record win in the 1954 5¾ mile road race, Belgrave's team win in the 1954 National 20 miles walk, and the club's victory in the 1939 National Cross Country Championship at Manchester. from the Belgravian ... ... 25 years ago The 5¾ mile road race ..... 27th March 1954 ..... Over 40 runners turned out and there was a surprise winner in Ron Linstead. His time of 28mins. 25secs. was a new course record and once his National Service training is finished he will prove a handful to the best in the country. Charlie Smart who is now back in England for good - we hope - finished 2nd, with John Bromley 3rd. (Editor's note: Ron was a Youth when winning this race in 1954). The National 20 miles Walking Championship ..... May 8th 1954 ..... The Championship was held at Birmingham this year and what a grand day it turned out to be for the Club. Once again we are holders of a National title and it was grand to see in a weekly paper "Belgrave National Champions". Our heartiest congratulations to all, particularly George Checkley (9th) who celebrated his birthday by gaining his honours badge. Bernard Eglington (13th) missed his by one position. George Beecham (17th) gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan (4th) the Sidney Bayliss Cup. ... and 40 years ago The National Cross Country Championship 1939 ..... As we go to press comes wonderful news of the winning of the English Cross Country Championship at Manchester ..... 43 teams lined up for the start. Our lads were reasonably well away and at 1½ miles Stimpson and Penny were near the leaders, with our other runners well placed. At three miles the same state of affairs existed, but the large field passing in a solid mass of mud and humanity, with the rain pouring down, prevented any very definite conclusions being drawn. We knew that both Birchfield and ourselves were doing well..... On the next lap (5.3 miles) rough calculations showed us to be leading by a few points from Birchfield. Our runners were advised of this and seemed to run with more determination than ever. As they came round again (7.6 miles) to start the last lap we still led, but the Birchfield crowd were urging their team to gain positions. Then to the finish to await the arrival of the runners. First home was Jack Holden, of Tipton H., a worthy winner. Our first man home was Ted Stimpson, in fourth position, scoring 3 for team purposes. He had improved from 14th to 4th position over the last lap of 2.3 miles, passing seasoned runners as though they were not in the race. His effort was an amazing one, and our team had an excellent start. Then came Arthur Penny (5), another to rise to the occasion on an awful day. A few seconds delay and Tom Carter (17) appeared, followed a little later by our Captain, Bert Footer (28), who had gained place after place in the second half of the race. We now wanted two others to complete our team, and three claret and gold vests came along together. Harry Shields (34) and Dan Patience (35) managed to catch and beat A.W.Jerman on the run-in, and we had won the "National" for the second time! items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Ray Hall's ladies' section column on Sunday training at Battersea Park, promotion in the Lily 'B' League, coming Southern League and GRE Cup fixtures, the ladies' cross-country season, coaching lectures by Bruce Longden, injured members and thanks to helpers, with photos of captains Dawn McNeil and Wendy Dunsford.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ray Hall's ladies' section column on Sunday training at Battersea Park, promotion in the Lily 'B' League, coming Southern League and GRE Cup fixtures, the ladies' cross-country season, coaching lectures by Bruce Longden, injured members and thanks to helpers, with photos of captains Dawn McNeil and Wendy Dunsford. WITH THE LADIES There was a young lady named Bright, Whose speed was faster than light, She set out one day In a relative way, And returned home the previous night. Sorry to inform you but we've no ladies called Bright. But I can promise you some fine sprinting from the ladies section during the coming season thanks to the training that takes place every Sunday morning at Battersea Park under the direction of that task-master Frank Simmons. It gladdens my heart (yes I do have one) when I arrive to find 25 young athletes waiting to start training. If you have not been to Battersea Park lately, it is still bloody cold, wet and depressing but in winter twice as bad. During the winter the numbers have been surprising considering the weather conditions and in spite of the amount of hard work done the previous week, the girls still come back for more. reports by Ray Hall With the track season coming up fast, we look forward with anticipation to the Girls and Juniors facing stronger opposition in Lily 'B' Division II after our sensational win in the last match of 1978 where the result gave us second place by 2 points - Belgrave 949 and Dorking St. Paul's 947. So we were finally promoted with Aldershot & Farnham. The only complaint was from the Aldershot Team Manager who stated, "Oh! no. I've not got your noisy lot again." Sorry but yes you have. The Lily 'B' League has been extended to four matches for this season and all these matches are away - Croydon, Guildford, Aldershot and Woking. In the Womens' Southern League our journeying is short - to Dartford, Bexley and a home match at Battersea Park where competition will come from Dartford, Bexley Borough, Havant and Hercules Wimbledon. For the Southern League our two Captains Dawn McNeil (Track) and Wendy Dunsford (Field) will select the teams to take some of the work off my shoulders. Also, for the first time, we have entered the Womens' GRE Cup, and our first round match is at Croydon on Sunday May 6th. This competition is for Seniors only. Other matches have been arranged at Dorking and Woking but the trip to Hastings could not be accepted because of clashing with other fixtures. WE NEED YOUR SUPPORT FOR ALL THESE FIXTURES....................... The cross-country season has not brought any outstanding athletes to light wearing Belgrave vests. We have competed in the new cross country league but the support on the whole has been disappointing. The best sections have been the 'Inters' and Seniors, ably led by Pam Davies whose age I will not reveal (her children are great company). The supporting team has been made up of joggers, shot putters and some whose events have not yet been classified. At the time of writing, after three matches, they lead with 11 points from Croydon and Surrey Beagles, both 8 points. In the other two sections Girls and Juniors, we are bottom but Alison Jones, Tina Jordon and Joanne Warnett have enjoyed the experience. In the County Cross Country Championships, Alison Jones had a tough race in the Middlesex event at Ruislip and Tina Jordon ran at Dorking in the "Surreys". I hope next year, perhaps, we will have a team competing. In the coaching area we arranged three lectures by Bruce Longden (Daley Thompson's coach). We all enjoyed the first on Sprinting and Relay racing but the second was cancelled because of the weather. Its a disgrace that in a club of our size this is possibly the first effort in this area for many years. We look forward to the Hurdles lecture with the Guy Drut film. Perhaps someone will answer the question: "Why is it that Belgrave is so far behind in coaching and why it needs so much work and thought to bring it up to date?" With some effort we could motor to the elite of British athletic clubs so please put down your history books and give us all the help you can. Invalids: Pleased to hear that the diminutive Mary McPartlin is getting better after a serious illness and we look forward to seeing her competing in the Lily B matches in the summer. Valerie Bridges' back injury is slowly getting better and we are pleased to see Rebecca Augustin training after the operation on her leg. Gordon Doubleday, our timekeeper, has spent six weeks in hospital getting his own "ticker" seen to. We hope his recovery is speedy and that he too will soon be in action again. Thanks: To Carl Lawton for all his good work with the women walkers, and congratulations for the first set of W.C.C. & R.W.A. National medals for 3rd team. Well done Linda Nicholls for winning the Southern "Inter" title, and Shirley Rook and Anna Matthews for 2nd and 3rd in the Southern Senior race in the snow. To Frank Simmons for all his work on Sundays at Battersea Park. After seeing the training you can understand why he gets no "valentines". Those two eyes see everything on the track. To Ian Jones and Ken Jordon for their support and encouragement during the winter. To Ted Weldin and Richard Dorman at the C.C. League and last but not least my Assistant Derek Jones, who is always there, even during the difficult personal times he's had lately. If I've forgotten anybody - sorry! Dawn McNeil, the Ladies Section Track Captain, raises a smile in spite of another punishing Sunday morning. Wendy Dunsford, owner of a surname already well known in Belgrave's walking circles, is our Ladies Field Events Captain. items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Obituary of Jack Bidgood MBE, Metropolitan Police chief superintendent and Belgrave walker who won the 1950 Barking to Southend walk and chaired the Southern R.W.A.
items.s: JACK BIDGOOD M.B.E. Obituary of Jack Bidgood MBE, Metropolitan Police chief superintendent and Belgrave walker who won the 1950 Barking to Southend walk and chaired the Southern R.W.A. JACK BIDGOOD M.B.E. We were sorry to learn that Jack Bidgood died early in December; he must have been well into his seventies. He was born and brought up in Devon and followed the normal sporting life of a Devonian. Later he came to London and joined the Metropolitan Police where he became interested in walking and joined Belgrave. This was in our days of walking supremacy and he figured in many of our teams in National Championships (20 miles and 50 kilos only in those days), the London to Brighton and many provincial walks. As a policeman he was, of course, a regular competitor in the Barking to Southend Walk which he won in 1950. He also won the Club's Long-Distance Championship - held in conjunction with the London to Brighton Walk. Obviously then a great performer himself, he was always ready to give advice and encouragement to newcomers to the sport. He also found time to help on the administrative side and served a term of office as Chairman of the Southern R.W.A. During this period of office the Southern Committee decided to launch a magazine for walkers only - "Race Walking Record". Remembering that this was in World War Two it was a brave decision. After retiring from the active side he was a Judge for many years. He had a great career in the Metropolitan Police, finishing with the rank of Chief Superintendent. He was awarded the M.B.E. for meritorious service to the Force. Volumes could be written about his personality. He did much to foster the idea that the off-duty policeman could be as good a club man as any. He insisted that whilst engaged in sport he was called Jack - and Jack he was to everybody. He was as likeable and as pleasant a fellow as one could wish to meet. He had suffered indifferent health over the last few years, but his passing came as a surprise. We say farewell to a fine character who not only set an example by his sportsmanship but was a stalwart friend. G.S.D. items.sum: Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's review of the walking season: rising numbers, the Juniors' National 10 kilometres team win, the girls' team prizes, John Newnham's comeback, individual honours, the finances of the club's Open 7 mile walk, and plans for a training camp and more out-of-London races.
items.s: WALKING Walking Secretary Carl Lawton's review of the walking season: rising numbers, the Juniors' National 10 kilometres team win, the girls' team prizes, John Newnham's comeback, individual honours, the finances of the club's Open 7 mile walk, and plans for a training camp and more out-of-London races. WALKING A few seasons ago the walking editorial queried "where have all the walkers gone?". Since that time there has been a promising upturn in our numbers and as a result the allocation of National numbers issued to Belgrave has almost been used up. Results have, on the whole, been very good since the previous issue of the magazine and turn-outs for races have improved though we seldom manage that magical 100% - a feat we did achieve in the National J/Y/B at Coventry. On studying the results it will be seen that we have not been having to rely on the basic four as some clubs do. In fact in the four "opens": Chippenham, Vauxhall, Enfield and Belgrave, no less than ten permutated to pick up team prizes. In addition to that another eight have appeared in placed teams in recent months. It has on certain occasions given the Secretary problems in deciding who to put into the 'A' team. Although we did not win a Senior National title last year the Juniors did their bit by winning the 10 kilometres. The second time in three years that we have won it and as a result congratulations go to Richard Dorman, Paul Blagg and Trevor McDermot and commiserations to the four behind them who, had they walked for other clubs, would have been in the scoring teams. In the Youths we did not do so well but it was not for the lack of trying. We could well have placed 3rd had we not had the misfortune of disqualifications but at least we started a team and congratulations to Mike Nicholls for his 3rd place. We have had our problems with the Girls this year. With our small numbers it does prove difficult to raise teams on every occasion through work and other reasons but when we have succeeded we have usually come away with a prize: first team at Chippenham and 3rd in the National 5 kilometres. The "National" was a very good performance but had we a full and fit team we could have done far better. It is rather impractical to mention everyone who has done his or her bit for the Club (it might be easier to mention those who have not) but outstanding this year is undoubtedly John Newnham. Although he dabbled about six years ago and reached the echelons of six miles an hour in the Highgate Hour walks, he decided to have another go last year and much to his own and the Club's suprise has turned into one of the regular team men. He has no secret of success - just dedication. Others worthy of mention are Paul Blagg, Junior International; Richard Dorman, 2nd in the National Junior; Mike Nicholls, 3rd in the National Youths; Graham Seatter and Allan Callow, Commonwealth Games competitors; Derek Howie, Scottish International; Linda Nicholls, 2nd in the W.A.A.A. Championship. We had County Champions in Graham Seatter, John Hall, Carl Lawton, Richard Dorman, Kevin McDermot, Trevor McDermot, Linda and Mike Nicholls. Derek Ellis was the Police Cadet Champion, Shirley Rook the National Police Champion (for running but she walks mostly) and John Dunsford placed 3rd in the European Veterans Championships. The Annual Belgrave promotion, the 'Open 7 mile walk', had as most of you know a revised course this year. This was to ease the worsening problem of the traffic around the Common. Generally it proved successful and once again thanks are due to those within the Belgrave circle but not actually members: Joan Goswell, Wyn Cook and Jean Middleton, who do such sterling work. We did have a small problem with pointsmen but that should not happen again. Thanks, in no small way, also go to those who, with their generosity, enable the Club to keep up a high standard of prizes. The cost of prizes last year came to nearly £120, with receipts from entries just £60. Thus another £60 had to be raised to cover the cost of the promotion and much of this came from the prize fund and the rest (total outlay was nearly £160) from teas, programmes and the raffle. Although very little is done within the Club with regard to coaching for walking, it being carried out on an individual basis, it is anticipated to try and hold a training camp over a long weekend. By the time you read this, plans should be well advanced. In addition it is planned to make more of an impact on races which the Club has not competed in for a while. The turn-out for the Leicester Mercury last year was rather poor so that is a good starting point. There is also the Birmingham 35kms plus possibly a couple of Northern races - the Morecambe 20kms and the Sheffield '15' or the Bradford 50kms. With our strength in depth there is no reason why we should not support more races out of London. If we expect other clubs to come to us we should return the compliment. It is a few years since we won the Leicester Mercury on the Saturday and then placed second in the Bradford event two days later with a completely different team. Two other races to prepare for this year will be the Surrey Walking Club 100 miles at Ewhurst and the inaugural 100 kilometre championship, both of which we should be able to support at full strength. At Birmingham on August 5th 1978 Linda Nicholls placed 2nd in the W.A.A.A. Intermediate 3kms in 16:56. The following week at Victoria Park Linda was 2nd again over the same distance but was this time clocked at 16:36. Jane Pritchard was 5th in 18:51. In the Youth/Junior 3kms event Richard Dorman was our first home, 2nd in 13:51, followed by M.Nicholls 5th 14:40 and K. McDermot 9th 15:04. The main event was the Southern Area 20kms, on this occasion won by Ilford's Gower in 90:39. Belgrave placings were: 4. C.Lawton 95:04; 16.D.Howie 104:14; 17.R.Picton 104:47; 19.L. Duquemin 105:27; 23.J.Dunsford 106:49; 24.J.Newnham 107:44; 41.D. Fotheringham 114:59. The team scored 41 points for 3rd, just behind Ilford's 40 and Steyning's 29. Brighton, on August 19th, saw a Belgrave 1, 2, 3 in another 20kms event with Carl winning in 98:28 from John Hall and Derek Howie. Glutton for punishment that he is, Carl was out the following day for the South Western Counties open track 10kms at Weymouth. It was another win for the Belgrave Walking Secretary in 46:35, with Len Duquemin placing 2nd in the Hampshire Championship in 51:56. Meanwhile, at Crystal Palace, Richard Dorman took a representative 3kms in 13:44. Six minutes 31.8 seconds. That was the personal best set by Carl Lawton in the Rotary Watches 1 mile event at Crystal Palace. (We have seen Belgrave runners clock more than that at this venue). items.s: Family Occasion Report and results of the Festival of Walking at Enfield on 26 August 1978, with team wins for Belgrave's youths and senior ladies, 4th team in the 20km, and the McDermot and Nicholls walking families. The report has Anna finishing 4th in the senior ladies race but the results list A.Matthews 2nd; both kept as printed. Race reports by Gordon Doubleday AUGUST 26th 1978 - ENFIELD. Family Occasion The Festival of Walking promoted by the Borough of Enfield H. drew a number of us to Enfield and amongst our participants we had three from each of the McDermot and Nicholls families with John Morris and son (Peter) as well. In the first event we had two Junior Ladies lined up for the 2,500 metres and it was good to see the fine styles (not to mention the enthusiasm) shown by the youngest members of the two families. They are both also keen swimmers. There were three teams contesting the Youths' 5,000m and with Mike walking strongly for 2nd place, well supported by Kevin and Peter, we took first team awards, scoring 10 points to the 14 of Waltham Forest. The Havering team failed to close in. About five minutes after the start of the Youths, the Senior Ladies started over the same course. Anna walked confidently all the way to finish 4th, followed home by a fast finishing Linda. With a fighting performance by Jane we gained another "first" scoring 12 points to beat Epsom & Ewell H 15, and Brighton & Hove 19. The "big'un", 20 kilometres over a six lap course, showed us to be without some of our top performers but our team gave a good account of themselves to finish a close 4th, the scoring being Ilford 36, Enfield 37, Brighton & Hove 37 and Belgrave 40. The hero of the race was Richard Dorman, walking his second 20kms. He was near to the leaders right from the start and a well judged performance gave him 7th place, 46 seconds over the 100 minute "barrier". Examination of the result sheet showed Richard to be ahead of several good men. Our next man was John Newnham who continues to make his presence felt - he deserved a team prize and his turn will surely come. Not far behind came the other John (Dunsford) - 1st Veteran home. Making his debut over the distance was Trevor McDermot who walked the first half with Ray and then showed us what a prospect he is by dropping Ray (his second 10kms was faster than his first), to get under 110 minutes. Our other walkers no doubt preferred the sunshine to the drenching they got last year! Keep a lookout for further references to the McDermots and Nicholls - these two walking families are surely going to grace our pages for many years. items.sum: Walking report on the 1978 London to Brighton walk, where Belgrave failed to start a team for the first time but Dave King and John Keown finished 18th and 26th; part of Gordon Doubleday's race reports series begun on page 40.
items.s: SEPTEMBER 2nd 1978 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON Walking report on the 1978 London to Brighton walk, where Belgrave failed to start a team for the first time but Dave King and John Keown finished 18th and 26th; part of Gordon Doubleday's race reports series begun on page 40. SEPTEMBER 2nd 1978 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON For the first time in the Club's history we failed to start a team in the London to Brighton walk. We had the minimum of four entered and when Ron Day announced his unfitness to walk owing to injury John Hall decided not to start. This left our two evergreen stalwarts Dave King and John Keown to carry our colours down this famous road. This they did to good effect, finishing 18th in 9:34:24 and 26th in 9:54:54. Our other starter, Derek Howie, entered as an individual, put up a plucky performance for his first "Brighton". For well over half way he was always near the leaders but over the last miles he began to lose places and became unsteady so wisely retired with just nine miles left. He was full of praise for his attendant Richard Dorman, escorting him by cycle, who had endeavoured to keep him going. One "regular" we missed was John Morris who was unfit. However, he didn't deny us for he soon came through the field on his motor-cycle, with Peter on the back, to help our pair along. Another motor-cyclist was Joe Coleman, a regular on the Judges Panel for this event. It was good to see Charlie Speechley at the finish - "Dr. Brighton" obviously plays a part in keeping him 90 years young! items.sum: Short report on John Morris regaining the Colnbrook long distance walk championship in December for his fifth win.
items.s: MORRIS DANCES TO FIFTH COLNBROOK TITLE. Short report on John Morris regaining the Colnbrook long distance walk championship in December for his fifth win. MORRIS DANCES TO FIFTH COLNBROOK TITLE. John Morris, Belgrave's stalwart long distance walker, showed that he is still a force to be reckoned with when in December he regained the Colnbrook long distance walk championship in 2 hours 21 minutes 34 seconds. John, who has now notched up five wins, although he has not won for the last four years, threw off an early challenge to win convincingly by five minutes to show that he is still in with a chance in this year's long distance events. John Morris John Morris won Colnbrook long distance walk championship, 2:21:34, his fifth win John Morris John Colnbrook long distance walk championship Colnbrook

items.s: Giant's View Report of Carl Lawton winning the South Western Counties Open 20km walk at Cerne Abbas on 17 September 1978, with Belgrave taking the team race. SEPTEMBER 17th 1978 - CERNE ABBAS - SOUTH WESTERN COUNTIES OPEN 20K. Giant's View One of the sights of the village of Cerne Abbas, Dorset, is the giant carved out of the turf of the surrounding hills. He must have looked down upon generations of pedestrians but none can have moved faster than Carl did when winning the S.W. Counties Open 20 Kilos over a four lap course. Twenty-odd walkers completed the tough course on a warm, sunny day. Various local championships were incorporated in the event but our interest was in the open team race where the opposition came from S.W. clubs. Carl led from the start and gave a fine exhibition of walking to win in 98 minutes 6 seconds, splendid considering the severity of the course. Getting back into form was Len whose crisp style is beginning to bite again. Bob and John fought it out for three laps but Bob proved stronger over the last lap to complete the winning team. John, a newcomer, stuck it out bravely - he won't find many courses as hilly. A handicap showed Len 2nd (he also took the Vet's prize) and Bob 3rd. Once again there was a warm welcome for us; the high regard in which Belgrave is held all over the country is always most gratifying. One of Carl's prizes will be a reminder of the Giant - a small model made by local craftsmen from horse-shoe nails, with very realistic detail. 1.C.Lawton 98:06; 5.L.Duquemin 109:45; 7.R.Picton 111:17; 11.J. items.s: Maud Heath's Causeway Report of the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles open road walk on 14 October 1978, where Carl Lawton won for the fifth time, Belgrave won the men's team and the ladies also won their race. OCTOBER 14th 1978 - CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE 6 MILES OPEN ROAD WALK. Maud Heath's Causeway Many years ago a lady of this name used to walk with the farm produce to market over the watery meadows in the Calne, Wiltshire, area. She spent her savings on building a road and bridges to ease the journey and there is now a column erected to her memory. Nowadays folk from many parts of the country walk from Chippenham to Calne and untramelled by baskets of eggs etc. no doubt go somewhat faster than did the good lady. Why all this? After seeing the start of this year's walk I was transported to Calne via the Causeway so as to avoid the heavy traffic at the start. The only part of the race I saw was the finish. Carl led the team home to notch up his 5th win with 41 seconds to spare. Seventh was Richard Dorman who took the prize for first Junior and four places later came Paul, further evidence of our growing strength in the Junior ranks. Fourth Belgravian to finish was Len but he had been declared in the 'B' team. It wasn't long before John Newnham came in to complete our winning scratch team - with three visits to the prize table it was a day he won't forget! Claret and gold vests came in thick and fast with 10 in the first 35. A great performance by one of the youngest in the race was that of Kevin McDermot, 53rd in a time which indicates that he will soon be under the hour for seven miles. John, Richard, Nigel Morris and Bob Picton won the handicap team award with a total time over six minutes better than the second team. John and Richard also took individual handicap awards. Walking the same course the Ladies had their own race. The winner was the diminutive Carol Tyson (Lakeland AC) in an excellent 48:21 - a time which would have given her 12th place in the mens' race! In 5th place, inside the hour, came Shirley - walk or run she always gives a good performance. Bang on the hour came Linda, having a spot of muscle trouble. Jane put up her usual supporting performance, one of her best, finishing in front of the second and third scorers of the other teams - another sterling win for our ladies. As if this wasn't enough, when the raffle was drawn Linda's number came out first. Just like old times with the added pleasure of having the ladies joining in the awards. National' Win For Juniors Richard Dorman spearheaded the Belgrave attack on the National Junior Team title, chasing hard with Paul Blagg close by after the early leaders Wordsworth (Tonbridge) and Miley (Harbourne) had made a small break. However, Wordsworth had problems with sickness. He recovered but then was disqualified leaving the way clear for Miley. Richard came home in 2nd spot, five seconds up on Yorkshire's Elliott and with Paul 6th and Trevor McDermot closing the team in with 10th, Belgrave took the team race for the second time in three years. items.s: Note that the Mayor of Chippenham, Councillor M. Plumb, a former Belgrave shot putter who joined in 1954 or 1955, spoke warmly of the club at the Chippenham to Calne walk prize-giving. When the Mayor of Chippenham, Councillor M. Plumb, spoke at the prize-giving after the Chippenham to Calne Walk he expressed his pleasure at the number going to Belgrave - a club of which he was once a member. He joined us in 1954 or 55 when he was a member of the Aristotle Road School Athletics team which won the South London Schools under 13 trophy. He was a shot putter and was introduced to us by his sportsmaster, Colin Collis. Colin very kindly sent us a photograph of the team and amongst those in it were Alan Black and his twin brother and one or two others who joined us for a while. He trained conscientiously at Battersea Park and Tooting Bec tracks and performed well at his chosen event. We certainly wish him and the Mayoress every happiness in his term of office, which obviously has its pleasant side when he sees his old club successfully competing down his way. M. Plumb M. items.s: PUT YOURSELF IN THE BELGRAVE PICTURE Appeal, in a decorative picture frame, for helpers to run the Youths and Boys Section now that Leo Coy cannot continue. PUT YOURSELF IN THE BELGRAVE PICTURE We desperately need help in running the Youths and Boys Section during the coming summer. Leo Coy has ably administered this area for the past few years, for which we thank him, but he now regrets that he cannot continue. We have a lot of young talent but it needs to be organised. We are not necessarily looking for just one person, the more the better. So if you would like to help on a regular basis please contact the General Hon. Secretary, Derek Crookes, whose address and phone number are on the inside front cover of this magazine. items.s: The Open Walk Report and results of the Belgrave Open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon on 25 November 1978, won by Mike Parker of Brighton & Hove with Carl Lawton 2nd and Belgrave 2nd team, plus the first Open Ladies race won by Carol Tyson. NOVEMBER 25th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN 7 MILES WALK. The Open Walk Once again we were blessed with good weather. The new three lap course was used which involves three times up the "hills" by what must be the steepest route (Cottenham Drive). Our President Ray started the race and then took his place in the field. The early leader was Mike Parker (Brighton & Hove) with Carl, closely followed by Brian Armstrong (Ilford), leading the rest. It was good to see Derek Howie on one of his trips from Stirling. Unfortunately he developed some leg trouble which proved a drawback - he is having this put right before competing again. Mike Scamell was showing us a taste of what to expect when he becomes eligible to represent us early in the New Year. John Hall was going well as were the younger brigade - Richard, Trevor, Kevin and Mike, plus the steadily improving John Newnham. Would the sharp pace be blunted by the "hills"? It didn't affect Mike Parker who finished strongly over two minutes ahead of Carl. John, Derek and Richard completed the team to give us 38 points and second place to Brighton & Hove, 31 points. We were closely followed by Surrey WC, 41 points, and it is good to see our old rivals back in the reckoning. Once again our non-scorers were hot on the heels of the team - it is pleasing to note the steady progress of Pete Morris, his name is creeping up the finishing lists. One other Belgravian had to make a trip to the prize table - Doug Fotheringham who took 8th individual handicap prize. The prizes were handed out by our President, Ray, and it was good to see the affection and goodwill which he enjoys amongst the race-walkers. The first Open Ladies Race to be held in conjunction saw some brilliant walking by Carol Tyson (Lakeland AC), her time would have brought her 29th position in the main race. Unfortunately there were only four starters. Our own Shirley earned applause for her efforts. The smooth conduct of the race was once again in the hands of Club "Old Faithfuls", and it was pleasing to see Joe Coleman active as Chief Judge. Once again our thanks to the Race Hon. Secretary Carl Lawton who organised things with his usual thoroughness. Ladies 7 miles: 1.C.Tyson (Lakeland AC) 58:26; 4.S.Rook 72:40. items.s: Shirley's Here ! Report and results of the Women's R.W.A. National Walking Championships at Melksham on 3 December 1978, where Shirley Rook, Linda Nicholls and Jane Pritchard won Belgrave's first National team medals in a women's event (3rd team). DECEMBER 3rd 1978 - MELKSHAM, WILTS. - WOMENS R.W.A. NATIONAL CHAMPS. Shirley's Here ! BELLES WIN THEIR FIRST SET OF NATIONAL MEDALS. The Womens' C.C. and R.W.A. National Walking Championships were held at Melksham, Wiltshire, on a cold, damp day and when we all met up we were disappointed to discover that we had only two competitors for each of the three events. Anna Matthews had already let us know that she wouldn't be competing and Caroline Khan, who has walked so well on the track, was missing from the 3,000 metres race. The first race, the under 13 2,500 metres, saw Bernadette Sexton and Tracey Nicholls in action. It was a small field and in spite of their lowly positions they showed what good competitors they are. Their experience should stand them in good stead for the next track season when they should pick up some good points in League fixtures Well warmed up for the under 15 3,000 metres were Tracey McDermot with brother Kevin in attendance, and Ros. There were some fast movers here and our pair showed what fine performers they are becoming. They came fighting their way through the finish in fine style. A short walk down the road took us to the start of the Seniors 5,000 metres. The rain was increasing and Linda and Jane, well wrapped up, were keeping warm before being called to the start. Suddenly a voice called out, "Shirley's here" and on looking round we saw a smiling Shirley who had motored down. The Belgrave morale shot up immediately - we had a team after all and they were going to have a go for some medals. At the start Carol Tyson (Lakeland AC) and evergreen Judy Farr (Trowbridge) were soon leading with many hot on their heels, walking impeccably. Our trio looked lively. With one mile to go Carol was clearly away with three others battling away for the placings. When the rest appeared Shirley was going strongly soon followed by fast moving Linda. Later came Jane, working hard to improve her position. Carol Tyson won convincingly but there must have been some battle for the placings, Karen Eden (Solihull) and Irene Bateman (Basildon) taking 2nd and 3rd places with Judy Farr 4th. When the "field" came in Shirley soon arrived followed by Linda - both had kept up the pressure over the closing stages to ensure good placings. Jane too had put in some good walking and din't relax until she had crossed the line. A happy group of Belgravians were at the finish speculating upon the team's position. Some hopefuls said third and this was soon officially confirmed. So, we had won our first set of National Team medals in a Womens' event - the first of many we hope. Congratulations to Shirley, Linda and Jane who made our trip to Melksham a day to remember. One thing which delighted me was the look of joy on the faces of the four who had walked earlier - you would have thought that they had won the medals! - their turn will come. items.s: FEBRUARY 3rd 1979 - MELKSHAM, WILTS. - SOUTHERN AREA GARNET 10 MILES. Report of the Southern Area Garnet 10 miles walk at Melksham on 3 February 1979, where only five of twelve Belgrave entries turned out and the team placed 5th. items.sum: Local-history note on the 1845 experimental railway track of a Mr. Prosser near the Windmill (on the route of the club's Yacht '3' course), with two engravings from the Illustrated London News.
items.s: COMMON KNOWLEDGE Local-history note on the 1845 experimental railway track of a Mr. Prosser near the Windmill (on the route of the club's Yacht '3' course), with two engravings from the Illustrated London News. COMMON KNOWLEDGE About halfway between the Kingsmere pond and the Windmill lies the site of an experimental railway track laid down in 1845 to test the invention of a Mr. Prosser. This part of the track was built in a circle but a further straight stretch leading off the circle probably extended well down Windmill Road, along which our Yacht '3' course also travels. The rails were rectangular in section and made of a chemically hardened wood. The train designed for this track had flangeless wheels but had guiding wheels set at 45° to the horizontal with right angled grooves which engaged the rails. The train was said to be more economic than the "iron railway" due to the lack of friction; the power needed was only about three-quarters of that required for a conventional locomotive. items.label: April 1979
items.sum: Linda Nicholls describes her three-week walking training holiday with the Swedish club Enhorna I.F. near Stockholm, including a weekend camp and a championship at Boras.
items.s: TRIP TO SWEDEN Linda Nicholls describes her three-week walking training holiday with the Swedish club Enhorna I.F. near Stockholm, including a weekend camp and a championship at Boras. Linda Nicholls writes of her TRIP TO SWEDEN In September, as a result of an invitation through my family, I travelled to Sweden for a three weeks training holiday. During my stay I trained with the Swedish club Enhorna I.F. They are an extremely pleasant group of people and were very helpful and friendly during the period I was with them. Their training sessions, usually two evenings a week, are held on the outskirts of Stockholm. The sessions are similar to those at Belgrave Hall but with more emphasis on exercising and sprinting. It was interesting to see that youngsters of eight and nine were training very seriously and walking quite long distances. At weekends when there were no races there would be a two day camp in the country. I was fortunate in being invited to one of these and it was again noticable that general exercises were a major part of their training. All of the walkers would carry out the same exercises and this would be followed by a long steady stroll over forest paths which are plentiful in that area. The distances covered over the two days were in the region of 25 kms. although the youngsters would only do about half that. Although the training was harder than I have ever done before it was an enjoyable weekend. There was an excellent club spirit amonst the walkers and Siw Gustavsson, with whom I trained and who is one of the leading Swedish walkers, made me feel very much at home. I was invited to walk in one of the major championships held at Boras There I found that many eight and nine year olds were racing. In fact there were seventeen different grades of walkers including the leading Finns and Swedes. Regrettably, with so much talent about, I suffered an inferiority complex. During my three week stay I managed a few trips around Stockholm and saw many of its notable sites, discovering that the city is made up of a number of islands all linked by a number of bridges. Overall I had an interesting and enjoyable trip and if all goes well I hope to have a reciprocal arrangement next year with some of their walkers coming over here. Linda Nicholls Linda Nicholls three-week training holiday in Sweden with Enhorna I.F. Siw Gustavsson Siw Gustavsson one of the leading Swedish walkers Sweden Stockholm Belgrave Hall Boras Enhorna I.F.

items.sum: Tribute to Shirley Rook, 20, who missed the coach to the women's National walk but drove 100 miles to compete and helped Belgrave win its first National team medals.
items.s: MOST MERITORIOUS PERFORMANCE ? Tribute to Shirley Rook, 20, who missed the coach to the women's National walk but drove 100 miles to compete and helped Belgrave win its first National team medals. MOST MERITORIOUS PERFORMANCE ? Imagine having been selected to represent Belgrave in a National only to arrive too late to catch the coach on a 200 mile round trip to compete. Would you have called it a day and gone home and apologised later or would you have done the alternative thing - gone home, got into your car, driven the 100 miles not knowing the exact venue and eventually finding it with minutes to spare? Most would have undoubtedly have settled on the former but Shirley Rook (20),to her credit, did the latter. As a result she helped Belgrave collect their first National Team Medals. Shirley did more for Belgrave in one day than most of us do in a year. Shirley Rook Shirley Rook aged 20; drove 100 miles to the women's National after missing the coach and helped win Belgrave's first National team medals Shirley Rook Shirley Women's R.W.A. items.sum: Alan Mead's profile of Belgrave high jumper, long jumper and pole vaulter Arnold Bentt: his best performances, schools and junior career in the 1960s (UK number one junior high jumper in 1968), his relaxed approach since, and his own view of the sport.
items.s: SPOTLIGHT ON - ARNOLD BENTT Alan Mead's profile of Belgrave high jumper, long jumper and pole vaulter Arnold Bentt: his best performances, schools and junior career in the 1960s (UK number one junior high jumper in 1968), his relaxed approach since, and his own view of the sport. SPOTLIGHT ON - ARNOLD BENTT Five times England Schools competitor 1965-1969. by Alan Mead One of the most talented and regular members of the Belgrave track and field team for the last decade and more, Arnold is second to very few other Belgravians when one considers the total number of points he has amassed for the club in League and inter-club matches during that period. Now twenty-eight, he admits that he hasn't really trained hard since he left school.... in fact more than that ....he now rarely trains at all! For Arnold getting fit now means beginning to compete in May, gradually overcoming the sore muscle stage and working up a competition edge as the season wears on. A typical trophy meeting will see him arrive well after the match has started (when travelling by coach we tell him to get there half an hour before anyone else), go straight into the fourth round of the pole vault (it's always worth declaring him even if he's not there yet), lazily soar over about 3 metres and then start looking round for something else to do. * * * Arnold was born in 1950 in Kingston, Jamaica, and came to London at the age of nine. He went to St. Gerard's School and by the time he was thirteen was already showing an interest in athletics. "Little Joe" Harvey, now long since fallen by the wayside but then one of Frank Simmons' regulars at the Ravenstone School weight training sessions, introduced Arnold to the Club and he became a member in June, 1963. Before long he was sweating his way round Frank's circuits like the rest of us, being shouted at to "Get your knees up!" and showing his enjoyment of this treatment by coming back for more punishment at Battersea Park track on Sunday mornings. Third place in the Boys' "Mrs. L. Ryan" Cup marked his entry to competition in 1964, covering thows, jumps and running events from 100 yards to half a mile; the ideal way to start off for a youngster in athletics - having a go at everything. By the following year though, it was obvious that jumping was to be his forte. From this period on Belgrave Harriers were fortunate in having a remarkable squad of long jumpers training under coach Dave Ansell's supervision: John Mitchell, Cliff Brooks, Bob Jones and later Alan Lerwill and Steve White. It was not surprising that in such a fertile atmosphere and under the careful nurturing of one of the best jumping coaches of the time, Arnold's talent bloomed. Having won the London Schools long jump in 1965 he went on to place second in the All-England event but "coach" was particularly impressed with his high jumping potential. The "Belgravian" reported that fourteen year old Arnold Bentt had reached 1.72 (5'8") at a time when the top ten juniors in the country ranged from 1.90 (6'3") down to 1.80 (5'11") but Arnold had another four years in hand over many of these top rankers and therefore had excellent prospects of leading the junior lists before reaching senior status. (Seniors were eighteen and over in those days.) In 1966 Arnold began to be plagued by a heel injury that was to hold back his progress for the next two years. Nevertheless, he took several long and high jump wins in junior trophy meetings, represented London Schools again in the long jump, set youth and junior Club records in the high jump, won his first Club Championship in the junior "high" with a silver medal in the senior event to boot, and even beat Steve White over 100 yards! He had more or less switched to the high jump full time by 1967, finding that jumping for length continued to pound his injury prone heel. In spite of not really improving his best leap since 1965 his competitive record was good. Retaining the junior Club title, he also annexed the senior event. The Surrey County junior title was added to his list of achievements and he represented Surrey in the Inter-Counties, placed 2nd in the London Schools and made his 3rd trip to the England Schools Championships where he reached 6th. Probably the highlight of the season, however, was his selection to take part in the Inter-Cities match in Denmark where he returned to the long jump. * * * The big break-through came the following year after concentrating on the technique side of his high jumping. Arnold was always an exponent of the straddle style, particularly admiring the art as executed by Russia's Valeriy Brumel before that man's career was wrecked by a motor-cycling accident. Paradoxically, it was this year, 1968, that the athletics world became introduced to the "Fosbury Flop" when Dick Fosbury (USA) won the Mexico Olympic event with his then unusual but now most common style; but for Arnold the practised discipline of the straddle was the key to his success. In a leisurely inter-club match at Tootirg he went over 6 feet for the first time. Then came the South London Schools title which he took in his stride at 1.86 (6'1½"), followed by his burst onto the National scene by winning the London event in 1.91 (6'3½") to become the United Kingdom's number one junior (fulfilling the "Belgravian" prediction) - seventh on the senior list. He came into the competi- continued on following page ... SPOTLIGHT ON ARNOLD BENTT continued ...... tion late, moving up from 1.82 (6'0") in 2 inch intervals to 1.93 (6'4") before failing at 1.98 (6'6"). It has always mystified him how this jump got written down to 6'3". As it was a record height the officials remeasured it by tape - 6'3½" - but finally it was reported as 6'3". As our senior club record is 1.91 (6'3½") dating back to 1936 one can understand his disappointment. Other landmarks in 1968 included competing in Strasbourg in the International Catholic Games, "failing" with fifth place and 1.77 (5'10") in the England Schools when the winner leapt only 1.85 (6'1") and retaining both Club high jump titles. Broadening his horizons and with injury problems overcome, Arnold set personal bests in 1969 in the long jump, 200 metres, and high hurdles, winning the Club Championship in the latter event. Six feet was all that was required of him to take the South London Schools event yet again but in the "London's" he was below form and his final trip to the England Schools was again disappointing with 1.77 (5'10") for sixth place on countback even though he equalled the silver medallists height. Further representative honours came his way when he carried Lambeth's colours in Germany against Vincennes and Castrop Rauxel. * * * Somehow, Arnold's athletic career failed to move on from this point. Perhaps it was the transition from school to work.....maybe Dave Ansell's subsequent migration to Leeds and the dissolving of our school of jumpers. Maybe it was a little of each of these things but probably the underlying reason is that for Arnold athletics is just not the "be all and end all". Notwithstanding this, he has not missed a season with us since and still pops out a really good performance now and then - witness that 13.99 triple jump a couple of seasons back. Arnold has dabbled at basketball, training and competing for Wandsworth in the early 70's but his real passion is reading. He avidly devours scientific literature, anything on parapsychology, the forces of nature, fringe medicine, the occult, UFO's; a list of subjects that makes him a most interesting conversationallist. His team mates mostly see him as a super-relaxed, happy-go-lucky individual but Arnold does not subscribe to this view of himself. "I suppose I've got a bit of talent and that might make it look casual when I compete but really it is just a matter of what is important to one. To me athletics is not that important. I enjoy it, and I'll carry on as long as I do enjoy it - and anyway, it's good for my physical well-being. "But I suppose I do miss the times when there was a group of us in the Club all working and training towards a particular group of events. A bit of competition in training, like going round "circuits" in pairs, encourages enthusiasm." * * * What stupendous performances might we have seen from an Arnold Bentt that trained through the 70's like he did when at school....taking on an ever increasing work load....aiming for the top....? We will never know but anyway, it just wouldn't be Arnold would it? 200m: 23.5 1969 110m hurdles: 16.9 1972 Long Jump: 6.76 1969 High Jump: 1.91 1968 Triple Jump: 13.99 1977 Pole Vault: 3.10 1974 Arnold Bentt ARNOLD BENTT born 1950 in Kingston, Jamaica; five times England Schools competitor 1965-69; joined Belgrave June 1963; pole vault best 3.10 (1974), triple jump 13.99 (1977); London Schools long jump winner 1965; UK number one junior high jumper 1968 with 1.91; competed at the International Catholic Games, Strasbourg 1968; represented Lambeth in Germany; played basketball for Wandsworth ARNOLD BENTT Arnold Arnold Bentt Alan Mead Alan Mead "Little Joe" Harvey "Little Joe" Harvey introduced Arnold Bentt to the club Frank Simmons Frank Simmons' ran weight training sessions at Ravenstone School and circuits Frank Simmons' Frank's Mrs. L. items.label: October 1979
items.sum: Unsigned editorial weighing the club's disappointments of the past six months (relegations, weak support) against the successes of the walkers, ladies and young athletes, and urging members to help the committee ahead of the 1987 centenary.
items.s: Unsigned editorial weighing the club's disappointments of the past six months (relegations, weak support) against the successes of the walkers, ladies and young athletes, and urging members to help the committee ahead of the 1987 centenary. For the pessimists among us events over the last 6 months may well have provided satisfaction. In Spring we were relegated to Div.2 of the N.Surrey C.C.League. Last month we just escaped relegation from Div.1 of the Southern T & F League on a technicality. On many occasions our members have failed to support events with good performers standing on the sidelines. Middle distance running which for years was our strength is now at a low ebb. And on the social side events held to make the most of our improved facilities at Belgrave that have received scant support. Not very encouraging. Fortunately there is a brighter side. Our Walkers continue to hold the banner high. Our Ladies continue to progress gaining promotion to Div.3 of the Southern T and F League and Linda Nicolls became our first Ladies International; but perhaps most encouraging of all is that for the first time in over a decade a fistful of track records have been broken by our Youths and Boys and Richard Dorman has gained his Junior International vest. Indeed, as we go to press we learn of a win by the Youths in the tough Surrey Road Relays. So, like the curate's egg we are good in parts. Why? If we look back over more successful years we find a veritable who's who of personalities dedicating time and effort to encouraging, managing and leading our active athletes. We see it today with Carl Lawton and the Walkers, Ray Hall and the Ladies, and Colin Pearson and the Youths. Such people would be the first to point out that they rely for support on a willing band of helpers. But the fact remains, it is a few dedicated individuals who provide the spark and effort to see things through. Our Committee must set the targets with regard to fund raising, recruiting, coaching or competing. It is our officials and athletes who must see they are achieved. To do this they need help and support. Sharing the work load is a practical way of helping so why not contact Derek Crookes and chat it over. Let us all aim to move Belgrave to a paramount position for our centenary year. Don't delay, its only 8 years away! items.label: October 1979
items.sum: Profile of the new club President Bill Merryman: his junior cross country days with Belgrave from 1932, an RAF air crash in 1940, wartime track and road relay racing, a spell as Field Events Secretary when Belgrave won the Sward Trophy, and his loyalty to the club.
items.s: OUR PRESIDENT Profile of the new club President Bill Merryman: his junior cross country days with Belgrave from 1932, an RAF air crash in 1940, wartime track and road relay racing, a spell as Field Events Secretary when Belgrave won the Sward Trophy, and his loyalty to the club. OUR PRESIDENT Photo by Bill Laws Our new President joined Belgrave Harriers in 1932 as a boy. He was a member of winning and placed Surrey Youths and Junior cross country teams, competed in the Southern Junior cross country team and ran in many senior team events, helped by the guiding influence of Dick Savage Snr. Bill joined the Royal Air Force in 1939, and during 1940 was involved in a Beaufighter crash at 200 mph at Fradley near Lichfield, resulting in injuries causing every muscle in his back to be badly torn. Bill was nursed back to health after many months of treatment by the R.A.F. and was very determined to run in top class company. He was told that serious running would be out, but set out to prove otherwise. By working in conjunction with Joe Binks who helped with advice and by giving medals for various races, a very strong unit Track team was formed in the Midlands, and in between war duties the team won many races, getting invitations in aid of the Red Cross. The team received an invitation from Joe Binks to appear in the "British Games" June 1943 which were sponsored by The News of The World and featured top athletes from our allies, U.S.A. France and Poland. Bill ran against Sydney Wooderson in the mile and was pulled along against foreign opposition to a time of 4.18 finishing fourth to Sydney Wooderson. Shortly after this Bill was posted to another unit and set about forming a good road team. He succeeded in this by getting other athletes from various clubs who were in the R.A.F. and were stationed around to join in forming a team. The team qualified to run in the war time London to Brighton relay road race held at Mitcham, The News of The World being the sponsors. The team was well in the lead until the last lap when beaten into third place. The winning army team was captained by none other than Les Cohen of Belgrave, who ran the last leg for the army. Bill introduced Norman Graves to Athletics who became a very good athlete, and today is a top grade AAA time keeper in the North of England, and a member of Wirral A.C. On leaving the services Bill went to Yorkshire to live for a period, where he ran for Leeds Harehills Harriers as a guest only, refusing to leave Belgrave. On returning to London he picked up the threads with Belgrave, helping now to take out new members and to give training hints and advice. Many are still members to this day, Clive Shippham was one, and when he got his county colours no one else could have been more overjoyed for him than Bill. Bill has served on many committees, eventually becoming Field Events Secretary and with the help of Charlie Jones, in the first year we won the famous Sward Trophy, the top trophy award for field events for teams at that time. Although he could not give so much time of late, through work commitments, Bill helped wherever possible on committees and at meetings and remains the most loyal and enthusiastic of Belgravians. We wish him good fortune in his year of office. items.label: October 1979
items.sum: Bill Merryman's message as new President for 1979/80, recalling the club's early days training from a Chelsea pub and calling on members to support the club and its teams.
items.s: From The President Bill Merryman's message as new President for 1979/80, recalling the club's early days training from a Chelsea pub and calling on members to support the club and its teams. From The President Dear Belgravians, May I take this opportunity to thank all those who voted for me as Club President for 1979/80. After many years in athletics it is an honour I shall always cherish. Times have changed considerably from when I first joined Belgrave, we used to train then from a back room of a pub called "The Sun" in Chelsea. As a young new member at that time, the main thing that struck me so strongly, was the tremendous enthusiasm and great determination to own our Club Headquarters and to make Belgrave a name to be remembered. That band of athletes and officials got our Club Headquarters, and they made Belgrave a name in athletics. I am pleased to say we still have a few members, both as athletes and officials who have that enthusiasm and Belgrave Hall has been improved still further through this. But having said that, it must be pointed out they do need all the help and co-operation they can get. Unfortunately too many jobs are left to the few. It is your Club, it is what you feel and want for Belgrave; it is more than ever that your efforts are needed for the Club. How strong is your determination and enthusiasm? Will it spread to others to get our teams back on top again? To all active members who get selected for teams on track, road, and cross country, do give all the support you can and you will find your own performances will improve with it. Good luck in the year ahead. Bill Merryman Bill Merryman Bill Merryman President 1979/80 Chelsea Belgrave Hall

items.label: October 1979
items.sum: Club gossip column: Tom Carter's 50th year with Belgrave, the weddings of John Martin, Gordon Biscoe and Ann Manning, news of old members Dennis Brickwood, Mrs. Savage and Gordon Doubleday, and sightings of Ranjit Bhatia and the 90-year-old Charlie Speechley at the open 20 miles run.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: Tom Carter's 50th year with Belgrave, the weddings of John Martin, Gordon Biscoe and Ann Manning, news of old members Dennis Brickwood, Mrs. Savage and Gordon Doubleday, and sightings of Ranjit Bhatia and the 90-year-old Charlie Speechley at the open 20 miles run. grapevine Congratulations to Tom Carter who enters his 50th year with Belgrave. We understand that when Tom joined in 1929 he came 2nd in the Yacht 3 and soon after made 5th in the British Legion Ballroom Championships. It was lucky for Belgrave that these positions were not reversed because Tom's past and present contributions to the Club are second to none. Wedding bells for John Martin! A late September event which took Dorset by storm due in no small part to the weekend attendance at Bridport of some 30 Belgravians and their families. Our very best wishes to John and Jenny who are setting up home in Streatham. Can it be contagious? Are the rumours true? We are not sure but has Gordon Biscoe made wedding plans without us knowing? The answers to these questions are all YES! Scoop. Gordon and Margaret are to wed in late October, but so good is the security best man Charlie Manning doesn't know the date. But then knowing Charlie .....!!! However, our best wishes to Gordon and Margaret. We hope to see you around soon to hear all about it. And yet another one. Ann Manning married on October 6th so Charlie is forgiven for being in a perpetual state of shock. Again congratulations and every happiness to Ann and John. Spotted recently in a sports shop, in the shadow of St. Pauls in the City, was Dennis Brickwood. Dennis, a well known figure in Belgrave road running circles during the 1950's, has now retired from BP and no longer runs, but looks immensely fit. Not surprising when one considers that he now coaches squash several times a week, not to mention playing regularly. Of course he wishes all his old friends well. It was good to hear from Win. Shepherd that her mother, Mrs. Savage, is out of hospital and home again. Her loyalty and devotion to the Club date back to longer than most of us can remember, we certainly remember those sandwiches and great slices of cake which she used to serve at sit down teas in the hall which preceded our Socials. We are delighted that Gordon Doubleday has recovered from his illness and is once again contributing to the 'Belgravian'. Gordon unfortunately missed the 100 x 1 mile relay where he usually represents Belgrave as official time-keeper. Our good performance this year and Gordon's absence are believed to be unconnected. It was good to see our Vice-President, Ranjit Bhatia, at the open 20 miles run. He brought his gear and was seen running around the course with Clive Shippen. He looked very fit (he put up many fine performance for us when he was studying over here) and is the Indian correspondent of Athletics Weekly. Another seen at the "20" was our oldest active member, Charlie Speechley, who, at over 90 years of age still "doubles up" over 100 and 200 metres - he's in a class of his own, there appears to be no takers in the 90 plus class! items.label: October 1979
items.sum: Introduction to the track and field section reviewing a season in which Belgrave narrowly avoided relegation from Division 1 of the Southern League, thanking retiring secretary Steve Crosbie and welcoming Alan Mead as his successor.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Introduction to the track and field section reviewing a season in which Belgrave narrowly avoided relegation from Division 1 of the Southern League, thanking retiring secretary Steve Crosbie and welcoming Alan Mead as his successor. TRACK AND FIELD Early hopes of a significant improvement over last year's performance in the Southern League, Division 1 were quickly dashed and we ended the season fearing relegation. Fortunately, the top teams gaining promotion included area clubs Aldershot F and D, and Blackheath and for geographical reasons this effectively prevented our demotion. Our past dependence on Ernest Obeng and Cliff Brookes was clearly illustrated by the effect of their absence on our points scores at crucial matches. Nonetheless a year is a long time in athletics and with our youngsters showing remarkable improvement we face next year with determination and hope. Our thanks are due to track and field secretary, Steve Crosbie who steps down due to pressure of business and the need to devote more time to his new home. Steve has been blooded during a difficult episode in our history and hopes to pick up the threads as part of the management team at a future date. His athletics career will, we hope, progress unhindered by official responsibilities. Alan Mead takes over Steve's duties and brings to the post the experience and knowledge of Belgravians both present and past which few can match. We know he would not have taken the post unless he was prepared to give it 100 per cent. Wish him good fortune and please give him your full support. Alan outlines his plans following the review of the season's performances. items.s: Early Titles Report and results from the Surrey Championships preliminaries at Motspur Park on 28-29 April 1979, where Belgrave won the senior 4 x 100m and John Gladwin (also printed Gladwyn) the junior 400m. APRIL 28th & 29th 1979 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY CHAMPIONSHIPS. Early Titles Two Surrey titles in these preliminaries to the main championships. The senior 4 x 100 team looked strong on paper and so it proved on the track even with an awkward last change over. Ernest Obeng put us into the lead from the start, Derrick Williams carried the clubs colours down the back straight, but as Charlie Gillett came off the final bend he had a sudden attack of cramp and Jim Evans had to slow down to get the baton. John Gladwyn started his season off well with a time of 51.1 to win the Junior 400m title. items.s: MAY 5th 1979 - SUTCLIFFE PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVN.1. Report and results of the Southern League Division 1 match at Sutcliffe Park on 5 May 1979, where a depleted Belgrave team set several personal bests and finished 4th; Mark Lindsay-Bayley is also printed Lindsey-Bayley. MAY 5th 1979 - SUTCLIFFE PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVN.1. Although the team was much depleted, injuries hitting many athletes even before the season started, several personal bests were achieved during the afternoon. John Gladwin set a personal best in winning the A 800m with 2.0.3 having stayed in fourth place until the final straight. Derrick Williams broke the 7 metre barrier to win the A string with 7.07m. other personal bests were set by Mark Waller in the 800m and Simon Holmes in the 5000m. Paul Whitby and Mark Lindsay-Bayley produced good wins in the 110 hurdles and Paul completed the double with the 400 hurdles. Surprise maximum points came from the shot with Cliff Brooks and John Martin while Mark Shippen returned to form with a 4.10m win in the Pole Vault. A marvellous last leg by Reg Hopkins, given a split time of 51.5 ended the afternoon on a winning and noisy note. 100m: 2.J.Evans 11.1; 3.C.Brooks 11.8. 200m: 3.J.Evans 22.5; 3.C.Gillett 23.9. 400m: 2.D.Williams 53.1; 4.D.Bailey 54.0. 800m: 1.J.Gladwin 2.00.3; 4.M.Waller 2.03.6; 1500m: 5.S.Holmes 4.29.6; 5.D.Crutcher 4.54.6 5000m: 5.S.Holmes 15.55.0; 3.I.Duncan 15.58.4; 3000m SC: 4.I.Duncan 10.38.0; 3.L.Coy 10.39.8. 4 x 100m: 5.49.8 (P.Lyttle, C.Brooks, D.Williams, J.Evans) 4 x 400m: 1. 3.29.9 (J.Gladwin 53.2; D.Williams 53.1; C.Gillett 52.1; R.Hopkins 51.5) 110 H: 1.P.Whitby 16.2; 1.M.Lindsey-Bayley 16.4 400 H: 1.P.Whitby 58.1; 4.M.Lindsey-Bayley 63.4. MAY 8,10,11,12 1979 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY CHAMPIONSHIPS. More Medals Peter Crosbie retained his Javelin title to make his tally now eight successive Javelin wins in the Surrey's. This was his first competition of the season and the distance of 59.62m was very creditable considering his knee injury. Other title winners were John Gladwin with 2.1.4 in the Youths 800m and Scott Wyld in the Boys High Jump with 1.68m. items.s: Wet 10,000m Humorous rain-soaked report, written as a child talking to its mummy, of the club 10000m championship at Battersea Park on 30 May 1979 won by Laurie O'Hara, with full results and a boys' 100m. MAY 30th 1979 - BATTERSEA PARK - 10000m CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS. Wet 10,000m Help! Mummy, Mummy! My feet are wet, my clothes are wet, my hair's wet, everybody's soaked and still these silly men play splash in the puddles. Why don't they stop mummy, then I could go into the dry? My pen won't write, my pencil won't write, my crayons won't write. I don't know who went past me mummy, its so dark and they still keep wading by. They are nasty mummy, they keep shouting at me "how many laps left". I won't play with them, their mummies never taught them manners, I tell them they got to say please. I'm at the lido now mummy, and its still the same swimmers. They very clever, they swim on the lake. A bell mummy! The lifeguards are telling them to clear the pool. Simon, Ian and Laurie are all racing for the changing rooms. Laurie wins mummy, he had more air in his water-wings to keep him afloat. I'm still here mummy and so are the lifeguards, I'll thank them mummy, they all got wet but they did stay to see all the pool was clear of swimmers mummy. 1.L.O'Hara 33.0; 2.S.Holmes 33.01; 3.I.Duncan 33.05; 4.P.O'Connor 33.27; 5.R.Lettins 33.49; 6.C.Walker 35.30; 7.D.Searle 35.30; 8.K.Duckett 35.30; 9.T.Dowdall 35.40; 10.D.Maughan 35.49; 11.R.Bale 37.57; 12.P.Hardwick 38.29; 13.B.Taylor 38.50; 14.L.McLean 39.00; 15.L.Mann 39.33; 16.J.Myddleton 40.10; 17.S.Cox 40.40; 18.C.Manning 46.29. JUNE 2nd 1979 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGE. DIV.1. Normally the field seems to be let down by the track but this day it was the other way round. The track was slow after all the heavy rain in the week, but even so Nick Kirmatzis gained a personal best in the 1500, John Bicourt gave us good points in the steeple-chase and with Ernest Obeng all the sprints and both relays were won. With no real back up on the field the club was again fourth but by the narrowest of margins. 100m: 1.E.Obeng 11.5; 1.J.Evans 11.5 200m: 1.J.Evans 22.7; 1.C.Gillett 23.2 400m: 2.J.Gladwin 52.4; 1.D.Williams 51.2 800m: 2.J.Munoz 1.59.9; 2.S.Holmes 2.0.2. 1500m: 4.N.Kirmatzis 4.6.0; 4.J.Rimmer 4.20.0 110H: 4.M.Lindsey-Bayley 16.6; 4.D.Bailey 20.3 400 H: 4.D.Bailey 62.7; 3.M.Lindsey-Bayley 60.9 3000 SC: 1.J.Bicourt 9.29.6; 2.I.Duncan 10.13 5000m: 4.L.O'Hara 15.25 5.T. items.s: JULY 28th - CROYDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE, DIV.1. Report and results of the Southern League Division 1 match at Croydon on 28 July 1979, where a weakened Belgrave team won only two events and tied fourth with Bracknell.
